- **Why:** Visible success does not establish that generated code respects the application contract.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Route local mail to a development catcher
- **Do:** Route local mail to a development catcher.
- **Flag when:** Flag when local development uses production delivery credentials and sends test messages to real recipients.
- **Why:** A local catcher makes mail review repeatable without unintended delivery.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Configure fonts through the fonts option
- **Do:** Use the Laravel Vite plugin fonts option for generated font CSS and preloads rather than treating font sources only as generic assets.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a project expects generated font faces or @fonts preload links from entries configured only under assets.
- **Why:** Generic asset inclusion emits files without the font-specific CSS and preload metadata.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
laravel({ assets: ['resources/fonts/**'] })
```

After:
```php
laravel({ fonts: [local('Inter', { alias: 'sans', src: 'resources/fonts/Inter.woff2' })] })
```

#### Prefer the Inertia Form component on supported versions
- **Do:** Use the Inertia Form component for conventional forms when the installed adapter supports it, as in the Laravel 13 Inertia 3 starter kits; use useForm when programmatic form state is needed.
- **Flag when:** Flag conventional forms that duplicate submission and error handling already supplied by the supported Form component, or import Form from an adapter version that does not provide it.
- **Why:** The supported form abstraction centralizes submission, errors, and processing state.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Inertia 2.0
import { Form } from '@inertiajs/vue3';
```

After:
```php
import { Form } from '@inertiajs/react';
<Form action="/profile" method="put">
    {({ processing, errors }) => (<>
        <input name="name" />
        {errors.name && <p>{errors.name}</p>}
        <button type="submit" disabled={processing}>Save</button>
    </>)}
</Form>
```

#### Use Url attributes for shareable Livewire state
- **Do:** Bind shareable search, filter, sort, and pagination state with #[Url] on Livewire 3+ instead of legacy component $queryString arrays.
- **Flag when:** Flag when shareable state disappears on refresh or the component retains legacy query-string configuration while adopting the attribute API.
- **Why:** URL state makes the view restorable and shareable.
- **Enforced by:** rector:LivewireComponentQueryStringToUrlAttributeRector

Before:
```php
protected $queryString = ['search'];
```

After:
```php
#[Url]
public string $search = '';
```

#### Match skeleton geometry to loaded content
- **Do:** Make delayed component skeletons approximate the final layout and dimensions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a placeholder has negligible or substantially different dimensions and shifts surrounding content when loaded.
- **Why:** A stable placeholder reduces visible layout movement.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<div>Loading</div>
```

After:
```php
<div class="h-64 animate-pulse rounded bg-gray-200"></div>
```

#### Generate conventional Laravel classes with Artisan
- **Do:** Generate conventional Laravel classes with Artisan.
- **Flag when:** Flag when new framework classes are manually scaffolded with missing standard structure despite an applicable generator.
- **Why:** Generators apply the project framework stubs and directory conventions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Register package components with a unique prefix during provider boot
- **Do:** Register package components with a unique prefix during provider boot.
- **Flag when:** Flag when package/module or nonstandard components are not discoverable or share an unqualified name with another package.
- **Why:** Boot-time scoped registration gives consumers stable component identities.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Blade::component('alert', Alert::class);
```

After:
```php
Blade::componentNamespace('Vendor\Views\Components', 'vendor');
```

#### Persist a light dark or system appearance choice
- **Do:** For interfaces offering appearance selection, persist the chosen light/dark/system mode, resolve system mode from prefers-color-scheme and react to OS changes while system mode is selected; use Flux's appearance state where available.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an appearance selector loses its preference, ignores system-mode changes or conflicts with the active framework appearance state.
- **Why:** A single persistent preference keeps theme behavior consistent across visits and operating-system changes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Centralize recurring view data in targeted composers
- **Do:** Register a view composer in a provider boot method for data required every time the same views render.
- **Flag when:** Flag when multiple rendering paths repeat the same view-specific data preparation or a composer is registered before framework services are booted.
- **Why:** A targeted composer keeps recurring data available regardless of which controller renders the view.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return view('profile', ['menu' => Menu::all()]);
```

After:
```php
View::composer('profile', ProfileComposer::class);
```

#### Reuse shared Blade layout markup
- **Do:** Extract duplicated page shell and markup into shared Blade layouts or components and use slots for page-specific content.
- **Flag when:** Flag when authenticated and guest layouts or multiple pages duplicate the same structural markup.
- **Why:** A shared shell keeps navigation, metadata, and accessibility fixes consistent.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<html><body>Page A</body></html>
```

After:
```php
<x-layout><x-slot:title>Page A</x-slot:title>Page A</x-layout>
```

#### Use Blade directives for conditional boolean attributes
- **Do:** Use @checked, @selected, @disabled, @readonly, and @required for conditional form attributes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when templates emit boolean form attributes through repeated ternary strings or hand-written echo conditions.
- **Why:** The directives express boolean intent and avoid malformed attribute values.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<input {{ $active ? 'checked' : '' }}>
```

After:
```php
<input @checked(old('active', $active))>
```

#### Use Blade if for custom conditionals
- **Do:** Define reusable conditional template checks with Blade::if rather than hand-written directive compiler strings.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom directive emits if/endif PHP solely to implement a reusable boolean check.
- **Why:** Blade::if handles the paired conditional syntax and keeps the callback focused on the condition.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Blade::directive('disk', fn () => '<?php if (config("filesystems.default") === "s3"): ?>');
```

After:
```php
Blade::if('disk', fn ($disk) => config('filesystems.default') === $disk);
```

#### Use Inertia links for internal page navigation
- **Do:** Use Inertia Link for same-application navigation, retaining ordinary anchors for downloads, external URLs, or deliberate full reloads.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an internal Inertia page link uses an ordinary anchor and unintentionally triggers a full document navigation.
- **Why:** Inertia links preserve client navigation behavior and page state handling.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<a href="/users">Users</a>
```

After:
```php
<Link href="/users">Users</Link>
```

#### Use the Inertia Vite plugin for v3 development SSR
- **Do:** Use @inertiajs/vite for Inertia v3 SSR during Vite development instead of maintaining a second development SSR process.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the v3 development workflow unnecessarily starts a separate Node SSR daemon while the Vite plugin can render the same pages.
- **Why:** The integrated development renderer follows Vite module changes without a separate server lifecycle.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use islands for useful one-off update isolation
- **Do:** Use Livewire 4 islands for expensive independently updated regions; avoid islands for static or tightly coupled fast content.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a one-off expensive region forces the whole component to rerender, or static markup is needlessly split into islands.
- **Why:** A focused island reduces rendering without introducing an unnecessary child lifecycle.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<section>{{ $this->expensiveReport }}</section>
```

After:
```php
@island(name: 'report')<section>{{ $this->expensiveReport }}</section>@endisland
```

#### Confirm destructive Livewire actions
- **Do:** Add an explicit confirmation to destructive Livewire actions, using typed confirmation for irreversible high-impact actions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a delete or account-removal action executes immediately without an appropriate confirmation.
- **Why:** Confirmation reduces accidental destructive input while server authorization remains necessary.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<button wire:click="deleteAccount">Delete</button>
```

After:
```php
<button wire:click="deleteAccount" wire:confirm.prompt="Type DELETE to confirm|DELETE">Delete</button>
```

#### Skip rendering for actions with no UI changes
- **Do:** Mark Livewire actions with no visible state changes renderless or call skipRender.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an action only records analytics or performs background work but re-renders an unchanged component.
- **Why:** Skipping rendering avoids needless queries, HTML transfer, and morphing.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function recordView() { /* analytics only */ }
```

After:
```php
#[Renderless]
public function recordView() { /* analytics only */ }
```

#### Match the existing Tailwind styling system
- **Do:** Follow the installed Tailwind version and existing utility and component conventions when adding styles.
- **Flag when:** Flag when new UI introduces a competing styling approach or unsupported utilities without a project requirement.
- **Why:** Consistent styling patterns make shared UI easier to maintain.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<div style="display:flex;align-items:center">
```

After:
```php
<div class="flex items-center">
```

#### Use DeferrableProvider for deferred service providers
- **Do:** Use DeferrableProvider for deferred service providers.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a provider relies on the removed $defer property.
- **Why:** The supported contract declares deferred provider behavior.
- **Enforced by:** rector:PropertyDeferToDeferrableProviderToRector

Before:
```php
protected $defer = true;
```

After:
```php
class ReportProvider extends ServiceProvider implements DeferrableProvider { /* provides() */ }
```

#### Use the official browser client for Fortify passkey ceremonies
- **Do:** Use the official browser client for Fortify passkey ceremonies.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom browser code hand-builds WebAuthn request/response transformations incompatible with the Fortify endpoint contract.
- **Why:** The matching client handles the browser/server ceremony contract.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Manually convert all WebAuthn binary fields.
```

After:
```php
// Use @laravel/passkeys with Fortify endpoints.
```

#### Use Inertia to bridge Laravel routes to React Vue or Svelte pages
- **Do:** Use Inertia to bridge Laravel routes to React Vue or Svelte pages.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Laravel-rendered JS frontend duplicates routing/authentication and release coordination despite a requirement for a unified full-stack application.
- **Why:** Inertia can retain server routes and auth while rendering framework page components.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Separate frontend implements a second router/auth layer without a need.
```

After:
```php
return Inertia::render('Dashboard', $data);
```

#### Declare the Laravel majors a package actually supports
- **Do:** Declare the Laravel majors a package actually supports.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Illuminate/framework constraints exclude a tested supported major or claim majors outside the package compatibility matrix.
- **Why:** Dependency constraints should match verified package compatibility.
- **Enforced by:** partial: shift:workbench/bump-laravel-package-dependencies

Before:
```php
"illuminate/support": "^12.0" // package also supports 13
```

After:
```php
"illuminate/support": "^12.0 || ^13.0"
```

#### Name Blade view files in kebab case
- **Do:** Name Blade view files in kebab case under the project convention.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a view filename uses camelCase or underscores where kebab-case naming is adopted.
- **Why:** Consistent names make view paths predictable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
openSource.blade.php
```

After:
```php
open-source.blade.php
```

#### Use Blade for Laravel server templates
- **Do:** Use Blade for server-rendered Laravel templates when adopting the standard Laravel view stack.
- **Flag when:** Flag when new server views introduce Twig without an established project requirement.
- **Why:** Using the existing engine keeps Laravel components and directives available.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return $twig->render('profile.twig', $data);
```

After:
```php
return view('profile', $data);
```

#### Return named fragments for partial HTML responses
- **Do:** Return a named Blade fragment for htmx or Turbo requests that replace only one region, while retaining the full response for normal visits.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a partial-update endpoint returns the entire layout to a client expecting one HTML region.
- **Why:** Named fragments share the page template without sending unrelated layout markup.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return view('users', $data);
```

After:
```php
return view('users', $data)->fragmentIf(request()->hasHeader('HX-Request'), 'users-list');
```

#### Use Blade class directives for conditional class lists
- **Do:** Use @class for conditional classes on ordinary elements, reserving attribute-bag merging for attribute-forwarding roots.
- **Flag when:** Flag when ordinary template elements concatenate conditional class strings or consume the component attribute bag only to add internal classes.
- **Why:** Class arrays keep conditions readable without forwarding unrelated attributes to internal elements.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<div class="{{ $active ? 'font-bold' : '' }}">Text</div>
```

After:
```php
<div @class(['font-bold' => $active])>Text</div>
```

#### Run the asset dev server while developing
- **Do:** Run the project asset dev server or rebuild assets after frontend changes when pages still use an old build or the manifest lacks an entry.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the development workflow serves stale built assets and lacks a running bundler or a fresh build for changed entries.
- **Why:** Blade changes and frontend source changes have different build requirements; the browser needs current assets.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Reload only required Inertia props
- **Do:** Limit polling and interaction reloads to the props that actually change using only or an equivalent partial reload.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a polling or local refresh request recomputes all page props even though only a known subset changes.
- **Why:** Partial reloads reduce database work and response size.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
router.reload();
```

After:
```php
router.reload({ only: ['stats'] });
```

#### Load off-screen Inertia data when it becomes visible
- **Do:** Use WhenVisible or the installed equivalent to fetch expensive below-the-fold regions when the user approaches them.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an off-screen optional region loads expensive data eagerly on every page visit.
- **Why:** Viewport-triggered loading avoids work for content the user never reaches.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<RelatedItems items={allRelated} />
```

After:
```php
<WhenVisible data="related" fallback={<Skeleton />}><RelatedItems /></WhenVisible>
```

#### Use flash data for one-time Inertia notifications
- **Do:** Send one-time notifications through Inertia::flash on supported versions rather than persistent page props.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a toast or one-time highlight is stored in page props and reappears when browser history restores the page.
- **Why:** Flash data avoids retaining transient notifications in page history state.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Inertia::render('Users', ['toast' => 'Saved']);
```

After:
```php
Inertia::flash('toast', 'Saved');
```

#### Use computed properties for derived page data
- **Do:** Expose expensive derived page data through #[Computed] instead of legacy accessor names or repeated queries in render.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a component uses getNameProperty accessors or unconditionally recomputes expensive data in render on every update.
- **Why:** Computed values memoize per request and are evaluated only when needed.
- **Enforced by:** partial: rector:LivewireComponentComputedMethodToComputedAttributeRector

Before:
```php
public function render() { return view('livewire.list', ['posts' => Post::all()]); }
```

After:
```php
#[Computed]
public function posts() { return Post::all(); }
```

#### Use Blade for presentation without an independent Livewire lifecycle
- **Do:** Extract a plain Blade component for reusable presentation and add a child Livewire component only when it needs server interaction, isolated state, or its own lifecycle.
- **Flag when:** Flag when nested Livewire components only render static presentation that a Blade component could provide.
- **Why:** Each Livewire child adds hydration and lifecycle overhead.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<livewire:card-title :title="$title" />
```

After:
```php
<x-card-title :title="$title" />
```

#### Use braces for every control-structure body
- **Do:** Use braces for every control-structure body.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a PHP control structure omits braces even for a single statement.
- **Why:** Braces prevent accidental scope changes when another statement is added.
- **Enforced by:** pint:control_structure_braces

Before:
```php
if ($active) save();
```

After:
```php
if ($active) { save(); }
```

#### Use intention-revealing prefix and suffix checks
- **Do:** Use intention-revealing prefix and suffix checks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a substring comparison only checks whether a string starts or ends with a value.
- **Why:** Dedicated checks avoid manual lengths and offsets.
- **Enforced by:** partial: rector:SubStrToStartsWithOrEndsWithStaticMethodCallRector

Before:
```php
substr($name, 0, 3) === 'api'
```

After:
```php
Str::startsWith($name, 'api')
```

#### Pre-render the maintenance response before replacing dependencies
- **Do:** Pre-render the maintenance response before replacing dependencies.
- **Flag when:** Flag when maintenance deployment depends on booting partially replaced Composer dependencies to render its error page.
- **Why:** A pre-rendered maintenance response can be served before the full application boots.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use Blade render instead of hand-written compiler execution
- **Do:** Use Blade render instead of hand-written compiler execution.
- **Flag when:** Flag when application code manually compiles and evaluates Blade strings despite the public Blade::render API.
- **Why:** The public rendering API owns the framework compilation and data-binding behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
eval('?>'.$compiler->compileString($template));
```

After:
```php
Blade::render($trustedTemplate, $data)
```

#### Organize related Livewire components by domain
- **Do:** Organize related Livewire components by domain.
- **Flag when:** Flag when unrelated component folders obscure coherent domain groupings in a large component set.
- **Why:** Domain organization keeps related screens and behavior near each other.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
app/Livewire/EditQuote.php // among many unrelated files
```

After:
```php
app/Livewire/Quotes/EditQuote.php
```

#### Provide minimal reproducible bug reports
- **Do:** Provide minimal reproducible bug reports.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a package bug report depends on a private production application or screenshots without executable reproduction steps.
- **Why:** A small reproduction lets maintainers verify the exact behavior independently.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Prefer a matching official starter kit for a new application
- **Do:** Prefer a matching official starter kit for a new application.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a new app recreates standard auth/frontend/bundler scaffolding despite a matching official starter kit and no custom requirement.
- **Why:** The matching kit supplies a coherent initial frontend and authentication setup.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Complete the selected Tailwind build integration
- **Do:** Complete the selected Tailwind build integration.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Tailwind integration omits the plugin or PostCSS configuration actually required by its installed major and selected build path.
- **Why:** Vite and PostCSS integrations have different setup requirements; configuration must match the chosen one.
- **Enforced by:** partial: shift:public/vite/postcss

Before:
```php
plugins: [laravel({ input: ['resources/css/app.css'] })] // v4 Tailwind not integrated
```

After:
```php
plugins: [laravel({ input: ['resources/css/app.css'] }), tailwindcss()] // import @tailwindcss/vite
```

#### Set Cloud push-to-deploy behavior deliberately
- **Do:** Review each Cloud environment's tracked branch and Push to deploy setting, and configure automatic deployment to match its release workflow.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a branch push can unexpectedly deploy an environment because its default automatic deployment setting was never reviewed.
- **Why:** Push to deploy automatically releases pushes to the environment branch when enabled.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Register Fortify view callbacks during application provider boot
- **Do:** Register custom Fortify login, registration and other authentication view callbacks together in FortifyServiceProvider::boot(), or a focused method called from boot().
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom Fortify view callbacks are registered per request in controllers or are missing from provider bootstrapping while those view routes are enabled.
- **Why:** Provider boot supplies the intended view callbacks before Fortify serves its authentication pages.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// A controller registers Fortify::loginView during a request.
```

After:
```php
public function boot(): void { Fortify::loginView(fn () => view('auth.login')); }
```

#### Name intentionally public frontend variables with the VITE prefix
- **Do:** Expose intentionally public build-time configuration through VITE_* variables and read it through import.meta.env; reuse suitable local .env values through interpolation when supported.
- **Flag when:** Flag when frontend code expects an unprefixed server environment variable to be available in the bundle or duplicates a public value inconsistently.
- **Why:** Vite exposes prefixed values at build time; the exposed values are public and must not contain secrets.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
import.meta.env.APP_NAME
```

After:
```php
import.meta.env.VITE_APP_NAME
```

#### Configure a class-driven dark variant for manual Tailwind themes
- **Do:** When the Tailwind 4 application selects dark mode with an ancestor .dark class, define the dark custom variant in CSS to match that selector.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a manual theme switch toggles .dark but dark utilities still follow only the system media query or use an obsolete Tailwind 3 configuration.
- **Why:** The selector driving dark utilities must agree with the application's appearance state.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));
```

#### Provide the stylesheet rule required by Alpine x-cloak
- **Do:** When markup uses x-cloak, make sure an early [x-cloak] { display: none !important; } rule is loaded. Livewire 3/4 styles inject it automatically; add it to your CSS for standalone Alpine or when Livewire asset injection is disabled.
- **Flag when:** Flag x-cloak usage on pages that load neither Livewire's injected styles nor an app [x-cloak] hiding rule, or where that rule is overridden.
- **Why:** Alpine removes x-cloak after initialization; CSS must hide the marked content beforehand.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<div x-cloak x-show="open">Menu</div> <!-- no cloak CSS -->
```

After:
```php
[x-cloak] { display: none !important; }
```

#### Apply the resolved theme before the first page paint
- **Do:** For class-driven themes, initialize the root dark class and initial document background in a small head script/style before the main bundle paints, using the persisted or system appearance preference.
- **Flag when:** Flag when dark-mode visitors see a light page flash because theme initialization waits for a deferred frontend bundle.
- **Why:** Theme-aware background and root classes must be present for the first visible frame.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use the established typed script-setup Vue component structure
- **Do:** For Vue components following the starter kit's Composition API convention, use <script setup lang="ts"> before the template and keep component logic in that typed setup block.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a new Vue SFC introduces an untyped or competing component authoring style without a project reason.
- **Why:** A shared typed component structure keeps frontend contracts visible and neighboring files consistent.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
<script setup lang="ts">
// component logic
</script>
<template>...</template>
```

#### Keep Tailwind border-color compatibility until callers are explicit
- **Do:** During a Tailwind 3-to-4 transition, retain the generated border-color compatibility base layer until every control relying on the old default has an explicit intended border color.
- **Flag when:** Flag when removing the compatibility rule changes existing border appearance because controls use border width utilities without a color utility.
- **Why:** Tailwind 4 changed the default border color, so removing the shim can change unmodified components.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Apply a Blade-aware formatter only to genuine Blade templates
- **Do:** Keep *.blade.php out of ordinary PHP formatting unless a Blade-aware rule such as Pint/laravel_blade is enabled, and exclude Envoy.blade.php task files from that Blade formatter.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the plain PHP formatter rewrites Blade syntax or an Envoy task definition is treated as an HTML Blade view.
- **Why:** Blade templates and Envoy task files have syntax and semantics that require different formatter handling.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use concise named-slot tags under the adopted Blade convention
- **Do:** When following the concise Blade slot convention, write static named slots as <x-slot:title> rather than repeating the name attribute.
- **Flag when:** Flag when equivalent static named slots inconsistently use the long form in code adopting the shorthand convention.
- **Why:** The shorthand removes repeated slot-name boilerplate without changing the slot interface.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<x-slot name="title">Settings</x-slot>
```

After:
```php
<x-slot:title>Settings</x-slot>
```

#### Declare related application entries in one Vite configuration
- **Do:** Use multiple entry points in the application's Vite configuration for related asset bundles rather than starting separate competing Vite development servers solely for each bundle.
- **Flag when:** Flag when related application bundles require multiple dev servers and conflicting hot-file or manifest settings without an independent build-system requirement.
- **Why:** One coherent configuration coordinates development serving and production output for the application.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Define component size and variant scales centrally
- **Do:** Use a shared component library with a small named size/variant scale and intentional defaults. Define the scale once through theme tokens, utilities or variant maps so equivalent controls align across the application.
- **Flag when:** Flag when equivalent controls implement independent size values or the same named size produces inconsistent dimensions without an intentional variant.
- **Why:** A shared scale keeps controls visually consistent and makes coordinated changes straightforward.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep substantial scripts and styles in asset files
- **Do:** Move substantial application JavaScript and CSS into the asset pipeline; use template stacks for small page-specific initialization.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Blade templates contain large script or style blocks implementing application behavior or reusable styling.
- **Why:** Asset files support bundling, caching, and reuse without making templates difficult to maintain.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<script>/* application implementation */</script>
```

After:
```php
@vite(['resources/js/app.js'])
```

#### Keep HTML markup in views
- **Do:** Render HTML through Blade views or components instead of assembling markup strings in PHP application classes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a controller or service concatenates substantial HTML strings.
- **Why:** Templates keep rendering separate from application behavior and make escaping easier to review.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return "<p>".$name."</p>";
```

After:
```php
return view('greeting', ['name' => $name]);
```

#### Make include dependencies explicit
- **Do:** Pass an explicit data array to partials when inherited variables obscure dependencies; use @includeIsolated when parent data must be excluded.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an include relies on unrelated parent variables or receives implicit data despite requiring isolation.
- **Why:** Explicit inputs make partials safe to reuse in different rendering contexts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
@include('partials.user')
```

After:
```php
@includeIsolated('partials.user', ['user' => $user])
```

#### Load repeated component scripts once
- **Do:** Deduplicate scripts pushed by repeatedly rendered components with consistently named @pushOnce blocks or equivalent @once wrappers.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a component rendered more than once pushes the same script through an unguarded @push.
- **Why:** Repeated script initialization can duplicate event handlers and network requests.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
@push('scripts')<script src="/widget.js"></script>@endpush
```

After:
```php
@pushOnce('scripts', 'widget')<script src="/widget.js"></script>@endPushOnce
```

#### Forward declared wrapper props explicitly
- **Do:** Declare wrapper component props and pass them explicitly to child components that need them.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a wrapper declares a prop but assumes it remains in $attributes and reaches the nested component automatically.
- **Why:** Declared props are removed from the attribute bag, so automatic forwarding can silently lose them.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
@props(['size'])<x-input {{ $attributes }} />
```

After:
```php
@props(['size'])<x-input :size="$size" {{ $attributes }} />
```

#### Keep contextual spacing outside reusable components
- **Do:** Let callers supply outer margins, positioning, and contextual widths through component classes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a reusable component hard-codes outer margins or positioning that callers must undo for other layouts.
- **Why:** Layout-neutral components can be reused across pages without override chains.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<div class="mt-8 fixed w-64">{{ $slot }}</div>
```

After:
```php
<div {{ $attributes->class(['rounded']) }}>{{ $slot }}</div>
```

#### Pass simple variables to Js::from
- **Do:** Compute complex expressions before the template and pass existing variables to Js::from.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Js::from in a Blade echo receives a complex nested expression that the template compiler may misparse.
- **Why:** Simple variable arguments avoid regex-based compilation ambiguity.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
{{ Js::from($users->map(fn ($u) => $u->id)) }}
```

After:
```php
{{ Js::from($userIds) }}
```

#### Do not locate Blade sources with PHP file constants
- **Do:** Resolve source templates through Laravel view names or known source paths rather than __DIR__ or __FILE__ inside Blade.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Blade template uses __DIR__ or __FILE__ to locate its source template directory.
- **Why:** Those constants point at the compiled cache file when the view executes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
@php $path = __DIR__.'/partial.blade.php'; @endphp
```

After:
```php
@include('partials.details')
```

#### Use Blade comments for private template notes
- **Do:** Write template-only notes as Blade comments so they are removed from rendered HTML.
- **Flag when:** Flag when internal implementation notes use HTML comments and are sent to the browser.
- **Why:** Blade comments keep implementation notes out of public responses.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<!-- Internal template note -->
```

After:
```php
{{-- Internal template note --}}
```

#### Keep Blade directives out of component tag attributes
- **Do:** Compute component attribute values with PHP expressions instead of placing Blade directives inside component tags.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a component attribute contains @env, @if, or another unsupported directive.
- **Why:** Blade does not compile such directives inside component tags.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<x-alert :live="@env('production')" />
```

After:
```php
<x-alert :live="app()->environment('production')" />
```

#### Avoid periods in view directory names
- **Do:** Use directory names without periods under view roots.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a view source directory includes a period that conflicts with dot-notation view lookup.
- **Why:** Dots separate view path segments and make such directories ambiguous.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
resources/views/admin.v2/index.blade.php
```

After:
```php
resources/views/admin-v2/index.blade.php
```

#### Use block PHP directives when template PHP is necessary
- **Do:** Write necessary template PHP with @php ... @endphp rather than inline @php(...) syntax.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Blade template uses the unsupported or discouraged inline @php(...) form.
- **Why:** Block syntax follows the documented compiler interface.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
@php($total = 0)
```

After:
```php
@php
    $total = 0;
@endphp
```

#### Use build-managed relative asset references
- **Do:** Reference component and stylesheet assets with paths Vite can rewrite and bundle, using relative source imports for build-managed assets.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a dedicated CSS entry or component references source assets through absolute application paths that resolve against the dev server or bypass bundling.
- **Why:** Processed references receive correct development URLs and production versioning.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
background-image: url(/resources/images/logo.png);
```

After:
```php
background-image: url(../images/logo.png);
```

#### Keep absolute asset references in public
- **Do:** Place intentionally absolute-path assets in public and use explicit CDN URLs when required; do not expect ASSET_URL to rewrite absolute references.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an absolute asset path points to a source-only file or assumes ASSET_URL will prefix it.
- **Why:** Vite leaves absolute references unchanged and does not copy those files from resources.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<img src="/resources/images/logo.png">
```

After:
```php
<img src="/images/logo.png"> <!-- public/images/logo.png -->
```

#### Use trusted certificates for HTTPS asset development
- **Do:** Use the site trusted TLS certificate for the Vite development server when the application is served over HTTPS.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an HTTPS local application loads Vite over insecure HTTP or an untrusted certificate despite an available trusted site certificate.
- **Why:** Consistent trusted HTTPS avoids mixed-content failures and certificate bypasses.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
server: { https: {} }
```

After:
```php
server: { https: { key: readFileSync(keyPath), cert: readFileSync(certPath) } }
```

#### Configure Vue asset URL transformation for Laravel Vite
- **Do:** Configure the Vue Vite plugin to preserve absolute public URLs and let Vite process relative component assets.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the Laravel Vue plugin rewrites absolute public URLs or resolves relative assets against the wrong base.
- **Why:** Correct transformAssetUrls settings keep public assets distinct from build-managed assets.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
vue()
```

After:
```php
vue({ template: { transformAssetUrls: { base: null, includeAbsolute: false } } })
```

#### Serve optimized fonts locally
- **Do:** Self-host interface fonts when privacy or availability requirements call for it, using the Vite font pipeline or an appropriate local Filament font provider.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a privacy-sensitive deployment loads fonts from a disallowed third-party CDN.
- **Why:** Local delivery reduces third-party requests and keeps font availability under application control.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
->font('Inter', provider: GoogleFontProvider::class)
```

After:
```php
->font('Inter', provider: LocalFontProvider::class)
```

#### Preload only the font variants a page needs
- **Do:** Limit font preloads and @fonts aliases to variants actually needed for the initial page.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a page preloads unused families or weights, competing with its critical assets.
- **Why:** Selective preloading avoids wasting bandwidth on fonts the first render will not use.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
@fonts // all configured families on every page
```

After:
```php
@fonts('sans')
```

#### Guard and display deferred prop loading states
- **Do:** Guard deferred props until they arrive and render a visible empty state or skeleton that fits the final region.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a page dereferences an undefined deferred prop or leaves its loading region blank without feedback.
- **Why:** Deferred data is initially absent; a guarded placeholder prevents errors and explains the pending content.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<Stats value={stats.total} />
```

After:
```php
<Deferred data="stats" fallback={<StatsSkeleton />}><Stats /></Deferred>
```

#### Start conditional Inertia polling explicitly
- **Do:** Set usePoll autoStart to false when refreshes should begin only after an explicit trigger.
- **Flag when:** Flag when polling starts immediately despite a screen requirement to wait for user activation or job creation.
- **Why:** Delayed startup avoids requests for inactive work.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
usePoll(2000);
```

After:
```php
const { start } = usePoll(2000, {}, { autoStart: false });
```

#### Render non-GET Inertia links as buttons
- **Do:** Set the explicit HTTP method and render non-GET Inertia actions as buttons.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a logout or destructive action uses a GET link or renders a non-GET operation as a navigable anchor.
- **Why:** Buttons express an action and avoid browser link behavior that assumes a GET navigation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<Link href="/logout">Log out</Link>
```

After:
```php
<Link href="/logout" method="post" as="button">Log out</Link>
```

#### Keep Inertia pages in the configured page directory
- **Do:** Return Inertia pages through Inertia::render and keep page components under the directory and filename convention used by the resolver.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an Inertia endpoint returns a plain Blade page or names a component outside its configured page resolver.
- **Why:** Server page names and client module lookup must agree.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return view('users.index');
```

After:
```php
return Inertia::render('Users/Index', ['users' => $users]);
```

#### Use the HTTP client supplied by the installed Inertia version
- **Do:** Use Inertia v3 built-in XHR behavior and interceptors, or declare Axios explicitly when application code requires it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Inertia v3 code imports or configures Axios as though it remains an undeclared bundled dependency.
- **Why:** An implicit removed dependency breaks builds or request customization.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
import axios from 'axios'; // undeclared dependency
```

After:
```php
"dependencies": { "axios": "^1.0" } // only if application code requires Axios; keep the lockfile current
```

#### Keep authoritative Livewire state on the server
- **Do:** Keep authoritative application state in Livewire and let the interface reflect validated server state, while keeping local-only presentation in Alpine.
- **Flag when:** Flag when independent client state is treated as authoritative for persisted business data without server validation or reconciliation.
- **Why:** A clear authority prevents client and server from disagreeing about accepted application state.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Client-only flag decides whether an invoice is paid.
```

After:
```php
public function pay(): void { $this->authorize('pay', $this->invoice); /* persist */ }
```

#### Keep large read-only datasets out of Livewire public state
- **Do:** Store only the minimal identifiers or primitive state needed by Livewire and expose large read-only datasets through computed values.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a component hydrates large objects or read-only collections as public state on every update.
- **Why:** Smaller state reduces serialization cost and unintended data exposure.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public $posts; // thousands of read-only records
```

After:
```php
#[Computed]
public function posts() { return Post::query()->paginate(); }
```

#### Reset pagination when filters change
- **Do:** Reset the relevant Livewire paginator when search, filter, or sort inputs change.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a filter change leaves the paginator on a now out-of-range page.
- **Why:** Resetting shows the first matching results instead of a misleading empty page.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function updatedSearch(): void {}
```

After:
```php
public function updatedSearch(): void { $this->resetPage(); }
```

#### Scope periodic refreshes to the region that changes
- **Do:** Place wire:poll inside an island when only that region needs periodic updates.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a small periodically changing region causes the whole large component to re-render.
- **Why:** Scoped polling reduces repeated queries and HTML morphing.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<div wire:poll>Whole dashboard</div>
```

After:
```php
@island(name: 'stats')<div wire:poll>{{ $this->stats }}</div>@endisland
```

#### Register global hooks during livewire init
- **Do:** Register Livewire directives, hooks, and global listeners in a livewire:init listener.
- **Flag when:** Flag when global registrations run before Livewire exists or after components have already initialized.
- **Why:** The init event provides the intended registration point.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Livewire.on('saved', callback);
```

After:
```php
document.addEventListener('livewire:init', () => { Livewire.on('saved', callback); });
```

#### Remove redundant and conflicting utility classes
- **Do:** Remove duplicate or overridden Tailwind utilities and place inheritable styles at the appropriate parent level.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a class list repeats utilities, contains conflicting equivalent variants, or duplicates inherited styles on every child without a need.
- **Why:** Shorter unambiguous class lists make the intended styles easier to assess.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<div class="text-sm text-sm p-2 p-4">
```

After:
```php
<div class="text-sm p-4">
```

#### Use utilities supported by the installed Tailwind major
- **Do:** Use only utilities supported by the installed Tailwind major and migrate removed v3 utility names when adopting v4.
- **Flag when:** Flag when markup uses utilities removed or renamed in the installed Tailwind major.
- **Why:** Unsupported utilities silently omit the intended styling.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<div class="flex-shrink-0 bg-opacity-50">
```

After:
```php
<div class="shrink-0 bg-blue-500/50">
```

#### Remove unsupported Tailwind 4 corePlugins settings
- **Do:** Remove unsupported corePlugins configuration when upgrading to Tailwind 4 and use supported replacements for the intended behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Tailwind 4 project relies on corePlugins configuration.
- **Why:** Tailwind 4 does not implement that configuration API.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
corePlugins: { preflight: false }
```

After:
```php
/* Use the documented v4 import selection for the desired layers. */
```

#### Replace removed opacity utilities in Tailwind 4
- **Do:** Replace removed color-opacity utilities with slash opacity modifiers on the associated color utilities in Tailwind 4.
- **Flag when:** Flag when v4 markup uses bg-opacity, text-opacity, border-opacity, divide-opacity, ring-opacity, or placeholder-opacity utilities.
- **Why:** Slash opacity expresses the color and opacity together through the supported utility.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class="bg-blue-500 bg-opacity-50"
```

After:
```php
class="bg-blue-500/50"
```

#### Use supported flex grow and shrink names
- **Do:** Replace flex-grow and flex-shrink utility names with grow and shrink in Tailwind 4.
- **Flag when:** Flag when v4 markup uses removed flex-grow-* or flex-shrink-* classes.
- **Why:** The renamed utilities keep flex behavior in the v4 build.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class="flex-shrink-0 flex-grow"
```

After:
```php
class="shrink-0 grow"
```

#### Preserve supported dark-mode behavior
- **Do:** Add the matching dark-mode styles to new UI in applications that support dark mode.
- **Flag when:** Flag when new text, borders, surfaces, or controls lack appropriate dark-mode styles while neighboring UI supports them.
- **Why:** Matching modes keeps the new interface readable and visually consistent.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<div class="bg-white text-black">
```

After:
```php
<div class="bg-white text-gray-900 dark:bg-gray-900 dark:text-gray-100">
```

#### Prefer utilities over repeated inline styles
- **Do:** Use the project Tailwind utilities for static styling and reserve inline values for dynamic or otherwise necessary styles.
- **Flag when:** Flag when static inline styles duplicate utilities used elsewhere in the project.
- **Why:** Utilities preserve the design vocabulary and responsive or dark-mode variants.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<div style="padding: 1rem">
```

After:
```php
<div class="p-4">
```

#### Write complete literal utility names
- **Do:** Write full Tailwind class names or map variants to complete literals instead of concatenating class fragments.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a runtime expression constructs class names that the Tailwind scanner cannot see.
- **Why:** The build only emits detected utilities, so constructed names can disappear in production.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class="bg-{{ $color }}-500"
```

After:
```php
@class(['bg-red-500' => $color === 'red', 'bg-blue-500' => $color === 'blue'])
```

#### Use components available in the installed Flux edition
- **Do:** Use Pro-only Flux components only when the project has the required Flux Pro package and license.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a free-edition project renders components available only in Flux Pro.
- **Why:** Unavailable components fail to resolve and cannot be assumed from free-edition installation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<flux:calendar /> <!-- Pro package absent -->
```

After:
```php
<flux:input type="date" label="Date" /> {{-- use an available control in the installed edition --}}
```

#### Choose rate-limit keys with shared-IP and lockout risks in mind
- **Do:** Choose rate-limit keys with shared-IP and lockout risks in mind.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a sensitive endpoint uses only a shared IP or an attacker-chosen victim identity in a way that enables unfair lockout.
- **Why:** Key design must balance abuse prevention with users behind shared networks and targeted denial of service.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Limit::perMinute(5)->by($request->ip())
```

After:
```php
// Apply appropriate layered IP and account limits with the application threat model.
```

#### Use PHP nullsafe access for simple optional chains
- **Do:** Use PHP nullsafe access for simple optional chains.
- **Flag when:** Flag when optional wraps a nullable object solely for a simple property or method access without a callback.
- **Why:** The native operator expresses the nullable access directly.
- **Enforced by:** rector:OptionalToNullsafeOperatorRector, shift:workbench/convert-optional-to-nullsafe

Before:
```php
optional($user)->name
```

After:
```php
$user?->name
```

#### Record inferred conventions within the authorized scope
- **Do:** Record inferred conventions within the authorized scope.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a rule-recording workflow saves inferred candidates without the required user authorization or hides conflicting evidence.
- **Why:** Approval should cover the concrete proposed scope and wording unless automatic recording was explicitly authorized.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Scope convention rules to the narrowest evidenced path
- **Do:** Scope convention rules to the narrowest evidenced path.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a rule uses a broad glob such as app/** even though its evidence applies only to a subtree.
- **Why:** Narrow scopes avoid applying local conventions to unrelated code.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Version shared project convention files
- **Do:** Version shared project convention files.
- **Flag when:** Flag when team convention files are untracked or ignored and therefore unavailable to other contributors and agents.
- **Why:** Versioned rules keep the shared guidance reproducible.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Record only useful project-specific conventions not already enforced by tooling
- **Do:** Record only useful project-specific conventions not already enforced by tooling.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a convention note duplicates an active formatter/framework default or repeats an existing rule without adding a deliberate project choice.
- **Why:** High-signal notes preserve context that tools and defaults cannot supply automatically.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Check Artisan command help instead of guessing arguments
- **Do:** Check Artisan command help instead of guessing arguments.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an automation invokes undocumented command arguments or options that the installed command does not accept.
- **Why:** Installed command help is the direct contract for generators and operational commands.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Separate preview identities and environments from production
- **Do:** Separate preview identities and environments from production.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production and preview/staging share privileged identities or the same mutable environment boundary.
- **Why:** Separate environments and nonproduction IAM roles contain preview changes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Explain verification and provide a resend action
- **Do:** Explain verification and provide a resend action.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the verification page does not explain the emailed link or offers no recovery for a missing/expired message.
- **Why:** Clear instructions and resending let users finish verification without support.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<p>Not verified</p>
```

After:
```php
<p>Use the link we emailed you.</p><form method="POST" action="/email/verification-notification">@csrf<button>Resend link</button></form>
```

#### Show authenticator enrollment and recovery information
- **Do:** Show authenticator enrollment and recovery information.
- **Flag when:** Flag when MFA enrollment hides the QR setup material or recovery codes needed to finish setup and recover access.
- **Why:** Users need both enrollment material and a recoverable authentication path.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<!-- Enrollment confirms enablement without setup/recovery information. -->
```

After:
```php
{{-- authenticated enrollment view; QR SVG generated by Fortify --}}
{!! auth()->user()->twoFactorQrCodeSvg() !!}
@foreach(auth()->user()->recoveryCodes() as $code)<code>{{ $code }}</code>@endforeach
```

#### Use lifecycle-managed Echo subscriptions
- **Do:** Use lifecycle-managed Echo subscriptions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when component channel subscriptions remain active after unmount or use the wrong public/private/presence channel contract.
- **Why:** Matching useEcho hooks manage subscription ownership and cleanup.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Echo.private(channel).listen(event, handler); // no unmount cleanup
```

After:
```php
useEcho(channel, event, handler);
```

#### Start with the simplest UI stack that meets the interaction needs
- **Do:** Start with the simplest UI stack that meets the interaction needs.
- **Flag when:** Flag when low-interaction screens adopt a heavy client architecture without a requirement beyond normal server rendering or small Alpine interactions.
- **Why:** Blade and small local interactions can keep simple screens easier to maintain.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Add a full client SPA solely for a basic settings form.
```

After:
```php
<form method="POST" action="/settings">@csrf ...</form>
```

#### Use Livewire for dynamic interfaces primarily authored in PHP
- **Do:** Use Livewire for dynamic interfaces primarily authored in PHP.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a PHP-focused team duplicates server state and reactive behavior in a bespoke client framework where Livewire meets the requirements.
- **Why:** Livewire integrates reactive UI with Blade and PHP application behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Custom JavaScript duplicates server form state for a PHP-oriented screen.
```

After:
```php
<form wire:submit="save">...</form>
```

#### Integrate package services and resources through its service provider
- **Do:** Integrate package services and resources through its service provider.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a package loads views, configuration, language files, or bindings through application-specific entry points instead of its provider lifecycle.
- **Why:** A provider gives Laravel a consistent package registration and boot boundary.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Require package view setup from an application controller.
```

After:
```php
public function boot(): void { $this->loadViewsFrom(__DIR__.'/../resources/views', 'pkg'); }
```

#### Bound framework dependency constraints to supported majors
- **Do:** Bound framework dependency constraints to supported majors.
- **Flag when:** Flag when framework/component dependencies use unbounded wildcards or allow unreviewed future Laravel majors.
- **Why:** Major bounds prevent silent adoption of an incompatible framework release.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"laravel/framework": "*"
```

After:
```php
"laravel/framework": "^13.0"
```

#### Use Hidden attributes for command visibility when adopting Laravel 13 attributes
- **Do:** Use Illuminate\Console\Attributes\Hidden for hidden command metadata when adopting the Laravel 13 attribute convention.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a command retains hidden-property metadata in a codebase standardized on the Laravel 13 Hidden attribute.
- **Why:** Attributes place command metadata on the class under the adopted convention; the legacy hidden property remains supported.
- **Enforced by:** rector:CommandHiddenPropertyToHiddenAttributeRector

Before:
```php
protected $hidden = true;
```

After:
```php
use Illuminate\Console\Attributes\Hidden;
#[Hidden]
class InternalReport extends Command {}
```

#### Keep substantial provider boot methods organized by concern
- **Do:** When a provider boot method configures several independent concerns, delegate them to focused private configure* methods such as configureViews(), configureActions() and configureRateLimiting().
- **Flag when:** Flag when a substantial boot() method interleaves unrelated setup blocks that are difficult to review or navigate.
- **Why:** Named concern-specific methods keep the boot sequence readable without changing provider lifecycle behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
public function boot(): void { $this->configureActions(); $this->configureViews(); $this->configureRateLimiting(); }
```

#### Ship standalone package dashboards with their built assets
- **Do:** For a package dashboard deliberately designed to require no host asset build or publishing, ship precompiled assets and render them through the package's layout helpers, including its compatible Livewire integration.
- **Flag when:** Flag when such a standalone dashboard requires consumers to run an undocumented frontend build or publish missing CSS/JavaScript before it works.
- **Why:** A self-contained dashboard keeps the installation contract independent of the host application's frontend pipeline.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Adapt reusable cards to their container width
- **Do:** Use container queries for cards whose internal layout should respond to the card width rather than the viewport; use the Tailwind 3 plugin or Tailwind 4 built-in support appropriate to the installed version.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a reusable card chooses a wide internal layout from viewport breakpoints even though its containing dashboard column is narrow.
- **Why:** The same card can occupy differently sized grid regions on one screen.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Preserve paired Chisel markers around optional starter-kit features
- **Do:** When maintaining a Chisel-based starter kit, enclose each removable feature's relevant PHP/TypeScript/template blocks in the installer's matching feature markers and preserve their pairing.
- **Flag when:** Flag when optional authentication feature code escapes its Chisel markers or markers become unbalanced, leaving broken references after feature removal.
- **Why:** The installer relies on those boundaries to remove a feature consistently across files.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep frontend-specific paths outside shared starter-kit installer logic
- **Do:** When the same Chisel installer serves React, Vue and Svelte kits, keep their differing file paths in a sibling path map and have the shared script consume that map.
- **Flag when:** Flag when copies of the shared installer hard-code different framework paths and drift in otherwise identical feature-removal behavior.
- **Why:** Separating path data from shared transformations permits one installer implementation across kits.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Exclude Blade templates from ordinary Larastan PHP analysis
- **Do:** When Larastan analysis paths include Blade template files, exclude *.blade.php through excludePaths unless an intentionally configured template-analysis integration handles them.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Larastan 3 is expected to exclude Blade implicitly and ordinary PHP analysis scans template syntax.
- **Why:** Larastan 3 no longer excludes Blade by default, so broad analysis paths need an explicit boundary.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
parameters:
    excludePaths:
        - *.blade.php
```

#### Avoid Blade wrappers with no reusable interface
- **Do:** Create a Blade component when it centralizes useful repeated behavior, styling, inputs or content composition; keep a plain HTML element when the proposed component adds none of these.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a component merely renames an unstyled native tag and adds navigation/indirection without a reusable contract.
- **Why:** An abstraction should remove meaningful duplication or expose a useful interface.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<x-form-tag /> <!-- only renders <form>, with no shared behavior -->
```

After:
```php
<form method="POST" action="/profile">@csrf ...</form>
```

#### Declare language-aware Git diff attributes
- **Do:** Declare appropriate built-in Git diff drivers for PHP, Blade/HTML and Markdown paths in .gitattributes. Put the specific Blade pattern after the general PHP pattern so its HTML driver remains effective.
- **Flag when:** Flag when language-aware diff attributes are absent under the repository's review convention, or a later general *.php assignment overrides the intended *.blade.php diff=html assignment.
- **Why:** Language-aware drivers improve diff hunk context; correct attribute precedence keeps Blade templates on the intended driver.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
*.blade.php diff=html
*.php diff=php
# The later PHP rule also matches Blade templates.
```

After:
```php
*.php diff=php
*.blade.php diff=html
*.md diff=markdown
```

#### Keep popovers and dropdowns inside the usable viewport
- **Do:** Use collision-aware positioning, such as Floating UI or supported CSS anchor positioning with fallbacks, for popovers and dropdowns that may open near viewport boundaries.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a floating control is clipped, overflows the viewport or hides its choices near an edge or after resizing.
- **Why:** Boundary-aware placement keeps controls reachable across positions and screen sizes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Extend the Tailwind scale without replacing familiar defaults
- **Do:** When adopting the standard Tailwind scale, add or adjust needed theme values while retaining unrelated defaults and the established sm/md/lg/xl/2xl breakpoint names; use the installed major's supported theme extension mechanism.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a customization unintentionally removes default spacing/breakpoints or renames the standard breakpoints without a coordinated design-system requirement.
- **Why:** Retaining the familiar scale preserves existing utility behavior and makes responsive code easier to understand.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Reserve important declarations for deliberate override boundaries
- **Do:** Resolve ordinary CSS conflicts through the component/style design instead of accumulating !important or important utility modifiers; reserve them for necessary overrides such as third-party styles that cannot be changed.
- **Flag when:** Flag when repeated important declarations mask competing application styles without a documented override boundary.
- **Why:** Escalating specificity makes later styling changes difficult to predict.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Build accessibility into shared UI primitives
- **Do:** Encode the relevant semantics, keyboard behavior and accessible naming contracts in shared button, link, heading and other design-system primitives so their consumers inherit a sound default.
- **Flag when:** Flag when every use of a shared primitive must independently repair the same accessibility defect.
- **Why:** Fixing the primitive improves every consumer and prevents recurring defects.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Limit responsive overrides to their intended range
- **Do:** When a Tailwind change applies only below a breakpoint or within a bounded width range, express that range with supported max-* or stacked min/max variants instead of applying a rule globally and undoing it later.
- **Flag when:** Flag when responsive utilities repeat compensating resets solely because a narrower range was not expressed directly.
- **Why:** A bounded variant keeps a local responsive exception from spilling into unrelated widths.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Extend Blade through public extension points
- **Do:** Use public Blade compiler extension points such as Blade::precompiler() instead of bypassing visibility to invoke protected compiler internals.
- **Flag when:** Flag when application or package code uses reflection or an invader to invoke protected compiler internals such as compileStatements().
- **Why:** Private implementation details may change without a supported extension contract.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
invade($compiler)->compileStatements($source);
```

After:
```php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Blade;

Blade::precompiler(fn (string $source) => transform($source));
```

#### Expose a browser-reachable Vite HMR endpoint
- **Do:** Expose the Vite server port from Sail and configure the HMR host to a browser-reachable address, including localhost for the documented WSL2 setup.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Vite runs in a container but its published port or HMR host cannot be reached by the browser.
- **Why:** HMR needs a reachable WebSocket endpoint in addition to the Laravel application.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
server: { hmr: { host: 'vite' } }
```

After:
```php
server: { hmr: { host: 'localhost' } }
```

#### Replace removed lazy props on Inertia v3
- **Do:** Replace Inertia::lazy and LazyProp with Inertia::optional when upgrading to Inertia v3.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an Inertia v3 application calls the removed lazy prop API.
- **Why:** Optional props preserve on-demand evaluation through the supported API.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Inertia::lazy(fn () => User::all())
```

After:
```php
Inertia::optional(fn () => User::all())
```

#### Remove obsolete Inertia v3 future options
- **Do:** Remove the future configuration namespace when upgrading the Inertia client to v3.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Inertia v3 configuration still sets v2 future flags.
- **Why:** Those behaviors are already enabled in v3 and the namespace has been removed.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
createInertiaApp({ future: { /* v2 flags */ } });
```

After:
```php
createInertiaApp({ /* v3 options */ });
```

#### Prefer automatic data-loading styling on Livewire 4
- **Do:** Use Livewire 4 data-loading selectors for trigger styling while preserving any required disabled behavior with wire:loading.attr or form submission handling.
- **Flag when:** Flag redundant loading-style markup when data-loading can express it, and flag replacements that remove a required disabled guard from an ordinary action button.
- **Why:** The automatic attribute simplifies trigger-specific loading styles.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<button wire:click="save" wire:loading.attr="disabled" wire:loading.class="opacity-50">Save</button>
```

After:
```php
<button wire:click="save" wire:loading.attr="disabled" class="data-loading:opacity-50">Save</button>
```

#### Extract cohesive interactive Livewire children
- **Do:** Split complex forms, result lists, or interactive tables into child Livewire components when regions need reusable behavior, distinct state, or a smaller update boundary.
- **Flag when:** Flag when one large component couples unrelated interactive regions and repeatedly morphs substantial unaffected HTML.
- **Why:** Cohesive children can isolate state and reduce rendering work.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<div><!-- one component owns form, filters, and all table behavior --></div>
```

After:
```php
<livewire:quote-form /><livewire:quote-results />
```

#### Use events for known component-triggered refreshes
- **Do:** Dispatch and listen for Livewire events when refreshes are caused by known component actions instead of continuously polling for those changes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a component polls solely to discover a change another component already knows it made.
- **Why:** Events refresh at the relevant moment without repeated idle requests.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<div wire:poll="refreshSecurity">...</div>
```

After:
```php
#[On('two-factor-enabled')]
public function refreshSecurity(): void {}
```

#### Migrate renamed Livewire 4 configuration
- **Do:** Rename layout and lazy_placeholder to component_layout and component_placeholder when upgrading to Livewire 4, and remove obsolete config or hooks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a v4 application still relies on removed v3 configuration keys or unsupported JavaScript hooks.
- **Why:** Removed settings no longer configure the intended component behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'layout' => 'components.layouts.app'
```

After:
```php
'component_layout' => 'layouts::app'
```

#### Close Livewire 4 component tags
- **Do:** Close every Livewire 4 component tag with /> or a matching closing tag.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Livewire v4 template contains an unclosed component tag.
- **Why:** Slot support can interpret following markup as component content.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<livewire:search>
<p>Results</p>
```

After:
```php
<livewire:search />
<p>Results</p>
```

#### Register JavaScript actions with the Livewire 4 API
- **Do:** Assign named JavaScript actions through $wire.$js.name or the corresponding component API on Livewire 4.
- **Flag when:** Flag when v4 scripts use deprecated $wire.$js(name, callback) or bare $js registration forms.
- **Why:** The supported registration API makes named actions available consistently.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$wire.$js('save', () => {});
```

After:
```php
$wire.$js.save = () => {};
```

#### Use async Livewire actions only for independent work
- **Do:** Use Livewire 4 async actions only for independent operations that do not mutate component state reflected in the UI.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an async action changes displayed component state or depends on serialized action order.
- **Why:** Parallel requests can race and leave state diverging across snapshots.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
#[Async]
public function increment() { $this->count++; }
```

After:
```php
public function increment() { $this->count++; }
```

#### Bundle delayed components only when their load profiles fit
- **Do:** Bundle lazy or deferred components only when batching helps and their loading times are similar; use bundle rather than deprecated isolate:false on v4.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a bundle makes fast regions wait for a much slower component or uses deprecated lazy isolation configuration.
- **Why:** Independent requests can reveal fast content sooner than a shared slow bundle.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
#[Lazy(isolate: false)]
```

After:
```php
#[Lazy(bundle: true)] // only for a suitable group
```

#### Avoid the reserved upload method name
- **Do:** Name custom Livewire actions and properties something other than upload.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a component declares a custom method or property named upload.
- **Why:** The framework upload mechanism reserves that name.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function upload(): void {}
```

After:
```php
public function savePhoto(): void {}
```

#### Access DOM refs after Alpine initialization
- **Do:** Access component refs and Alpine state from init or after $wire.$nextTick rather than at a component script top level.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a component script reads $refs before the Alpine component and its DOM are initialized.
- **Why:** Initialization timing otherwise leaves refs undefined.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
const chart = $refs.chart;
```

After:
```php
Alpine.data('chart', () => ({ init() { const chart = this.$refs.chart; } }));
```

#### Split large single-file components into multiple files
- **Do:** Convert a single-file Livewire component to multi-file format when substantial PHP, markup, and JavaScript make it difficult to maintain.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an SFC combines large independent PHP, template, and script sections that impede focused editing.
- **Why:** Multi-file structure separates concerns without changing the component interface.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// One large SFC contains PHP, Blade, and extensive JavaScript.
```

After:
```php
{{-- resources/views/components/report/report.blade.php: markup --}}
<section>{{ $this->reportTitle }}</section> {{-- behavior in report.php; JS in report.js --}}
```

#### Use gap for spacing sibling layout items
- **Do:** Use flex or grid gap utilities for uniform sibling spacing when the parent layout supports them.
- **Flag when:** Flag when uniform sibling spacing is implemented with repeated child margins or first/last-child margin exceptions.
- **Why:** Gap keeps spacing on the layout container and handles wrapping consistently.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<div class="flex"><span class="mr-4">A</span><span>B</span></div>
```

After:
```php
<div class="flex gap-4"><span>A</span><span>B</span></div>
```

#### Enable OPcache in production
- **Do:** Enable and tune PHP OPcache in production runtimes serving Filament.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production PHP has opcache.enable disabled or an undersized cache causes repeated script compilation.
- **Why:** OPcache avoids recompiling framework and component PHP on each request.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Give informative icons accessible names
- **Do:** Give informative Filament icons an accessible name or equivalent adjacent text.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an icon conveys unique information without equivalent text or an accessible label.
- **Why:** Users who cannot perceive the icon still need its meaning.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Icon::make(Heroicon::OutlinedExclamationTriangle)
```

After:
```php
Icon::make(Heroicon::OutlinedExclamationTriangle)->extraAttributes(['role' => 'img', 'aria-label' => 'Warning'])
```

#### Import Blade View and Vite facades explicitly
- **Do:** Import Blade View and Vite facades explicitly.
- **Flag when:** Flag when namespaced PHP relies on global facade aliases instead of explicit imports under the project import convention.
- **Why:** Explicit imports make symbol resolution and tooling behavior predictable.
- **Enforced by:** rector:RenameClassRector

Before:
```php
\Blade::if('staff', $callback);
```

After:
```php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Blade;
Blade::if('staff', $callback);
```

#### Inject the Blade compiler when adopting dependency injection
- **Do:** Inject the Blade compiler when adopting dependency injection.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a dependency-injection-oriented class locates Blade or action services manually instead of accepting their types.
- **Why:** Injected dependencies are explicit and replaceable in tests.
- **Enforced by:** rector:StaticCallToMethodCallRector

Before:
```php
app(BladeCompiler::class)->compileString($source);
```

After:
```php
public function __construct(private BladeCompiler $blade) {}
```

#### Replace obsolete view expression types
- **Do:** Replace obsolete view expression types.
- **Flag when:** Flag when application code references legacy Illuminate\View\Expression instead of the supported HTML string type.
- **Why:** The current type exposes the supported trusted-HTML contract.
- **Enforced by:** rector:RenameClassRector

Before:
```php
new Illuminate\View\Expression($trustedHtml)
```

After:
```php
new Illuminate\Support\HtmlString($trustedHtml)
```

#### Apply available project skills for the active framework
- **Do:** Apply available project skills for the active framework.
- **Flag when:** Flag when project-required available frontend guidance is bypassed and resulting code contradicts its applicable conventions.
- **Why:** Installed project guidance captures framework-specific constraints that generic generation can miss.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Review package upgrade guides and changes beyond automated upgrades
- **Do:** Review package upgrade guides and changes beyond automated upgrades.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an upgrade retains removed APIs/configuration or omits relevant skeleton and environment changes because automation did not handle them.
- **Why:** Automated transforms do not cover every package behavior or skeleton change.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Enforce agreed formatting with automated tooling
- **Do:** Enforce agreed formatting with automated tooling.
- **Flag when:** Flag when repository formatting policy is enforced only through repetitive human review despite an available configured formatter.
- **Why:** Automated checks keep reviews focused on behavior and reduce style churn.
- **Enforced by:** partial: pint:Pint/laravel_blade

#### Verify generated Wayfinder imports and URLs
- **Do:** Verify generated Wayfinder imports and URLs.
- **Flag when:** Flag when generated route helpers fail TypeScript resolution or produce URLs inconsistent with the registered route.
- **Why:** Generated bindings must match both the route collection and the client module paths.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use pagination templates matching the frontend CSS framework
- **Do:** Use pagination templates matching the frontend CSS framework.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Bootstrap frontend pages render Tailwind-only paginator markup without the corresponding styles.
- **Why:** The selected pagination view must match the delivered stylesheet.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Bootstrap app keeps default Tailwind pagination.
```

After:
```php
Paginator::useBootstrapFive(); // provider boot
```

#### Install Node in runtimes that run the Pint Blade formatter
- **Do:** Provide a compatible JavaScript runtime, Node.js or Bun, and the formatter dependencies in local or CI environments that run Pint’s Blade formatter.
- **Flag when:** Flag Pint Blade formatting environments lacking both supported JavaScript runtimes or the formatter dependencies required by their package-manager setup.
- **Why:** The Blade rule invokes the configured Prettier plugins through Node.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Precompile Blade views during production deployment
- **Do:** Precompile Blade views during production deployment.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production deployments omit view precompilation and leave first requests to compile the view set.
- **Why:** View caching moves compilation work into the controlled deployment process.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Normalize package view directories before registration
- **Do:** Normalize package view directories before registration.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the same package view directory is registered through inconsistent relative/symlink paths and produces duplicate compiled cache entries.
- **Why:** Canonical paths give the compiler a consistent source identity.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$this->loadViewsFrom(__DIR__.'/../resources/views', 'pkg');
```

After:
```php
$this->loadViewsFrom(realpath(__DIR__.'/../resources/views'), 'pkg');
```

#### Append only new feed items with an island update
- **Do:** Append only new feed items with an island update.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Livewire infinite feed replaces and morphs all earlier entries for every load-more operation despite an independent append region.
- **Why:** An append island reduces HTML transfer and DOM work for growing feeds.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
