- **Why:** Meaningful commits improve review and later diagnosis.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep Xdebug disabled by default and enable it only for debugging sessions
- **Do:** Keep Xdebug disabled by default and enable it only for debugging sessions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Xdebug runs in normal non-debug workloads.
- **Why:** Debug instrumentation adds runtime overhead.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Reduce Inertia response payloads to the attributes needed by the current view
- **Do:** Reduce Inertia response payloads to the attributes needed by the current view.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Inertia props contain attributes unused by the current page.
- **Why:** Minimal props reduce payload and accidental disclosure.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return Inertia::render('Profile', ['user' => $user]);
```

After:
```php
return Inertia::render('Profile', ['user' => $user->only(['id', 'name'])]);
```

#### Use method spoofing for HTML forms that target update or delete routes
- **Do:** Use method spoofing for HTML forms that target update or delete routes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when HTML update/delete forms omit the method override or try unsupported form methods.
- **Why:** Browsers submit forms as GET/POST; the hidden override selects Laravel’s intended route.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<form method="DELETE">
```

After:
```php
<form method="POST">
@csrf
@method('DELETE')
```

#### Evaluate Octane when application boot overhead limits throughput or response time
- **Do:** Evaluate Octane when application boot overhead limits throughput or response time.
- **Flag when:** Flag when server selection ignores measured application boot overhead.
- **Why:** Octane can help when repeated boot cost is a demonstrated bottleneck.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Start with a small server and expand infrastructure in response to measured needs
- **Do:** Start with a small server and expand infrastructure in response to measured needs.
- **Flag when:** Flag when infrastructure is expanded without measured capacity or latency needs.
- **Why:** Measured growth avoids unnecessary cost and complexity.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Route directly to an already routable action class when a wrapper controller adds no behavior
- **Do:** Route directly to an already routable action class when a wrapper controller adds no behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a controller only forwards to an already routable action without adding HTTP behavior.
- **Why:** Routing directly avoids a redundant adapter layer.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::post('/articles', [ArticleController::class, 'publish']); // forwards to PublishArticle
```

After:
```php
Route::post('/articles', PublishArticle::class);
```

#### Export retained Cloud data before cancellation terminates resources
- **Do:** Move any data that must be retained off Cloud before the cancellation effective date and verify the export before the billing cycle ends.
- **Flag when:** Flag Cloud cancellation plans whose required data remains only in resources scheduled for termination.
- **Why:** Subscription termination removes active resources; retained data must be recovered beforehand.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep confidential session payloads in a server-side store
- **Do:** For session data that must remain server-side, use a server-backed session driver and send only the opaque session identifier in the browser cookie.
- **Flag when:** Flag confidential application payloads being placed in custom cookies or a cookie-backed session despite a server-side confidentiality requirement.
- **Why:** Keeping the payload on the server limits exposure and simplifies revocation and retention.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Centralize Markdown mail styling in a configured theme
- **Do:** For a shared custom Markdown mail appearance, define a CSS theme in the published mail theme directory and select it through mail configuration or notification theme selection.
- **Flag when:** Flag repeated inline edits to standard mail components that duplicate a shared theme.
- **Why:** A theme keeps reusable mail styling in one supported customization point.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Give optional route arguments matching PHP defaults
- **Do:** For optional route segments, give the corresponding action argument a compatible default, including a deliberate enum case or explicit nullable default where appropriate.
- **Flag when:** Flag optional URI parameters bound to required action arguments that cannot be omitted.
- **Why:** An optional URL segment must also be callable when its argument is absent.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Pass middleware metadata through request attributes
- **Do:** Store server-computed objects and internal middleware flags in request attributes rather than merging them into user input.
- **Flag when:** Flag internal request metadata mixed into the input bag used by validation or application payload mapping.
- **Why:** Attributes separate application-owned metadata from client-supplied input.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Preserve JsonResource constructor compatibility
- **Do:** Keep JsonResource construction compatible with the framework resource argument; supply extra response context through supported metadata or explicit configuration instead of new required constructor parameters.
- **Flag when:** Flag Resource subclasses requiring extra constructor arguments that framework collection or pagination construction does not supply.
- **Why:** Laravel constructs Resource instances internally when mapping collections.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use distinct field names for text and uploaded files
- **Do:** Do not assign the same request field name to both ordinary input and an upload; validate and consume each through its intended input API.
- **Flag when:** Flag overlapping text and file keys whose selected value depends on Request::all merge precedence.
- **Why:** Laravel 13 input precedence can select the text value where older code expected the uploaded file.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep exception-specific HTTP rendering with the exception when cohesive
- **Do:** For a custom exception with one cohesive HTTP response, implement its render method or a focused response conversion instead of adding repeated type branches to a global handler.
- **Flag when:** Flag a global exception handler accumulating per-exception response branches that can live with their exception types.
- **Why:** Local rendering keeps a specific exception contract close to its implementation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Scale hot monolith areas with traffic routing before extracting a service
- **Do:** When one monolith area needs more compute but shares the same application semantics, evaluate routing its URL traffic to a dedicated instance group before a microservice extraction.
- **Flag when:** Flag a service split motivated only by uneven compute demand without evaluating independently scaled monolith instances.
- **Why:** Traffic-based scaling can add capacity without introducing a distributed application boundary.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use a controlled egress path when integrations require a stable origin
- **Do:** When an application requires a controlled network presence, route the relevant outbound traffic through a deliberate egress point and manage its availability and capacity.
- **Flag when:** Flag outbound integrations requiring a known origin while requests leave through unpredictable addresses.
- **Why:** A controlled egress path can satisfy allowlists and network policy consistently.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Treat permission checks and row-level access constraints as separate requirements
- **Do:** Treat permission checks and row-level access constraints as separate requirements.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a general permission check is treated as sufficient without restricting accessible rows.
- **Why:** Permission to perform an action does not imply access to every tenant record.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Gate::authorize('view-orders');
return Order::findOrFail($id);
```

After:
```php
Gate::authorize('view-orders');
return $tenant->orders()->findOrFail($id);
```

#### Disable package default routes when replacing them
- **Do:** If you register your own route/controller for a package's feature (e.g. short URLs), disable the package's default route so it is not reachable unintentionally.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom package endpoint leaves the package’s default endpoint unintentionally reachable.
- **Why:** An unused default route can bypass intended middleware or exposure boundaries.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Custom route added; package default remains enabled.
```

After:
```php
// Package config: disable its default route, then register the protected replacement.
```

#### Keep API field names and date formats consistent (e.g. ISO 8601 via toISOString())
- **Do:** Keep API field names and date formats consistent (e.g. ISO 8601 via toISOString()).
- **Flag when:** Flag when equivalent API fields use inconsistent naming or date formats.
- **Why:** A stable field vocabulary and date format simplify clients.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return ['createdAt' => $this->created_at->format('d/m/Y')];
```

After:
```php
return ['created_at' => $this->created_at?->toISOString()];
```

#### Do not return HTTP 200 with a generic error message payload for failures
- **Do:** Do not return HTTP 200 with a generic error message payload for failures.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an API failure is returned with HTTP 200.
- **Why:** Clients and monitoring depend on status codes to distinguish failure.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return response()->json(['error' => 'Forbidden']);
```

After:
```php
return response()->json(['message' => 'Forbidden'], 403);
```

#### Use one consistent JSON error shape (message plus field-level errors) across all API failures
- **Do:** Use one consistent JSON error shape (message plus field-level errors) across all API failures.
- **Flag when:** Flag when API errors use incompatible envelope and field-error structures.
- **Why:** A consistent structure lets clients handle validation and application failures uniformly.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return response()->json(['error_text' => 'Invalid'], 422);
```

After:
```php
return response()->json(['message' => 'Invalid', 'errors' => ['email' => ['Invalid address']]], 422);
```

#### Use a stable session driver (file, redis, etc.) and verify sessions persist across requests
- **Do:** Use a stable session driver (file, redis, etc.) and verify sessions persist across requests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when sessions disappear between requests because the driver is transient or storage is unavailable.
- **Why:** Authentication and CSRF checks require persistent session storage.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Do not mix HTTP and HTTPS between page load and subsequent API calls
- **Do:** Do not mix HTTP and HTTPS between page load and subsequent API calls.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an HTTPS page calls application APIs using HTTP.
- **Why:** Mixed schemes cause browser blocking and cookie inconsistencies.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$api = 'http://app.example.com/api';
```

After:
```php
$api = 'https://app.example.com/api';
```

#### Do not add a permanent /clear-cache web route, even behind authentication
- **Do:** Do not add a permanent /clear-cache web route, even behind authentication.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an HTTP endpoint exposes routine cache-clearing administration.
- **Why:** Cache invalidation belongs in controlled operational tooling.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::get('/clear-cache', fn () => Artisan::call('optimize:clear'));
```

After:
```php
// Run php artisan optimize:clear through controlled deployment/operations access.
```

#### Expose bounded JSON health checks for external monitors
- **Do:** Expose your app's health check results as JSON on an endpoint so an external monitor (e.g. Oh Dear) can poll it and notify you, instead of letting the monitor run code on your server.
- **Flag when:** Flag when external uptime monitoring requires executing arbitrary code inside the application host.
- **Why:** A bounded health endpoint provides a simpler monitoring contract.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Declare packages your application directly uses and avoid unnecessary constraints on unused transitive dependencies
- **Do:** Declare packages your application directly uses and avoid unnecessary constraints on unused transitive dependencies.
- **Flag when:** Flag when application code uses undeclared transitive packages or declares unused framework internals without a requirement.
- **Why:** Direct dependencies document actual coupling while unnecessary constraints hinder upgrades.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// composer.json omits vendor/sdk although application imports its classes.
```

After:
```php
// composer.json
{"require": {"vendor/sdk": "^2.0"}}
```

#### Use the vendor SDK for complex services such as AWS rather than hand-rolling Http client calls
- **Do:** Use the vendor SDK for complex services such as AWS rather than hand-rolling Http client calls.
- **Flag when:** Flag when complex provider protocols are hand-built despite a suitable maintained vendor SDK.
- **Why:** SDKs handle provider-specific authentication, pagination and error semantics.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Http::post($awsEndpoint, $manuallySignedPayload);
```

After:
```php
$s3->putObject($parameters);
```

#### Use Route::domain() groups to restrict routes to specific domains when one Laravel app serves several sites
- **Do:** Use Route::domain() groups to restrict routes to specific domains when one Laravel app serves several sites.
- **Flag when:** Flag when routes for one site also respond on another site’s hostname.
- **Why:** Domain groups separate sites served by the same application.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::get('/dashboard', AdminController::class);
```

After:
```php
Route::domain('admin.example.com')->group(fn () => Route::get('/dashboard', AdminController::class));
```

#### Do not run route:cache or view:cache in local development
- **Do:** Keep local route registration uncached while editing routes; clear stale route or view artifacts when diagnosing missing edits, and retain Blade timestamp checking during development.
- **Flag when:** Flag local route caches masking route changes, or compiled-view configurations disabling timestamp checks while templates are being edited.
- **Why:** Uncached local execution keeps code changes immediately visible.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Do not define overlapping routes for the same URI and verb, because the winning route differs with and without route caching
- **Do:** Avoid conflicting route definitions for overlapping HTTP methods, domains and URI patterns; keep one intentional handler per route contract and verify any deliberate precedence in cached and uncached routing.
- **Flag when:** Flag overlapping routes whose intended handler depends on accidental registration order, or claims that exact duplicates necessarily choose different handlers with route caching.
- **Why:** Overlaps make behavior depend on registration and caching details.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::get('/orders', $old);
Route::get('/orders', $new);
```

After:
```php
Route::get('/orders', [OrderController::class, 'index']);
```

#### Use JSON rather than PHP object deserialization for untrusted browser data
- **Do:** Use JSON rather than PHP object deserialization for untrusted browser data.
- **Flag when:** Flag when untrusted browser data is passed to unserialize().
- **Why:** Object deserialization can instantiate attacker-controlled object graphs.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$data = unserialize($request->input('data'));
```

After:
```php
$data = json_decode($request->input('data'), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
```

#### Either use resource-controller authorisation only for standard resource actions, or explicitly authorise every action
- **Do:** Either use resource-controller authorisation only for standard resource actions, or explicitly authorise every action.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom resource-controller actions rely on automatic CRUD authorization mappings.
- **Why:** Automatic mappings do not cover arbitrary action names.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function publish(Post $post) { $post->publish(); }
```

After:
```php
public function publish(Post $post) { Gate::authorize('publish', $post); $post->publish(); }
```

#### Skip readonly on properties the framework or a package hydrates or mutates after construction
- **Do:** Exception to style-032: leave properties writable (no readonly) on classes whose state the framework or a package fills in or changes after construction, such as Livewire form objects and component properties, Filament form state, Eloquent models and other hydrated objects.
- **Flag when:** Flag when readonly is added to a property that the framework or a package assigns after construction (Livewire/Filament form state, hydrated or model attributes), which fails as soon as the framework tries to assign it.
- **Why:** readonly properties can only be initialised once from inside the class scope, so framework hydration or later mutation fails; readonly by default (style-032) only fits state that is fixed at construction.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class PostForm extends Form
{
    public readonly string $title;
}
```

After:
```php
class PostForm extends Form
{
    public string $title = '';
}
```

#### Use camelCase route parameter names (e.g. {userId}, {newsItem})
- **Do:** Use camelCase route parameter names (e.g. {userId}, {newsItem}).
- **Flag when:** Flag when multiword route parameter names use inconsistent casing.
- **Why:** Consistent parameter names simplify binding and generated callers.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::get('users/{user_id}', $handler);
```

After:
```php
Route::get('users/{userId}', $handler);
```

#### Limit deep nesting of API routes; prefer /error-occurrences/1 over /projects/1/errors/1/error-occurrences/1
- **Do:** Limit deep nesting of API routes; prefer /error-occurrences/1 over /projects/1/errors/1/error-occurrences/1.
- **Flag when:** Flag when resource URIs embed several unnecessary parent identifiers.
- **Why:** Shallow routes reduce coupling when a child is globally identifiable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::get('projects/{project}/errors/{error}/occurrences/{occurrence}', $handler);
```

After:
```php
Route::get('error-occurrences/{occurrence}', $handler);
```

#### Commit application Composer and frontend package-manager lockfiles
- **Do:** Commit application Composer and frontend package-manager lockfiles.
- **Flag when:** Flag when application dependency lockfiles are absent from version control.
- **Why:** Lockfiles make installed builds reproducible.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Remove the obsolete fideloper/proxy package and use Laravel's built-in Illuminate\Http\Middleware\TrustProxies for trusted proxies
- **Do:** Remove fideloper/proxy and configure the built-in Illuminate\Http\Middleware\TrustProxies through withMiddleware in bootstrap/app.php; trust only the intended proxy addresses and forwarded-header policy.
- **Flag when:** Flag fideloper/proxy dependencies or trusted-proxy setup that still assumes a scaffolded App\Http\Middleware\TrustProxies class in a modern application.
- **Why:** The framework supplies its own proxy middleware.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class TrustProxies extends Fideloper\Proxy\TrustProxies {}
```

After:
```php
// bootstrap/app.php
->withMiddleware(function (\Illuminate\Foundation\Configuration\Middleware $middleware): void {
    $middleware->trustProxies(at: ['192.0.2.10']);
})
```

#### Initialize bundled JavaScript dependencies in the entry module
- **Do:** Put page JavaScript that depends on Vite-bundled libraries (e.g. jQuery) inside the Vite entry module (resources/js/app.js) instead of inline scripts, because Vite loads bundles as deferred modules.
- **Flag when:** Flag when inline scripts use Vite-bundled libraries before deferred modules execute.
- **Why:** Module execution order differs from classic blocking scripts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<script>$(".table").enhance()</script>
```

After:
```php
// resources/js/app.js
import $ from 'jquery';
$('.table').enhance();
```

#### Disable Passport’s default routes before registering an intentional custom OAuth route set
- **Do:** Disable Passport’s default routes before registering an intentional custom OAuth route set.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom OAuth routes coexist with Passport’s default route set.
- **Why:** Disabling defaults avoids unintended OAuth endpoints and overlaps.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Custom OAuth routes added without disabling defaults.
```

After:
```php
// AppServiceProvider::register()
Passport::ignoreRoutes();
```

#### Stabilize production first (roll back the deploy, toggle a feature flag off, bypass a failing API) before chasing the root cause
- **Do:** Stabilize production first (roll back the deploy, toggle a feature flag off, bypass a failing API) before chasing the root cause.
- **Flag when:** Flag when incident response investigates root cause while a reversible mitigation remains unapplied.
- **Why:** Stabilizing service limits user impact and creates room for diagnosis.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep polling payloads small by returning only records newer than the last one the user saw (e.g. an ID stored in the session)
- **Do:** Keep polling payloads small by returning only records newer than the last one the user saw (e.g. an ID stored in the session).
- **Flag when:** Flag when polling repeatedly sends the entire history instead of new records.
- **Why:** Incremental payloads bound network and rendering cost.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return Message::all();
```

After:
```php
return Message::where('id', '>', $lastSeenId)->limit(100)->get();
```

#### Use PATCH for partial resource updates
- **Do:** Use PATCH for partial resource updates.
- **Flag when:** Flag when partial updates replace unspecified attributes or use a misleading full-replacement contract.
- **Why:** PATCH expresses changes to supplied fields only.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::put('/profile', $partialUpdate);
```

After:
```php
Route::patch('/profile', $partialUpdate)->middleware('auth');
```

#### Integrate Wayfinder with Vite so route and controller changes regenerate TypeScript helpers
- **Do:** Integrate Wayfinder with Vite so route and controller changes regenerate TypeScript helpers.
- **Flag when:** Flag when route helpers become stale because route generation is not integrated into an adopted Vite build.
- **Why:** Build integration keeps generated frontend routes synchronized.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Profile actual request and query behavior before choosing a performance optimization
- **Do:** Profile actual request and query behavior before choosing a performance optimization.
- **Flag when:** Flag when performance changes are chosen without measuring the affected request/query behavior.
- **Why:** Measurements identify the bottleneck and establish a baseline.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Consume OAuth state from the session and compare it in constant time
- **Do:** Consume OAuth state from the session and compare it in constant time.
- **Flag when:** Flag when OAuth callbacks reuse session state or compare it non-constantly.
- **Why:** Consumed unpredictable state binds one callback to its initiating session.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$expected = session('state');
if ($expected == $request->state) { /* login */ }
```

After:
```php
$expected = session()->pull('state');
abort_unless(is_string($expected) && hash_equals($expected, (string) $request->input('state')), 403);
```

#### Start Nightwatch request sampling conservatively, at 0.1 or lower, and tune it using observed traffic
- **Do:** Start Nightwatch request sampling conservatively, at 0.1 or lower, and tune it using observed traffic.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Nightwatch full request capture is enabled at a high rate before measuring overhead and volume.
- **Why:** Start conservatively and tune sampling using observed coverage and cost.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Stream very large responses rather than materializing the entire payload
- **Do:** Stream very large responses rather than materializing the entire payload.
- **Flag when:** Flag when large generated responses are completely built in memory before sending.
- **Why:** Streaming bounds memory and lets clients start consuming sooner.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$body = implode("", $largeChunks);
return response($body);
```

After:
```php
return response()->stream(function () use ($largeChunks) { foreach ($largeChunks as $chunk) { echo $chunk; ob_flush(); flush(); } });
```

#### Use wasChanged after saving models
- **Do:** After save(), use wasChanged() (optionally with attribute names) to determine which attributes changed during the last save in the current request cycle, since isDirty() is reset by saving.
- **Flag when:** Flag when post-save logic checks isDirty() to discover persisted changes.
- **Why:** Saving resets dirty state; wasChanged() reports the last save.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$user->save();
if ($user->isDirty('email')) { notify(); }
```

After:
```php
$user->save();
if ($user->wasChanged('email')) { notify(); }
```

#### Provide a valid guest login destination
- **Do:** Name your login route `login` (the auth middleware redirects guests there by default) or configure a different target with $middleware->redirectGuestsTo() in bootstrap/app.php.
- **Flag when:** Flag when auth middleware redirects to a nonexistent login route.
- **Why:** A valid guest destination is required for browser authentication flows.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::get('/sign-in', $handler); // no configured guest target
```

After:
```php
Route::get('/sign-in', $handler)->name('login');
```

#### Keep email Blade templates together in a resources/views/mail directory (referenced as e.g. mail.orders.shipped)
- **Do:** Keep email Blade templates together in a resources/views/mail directory (referenced as e.g. mail.orders.shipped).
- **Flag when:** Flag when mail templates are scattered across unrelated view directories.
- **Why:** A shared mail namespace makes email presentation easy to locate.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
view('orders-shipped-email');
```

After:
```php
view('mail.orders.shipped');
```

#### Import SPA CSS from the JavaScript entry
- **Do:** For SPAs, including Inertia applications, remove CSS entry points from the Vite config and import the CSS from JavaScript (typically `resources/js/app.js`).
- **Flag when:** Flag when an Inertia/SPA build treats CSS as an unrelated entry despite requiring JavaScript-managed page asset loading.
- **Why:** Importing CSS from the entry module keeps SPA assets in the same dependency graph.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Vite inputs list app.css separately from app.js.
```

After:
```php
// resources/js/app.js
import '../css/app.css';
```

#### Avoid translation key and filename collisions
- **Do:** Do not define translation string keys that conflict with translation filenames (e.g. `__('Action')` with `nl/action.php` but no `nl.json`), or the translator returns the entire file's contents.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a string translation key collides with a PHP translation filename.
- **Why:** Such collisions can return an entire translation array instead of a string.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
__('Action'); // conflicts with action.php and no matching JSON key
```

After:
```php
__('actions.label');
```

#### Expire signed bearer links when access must be bounded
- **Do:** Use `URL::temporarySignedRoute('unsubscribe', now()->plus(minutes: 30), [...])` for signed links that should expire after a set amount of time.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a bearer-style signed link needing bounded access is generated without expiration.
- **Why:** Expiration limits how long a leaked link remains usable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
URL::signedRoute('download', ['file' => $file]);
```

After:
```php
URL::temporarySignedRoute('download', now()->addMinutes(30), ['file' => $file]);
```

#### Read signed URL values from route/query parameters and separately validate all unsigned body input
- **Do:** Read signed URL values from route/query parameters and separately validate all unsigned body input.
- **Flag when:** Flag when authorization-relevant signed values are read from combined input where an unsigned body can override them.
- **Why:** URL signatures protect the URL query/path, not form or JSON bodies.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$email = $request->input('email'); // signature validates URL only
```

After:
```php
$email = $request->query('email');
```

#### Depend on contracts in cross-framework packages
- **Do:** In a package that integrates with multiple PHP frameworks, depend on the decoupled `illuminate/contracts` package rather than requiring Laravel's concrete implementations in `composer.json`.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a cross-framework package unnecessarily depends on the concrete Laravel framework.
- **Why:** Decoupled contracts keep the package usable outside a full Laravel install.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
{"require":{"laravel/framework":"^13.0"}}
```

After:
```php
{"require":{"illuminate/contracts":"^13.0"}}
```

#### Observe slow full request lifecycles
- **Do:** Register app(Illuminate\Contracts\Http\Kernel::class)->whenRequestLifecycleIsLongerThan($interval, $handler) to log slow requests as a lightweight starting point; it does not replace a full APM tool.
- **Flag when:** Flag when slow full request lifecycles are unobserved despite a latency objective.
- **Why:** Lifecycle timing provides a lightweight signal beyond individual queries.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// No full request latency hook.
```

After:
```php
app(Illuminate\Contracts\Http\Kernel::class)->whenRequestLifecycleIsLongerThan(1000, $handler);
```

#### Observe queries during response preparation
- **Do:** Listen to the PreparingResponse and ResponsePrepared routing events together with DB::listen() to detect queries executed while a response or view is being prepared (log in production, throw locally).
- **Flag when:** Flag when query monitoring misses database queries executed while preparing a view/response.
- **Why:** Render-time queries can hide latency and N+1 behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Measure queries only until the controller returns.
```

After:
```php
// Observe PreparingResponse/ResponsePrepared with DB::listen to track render-time queries.
```

#### Centralize globally needed Inertia props
- **Do:** Share globally needed data such as the authenticated user and flash messages via HandleInertiaRequests::share() / Inertia::share() instead of passing it from every controller.
- **Flag when:** Flag when globally required Inertia props are repeated in each controller.
- **Why:** Shared middleware centralizes common user/flash data.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Each controller repeats the same auth and flash props.
```

After:
```php
public function share(Request $request): array { return [...parent::share($request), 'auth' => ['user' => $request->user()?->only(['id', 'name'])]]; }
```

#### Run Tighten's Tlint on pull requests to catch Tighten-specific Laravel style issues before review
- **Do:** Run Tighten's Tlint on pull requests to catch Tighten-specific Laravel style issues before review.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the adopted Tlint project convention is checked only after review.
- **Why:** CI catches selected Laravel style issues before review.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep high-frequency local Livewire state changes client-side until a server round trip is needed
- **Do:** Keep high-frequency local Livewire state changes client-side until a server round trip is needed.
- **Flag when:** Flag when high-frequency local state changes trigger unnecessary server actions.
- **Why:** Local assignment can defer synchronization to the next needed request.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// JS: $wire.set("content", editor.value) on every keystroke.
```

After:
```php
<div x-on:trix-change="$wire.content = $event.target.value"></div>
```

#### Exclude sensitive files from Log Viewer and keep unknown-file hiding enabled
- **Do:** Exclude sensitive files from Log Viewer and keep unknown-file hiding enabled.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Log Viewer patterns include sensitive or unknown non-log files.
- **Why:** Explicit exclusions keep unintended files out of UI/API responses.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'hide_unknown_files' => false, 'exclude_files' => [],
```

After:
```php
'hide_unknown_files' => true, 'exclude_files' => ['secrets.log'],
```

#### Load expensive nested data lazily
- **Do:** When using spatie/laravel-data, type large or expensive nested properties as Lazy|Type and wrap them in Lazy::create(fn () => ...) so they are only computed and sent when explicitly included.
- **Flag when:** Flag when expensive nested Laravel Data properties are built even when not included.
- **Why:** Lazy values avoid unneeded computation and payload.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public ArtistData $artist;
```

After:
```php
public Lazy|ArtistData $artist; // initialize with Lazy::create(fn () => ...)
```

#### Exclude sensitive routes from broad response caching
- **Do:** Exclude state-changing or personal routes (logout, account pages, store actions) from response caching with the doNotCacheResponse middleware or the #[NoCache] attribute.
- **Flag when:** Flag when logout, account or state-changing routes inherit broad response caching.
- **Why:** Explicit exclusions prevent stale or sensitive responses from being cached.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::get('/account', $handler)->middleware(CacheResponse::class);
```

After:
```php
Route::get('/account', $handler)->middleware('doNotCacheResponse');
```

#### Lint and fix code style with tighten/duster, exposed as composer lint and composer fix scripts
- **Do:** Lint and fix code style with tighten/duster, exposed as composer lint and composer fix scripts.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a project adopting Duster lacks reproducible lint/fix commands.
- **Why:** Shared scripts make the formatter entry point discoverable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Reinitialize request-local protected component dependencies in boot() when they are needed on every request
- **Do:** Reinitialize request-local protected component dependencies in boot() when they are needed on every request.
- **Flag when:** Flag when protected request-local dependencies initialize only in mount and disappear on subsequent requests.
- **Why:** boot runs on each request and can reconstruct runtime-only dependencies.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
protected Service $service;
public function mount(Service $service) { $this->service = $service; }
```

After:
```php
protected Service $service;
public function boot(Service $service) { $this->service = $service; }
```

#### Use JsonResource conditional attributes to omit fields that a particular API response does not need
- **Do:** Use JsonResource conditional attributes to omit fields that a particular API response does not need.
- **Flag when:** Flag when API resources send optional attributes unnecessary for the selected response.
- **Why:** Conditional fields keep the response contract focused.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return ['id' => $this->id, 'details' => $this->details];
```

After:
```php
return ['id' => $this->id, 'details' => $this->when($includeDetails, $this->details)];
```

#### Allow bounded stale responses during background refresh when freshness requirements permit it
- **Do:** Allow bounded stale responses during background refresh when freshness requirements permit it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a cacheable response blocks on refresh despite accepting a bounded stale window.
- **Why:** Serving bounded stale content can reduce refresh latency and dependency bursts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Cache-Control: public, max-age=60
```

After:
```php
Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=30
```

#### Stream long AI responses to clients as their content becomes available
- **Do:** Stream long AI responses to clients as their content becomes available.
- **Flag when:** Flag when long AI output is buffered in full despite a client able to consume incremental content.
- **Why:** Streaming improves time to first visible output.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$response = $agent->prompt($input);
return $response->text;
```

After:
```php
return $agent->stream($input);
```

#### Do not extract microservices or publish APIs before a concrete integration need exists
- **Do:** Do not extract microservices or publish APIs before a concrete integration need exists.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a microservice or public API is extracted without a concrete integration or independent-deployment need.
- **Why:** Premature boundaries add operational and compatibility costs.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Protect subscription-only endpoints with an authenticated subscription-status check
- **Do:** Protect subscription-only endpoints with an authenticated subscription-status check.
- **Flag when:** Flag when subscription-only routes do not check the authenticated account’s current subscription.
- **Why:** Authentication alone does not grant paid-feature access.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::get('/paid/report', $handler)->middleware('auth');
```

After:
```php
Route::get('/paid/report', $handler)->middleware(['auth', EnsureUserIsSubscribed::class]);
```

### Infrastructure & operations

#### Automatically fix and commit formatting in CI
- **Do:** Run the formatter on pushes and commit its changes through a deliberately configured fixing workflow.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a repository adopting automatic formatting commits runs only a check or never commits the generated fixes.
- **Why:** An automatic fixing policy removes manual formatting work and keeps branches consistently formatted.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Enforce PHP static analysis automatically
- **Do:** Run PHPStan or Larastan in required CI checks, optionally also in commit hooks, and propagate failures.
- **Flag when:** Flag when PHP static analysis is only documented as a manual command or its CI exit code is ignored.
- **Why:** Automatic analysis catches type and framework integration errors before they reach production.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Mount shared feedback renderers once
- **Do:** Mount one Toast, Dialog, and Banner renderer in the shared layout when using those application interactions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when page components duplicate global feedback renderers or the layout omits the renderer needed by an interaction.
- **Why:** A single renderer avoids duplicate notifications and keeps feedback consistently available.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<x-toast />
<x-toast />
```

After:
```php
<x-toast />
```

#### Collect Pulse server metrics on every monitored server
- **Do:** Run pulse:check on every application server whose system metrics should appear in Pulse.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a server expected in Pulse has no running pulse:check process.
- **Why:** Pulse server metrics require a collector on each monitored host.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Space the logical NOT operator consistently
- **Do:** Put one space after the logical NOT operator in PHP and enforce it with the project formatter.
- **Flag when:** Flag when PHP uses ! immediately followed by its operand under the Laravel style convention.
- **Why:** Consistent spacing matches the Laravel formatter and reduces style churn.
- **Enforced by:** pint:not_operator_with_successor_space

Before:
```php
if (!$ready) { return; }
```

After:
```php
if (! $ready) { return; }
```

#### Enforce one Laravel formatting preset
- **Do:** Configure and enforce the Laravel style preset consistently across automated PHP formatters.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Pint, StyleCI, or PHP-CS-Fixer use conflicting presets or no enforced project convention.
- **Why:** A shared preset prevents contributors and automation from repeatedly reformatting one another’s code.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
{"preset": "psr12"}
```

After:
```php
{"preset": "laravel"}
```

#### Use zero-downtime release activation
- **Do:** Use atomic zero-downtime release activation for production deployments when availability must be preserved; enable it when provisioning Forge sites that require it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when ordinary releases take the application into maintenance mode despite a zero-downtime availability requirement.
- **Why:** Building a new release before switching traffic avoids an avoidable service interruption.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Register package daemon reload commands
- **Do:** Register package-specific long-running service restart commands with the provider reloads() hook.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a package owns a long-running daemon but php artisan reload does not include its restart command.
- **Why:** Reload integration lets application deployments refresh package workers alongside framework services.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Provider omits the package daemon restart command.
```

After:
```php
public function boot(): void
{
    $this->reloads('package:restart');
}
```

#### Write actionable structured production logs
- **Do:** Log production failures with stable event messages and structured identifiers, status, and safe diagnostic fields.
- **Flag when:** Flag when failure logs contain only ambiguous text without the identifiers or outcome needed for investigation.
- **Why:** Structured fields make related failures searchable and explain what operation needs attention.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Log::error('failed');
```

After:
```php
Log::error('Invoice delivery failed', ['invoice_id' => $invoice->id, 'provider_status' => $status]);
```

#### Bound CI dependency-install retries
- **Do:** Retry transient dependency-installation failures only a finite number of times and preserve the final failure status.
- **Flag when:** Flag when CI install retry loops are unbounded or report success after every attempt failed.
- **Why:** Bounded retries tolerate network failures without hiding dependency errors or consuming unlimited runner time.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Check formatting in CI
- **Do:** Run the project formatter in CI and make formatting drift fail a check or trigger an explicit fixing workflow.
- **Flag when:** Flag when CI has no formatting check or fixing workflow despite a configured formatter.
- **Why:** Automation keeps formatting consistent across contributors.
- **Enforced by:** partial: shift:public/ci/style

#### Keep CI actions updated automatically
- **Do:** Configure recurring Dependabot updates for github-actions; group updates and apply a cooldown where the project requires it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when GitHub Actions dependencies have no periodic update configuration or the configured schedule is disabled.
- **Why:** Pinned actions still require updates for fixes and security patches.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Document releases and follow semantic versioning
- **Do:** Update the changelog for each release, mark breaking changes explicitly, and select a semantic version that matches compatibility impact.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a release lacks a changelog entry or introduces an undocumented breaking change under a non-breaking version.
- **Why:** A release contract lets consumers judge upgrades and avoid unexpected incompatibilities.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
## 1.2.1
- Changes
```

After:
```php
## 2.0.0
### Breaking
- Remove the deprecated export() argument.
```

#### Resolve reusable library dependencies without a committed lockfile
- **Do:** For reusable library packages following this policy, ignore composer.lock and resolve dependencies independently in compatibility CI lanes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a reusable library commits its development lockfile and CI treats that one resolution as supported-range coverage.
- **Why:** A package consumer resolves its own dependencies. Fresh CI resolutions test the ranges the package declares.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
# .gitignore for a reusable library
/vendor/
```

After:
```php
# .gitignore for a reusable library
/vendor/
/composer.lock
```

#### Schedule Cloud capacity for predictable traffic windows
- **Do:** For predictable traffic peaks on a Cloud plan supporting scheduled autoscaling, configure timed replica/threshold overrides on a bounded autoscaling cluster. Set the intended timezone and split recurring overnight windows into two same-day schedules.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a known peak needs capacity before reactive scaling can respond, or an overnight recurring override is represented by an unsupported cross-midnight window.
- **Why:** Planned overrides make capacity available for known demand and same-day schedules express the actual supported recurring window.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Aggregate intended log destinations through a stack
- **Do:** When logs must reach multiple destinations, use Laravel's stack channel with the intended configured members, including Nightwatch alongside the existing local or Cloud log channel rather than replacing it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when adding Nightwatch or another destination silently replaces an existing required log sink, or LOG_STACK does not contain the intended channels.
- **Why:** A stack fans out each log event to the selected sinks and preserves the application's existing logging destinations.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Attach the active release identity to Nightwatch telemetry
- **Do:** On hosting without Nightwatch deployment auto-detection, set NIGHTWATCH_DEPLOY to a stable identifier for the active release and update it when that release is activated.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom-hosted Nightwatch executions have no release identity or continue reporting the previous release after deployment.
- **Why:** A release identifier lets operators connect new exceptions and performance changes to the code that produced them.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Inspect development logs through a driver-aware tail
- **Do:** Use Laravel Pail when debugging development logs, especially when the configured log destinations cannot be inspected by tailing one local laravel.log file.
- **Flag when:** Flag a documented development debugging workflow that assumes all application logs exist in one local file despite configured remote or multiple drivers.
- **Why:** A driver-aware tail lets developers inspect the events emitted by the application without depending on one file destination.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Automate committed asset and style regeneration
- **Do:** Regenerate committed frontend assets and formatting on the main branch and commit the resulting changes through CI.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a project that tracks generated assets has no main-branch regeneration step or produces uncommitted build changes.
- **Why:** Automating tracked outputs prevents the source and distributed assets from diverging.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Check configured Rector refactorings in CI
- **Do:** Run Rector --dry-run in CI using the project configuration and fail on pending required refactorings.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Rector is configured but CI never checks it, mutates source silently, or ignores a failing dry run.
- **Why:** A non-mutating CI check enforces the selected upgrade and PHP conventions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Reserve inline comments for complex logic
- **Do:** Prefer PHPDoc for declaration documentation and add inline comments only when complex logic needs an explanation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when inline comments restate obvious operations or declaration documentation is scattered through method bodies.
- **Why:** Useful documentation explains contracts and non-obvious decisions without obscuring readable code.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Get the user ID.
$id = $user->id;
```

After:
```php
$id = $user->id;
```

#### Capture output and failures from background schedules
- **Do:** Capture scheduled command output and report failures, including for commands run in the background.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a background or operationally important scheduled command discards all output and has no failure alert.
- **Why:** Detached failures otherwise go unnoticed and lack diagnostics.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep domain logic out of HTTP and console entry points
- **Do:** Have HTTP controllers and console commands delegate business operations to application services or domain classes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when controllers or commands implement domain workflows that belong to the application core.
- **Why:** Thin entry points let the same business operation serve multiple interfaces and be tested independently.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function handle(): int { /* calculate and settle every invoice here */ return 0; }
```

After:
```php
public function handle(SettleInvoices $settle): int { $settle->run(); return self::SUCCESS; }
```

#### Restart Pulse processes during deployments
- **Do:** Run pulse:restart during deployments on hosts that keep Pulse processes running.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a deployment leaves long-running Pulse processes on the prior release without a platform-managed restart.
- **Why:** Collectors and ingestion processes must reload code and configuration after release changes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Start with traditional servers until autoscaling is justified
- **Do:** Start a new application on traditional managed servers and move to serverless hosting when measured scaling needs justify the migration.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a new application adopts serverless complexity without a documented scaling requirement or operational benefit.
- **Why:** A simple initial deployment reduces infrastructure work until actual load demonstrates a need for automatic scaling.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use an edge proxy when edge protection is required
- **Do:** Put a compatible edge proxy such as Cloudflare in front of public sites that need DDoS and bot filtering.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a public service has an explicit edge-protection requirement but exposes its origin without an equivalent control.
- **Why:** Edge filtering can absorb malicious traffic before it consumes application capacity.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Choose compute and telemetry regions from residency requirements
- **Do:** Choose the application compute region and each telemetry application data region explicitly against the data-residency requirements for the data they hold; also consider user latency for compute placement.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a default Cloud or Nightwatch region is accepted without checking an applicable residency requirement.
- **Why:** Application data and exported telemetry have separate storage locations, and a nearby compute region alone does not establish telemetry residency.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Prefer compatible ARM runtimes for Vapor workloads
- **Do:** Prefer a supported Vapor ARM native or docker-arm runtime when its dependencies and measured workload are compatible; for Laravel 13 use PHP 8.3 or newer and a maintained OS base.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Vapor runtime architecture selection ignores a compatible ARM option despite a cost/performance requirement.
- **Why:** Vapor ARM offerings can improve cost and performance, provided native dependencies match the target architecture.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Enable interpolation for PSR-3 contextual log placeholders
- **Do:** Enable replace_placeholders on Laravel log channels whose message templates use PSR-3 {name} placeholders, supplying the corresponding values through structured context.
- **Flag when:** Flag when retained log messages contain unresolved context placeholders because the channel's placeholder processor is disabled.
- **Why:** Placeholder interpolation makes contextual messages readable while keeping call-site data structured.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use Laravel lotteries for infrequent inline housekeeping
- **Do:** When housekeeping is intentionally probabilistic, use Illuminate\Support\Lottery with explicit odds rather than hand-rolled random checks. Configure Pulse ingestion trim odds so cleanup does not run on every flush.
- **Flag when:** Flag when costly inline cleanup runs on every telemetry flush despite an intended lower cadence, or its random gating is duplicated in ad hoc checks.
- **Why:** Explicit lottery odds bound expected housekeeping frequency and use a framework mechanism with controllable outcomes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Include the intended filesystems in Pulse server monitoring
- **Do:** Set PULSE_SERVER_DIRECTORIES or the Servers recorder directories to the mount paths whose disk usage needs monitoring, including separately mounted data/storage volumes rather than assuming / covers them.
- **Flag when:** Flag when disk monitoring covers only the root filesystem while a required separately mounted application volume is absent from the configured paths.
- **Why:** The server recorder reports the selected paths; a root-only default can miss storage pressure on other filesystems.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Customize Pulse user display through its display callback
- **Do:** When only dashboard user presentation needs changing, register Pulse::user with the intended name, avatar and extra display fields instead of replacing the entire user-resolution implementation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom Pulse user resolver exists solely to change presentation fields supported by the Pulse::user callback.
- **Why:** The display callback provides the narrower extension point and avoids duplicating identity-resolution behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use interoperable names for custom HTTP headers
- **Do:** Use hyphenated custom HTTP header names and avoid underscores unless every deployed proxy and web server is explicitly configured to pass them.
- **Flag when:** Flag an application contract that relies on an underscored header while Nginx or another intermediary drops that header by default.
- **Why:** Header names accepted by the application can disappear before the request reaches PHP because of intermediary defaults.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Suppress dependency lifecycle scripts in CI installs
- **Do:** Use npm ci --ignore-scripts for CI dependency installation and run any required trusted build steps explicitly.
- **Flag when:** Flag when npm installation executes arbitrary dependency lifecycle scripts without an explicit project decision.
- **Why:** Disabling install hooks reduces the execution surface of third-party dependencies.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use explicit callbacks for nontrivial collection operations
- **Do:** Use an explicit collection callback when arguments or multi-step logic would be clearer than a higher-order message.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a higher-order collection expression obscures arguments or conditional behavior.
- **Why:** An explicit callback exposes the operation and its inputs at the call site.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$users->each->notify($notice, $options);
```

After:
```php
$users->each(fn (User $user) => $user->notify($notice, $options));
```

#### Give singleton scheduled closures unique names
- **Do:** Name every scheduled closure that must run on one server, using distinct names for parameterized variants even when alwaysOnOneServer() is enabled.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an unnamed closure relies on onOneServer or alwaysOnOneServer, or distinct closures share the same lock name.
- **Why:** Singleton scheduling uses task identities for locks. Unnamed closures are excluded from the global singleton policy.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Schedule::call(fn () => sendReport('eu'))->daily()->onOneServer();
```

After:
```php
Schedule::call(fn () => sendReport('eu'))->daily()->name('report:eu')->onOneServer();
```

#### Use background scheduling only with command or exec
- **Do:** Apply runInBackground() only to scheduled command() or exec() events; move a closure into an Artisan command if background execution is needed.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a scheduled closure or callback event calls runInBackground().
- **Why:** Laravel background scheduling is limited to executable command events.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Schedule::call(fn () => generateReports())->daily()->runInBackground();
```

After:
```php
Schedule::command('reports:generate')->daily()->runInBackground();
```

#### Set protected form values on the server
- **Do:** Derive protected fields such as ownership from the authenticated context in server-side form hooks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when user_id or another protected field is accepted from submitted form state without being overwritten or authorized.
- **Why:** Client-controlled form state can be modified even when the field is hidden.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$data['user_id'] = request('user_id');
```

After:
```php
$data['user_id'] = auth()->id();
```

#### Avoid competing local web servers
- **Do:** Use the local web server already assigned to the application and resolve port conflicts before installing Herd or Valet services.
- **Flag when:** Flag when project startup launches another server on the same port as Herd or Valet.
- **Why:** Competing listeners prevent the intended local application server from starting reliably.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Wait for Cloud deployment results and inspect failures
- **Do:** Monitor each Cloud deployment to completion and inspect the failed step logs before deciding how to recover.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a workflow triggers Cloud deployment and reports success without waiting for the deployment result, or retries failed deployments without collecting their logs.
- **Why:** Trigger acceptance does not prove a successful release. Step output explains which operation failed.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Gate destructive Cloud operations explicitly
- **Do:** Require an explicit approval step identifying the target and command before automated destructive Cloud operations.
- **Flag when:** Flag when automation can delete Cloud applications or resources without an explicit target-specific approval gate.
- **Why:** A reviewable gate reduces accidental destruction from ambiguous targets or command construction.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Deploy independent monorepo apps from their own roots
- **Do:** Create a separate Cloud application for each independently deployed monorepo app and set its root directory to that app subdirectory.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a monorepo Cloud deployment builds from the repository root or shares one application across independently released apps.
- **Why:** An explicit application boundary and root directory make builds and releases target the intended code.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Fit Cloud build and deploy stages within platform deadlines
- **Do:** Keep each Cloud build and deploy stage within its documented 15-minute limit, and move longer work to an appropriate background workflow.
- **Flag when:** Flag when build or deploy commands intentionally perform work exceeding the stage deadline.
- **Why:** Exceeding the platform deadline fails the release. Deploy-command filesystem writes are also temporary and must not be used as persistent build outputs.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Avoid optimize:clear in Cloud deploy commands
- **Do:** Remove optimize:clear from Cloud deploy commands.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Cloud deploy command invokes optimize:clear.
- **Why:** Cloud manages release optimization and cache lifecycle; clearing caches during deployment can disrupt shared application state. The composite source also warns against storage:link, covered separately.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Do not send object ACLs to Cloud R2
- **Do:** Choose Cloud R2 visibility at bucket level and omit per-object public visibility or ACL options.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an R2 disk configuration or write operation sends visibility: public or an object ACL.
- **Why:** Cloudflare R2 rejects per-object ACL operations; a public bucket provides public access without object ACLs.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Storage::disk('r2')->put('photo.jpg', $contents, ['visibility' => 'public']);
```

After:
```php
Storage::disk('r2')->put('photo.jpg', $contents); // Bucket visibility controls access.
```

#### Include the Resend runtime SDK
- **Do:** Declare resend/resend-php as a production dependency when using the Resend mail transport.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production selects the Resend transport but its SDK is absent or only a development dependency.
- **Why:** The mail transport depends on the SDK at runtime.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep private storage and logs off the public web
- **Do:** Block HTTP access to private storage and application logs, exposing only intentionally public files through a narrow public disk mapping.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a web alias or symlink exposes storage/logs, storage/framework, or private application storage.
- **Why:** Logs and runtime storage can contain credentials, personal data, and internal diagnostics.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use the production environment for production releases
- **Do:** Set APP_ENV=production on production deployments and deliberately review the safeguards required by any world-accessible non-production environment.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a production deployment uses local/testing environment settings or public staging relies on local-only protections.
- **Why:** Laravel and packages use the environment name for safety and feature decisions. Public staging must also retain secure production-equivalent settings.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Respect the Pulse authenticated-user resolver
- **Do:** Use Pulse::resolveAuthenticatedUserId() in custom recorders that capture the current user.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom Pulse recorder reads auth()->id() directly and bypasses the configured Pulse user resolver.
- **Why:** Applications can customize Pulse identity resolution, which package recorders must respect.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$userId = auth()->id();
```

After:
```php
$userId = Pulse::resolveAuthenticatedUserId();
```

#### Disable expensive Pulse SQL highlighting when needed
- **Do:** Disable Pulse SQL syntax highlighting when large query rendering measurably slows the dashboard.
- **Flag when:** Flag when very large queries stall the Pulse dashboard while syntax highlighting remains enabled.
- **Why:** Highlighting is optional presentation work and can dominate rendering for very large SQL strings.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<livewire:pulse.slow-queries />
```

After:
```php
<livewire:pulse.slow-queries without-highlighting />
```

#### Let applications opt into package schedules
- **Do:** Expose package maintenance commands and let the consuming application register their schedules.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a reusable package silently registers recurring commands during provider boot without an application opt-in.
- **Why:** The application owner must control scheduling frequency, resource use, and maintenance timing.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$this->callAfterResolving(Schedule::class, fn ($s) => $s->command('package:clean')->daily());
```

After:
```php
// Application routes/console.php
Schedule::command('package:clean')->daily();
```

#### Build the new Forge release in its release directory
- **Do:** Change to FORGE_RELEASE_DIRECTORY before running new-code dependency installation or asset build tasks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a zero-downtime script runs build tasks from the old current directory or another release.
- **Why:** Build operations must populate the release that will be activated.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Replace Forge servers for major OS upgrades
- **Do:** Provision a new supported Forge server and migrate sites when upgrading Ubuntu major versions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Forge host runbook performs an unsupported Ubuntu upgrade in place.
- **Why:** A clean replacement preserves the supported provisioning baseline and provides a migration rollback path.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep generated files out of source-controlled server paths
- **Do:** Write generated application files to designated runtime storage instead of source-controlled release directories.
- **Flag when:** Flag when runtime code modifies tracked application paths on the server.
- **Why:** Generated files can conflict with deployment updates and disappear when releases are replaced.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Supervise long-running application daemons
- **Do:** Run application daemons through a process supervisor with a defined working directory, user, and restart policy.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a required long-running daemon is started with an unmanaged background shell process.
- **Why:** Supervision restores failed processes and makes their operating context explicit.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Attach tenant identity to execution context
- **Do:** Add an approved tenant identifier to Laravel Context for tenant-specific requests, jobs, and commands.
- **Flag when:** Flag when tenant-specific telemetry cannot be associated with its tenant despite a diagnostic requirement.
- **Why:** Tenant context lets operators isolate failures affecting a particular tenant.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Tenant resolved but absent from execution metadata.
```

After:
```php
Context::add('tenant_id', $tenant->id);
```

#### Use client whispers for non-authoritative peer events
- **Do:** Use client whispers for ephemeral peer-to-peer events that require no application-server decision, and never treat them as authoritative business state.
- **Flag when:** Flag when typing/presence-like peer events unnecessarily invoke application endpoints or a client whisper is trusted as a payment or authorization fact.
- **Why:** Whispers reduce server work for transient client coordination but carry client-supplied data.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Each keystroke sends a request to an application endpoint.
```

After:
```php
// In an authorized private channel:
Echo.private('chat.' + roomId).whisper('typing', { user: displayName });
```

#### Automate repeatable deployments in CI
- **Do:** Implement the deployment procedure as a version-controlled GitHub Actions workflow or equivalent CI automation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production deployments require undocumented manual command sequences.
- **Why:** A repeatable workflow makes release steps reviewable and consistent.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Reduce noisy Cloud build output before it is truncated
- **Do:** When Cloud build logs are truncated, reduce verbose dependency-install output with supported quiet or no-progress flags while preserving exit-status checks and access to failure diagnostics.
- **Flag when:** Flag when oversized dependency-install output repeatedly truncates Cloud deployment diagnostics and no verbosity control is applied.
- **Why:** Excess routine output can consume the platform log limit and hide useful deployment failures.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep an explicit CLI interface for automatable operations
- **Do:** Expose operations needed by scripts or deployment hooks as noninteractive Artisan/CLI commands with explicit inputs, including when an interactive menu also exists; have the interfaces reuse the same business operation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when automation must navigate an interactive UI or call an otherwise unnecessary HTTP endpoint to perform an internal operational task.
- **Why:** A scriptable command interface supports repeatable automation while shared business logic keeps interactive and automated behavior aligned.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Let unhandled failures reach Laravel exception reporting
- **Do:** Allow unexpected exceptions to propagate to Laravel reporting when the caller has no recovery or user-flow behavior to perform. Remove catch blocks whose only effect is logging and swallowing the failure.
- **Flag when:** Flag a catch block that only writes a log entry and then lets the operation appear successful, with no intentional recovery or handled-error result.
- **Why:** Laravel reports uncaught failures through its configured pipeline; swallowing them can hide failure semantics and bypass centralized diagnostics.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Limit incremental Pint checks to changed files
- **Do:** Use Pint --diff against the appropriate base branch for incremental CI formatting checks, and fetch that base ref.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an incremental formatting job scans the entire repository or references a base branch unavailable in its checkout.
- **Why:** Diff-based checking reduces formatting time for large repositories.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Grant formatting commit jobs write access
- **Do:** Grant contents: write to the specific CI job that commits formatter fixes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an automatic formatting commit job has a read-only token and consequently cannot push its changes.
- **Why:** Formatting commit workflows require repository write access. Restricting that access to the writing job preserves least privilege.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Declare least-privilege CI permissions
- **Do:** Declare explicit GitHub Actions permissions and grant each job only the scopes it needs.
- **Flag when:** Flag when workflow token permissions are implicit or broad write scopes are granted to jobs that only read source.
- **Why:** Reducing token authority limits the impact of a compromised action or workflow.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Lint PHP syntax in CI
- **Do:** Check PHP source files for syntax errors in CI using the supported PHP runtime.
- **Flag when:** Flag when CI lacks a PHP syntax check and no executed analyzer or test step parses the relevant files.
- **Why:** Syntax checking catches invalid PHP even in paths not exercised by tests.
- **Enforced by:** partial: shift:public/ci/syntax

#### Resolve the selected Laravel version in each CI lane
- **Do:** Constrain laravel/framework to the matrix version before composer update in package compatibility jobs.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the Laravel matrix label changes but Composer is free to install the same framework version in every lane.
- **Why:** A nominal version matrix provides no coverage unless dependency resolution enforces each target version.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Publish PHPStan diagnostics as CI annotations
- **Do:** Use PHPStan --error-format=github in GitHub Actions when review annotations are desired.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a workflow intended to annotate PHPStan findings uses an output format that GitHub cannot interpret.
- **Why:** Inline annotations make static-analysis failures easier to locate during review.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Allowlist activity-log attributes
- **Do:** Use logOnly() to allowlist the model attributes that belong in the activity audit trail.
- **Flag when:** Flag when activity logging records every model attribute when only selected changes are intended for the audit trail.
- **Why:** An explicit allowlist limits sensitive or irrelevant data and stabilizes audit meaning.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return LogOptions::defaults()->logAll();
```

After:
```php
return LogOptions::defaults()->logOnly(['status', 'total']);
```

#### Record only changed audit attributes
- **Do:** Enable logOnlyDirty() when update activities should contain only changed tracked attributes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when update audit entries repeat unchanged tracked model values.
- **Why:** Recording deltas keeps activity entries focused on what changed.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return LogOptions::defaults()->logOnly(['status']);
```

After:
```php
return LogOptions::defaults()->logOnly(['status'])->logOnlyDirty();
```

#### Suppress empty activity entries
- **Do:** Enable dontLogEmptyChanges() when updates with no tracked changes should not create activity records.
- **Flag when:** Flag when model updates produce empty activity records after filtering tracked attributes.
- **Why:** Empty entries add noise without explaining a domain change.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return LogOptions::defaults()->logOnlyDirty();
```

After:
```php
return LogOptions::defaults()->logOnlyDirty()->dontLogEmptyChanges();
```

#### Suppress audit events for noise-only updates
- **Do:** Configure dontLogIfAttributesChangedOnly() for timestamp or counter changes that do not belong in the audit trail.
- **Flag when:** Flag when updates changing only designated noise attributes still create activity entries.
- **Why:** Explicit noise filtering keeps audit history focused on meaningful changes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return LogOptions::defaults()->logAll();
```

After:
```php
return LogOptions::defaults()->logAll()->dontLogIfAttributesChangedOnly(['updated_at']);
```

#### Automate release changelog synchronization
- **Do:** Update CHANGELOG.md from release notes through a release-triggered workflow and commit the result to the maintained branch.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a project adopting release-note-driven changelogs publishes releases without synchronizing CHANGELOG.md.
- **Why:** Automation keeps published release information and the repository changelog aligned.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Monitor production uptime and server health externally
- **Do:** Monitor production sites and server health from an external service and route actionable alerts to the operations owner.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production has no external uptime/health monitor or failed probes produce no alert.
- **Why:** An application cannot reliably report its own complete outage.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Avoid daylight-saving scheduler ambiguities
- **Do:** Prefer UTC schedules where practical; if local wall-clock time is required, choose safe times and handle daylight-saving duplicate or skipped runs.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a critical task or backup is scheduled in a daylight-saving transition window without skip/duplicate handling.
- **Why:** Clock transitions can make a wall-clock time occur twice or not at all.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Schedule::command('backup:run')->dailyAt('02:30')->timezone('Europe/Berlin');
```

After:
```php
Schedule::command('backup:run')->dailyAt('01:00')->timezone('UTC');
```

#### Enforce account eligibility during login
- **Do:** Include required eligibility conditions such as active status in the authentication attempt.
- **Flag when:** Flag when inactive or otherwise ineligible accounts can authenticate because the login credentials check only identity and password.
- **Why:** A valid password alone does not establish that the account may currently sign in.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Auth::attempt($request->only('email', 'password'));
```

After:
```php
Auth::attempt([...$request->only('email', 'password'), 'active' => true]);
```

#### Verify required extensions before moving to Cloud
- **Do:** Compare all required PHP extensions with Cloud runtime support before migrating the application.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the application is migrated to Cloud despite depending on an extension unavailable in the selected runtime.
- **Why:** A platform migration cannot succeed if the workload requires unsupported native extensions.
- **Enforced by:** partial: shift:public/cloud/extensions

#### Enable Xdebug only for the intended Sail command
- **Do:** Use sail debug <command> to trigger debugging for an individual Artisan command instead of enabling Xdebug for every process.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a one-command debugging task globally activates Xdebug for unrelated Sail processes.
- **Why:** Scoped debugging avoids unnecessary overhead and unintended debug connections.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use repository-specific deploy keys for isolated sites
- **Do:** Use site- or repository-specific deploy keys when shared server keys are disabled, including isolated-user Bitbucket sites.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an isolated deployment relies on a shared key it cannot access or a key with unnecessary cross-repository access.
- **Why:** A site-specific key provides the required repository access with a smaller access scope.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Isolate sites that need filesystem separation
- **Do:** Provision a dedicated isolated system user for sites that require filesystem isolation from other hosted applications.
- **Flag when:** Flag when mutually untrusted sites share the same operating-system user and can read or write one another’s files.
- **Why:** User-level separation limits cross-site access on a shared server.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Schedule backup cleanup alongside creation
- **Do:** Schedule backup:clean alongside backup:run using an appropriate retention policy.
- **Flag when:** Flag when backup creation is scheduled but no automatic cleanup or equivalent destination lifecycle policy exists.
- **Why:** Unbounded backup growth can exhaust destination capacity.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep bundled skill descriptions within client limits
- **Do:** Keep bundled agent skill descriptions within the 1024-character compatibility limit and validate the manifest when packaging.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a bundled SKILL.md frontmatter description exceeds 1024 characters.
- **Why:** Oversized descriptions can prevent supported agent clients from loading a skill.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
description: <a description longer than 1024 characters>
```

After:
```php
description: Apply the package conventions for model slugs.
```

#### Provide intentional runtime extension points with Macroable
- **Do:** Use Macroable on public classes intentionally designed for application-defined runtime methods.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an explicitly extensible API forces consumers to subclass or modify vendor files merely to add supported convenience methods.
- **Why:** An intentional macro extension point can accommodate application-specific behavior without replacing the package class.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class Formatter { /* consumers replace this class to add methods */ }
```

After:
```php
class Formatter { use Illuminate\Support\Traits\Macroable; }
```

#### Extract repeated server tasks into Forge recipes
- **Do:** Turn repeated server-level setup or maintenance scripts into version-controlled reusable Forge recipes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the same server operation is copied and edited independently across hosts.
- **Why:** Reusable recipes reduce drift and centralize fixes to common operations.
