- **Flag when:** Flag when stop-when-empty exit is taken as proof that all delayed jobs have completed.
- **Why:** A worker can find no immediately available job while delayed work remains.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use bounded Redis reconnection with backoff
- **Do:** Configure finite Redis reconnect retries and a supported backoff strategy, including cluster parameter placement.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Redis outages fail immediately despite a recovery requirement or reconnect in an aggressive unbounded loop.
- **Why:** Bounded jittered recovery handles short restarts without a retry storm.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Capture the results of nonmutating collection methods
- **Do:** Assign or chain results from collection methods that return new collections.
- **Flag when:** Flag when code calls map/filter/reject and then consumes the untouched original as though it were modified.
- **Why:** Many collection transformations return a new instance; mutating methods must be assessed separately.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$items->filter($keep); return $items;
```

After:
```php
return $items->filter($keep);
```

#### Use lazy pipelines for large collection transformations
- **Do:** Use lazy collection transformations when processing a large iterable without needing intermediate materialized arrays.
- **Flag when:** Flag when large filter/map pipelines allocate several full intermediate collections.
- **Why:** Lazy evaluation reduces additional pipeline memory; an already materialized source still occupies memory.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$count = $items->filter($keep)->map($transform)->count();
```

After:
```php
$count = $items->lazy()->filter($keep)->map($transform)->count();
```

#### Capture explicit actor context before queueing
- **Do:** Capture the authenticated actor and request-derived context before dispatch and resolve worker credentials from that explicit actor.
- **Flag when:** Flag when queued work uses Auth::user or request-only IP/URL data as though it had an active HTTP request.
- **Why:** Workers have no originating authenticated request and may otherwise use missing or wrong context.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$credentials = credentialsFor(Auth::user());
```

After:
```php
$credentials = credentialsFor(User::findOrFail($this->actorId));
```

#### Choose connection and queue separately
- **Do:** Use onConnection to select a backend and onQueue to select a named queue on that backend.
- **Flag when:** Flag when onQueue is passed a connection name when a backend switch is intended.
- **Why:** Queue names and connection names select different levels of routing.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Sync::dispatch()->onQueue("sqs");
```

After:
```php
Sync::dispatch()->onConnection("sqs")->onQueue("imports");
```

#### Install queue backend runtime dependencies
- **Do:** Install the SDK, client, or PHP extension required by the selected queue/storage driver.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a configured driver lacks its required AWS SDK, Redis client, Pheanstalk, or MongoDB integration.
- **Why:** Missing driver dependencies prevent runtime dispatch or inspection.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use a separate process for disposable post-response work when needed
- **Do:** Use the background connection rather than deferred when disposable work must free the application worker promptly.
- **Flag when:** Flag when in-process post-response work occupies scarce application workers despite no durability requirement.
- **Why:** Background uses a separate process; durable retry requirements still call for a real queue.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Task::dispatch()->onConnection("deferred");
```

After:
```php
Task::dispatch()->onConnection("background");
```

#### Mark timeouts failed when retries are inappropriate
- **Do:** Use FailOnTimeout on jobs or queued listeners whose timeout should be terminal.
- **Flag when:** Flag when timed-out work retries even though its workflow requires terminal timeout failure.
- **Why:** Explicit terminal behavior avoids repeating unsuitable timed-out work.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
#[Timeout(30)] class OneShot implements ShouldQueue {}
```

After:
```php
#[Timeout(30)] #[FailOnTimeout] class OneShot implements ShouldQueue {}
```

#### Group standard SQS work for tenant fairness
- **Do:** Assign standard-queue message groups by tenant/workload when using SQS fair delivery.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a noisy tenant dominates a shared standard SQS queue without fair grouping.
- **Why:** Standard-queue grouping improves fairness without FIFO ordering guarantees.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
SyncTenant::dispatch($tenantId);
```

After:
```php
SyncTenant::dispatch($tenantId)->onGroup("tenant:".$tenantId);
```

#### Recycle queue workers using finite resource limits
- **Do:** Configure memory, max-jobs, or max-time limits with automatic replacement; use absolute memory values when PHP memory_limit is unlimited.
- **Flag when:** Flag when persistent workers have no suitable recycling limits or percentage memory limits assume a finite PHP limit.
- **Why:** Controlled recycling releases accumulated memory and keeps worker capacity available.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Force maintenance-mode processing only when required
- **Do:** Use queue worker --force or Horizon force only for workloads intentionally allowed during maintenance.
- **Flag when:** Flag when maintenance-sensitive work is forced through maintenance mode or required maintenance work silently pauses.
- **Why:** The bypass must reflect whether jobs are safe during the maintenance operation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Share a working cache for worker restart signals
- **Do:** Configure a reachable cache store shared by restart commands and the target queue workers.
- **Flag when:** Flag when deployment restart signals are written to a cache different from the worker cache.
- **Why:** Queue restart signalling uses cache state.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Version Horizon worker configuration
- **Do:** Keep Horizon supervisor options in version-controlled config/horizon.php and change them through deployment.
- **Flag when:** Flag when worker configuration exists only as undocumented server-side state.
- **Why:** Versioned settings make capacity changes reproducible and reviewable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Avoid Horizon reserved Redis connection names
- **Do:** Do not name application Redis connections horizon or set Horizon use to that reserved connection.
- **Flag when:** Flag when application configuration claims Horizon internally reserved connection name.
- **Why:** The reserved name is managed by Horizon and can conflict with application configuration.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Generate Horizon CSP nonces per request
- **Do:** Call Horizon::cspNonce from request middleware in Horizon middleware configuration.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Horizon CSP nonce generation happens only at worker boot or outside per-request middleware.
- **Why:** Persistent workers must not reuse one nonce across responses.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Provider boot: Horizon::cspNonce($nonce);
```

After:
```php
public function handle($request, Closure $next) { Horizon::cspNonce(freshNonce()); return $next($request); }
```

#### Centralize shared Horizon supervisor defaults
- **Do:** Put repeated supervisor settings in Horizon defaults and override only differing environment values.
- **Flag when:** Flag when environment supervisor arrays repeat the same options and drift.
- **Why:** Shared defaults reduce inconsistent worker configuration.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Allow job timeouts to expire before Horizon supervisor timeout
- **Do:** Set Horizon supervisor timeout above every job-level timeout and below retry_after.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Horizon supervisor timeout is at or below a valid job timeout.
- **Why:** Autoscaling may kill an active job before its own timeout handling completes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Silence routine queue noise without hiding failures
- **Do:** Use Horizon silenced classes/tags or Silenced for routine jobs that clutter the completed list.
- **Flag when:** Flag when high-volume routine completions obscure operationally meaningful jobs.
- **Why:** Selective silencing improves dashboard usefulness while failure reporting remains necessary.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"silenced" => [],
```

After:
```php
"silenced" => [QueueHeartbeat::class],
```

#### Allocate valid Horizon auto-balancing process bounds
- **Do:** Set auto-balancing minProcesses at least one per queue and maxProcesses above the sum of queue minima.
- **Flag when:** Flag when auto-balancing process bounds cannot cover all queue minima or leave no scaling headroom.
- **Why:** Consistent bounds ensure queue coverage and room to scale.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use logarithmic allocation when large queues would dominate
- **Do:** Choose Horizon log autoScalingStrategy when allocation should temper the advantage of a much larger queue.
- **Flag when:** Flag when one large queue receives a disproportionate share under the current allocation strategy.
- **Why:** Logarithmic weighting can improve resource distribution for this workload policy.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Tune Horizon scaling responsiveness
- **Do:** Set balanceMaxShift and balanceCooldown according to measured demand changes and capacity limits.
- **Flag when:** Flag when automatic balancing reacts too slowly or oscillates due to unsuitable scaling rates.
- **Why:** Scaling cadence controls how quickly workers move between queue demands.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Configure Horizon priority explicitly
- **Do:** Use separate supervisor allocations for relative capacity priority, or balance=false for strict listed queue polling; do not rely on auto queue order.
- **Flag when:** Flag when auto-balanced Horizon queues are expected to obey list-order priority.
- **Why:** Auto allocation follows load rather than ordered polling.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Satisfy alert transport prerequisites
- **Do:** Install and configure the selected Slack, SMS, or email transport before routing Horizon alerts to it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Horizon notifications target an unconfigured transport.
- **Why:** An alert route cannot deliver without its transport credentials and dependencies.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Set snapshot count from desired history duration
- **Do:** Size Horizon metrics.trim_snapshots using snapshot frequency and desired retention duration.
- **Flag when:** Flag when trim_snapshots is interpreted as an age rather than a count.
- **Why:** Changing snapshot cadence changes the history duration retained by a fixed count.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Require values explicitly when missing input must fail
- **Do:** Use required/present or an implicit rule when validation must run for missing or empty input.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a nonimplicit custom or unique rule is expected to reject an omitted or empty attribute.
- **Why:** Ordinary rules are skipped for missing or empty values.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"code" => [new ValidCode],
```

After:
```php
"code" => ["required", new ValidCode],
```

#### Back upsert conflict keys with the correct unique index
- **Do:** Create the intended primary/unique conflict index for upsert and account for MySQL/MariaDB choosing actual indexes rather than uniqueBy.
- **Flag when:** Flag when upsert relies on an unindexed conflict key or uniqueBy to override MySQL indexes.
- **Why:** The database arbitrates conflicts through its indexes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Item::upsert($rows, ["sku"], ["price"]); // sku has no index
```

After:
```php
$table->unique("sku"); // then upsert using sku
```

#### Group OR predicates inside relationship constraints
- **Do:** Wrap alternative predicates in a nested where when applying OR conditions to a relationship query.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an ungrouped relationship orWhere can escape the parent foreign-key constraint.
- **Why:** SQL OR precedence can include rows belonging to other parents.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$user->posts()->where("active", true)->orWhere("votes", ">", 100)->get();
```

After:
```php
$user->posts()->where(fn ($q) => $q->where("active", true)->orWhere("votes", ">", 100))->get();
```

#### Queue remote search indexing
- **Do:** Enable Scout queueing on a real asynchronous connection for third-party search engines.
- **Flag when:** Flag when remote indexing runs on the request path despite asynchronous delivery requirements.
- **Why:** Queueing moves network indexing out of the response; database/collection engines have different needs.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"queue" => false,
```

After:
```php
"queue" => ["connection" => "redis", "queue" => "search"],
```

#### Deduplicate high-volume Scout indexing jobs
- **Do:** Use Scout unique make-searchable and remove-from-search jobs for write-heavy models.
- **Flag when:** Flag when many rapid updates enqueue redundant indexing operations for the same records.
- **Why:** Unique indexing jobs reduce redundant search traffic.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Default indexing jobs despite heavy repeated writes
```

After:
```php
Scout::makeSearchableUsing(MakeSearchableUniquely::class); Scout::removeFromSearchUsing(RemoveFromSearchUniquely::class);
```

#### Chunk large search-index imports
- **Do:** Use queued/chunked Scout import or query searchable operations for large existing datasets.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a large index import materializes all records or holds one process for the entire dataset.
- **Why:** Chunking bounds memory and queued imports distribute the work.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Post::all()->searchable();
```

After:
```php
Post::query()->searchable(); // or scout:queue-import with bounded --chunk
```

#### Dispatch Registered after manual registration
- **Do:** Dispatch Registered after successful manual user creation when registration listeners provide verification or follow-up behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom registration path omits the registration event required by configured listeners.
- **Why:** Manual persistence alone does not invoke the registration event workflow.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$user = User::create($data);
```

After:
```php
$user = User::create($data); event(new Registered($user));
```

#### Dispatch Verified after manual email verification
- **Do:** Emit Verified once a custom verification flow successfully marks the email verified.
- **Flag when:** Flag when manual verification updates state but omits configured Verified listeners.
- **Why:** Event consumers need a successful verification signal.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$user->markEmailAsVerified();
```

After:
```php
if ($user->markEmailAsVerified()) event(new Verified($user));
```

#### Choose a Cashier operation that honors the proration policy
- **Do:** Use noProrate on supported add/remove-price operations when avoiding proration; do not expect it to override swapAndInvoice.
- **Flag when:** Flag when billing code combines noProrate with swapAndInvoice expecting no invoice/proration.
- **Why:** The selected operation determines whether the modifier is honored.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$subscription->noProrate()->swapAndInvoice($price);
```

After:
```php
$subscription->noProrate()->swap($price); // do not request immediate invoicing
```

#### Use immediate broadcast execution when the workflow requires it
- **Do:** Implement ShouldBroadcastNow only for broadcasts that must execute synchronously before the caller continues.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an immediate delivery requirement is implemented with default asynchronous broadcast dispatch.
- **Why:** Synchronous broadcasting changes latency and failure propagation intentionally.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class CriticalUpdate implements ShouldBroadcast {}
```

After:
```php
class CriticalUpdate implements ShouldBroadcastNow {}
```

#### Scale Reverb horizontally for higher connection capacity
- **Do:** Prefer more Reverb replicas when a single-server connection ceiling is reached.
- **Flag when:** Flag when capacity growth relies on continually widening local port ranges instead of adding replicas.
- **Why:** Horizontal capacity avoids concentrating all connections on one server.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Balance connections across Reverb replicas
- **Do:** Put horizontally scaled Reverb servers behind a suitable load balancer.
- **Flag when:** Flag when multiple Reverb servers have no shared balanced client entrypoint.
- **Why:** A balancer distributes persistent client connections across available replicas.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Declare value-taking command options as value-taking
- **Do:** Use an equals suffix in an Artisan option signature when the option needs a value.
- **Flag when:** Flag when command code reads an option value but its signature declares a boolean switch.
- **Why:** Incorrect signatures parse supplied values incorrectly.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
protected $signature = "import {--queue}";
```

After:
```php
protected $signature = "import {--queue=default}";
```

#### Use deferred fallback only when reduced durability is acceptable
- **Do:** Choose deferred over sync as a last-resort fallback only for work allowed to lose backend durability and complete after the response.
- **Flag when:** Flag when latency-sensitive fallback uses sync or a supposedly durable workflow silently falls back in-process.
- **Why:** Deferred preserves response latency but cannot replace durable persistence.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep Redis retry configuration cacheable
- **Do:** Configure Predis retry policies with supported scalar arrays rather than live retry strategy objects in config files.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Redis config instantiates retry objects that cannot be exported by config:cache.
- **Why:** Cacheable configuration must survive serialization into the compiled config.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"retry" => new Retry(new ExponentialBackoff()),
```

After:
```php
"retry" => [ExponentialBackoff::class => []],
```

#### Avoid duplicate client-side rules in optimized precognition
- **Do:** Limit precognitive server validation to server-dependent rules when equivalent stateless rules already execute client-side.
- **Flag when:** Flag when precognitive requests repeat expensive redundant validation without needing the server.
- **Why:** Targeted validation reduces round trips and server work while final submission still validates fully.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return $this->allRules();
```

After:
```php
return $this->isPrecognitive() ? $this->serverOnlyRules() : $this->allRules();
```

#### Resolve queued job identity through framework metadata
- **Do:** Use the queue job metadata APIs for identity: resolveQueuedJobClass() for the queued class and resolveName() for the display name. Use getResolvedJob() only when the resolved handler instance is needed.
- **Flag when:** Flag class-name extraction from exception text, assigning getResolvedJob() to a class string, or reporting only a framework queue wrapper instead of the intended queued class.
- **Why:** Framework metadata identifies the wrapped queueable object reliably.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$class = parseClassName($e->getMessage());
```

After:
```php
$class = $event->job->resolveQueuedJobClass();
$displayName = $event->job->resolveName();
```

#### Separate Pulse ingestion and queue Redis connections
- **Do:** Use distinct Redis connections for Pulse ingestion and Redis-backed queues.
- **Flag when:** Flag when telemetry ingestion shares the same configured Redis connection as queue transport.
- **Why:** Separate connection roles avoid interference between ingestion and queue processing.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Index the database queue name
- **Do:** Keep an index on the queue-name column of database-backed jobs tables.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a database queue jobs table lacks a queue index.
- **Why:** Workers repeatedly select jobs by queue name.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$table->string("queue");
```

After:
```php
$table->string("queue")->index();
```

#### Use public events between independent modules
- **Do:** Have independent modules react through public events/listeners rather than calling one another internal implementation classes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a module imports another module internal services for independent reactions.
- **Why:** Public event contracts reduce direct implementation coupling.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
InventoryInternalService::updateFromOrder($order);
```

After:
```php
event(new OrderPlaced($order->id)); // inventory module subscribes
```

#### Run Composer noninteractively in CI
- **Do:** Set COMPOSER_NO_INTERACTION=1 or pass --no-interaction in automated Composer steps.
- **Flag when:** Flag when CI Composer commands can prompt and block unattended execution.
- **Why:** Noninteractive execution fails or uses defaults instead of hanging.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Give Pulse reporting servers unique names
- **Do:** Set a distinct Pulse server name for every reporting host.
- **Flag when:** Flag when separate reporting hosts publish under the same server name.
- **Why:** Unique server identities prevent mixed host metrics.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Enforce passkey credential uniqueness and user ownership
- **Do:** Persist passkeys with a user foreign key and appropriate deletion behavior, a unique credential_id and the structured credential JSON required by the passkey implementation.
- **Flag when:** Flag a passkey table allowing duplicate credential IDs or orphaned ownership references.
- **Why:** A credential must identify one stored passkey owned by a valid account.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep the Horizon runtime aligned with the application
- **Do:** Run a separate Horizon service with the same selected PHP version and compatible application dependencies as the web application.
- **Flag when:** Flag a Horizon container using a different unreviewed PHP version or incompatible application runtime.
- **Why:** Background execution must support the same application code as HTTP execution.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Provide an operational failed-job inspection and retry workflow
- **Do:** Expose failed-job details and controlled retry actions through the queue platform dashboard, Horizon, Nightwatch or an equivalent authorized operations interface.
- **Flag when:** Flag production recovery that requires ad-hoc database queries to identify failures or offers no supported operator retry workflow.
- **Why:** Accessible failure context and supported retries make queue recovery repeatable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Name scheduled operations and worker clusters by purpose
- **Do:** Give scheduled operations and separately operated worker clusters descriptive names or descriptions that identify their workloads in the operations inventory.
- **Flag when:** Flag generic schedule or worker-cluster labels that make their purpose difficult to identify during scaling, support or incident response.
- **Why:** Operators need to target the intended workload without reverse-engineering cron commands or queue routes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Expose API operations through explicit routes
- **Do:** Give API operations explicit route/controller actions instead of routing every operation through one controller method that switches on an arbitrary JSON action string.
- **Flag when:** Flag an application API implemented as one unstructured action-dispatch switch whose authorization, validation and response contracts vary by payload selector.
- **Why:** Explicit routes let Laravel apply per-operation middleware, validation and discoverable contracts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::post("/api", DispatcherController::class); // switch($request->action) handles all operations
```

After:
```php
Route::post("/reports", StoreReportController::class);
Route::get("/reports/{report}", ShowReportController::class);
```

#### Stage required or unique columns on populated tables
- **Do:** Add nullable schema, deploy compatible code, backfill in bounded steps, and only then enforce required or unique constraints.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a migration adds a required or unique populated-table column without a data transition.
- **Why:** Existing rows may violate the new constraint or require a blocking backfill.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$table->string("slug")->unique();
```

After:
```php
$table->string("slug")->nullable(); // backfill and constrain in later releases
```

#### Update Inertia 3 error event names
- **Do:** Use httpException and networkError in Inertia 3 event listeners.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Inertia 3 listeners still subscribe to invalid or exception.
- **Why:** Renamed events leave old listeners inactive.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
router.on("exception", onFailure);
```

After:
```php
router.on("networkError", onFailure);
```

#### Batch spreadsheet import reads and writes
- **Do:** Use WithChunkReading and WithBatchInserts for large model imports.
- **Flag when:** Flag when large imports load the entire workbook or save every row individually.
- **Why:** Chunked reads bound memory; batch inserts reduce database round trips.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class UsersImport implements ToModel {}
```

After:
```php
class UsersImport implements ToModel, WithChunkReading, WithBatchInserts { public function chunkSize(): int { return 500; } public function batchSize(): int { return 500; } }
```

#### Use unique opaque public references when identifiers should not enumerate
- **Do:** Add a uniquely indexed random public identifier while retaining an internal model key when public enumeration is undesirable.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a privacy-sensitive public resource exposes a sequential database key without an opaque reference.
- **Why:** Opaque references reduce enumeration; authorization remains necessary.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::get("orders/{order:id}", ShowOrder::class);
```

After:
```php
$table->uuid("public_id")->unique(); // bind orders by public_id
```

#### Keep conditional query pipelines fluent
- **Do:** Use when or unless for simple optional query and collection steps.
- **Flag when:** Flag when simple optional pipeline steps require breaking and rebuilding a fluent expression.
- **Why:** A fluent conditional keeps related transformations together.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
if ($active) $query->where("active", true);
```

After:
```php
$query->when($active, fn ($q) => $q->where("active", true));
```

#### Use random storage names with collision protection
- **Do:** Use storage-generated or long random filenames and enforce database uniqueness when a collision must be rejected.
- **Flag when:** Flag when stored uploads use predictable names or race-prone check-then-name loops.
- **Why:** Random names avoid overwrites and constraints provide the final collision guard.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$file->storeAs("uploads", $file->getClientOriginalName());
```

After:
```php
$path = $file->store("uploads"); // persist with unique index if required
```

#### Clone shared query builders before specialization
- **Do:** Clone a shared base builder before adding case-specific conditions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when multiple query variants mutate the same builder instance.
- **Why:** Builder mutations otherwise accumulate into later variants.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$active = $base->where("active", true)->get(); $inactive = $base->where("active", false)->get();
```

After:
```php
$active = $base->clone()->where("active", true)->get(); $inactive = $base->clone()->where("active", false)->get();
```

#### Store cross-worker job files in shared remote storage
- **Do:** Use shared object or remote temporary storage for files needed by jobs that may execute on different servers.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a later queued execution depends on a file stored only on another worker local filesystem.
- **Why:** Workers and retries may land on different machines.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Storage::disk("local")->put($path, $contents);
```

After:
```php
Storage::disk("s3")->put($path, $contents);
```

#### Namespace shared caches and Horizon metadata
- **Do:** Give every application or preview environment unique cache/Redis prefixes and Horizon metadata prefixes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when independent applications or previews share default cache or Horizon keys.
- **Why:** Shared-key collisions mix state and monitoring between applications.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use synchronous dispatch explicitly for synchronous commands
- **Do:** Call dispatchSync or dispatch_sync for work intended to execute immediately without ShouldQueue.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a nonqueued command uses generic dispatch despite a synchronous execution contract.
- **Why:** Explicit dispatch communicates that execution and exceptions occur in the caller.
- **Enforced by:** rector:DispatchNonShouldQueueToDispatchSyncRector

Before:
```php
dispatch(new RecalculateTotal($id));
```

After:
```php
dispatch_sync(new RecalculateTotal($id));
```

#### Keep backed enums valid
- **Do:** Give backed enum cases distinct values of the declared type and avoid forbidden native enum method declarations.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a backed enum duplicates a value, uses the wrong type, or declares a forbidden method.
- **Why:** Invalid enums fail compilation or use.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Classes\EnumSanityRule

Before:
```php
enum State: string { case Open = "x"; case Closed = "x"; }
```

After:
```php
enum State: string { case Open = "open"; case Closed = "closed"; }
```

#### Use unique parameter names
- **Do:** Declare each function or method parameter name once per signature.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a function signature repeats a parameter name.
- **Why:** Duplicate parameter names are invalid PHP.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Functions\RedefinedParametersRule

Before:
```php
function send($user, $user) {}
```

After:
```php
function send($sender, $recipient) {}
```

#### Bound burst debouncing with a maximum wait
- **Do:** Set DebounceFor maxWait and a stable logical debounce identifier when repeated activity must eventually execute.
- **Flag when:** Flag when continuous redispatch can postpone a debounced operation indefinitely or merges unrelated entities.
- **Why:** A maximum wait prevents starvation while keeping bursts coalesced.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
#[DebounceFor(30)] class Rebuild {}
```

After:
```php
#[DebounceFor(30, maxWait: 300)] class Rebuild { public function debounceId(): string { return (string) $this->id; } }
```

#### Keep debouncing and unique dispatch mutually exclusive
- **Do:** Do not combine DebounceFor with ShouldBeUnique on jobs, listeners, or queued actions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a debounced queued class also implements ShouldBeUnique.
- **Why:** The queue mechanisms are mutually exclusive and may reject the configuration.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
#[DebounceFor(30)] class Sync implements ShouldBeUnique {}
```

After:
```php
#[DebounceFor(30)] class Sync implements ShouldQueue {}
```

#### Chain jobs that require successful predecessors
- **Do:** Use Bus::chain for sequential queued operations whose next step requires the previous job to succeed.
- **Flag when:** Flag when dependent queued jobs are dispatched independently and can run out of order.
- **Why:** Chains advance after successful processing and stop on failure.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
CreateArchive::dispatch($id); UploadArchive::dispatch($id);
```

After:
```php
Bus::chain([new CreateArchive($id), new UploadArchive($id)])->dispatch();
```

#### Express batch dependencies as explicit chains
- **Do:** Keep independent jobs parallel in batches and use chains within or between batches when ordering is required.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a batch relies on insertion order to serialize dependent jobs.
- **Why:** Batch jobs can execute concurrently and finish out of order.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Bus::batch([new Download, new Transform])->dispatch();
```

After:
```php
Bus::batch([[new Download, new Transform]])->dispatch();
```

#### Match unique validation to business scope
- **Do:** Scope unique validation by the trusted tenant/account key when uniqueness is local to that scope.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a tenant-local value is validated globally or under an untrusted tenant identifier.
- **Why:** Validation must reflect the domain unique index and authenticated tenant boundary.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Rule::unique("projects", "name");
```

After:
```php
Rule::unique("projects", "name")->where("tenant_id", $tenant->id);
```

#### Use stateless authentication for one-request credentials
- **Do:** Use Auth::once when credentials should authenticate only the current request without session or cookie persistence.
- **Flag when:** Flag when temporary one-request credentials create a persistent login session.
- **Why:** Stateless authentication avoids persisting a session unnecessarily; it does not emit Login.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Auth::attempt($credentials);
```

After:
```php
Auth::once($credentials);
```

#### Observe actual mail transmission through mail events
- **Do:** Use MessageSending/MessageSent for hooks that must run at transport time rather than queue dispatch time.
- **Flag when:** Flag when delivery accounting marks mail sent when it was only queued.
- **Why:** Queue acceptance and transmission are different lifecycle steps.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Mail::to($user)->queue($mail); markSent();
```

After:
```php
Event::listen(MessageSent::class, RecordTransmission::class);
```

#### Persist the generated stored file path
- **Do:** Save the path returned by store/putFile rather than reconstructing a filename from client input.
- **Flag when:** Flag when file records assume a client filename although storage generated a different path.
- **Why:** The returned path identifies the actual stored object.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$file->store("avatars"); $user->avatar = $file->getClientOriginalName();
```

After:
```php
$user->avatar = $file->store("avatars"); $user->save();
```

#### Keep persistent data outside volatile Octane storage
- **Do:** Use durable external storage for values that must survive worker/server restarts; reserve Octane cache and Swoole tables for ephemeral data.
- **Flag when:** Flag when durable state exists only in Octane memory stores.
- **Why:** In-memory Octane data disappears on restart.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Cache::store("octane")->forever("workflow", $state);
```

After:
```php
Cache::store("redis")->put("workflow", $state, now()->addDay());
```

#### Monitor individual slow queries separately
- **Do:** Use DB::listen or equivalent per-query timing for individual slow-query alerts.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a cumulative query hook is used as though it reports every slow individual query.
- **Why:** Per-query duration and total execution database time answer different questions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Assume cumulative threshold identifies each slow statement.
```

After:
```php
DB::listen(function ($query) { if ($query->time > 200) logSlowQuery($query); });
```

#### Resolve container services after application bootstrap
- **Do:** Keep low-level worker startup independent of unbootstrapped container services and do not assume configuration is cached.
- **Flag when:** Flag when worker startup resolves config/container services before application bootstrap.
- **Why:** Bootstrap order differs from ordinary request execution.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Low-level worker entrypoint before app boot: config("app.name")
```

After:
```php
// Resolve application config only after the application bootstrap completes.
```

#### Flush activity buffers at every execution boundary
- **Do:** Keep response-termination flushing and flush the activity buffer after every job attempt, including retryable exceptions. Resolve the scoped buffer inside the listener and preserve the package shutdown fallback.
- **Flag when:** Flag activity flushing that listens only for JobProcessed and JobFailed, misses retryable exceptions, or captures a stale scoped buffer across worker executions.
- **Why:** Persistent workers need explicit execution-boundary flushing.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Event::listen(JobProcessed::class, fn () => $buffer->flush());
```

After:
```php
use Illuminate\Queue\Events\JobAttempted;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Event;
use Spatie\Activitylog\Support\ActivityBuffer;
// Provider boot; supplement the package hooks to cover retryable failures.
Event::listen(JobAttempted::class, static fn (JobAttempted $event) => app(ActivityBuffer::class)->flush());
// Preserve the package response-termination and shutdown flushing.
```

#### Wrap closure-valued state before supported serialization
- **Do:** Use Laravel SerializableClosure in serialization hooks for trusted closure-valued properties that must cross a queue boundary.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a queued object contains a native Closure property that ordinary serialization cannot encode.
- **Why:** Native closures are not directly serializable; live resources and unsafe captures still need removal.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return ["callback" => $this->callback];
```

After:
```php
return ["callback" => new SerializableClosure($this->callback)];
```

#### Publish customizable providers from stubs
- **Do:** Ship application-customizable provider code as publishable stubs instead of requiring edits in vendor code.
- **Flag when:** Flag when consumers must modify a vendor provider to configure supported application behavior.
- **Why:** Published providers remain under application ownership across package updates.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Ask users to edit vendor/package/src/Provider.php.
```

After:
```php
$package->name("package")->publishesServiceProvider("PackageProvider"); // resources/stubs/PackageProvider.php.stub
```

#### Keep form instruction IDs unique
- **Do:** Generate unique instruction and description IDs for every field instance, including repeater rows.
- **Flag when:** Flag when multiple form elements share the same instruction ID referenced by accessibility attributes.
- **Why:** Duplicate IDs associate instructions with the wrong field.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
id="email-help" // repeated per row
```

After:
```php
id="email-help-{{ $rowId }}" // matching aria-describedby
```

#### Allow package job classes to be replaced
- **Do:** Expose a supported job-class binding or configuration override for consumer-specific queue behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag when consumers must fork a package to change job queue policy or behavior.
- **Why:** A replacement boundary lets applications own queue integration details.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
dispatch(new FixedPackageJob($id));
```

After:
```php
dispatch(new (config("package.jobs.process"))($id));
```

#### Persist asynchronous workflow progress
- **Do:** Store orchestration state and completed-step checkpoints in the database.
- **Flag when:** Flag when workflow progress exists only in worker memory.
- **Why:** Persistent state survives worker restarts and supports recovery.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$this->completedSteps[] = $step;
```

After:
```php
$workflow->steps()->updateOrCreate(["name" => $step], ["status" => "completed"]);
```

#### Split oversized jobs into bounded work units
- **Do:** Partition a memory-heavy job into smaller independently retryable jobs when its data can be processed in bounded units; keep each unit within the worker memory budget.
- **Flag when:** Flag a job materializing an entire large workload although independent bounded partitions would fit the available workers.
- **Why:** Bounded work reduces peak memory and permits parallel processing.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
ExportEverything::dispatch(); // One job holds every account export in memory.
```

After:
```php
foreach ($accountIds as $id) { ExportAccount::dispatch($id); }
```

#### Default database-generated timestamps for non-ORM writes
- **Do:** Use a database current-timestamp default for creation timestamps that must be populated by inserts outside Eloquent when the writer intentionally omits the column.
- **Flag when:** Flag non-ORM insert paths omitting a required creation timestamp without a database default.
- **Why:** Eloquent timestamp handling does not run for raw table inserts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$table->timestamp('failed_at'); // Raw inserts omit this field.
```

After:
```php
$table->timestamp('failed_at')->useCurrent();
```

#### Correlate diagnostic entries within one execution batch
- **Do:** Assign one shared batch identifier to all diagnostic entries from a request, command or job, and reset it before the next worker lifecycle.
- **Flag when:** Flag queries, logs and exceptions from one execution stored without a common correlation identifier, or multiple executions sharing stale batch state.
- **Why:** A shared identifier makes the complete execution trace retrievable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Tolerate malformed UTF-8 in diagnostic payload encoding
- **Do:** Use an explicit malformed-UTF-8 policy such as JSON_INVALID_UTF8_SUBSTITUTE when encoding captured diagnostic payloads so one malformed string does not prevent storing the execution trace.
- **Flag when:** Flag diagnostic JSON writes failing entirely on malformed captured strings without an intended fallback.
- **Why:** Diagnostics should remain available when inspected inputs contain invalid text.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
json_encode($entry->content);
```

After:
```php
json_encode($entry->content, JSON_INVALID_UTF8_SUBSTITUTE | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
```

#### Split Cloud managed queues by resource policy
- **Do:** Start with one Cloud managed queue when workloads share a resource policy; create separate queues when they require different worker memory allocations or autoscaling ranges.
- **Flag when:** Flag when workloads needing different memory or scaling policies share one managed worker pool, or extra pools have no demonstrated isolation requirement.
- **Why:** Each managed queue owns its worker pool, so separate queues are the boundary for independently sized and scaled workloads.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep immediate user-confirmed writes synchronous
- **Do:** Perform a small core database mutation in the request when its success must be confirmed to the user immediately; queue slow follow-up effects after the write succeeds.
- **Flag when:** Flag a quick user edit reported successful before a queued write can encounter validation, uniqueness or database failures.
- **Why:** Immediate write outcomes let the request communicate actual failure while background effects remain asynchronous.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
UpdateEmail::dispatch($user->id, $email); return back()->with("success", "Email changed");
```

After:
```php
$user->update(["email" => $email]); SendEmailChangeNotice::dispatch($user)->afterCommit();
```

#### Replace removed unsigned floating-point schema helpers
- **Do:** Replace unsignedDecimal, unsignedDouble and unsignedFloat schema calls with their supported base column methods. Retain an unsigned modifier only for an intentionally supported legacy MySQL requirement.
- **Flag when:** Flag migrations or reusable schema code calling removed unsigned floating-point/decimal Blueprint methods.
- **Why:** Those helpers were removed in Laravel 11 and remain unavailable in Laravel 13; MySQL also deprecated unsigned floating types.
- **Enforced by:** partial: rector:RenameMethodRector

Before:
```php
$table->unsignedDecimal("amount", 10, 2);
```

After:
```php
$table->decimal("amount", 10, 2); // enforce the domain range deliberately
```

#### Use a uniqueness-aware job dispatch entrypoint
- **Do:** Dispatch ShouldBeUnique jobs through Job::dispatch() or the dispatch() helper that creates PendingDispatch; do not assume a direct bus/controller dispatch path acquires the uniqueness lock.
- **Flag when:** Flag correctness relying on ShouldBeUnique while the caller bypasses PendingDispatch uniqueness acquisition.
- **Why:** Declaring a uniqueness contract is insufficient when the selected dispatch entrypoint does not enforce it.
- **Enforced by:** partial: larastan:NoBatchedUniqueJobRule

Before:
```php
Bus::dispatch(new ReindexProduct($id)); // assumes ShouldBeUnique is enforced here
```

After:
```php
ReindexProduct::dispatch($id);
```

#### Use dedicated classes for substantial background work
- **Do:** Extract non-trivial queued work into a named job class when it needs a meaningful operation identity, reusable behavior or explicit retry/failure configuration.
- **Flag when:** Flag substantial queued closures mixing multiple steps and bespoke failure/retry logic without a clear job boundary.
- **Why:** Named jobs make behavior and queue policy easier to inspect, test and monitor.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
dispatch(function () { /* substantial multi-step processing and ad-hoc retry logic */ });
```

After:
```php
ProcessFeed::dispatch($feedId);
```

#### Validate registration email uniqueness before persistence
- **Do:** When email uniquely identifies user accounts, apply server-side users.email uniqueness validation during registration, backed by the matching database unique constraint.
- **Flag when:** Flag a registration form accepting an existing account email until an unhandled database constraint error occurs.
- **Why:** Validation gives the intended registration feedback while the database still protects concurrent writes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"email" => ["required", "email"] // account email is unique in the domain
```

After:
```php
"email" => ["required", "email", Rule::unique(User::class, "email")]
```

#### Restrict global scopes to universal filters
- **Do:** Use explicit local scopes for filters that some application workflows must bypass.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a global scope hides records needed by administrative, reporting, or job queries.
- **Why:** Implicit filters affect every query and can silently exclude required data.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
static::addGlobalScope("published", fn ($q) => $q->where("published", true));
```

After:
```php
Post::query()->where("published", true)->get();
```

#### Send mail synchronously when immediate acceptance matters
- **Do:** Use synchronous mail delivery when the caller must receive immediate acceptance feedback or a queue worker is unavailable.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a workflow promises immediate acceptance feedback but only enqueues the mail.
- **Why:** Enqueueing confirms dispatch rather than remote delivery acceptance.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class CriticalMail extends Mailable implements ShouldQueue {}
```

After:
```php
class CriticalMail extends Mailable {} // Mail::send propagates transport failures
```

#### Avoid duplicate per-job failure reporting
- **Do:** Add job-level failure logs only for context or behavior not already supplied by central queue reporting.
- **Flag when:** Flag when every job unconditionally reports the same failure already reported by the queue system.
- **Why:** Duplicate reports obscure incidents and inflate monitoring noise.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function failed(?Throwable $e): void { report($e); }
```

After:
```php
public function failed(?Throwable $e): void { Import::whereKey($this->id)->update(["status" => "failed"]); }
```

#### Rate-limit jobs sharing an external quota
- **Do:** Attach RateLimited with a named limiter keyed to the actual shared service quota.
- **Flag when:** Flag when parallel jobs call a quota-limited service without shared rate limiting.
- **Why:** Shared middleware coordinates callers and reduces throttling failures.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function middleware(): array { return []; }
```

After:
```php
public function middleware(): array { return [(new RateLimited("vendor"))->releaseAfter(30)]; }
```

#### Handle partial batch effects explicitly
- **Do:** Treat batches as independently committed work and provide compensation or resumability for partial success.
- **Flag when:** Flag when batch failure handling assumes previously completed job effects roll back.
- **Why:** Batch cancellation stops future work; it does not undo completed side effects.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// On batch failure assume all imported rows disappeared.
```

After:
```php
// Persist per-part completion and compensate or resume explicitly.
```

#### Run consumers for every asynchronous failover backend
- **Do:** Start dedicated workers for each asynchronous connection in the failover list, including database alongside Horizon.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a fallback backend receives jobs without a consumer or a Horizon supervisor consumes the failover wrapper.
- **Why:** Fallback jobs remain stranded without a matching backend consumer.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use finite Redis blocking waits to reduce polling
- **Do:** Tune Redis block_for to queue load using a finite wait.
- **Flag when:** Flag when idle workers repeatedly poll Redis with no blocking wait despite avoidable polling load.
- **Why:** Finite blocking reduces round trips while retaining responsive worker control.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep opinionated collection extensions application-local
- **Do:** Add readable collection macros in application or organization code when their semantics are project-specific.
- **Flag when:** Flag when project-specific collection behavior is proposed as a universal framework convention.
- **Why:** Local macros make extensions reusable without imposing unrelated semantics.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Patch vendor Collection for a project-specific operation.
```

After:
```php
Collection::macro("forReporting", function () { return $this->filter(/* ... */); });
```

#### Chunk very large retention deletes
- **Do:** Delete enormous retention datasets in bounded queued batches when a bulk prune creates excessive load.
- **Flag when:** Flag when retention pruning holds long locks or overloads the database with a huge delete.
- **Why:** Bounded deletes reduce contention and make progress resumable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
LogEntry::where("created_at", "<", $cutoff)->delete();
```

After:
```php
PurgeLogChunk::dispatch($cutoff); // bounded ID ranges
```

#### Schedule jobs directly
- **Do:** Use Schedule::job for recurring queued work instead of a callback whose sole action dispatches that job.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a scheduled callback exists only to dispatch one queued job.
- **Why:** Direct job scheduling exposes routing and scheduling intent clearly.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Schedule::call(fn () => RebuildIndex::dispatch())->daily();
```

After:
```php
Schedule::job(new RebuildIndex)->daily();
```

#### Create actual foreign-key constraints
- **Do:** Chain constrained or define an explicit foreign key for foreignId columns requiring referential integrity.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a foreignId column is assumed to create a foreign key without constrained or an explicit reference.
- **Why:** The column helper alone does not enforce parent existence.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$table->foreignId("user_id");
```

After:
```php
$table->foreignId("user_id")->constrained();
```

#### Dispatch a job for one deferred action
- **Do:** Dispatch a queued job when the requirement is simply to perform one deferred action.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an event and a single listener exist only as queue dispatch indirection.
- **Why:** A job expresses the requested action directly.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
event(new PleaseGenerateReport($id));
```

After:
```php
GenerateReport::dispatch($id);
```

#### Limit unnecessary dependencies
- **Do:** Add packages only when their maintained capabilities justify their operational and supply-chain cost.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a dependency duplicates trivial existing functionality without a documented benefit.
- **Why:** Each dependency adds code and maintenance exposure.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Start route definitions with the HTTP verb
- **Do:** Define the HTTP route first and chain route-specific options afterward.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a route definition obscures its HTTP verb behind single-route option wrappers.
- **Why:** Verb-first definitions expose the endpoint behavior immediately.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::name("users")->get("/users", $handler);
```

After:
```php
Route::get("/users", $handler)->name("users");
```

#### Distinguish command classes from jobs
- **Do:** Suffix Artisan command classes with Command where that is the repository convention.
- **Flag when:** Flag when command and job classes have ambiguous identical action names.
- **Why:** Distinct command names clarify the execution entrypoint.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class PublishPosts extends Command {}
```

After:
```php
class PublishPostsCommand extends Command {}
```

#### Isolate queue namespaces between applications
- **Do:** Use unique queue names or backend prefixes for projects and environments sharing queue infrastructure.
- **Flag when:** Flag when independent applications consume the same queue namespace.
- **Why:** A worker may deserialize and execute another application jobs.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Ping queue monitors only after successful processing
- **Do:** Send completion heartbeats from the successful final step of a queued job.
- **Flag when:** Flag when scheduler thenPing or dispatch completion is treated as evidence that an asynchronous job finished.
- **Why:** Dispatch success does not prove processing succeeded.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Schedule::job(new Heartbeat)->everyFiveMinutes()->thenPing($url);
```

After:
```php
public function handle(): void { runCheck(); Http::get($heartbeatUrl)->throw(); }
```

#### Prevent duplicate link-table assignments
- **Do:** Add parent foreign keys, appropriate delete behavior, and a composite unique or primary key to link tables.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a pivot permits duplicate pairs or orphan links despite the domain requiring one assignment.
- **Why:** Constraints preserve relation integrity under concurrent writes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$table->unsignedBigInteger("role_id"); $table->unsignedBigInteger("permission_id");
```

After:
```php
$table->foreignId("role_id")->constrained()->cascadeOnDelete(); $table->foreignId("permission_id")->constrained()->cascadeOnDelete(); $table->unique(["role_id", "permission_id"]);
```

#### Limit queue concurrency to protect dependencies
- **Do:** Set global and per-queue concurrency limits according to downstream capacity and fairness needs.
- **Flag when:** Flag when one queue can exhaust all concurrency or overload a constrained dependency.
- **Why:** Concurrency bounds protect databases and external services and reserve capacity for other queues.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use FIFO when ordering is required within a message group
- **Do:** Choose FIFO queues for ordered, deduplicated arrival and group messages by the entity whose ordering matters.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an order-sensitive workflow relies on standard-queue global ordering.
- **Why:** FIFO ordering is scoped to message groups and does not replace application idempotency.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Set Cloud worker replica floors from workload needs
- **Do:** Set a sufficient Worker cluster minimum replica count when CPU/memory autoscaling alone will not track queue demand.
- **Flag when:** Flag when queue backlog can grow while CPU/memory signals leave too little worker capacity.
- **Why:** IO-heavy queue demand may not trigger the platform scaling signals.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Reserve explicit Vapor queue concurrency before lowering CLI capacity
- **Do:** Set queue-concurrency explicitly before reducing cli-concurrency.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a lower CLI concurrency setting unintentionally reduces the queue processing budget.
- **Why:** Queue and command capacity share platform limits unless configured intentionally.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Match queued dispatch arguments to constructors
- **Do:** Type job constructor parameters and supply dispatch arguments with the required arity and types.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a static job dispatch has missing, extra, or incompatible constructor arguments.
- **Why:** Constructor contracts allow static analysis to catch dispatch failures before enqueueing.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:CheckDispatchArgumentTypesCompatibleWithClassConstructorRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Methods\MissingMethodParameterTypehintRule

Before:
```php
SendReceipt::dispatch();
```

After:
```php
SendReceipt::dispatch($orderId); // __construct(public int $orderId)
```

#### Return the model explicitly after updating it
- **Do:** Use tap or an explicit model return when callers need the updated model rather than update success status.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a method promises a model but returns the boolean result of model update.
- **Why:** Model update returns a success value, not the model.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return $user->update($values);
```

After:
```php
return tap($user)->update($values);
```

#### Handle both queued AI completion and failure
- **Do:** Register completion and exception handling for queued AI requests that need to publish a result or failure state.
- **Flag when:** Flag when queued AI execution has no handler to persist or expose its final outcome.
- **Why:** A dispatched prompt alone does not make its eventual result available to the application.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$agent->queue($prompt);
```

After:
```php
$agent->queue($prompt)->then(fn ($response) => saveResult($response))->catch(fn ($e) => markFailed($e));
```

#### Keep application jobs in the conventional job directory
- **Do:** Generate or place ordinary application job classes in app/Jobs following repository conventions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when ordinary jobs are scattered without an established alternative organization.
- **Why:** A conventional location makes jobs easier to discover and generate.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
namespace App\Misc; class ProcessOrder {}
```

After:
```php
namespace App\Jobs; class ProcessOrder {}
```

#### Encode binary job payload data
- **Do:** Base64-encode raw binary data before including it in JSON queue payloads, or store it remotely and pass a reference.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a queued payload contains arbitrary non-UTF-8 binary bytes.
- **Why:** Queue payload JSON cannot reliably represent arbitrary raw bytes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
ProcessImage::dispatch($rawBytes);
```

After:
```php
ProcessImage::dispatch(base64_encode($rawBytes));
```

#### Implement reusable queue concerns as middleware
- **Do:** Extract reusable queue processing concerns into middleware and invoke the next callback when processing should continue.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the same cross-cutting queue logic is copied across handlers or custom middleware forgets to call next.
- **Why:** Middleware centralizes execution concerns across jobs and other queueable objects.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function handle($job, $next) { attachContext($job); }
```

After:
```php
public function handle($job, $next) { attachContext($job); return $next($job); }
```

#### Use bulk dispatch for independent untracked jobs
- **Do:** Use Bus::bulk for many independent jobs that need neither batch tracking nor callbacks and do not depend on unique dispatch locks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when large independent untracked groups are dispatched one by one or wrapped in batches solely for submission.
- **Why:** Bulk groups pushes by destination without batch tracking overhead.
- **Enforced by:** partial: larastan:NoBatchedUniqueJobRule

Before:
```php
foreach ($jobs as $job) dispatch($job);
```

After:
```php
Bus::bulk($jobs);
```

#### Avoid capturing this in serialized queue callbacks
- **Do:** Capture only required serializable values in chain, batch, and queued-closure failure callbacks; do not reference this.
- **Flag when:** Flag when serialized queue callbacks reference the current object through this.
- **Why:** Callbacks execute later and should not depend on a live caller object.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Bus::batch($jobs)->then(fn () => $this->finish())->dispatch();
```

After:
```php
Bus::batch($jobs)->then(static fn (Batch $batch) => finishBatch($batch->id))->dispatch();
```

#### Avoid implicit-commit statements in batched jobs
- **Do:** Keep DDL or other implicit-commit statements outside transaction-wrapped batch jobs.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a batched job executes statements that implicitly commit its transaction.
- **Why:** Implicit commits can leave Laravel transaction accounting inconsistent.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function handle(): void { DB::statement("CREATE TABLE scratch (id INT)"); }
```

After:
```php
// Create required schema in migrations; batch jobs perform transactional data work.
```

#### Use one destination for all jobs in a batch
- **Do:** Keep every job in a batch on the same connection and queue and set the batch destination explicitly when needed.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a batch mixes incompatible job connections or queue destinations.
- **Why:** Batch execution requires a consistent destination.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Bus::batch([new A, (new B)->onQueue("other")])->dispatch();
```

After:
```php
Bus::batch([new A, new B])->onQueue("imports")->dispatch();
```

#### Release heavyweight resources after each job
- **Do:** Close or release heavyweight images, streams, and external resources at the end of each job, including failure paths.
- **Flag when:** Flag when persistent workers retain heavyweight resources after processing.
- **Why:** Workers do not reboot between jobs, so unreleased resources accumulate.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$image = imagecreatefromstring($bytes); transform($image);
```

After:
```php
$image = imagecreatefromstring($bytes); try { transform($image); } finally { imagedestroy($image); }
```

#### Checkpoint interruptible long-running jobs
- **Do:** Implement Illuminate\Contracts\Queue\Interruptible for resumable long-running jobs. Accept the signal number, set a stop flag in interrupted, and let handle stop taking new subwork and persist its checkpoint.
- **Flag when:** Flag Interruptible jobs with an incompatible callback signature or long-running resumable work that ignores termination signals.
- **Why:** A signal callback can checkpoint progress before shutdown.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class ImportAll implements ShouldQueue {}
```

After:
```php
use Illuminate\Contracts\Queue\Interruptible;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Queue\ShouldQueue;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Queue\Queueable;
class ImportAll implements ShouldQueue, Interruptible {
    use Queueable;
    protected bool $shouldStop = false;
    public function interrupted(int $signal): void { $this->shouldStop = true; }
    public function handle(): void { foreach ($this->pendingRows() as $row) { if ($this->shouldStop) break; $this->processRow($row); } $this->saveProgress(); }
}
```

#### Handle synchronous dispatch failures in the caller
- **Do:** Catch or propagate synchronous job exceptions in the invoking workflow rather than relying on failed_jobs recovery.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a synchronous dispatch depends on a failed_jobs entry to expose failure.
- **Why:** Synchronous exceptions are delivered immediately to the application.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
dispatch_sync(new Charge($id)); // caller assumes queue:retry can recover
```

After:
```php
try { dispatch_sync(new Charge($id)); } catch (Throwable $e) { markChargeFailed($id); throw $e; }
```

#### Run scheduled work in maintenance only intentionally
- **Do:** Use evenInMaintenanceMode only for tasks explicitly safe and required during maintenance.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a task bypasses maintenance mode without a maintenance requirement.
- **Why:** Maintenance may involve state transitions that background tasks must not interrupt.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Schedule::command("orders:process")->evenInMaintenanceMode();
```

After:
```php
Schedule::command("orders:process");
```

#### Do not depend on model events for mass deletes or restores
- **Do:** Load and operate on individual models when required delete/restore side effects depend on model events, or implement the effects explicitly.
- **Flag when:** Flag when query-based mass delete or restore assumes per-model lifecycle events fire.
- **Why:** Mass operations skip per-model event dispatch.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Post::where("expired", true)->delete(); // observer required
```

After:
```php
Post::where("expired", true)->eachById(fn (Post $post) => $post->delete());
```

#### Use a polymorphic many-to-many relation for shared related records
- **Do:** Use morphToMany with a keyed pivot when several model types share one set of related records.
- **Flag when:** Flag when each parent type duplicates a shared tags-like record table.
- **Why:** A polymorphic pivot preserves one related record identity across parent types.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Duplicate post_tags and video_tags tag records.
```

After:
```php
return $this->morphToMany(Tag::class, "taggable");
```

#### Manage indexes explicitly when changing columns
- **Do:** Add or drop index modifiers explicitly when change operations also require index changes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a migration assumes change alone adds or removes an index.
- **Why:** Column changes do not implicitly manage index definitions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$table->string("code")->change(); // expects unique removed
```

After:
```php
$table->string("code")->unique(false)->change();
```

#### Set queued mail locale explicitly when overriding request locale
- **Do:** Set the mailable locale from the intended recipient language before queueing.
- **Flag when:** Flag when queued mail uses an arbitrary current locale instead of the required recipient language.
- **Why:** The configured locale is retained with queued delivery.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Mail::to($user)->queue(new Receipt($order));
```

After:
```php
Mail::to($user)->locale($user->locale)->queue(new Receipt($order));
```

#### Scope broadcast authorization explicitly
- **Do:** Authorize broadcast resources by their own unique model identifiers and explicit ownership checks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when nested broadcast channel binding is assumed to scope a child to its parent.
- **Why:** Channel binding does not supply implicit nested model scoping.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Broadcast::channel("users.{user}.orders.{order}", fn ($user, $owner, $order) => true);
```

After:
```php
Broadcast::channel("orders.{order}", fn ($user, Order $order) => $order->user_id === $user->id);
```

#### Rescue noncritical broadcast failures
- **Do:** Implement ShouldRescue on supplementary broadcasts whose transport failure should be reported without failing the user action.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a noncritical broadcast outage turns an otherwise successful action into a user error.
- **Why:** Supplementary delivery failures should remain visible without breaking the primary operation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class PresenceUpdated implements ShouldBroadcast {}
```

After:
```php
class PresenceUpdated implements ShouldBroadcast, ShouldRescue {}
```

#### Recheck notification delivery eligibility in the worker
- **Do:** Implement shouldSend when queued notification eligibility can change between dispatch and delivery.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a stale queued notification is delivered after its business condition becomes false.
- **Why:** Queue delay can invalidate an earlier delivery decision.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Delivery assumes eligibility at enqueue time.
```

After:
```php
public function shouldSend(object $notifiable, string $channel): bool { return $this->order->isStillRelevant(); }
```

#### Use push updates for scalable database notifications
- **Do:** Broadcast database-notification changes through Echo and lengthen or disable frequent notification polling.
- **Flag when:** Flag when many clients frequently poll database notifications despite available push delivery.
- **Why:** Push updates reduce repeated database reads.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
->databaseNotificationsPolling("5s")
```

After:
```php
->databaseNotificationsPolling(null) // sendToDatabase($user, isEventDispatched: true) with Echo
```

#### Call parent actions directly for simple child-to-parent commands
- **Do:** Use the parent action binding when a child only needs to invoke one parent method.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a simple parent invocation requires an event dispatch/listener round trip.
- **Why:** A direct binding removes unnecessary coordination.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
wire:click="$dispatch('close-parent')"
```

After:
```php
wire:click="$parent.close()"
```

#### Shard long independent test suites
- **Do:** Split long CI test suites across independent matrix shards when test isolation permits it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when one long test process dominates feedback despite independently runnable tests.
- **Why:** Parallel shards reduce overall test latency.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Expose eventual consistency in queued module reactions
- **Do:** Design cross-module reads and UI states to tolerate queued listener delay and track completion when consistency is required.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a module immediately reads another module projection as though queued reactions have already completed.
- **Why:** Queued reactions update state after the originating transaction.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
placeOrder(); return inventoryProjectionMustAlreadyBeUpdated();
```

After:
```php
placeOrder(); return response(["status" => "processing"]);
```

### Security

#### Use Laravel 13 model attributes when adopting the attribute convention
- **Do:** Use Laravel 13 model attributes when adopting the attribute convention.
- **Flag when:** Flag when guard/fillable declarations mix old properties and attributes contrary to the selected convention.
- **Why:** An automated migration should preserve the exact guard values.
- **Enforced by:** partial: rector:EmptyGuardedPropertyToUnguardedAttributeRector, partial: rector:FillablePropertyToFillableAttributeRector, partial: rector:GuardedPropertyToGuardedAttributeRector, partial: shift:workbench/laravel-property-attributes

Before:
```php
protected $fillable = ["name"];
```

After:
```php
#[\Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Fillable(["name"])]
```

#### Use readable PHPUnit test names
- **Do:** Separate words in PHPUnit test method names with underscores when using the test_ naming convention.
- **Flag when:** Flag when test_ method names concatenate words into difficult-to-read names.
- **Why:** Readable names improve failure reports.
- **Enforced by:** pint:php_unit_method_casing

Before:
```php
public function testReturns401WhenNoTokenIsProvided(): void {}
```

After:
```php
public function test_returns_401_when_no_token_is_provided(): void {}
```

#### Aggregate and check existence in SQL instead of loading full collections
- **Do:** Aggregate and check existence in SQL instead of loading full collections.
- **Flag when:** Flag when large result sets are loaded only to count, sum, group or test existence.
- **Why:** Database aggregation reduces memory, transfer and application work.
- **Enforced by:** partial: larastan:NoUnnecessaryCollectionCallRule

Before:
```php
Order::all()->sum("total");
```

After:
```php
Order::sum("total");
```

#### Generate password-manager rules from server password defaults
- **Do:** Generate password-manager rules from server password defaults.
- **Flag when:** Flag when client password-rule metadata disagrees with server requirements.
- **Why:** One definition avoids rejected generated passwords.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<!-- Hard-coded client minimum differs from server rules. -->
```

After:
```php
<!-- Generate supported passwordrules metadata from Password::defaults(). -->
```

#### Use the direct complementary helper instead of negating its counterpart
- **Do:** Use the direct complementary helper instead of negating its counterpart.
- **Flag when:** Flag when when/unless, filled/blank or contains/doesntContain calls wrap a negated equivalent.
- **Why:** Direct positive predicates reduce double-negation noise.
- **Enforced by:** rector:AvoidNegatedCollectionContainsOrDoesntContainRector, rector:NotFilledBlankFuncCallToBlankFilledFuncCallRector, rector:ReverseConditionableMethodCallRector

Before:
```php
$items->when(! $ready, $callback);
```

After:
```php
$items->unless($ready, $callback);
```

#### Use interfaces at interchangeable boundaries
- **Do:** Depend on an interface at external-service boundaries when swapping implementations or testing requires it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a payment or external-service consumer constructs a concrete client despite needing interchangeable implementations.
- **Why:** A boundary contract isolates provider details and enables substitutes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$gateway = new StripeGateway;
```

After:
```php
public function __construct(private PaymentGateway $gateway) {}
```

#### Distribute secrets through managed stores
- **Do:** Store deployment secrets in a protected platform secret store or password manager and inject them into the target environment.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production secrets are distributed by copying plaintext environment files through uncontrolled channels.
- **Why:** Central storage supports access control and controlled updates.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use the hashed cast for password writes under a cast-based convention
- **Do:** Use the hashed cast for password writes under a cast-based convention.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a cast-based password model relies on callers to remember hashing for every assignment.
- **Why:** The cast places supported hashing at the model assignment boundary.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
protected function casts(): array { return []; }
```

After:
```php
protected function casts(): array { return ["password" => "hashed"]; }
```

#### Require password confirmation using the shared password rule
- **Do:** Require password confirmation using the shared password rule.
- **Flag when:** Flag when password creation/change lacks a confirmed rule or uses divergent requirements.
- **Why:** Confirmation catches unintended input and shared rules keep requirements consistent.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"password" => "required|string",
```

After:
```php
"password" => ["required", "confirmed", Password::defaults()],
```

#### Disable checkout credential persistence when jobs do not need it
- **Do:** Disable checkout credential persistence when jobs do not need it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when actions/checkout leaves its token in git config for a job that does not push.
- **Why:** Removing retained credentials narrows their exposure to later steps.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Group repeated telemetry under stable diagnostic identities
- **Do:** Normalize dynamic telemetry dimensions into stable groups, such as route templates, endpoint patterns and cache-key groups. Group recurring exceptions or SQL patterns by a stable diagnostic family while retaining occurrence counts and useful detail.
- **Flag when:** Flag when per-record IDs or concrete URLs produce a separate metric series for every event, or repeated identical exception/query patterns obscure their frequency.
- **Why:** Stable grouping bounds cardinality and reveals recurring failures and expensive query families.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Throttle noisy exception reports
- **Do:** Throttle or sample repetitive high-volume exception reports centrally.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a repeatedly failing integration can send an unbounded stream of identical error reports.
- **Why:** Sampling or limits prevent log floods from obscuring other failures.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Every upstream failure is reported.
```

After:
```php
$exceptions->throttle(fn (Throwable $e) => $e instanceof UpstreamFailure ? Limit::perMinute(10) : Limit::none());
```

#### Keep rate limiter declarations consistent
- **Do:** Follow the repository convention for named or inline route rate limiters.
- **Flag when:** Flag when equivalent limiters use inconsistent styles without a functional reason.
- **Why:** A consistent declaration style makes budgets easier to find.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
->middleware("throttle:60,1")
```

After:
```php
->middleware("throttle:api")
```

#### Match visible actions to permissions
- **Do:** Show action controls only when the actor is authorized, while retaining server enforcement.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the UI advertises an action that its actor cannot perform.
- **Why:** Permission-aware controls reduce misleading user paths.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<button wire:click="delete">Delete</button>
```

After:
```php
@can("delete", $post)<button wire:click="delete">Delete</button>@endcan
```

#### Key authenticated API limits by user with an IP fallback
- **Do:** Key authenticated API limits by user with an IP fallback.
- **Flag when:** Flag when authenticated API limits use only IP addresses or no stable actor identity.
- **Why:** User keys avoid grouping unrelated users behind a shared network.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Limit::perMinute(60)->by($request->ip());
```

After:
```php
Limit::perMinute(60)->by($request->user()?->id ?? $request->ip());
```

#### Reuse a test password hash across factory users
- **Do:** Reuse a test password hash across factory users.
- **Flag when:** Flag when every factory user creation repeats an expensive identical password hash.
- **Why:** One cached hash speeds fixtures without weakening production credentials.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"password" => Hash::make("password"),
```

After:
```php
"password" => static::$password ??= Hash::make("password"),
```

#### Keep the nonsecret environment template complete
- **Do:** Keep the nonsecret environment template complete.
- **Flag when:** Flag when first-deployment setup cannot discover required variables from .env.example.
- **Why:** A complete template makes required configuration reviewable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Missing SERVICE_TOKEN variable entirely.
```
