
After:
```php
SERVICE_TOKEN=
```

#### Document a private vulnerability reporting channel and use it for initial disclosure
- **Do:** Document a private vulnerability reporting channel and use it for initial disclosure.
- **Flag when:** Flag when security reports are directed to public issues or the project publishes no private reporting route.
- **Why:** Private coordination allows a fix and release before public exploitation details spread.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Align asset URLs and cross-origin file-host policies with deployed origins
- **Do:** Align asset URLs and cross-origin file-host policies with deployed origins.
- **Flag when:** Flag when APP_URL or file-host CORS configuration does not match the browser application URL.
- **Why:** Mismatched origins can break secure loading of hosted assets.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use explicit HTML assertions for unescaped response assertions
- **Do:** Use explicit HTML assertions for unescaped response assertions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when text assertions use escape:false where the installed test framework supplies a dedicated HTML assertion.
- **Why:** The explicit API makes assertion intent clearer.
- **Enforced by:** rector:AssertSeeToAssertSeeHtmlRector

Before:
```php
$response->assertSee("<h1>Title</h1>", escape: false);
```

After:
```php
$response->assertSeeHtml("<h1>Title</h1>");
```

#### Persist protected OAuth refresh state and renew expiring tokens
- **Do:** Persist protected OAuth refresh state and renew expiring tokens.
- **Flag when:** Flag when linked integrations use expired access tokens or lose required refresh/expiry data.
- **Why:** Refresh metadata supports continued access without repeated authorization.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Store only the expiring access token.
```

After:
```php
// Encrypt access/refresh tokens, store expires_at and refresh before use.
```

#### Use wire:navigate for internal links when adopting Livewire navigation
- **Do:** Use wire:navigate for internal links when adopting Livewire navigation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when internal links bypass the selected navigation model without a reason.
- **Why:** Consistent navigation preserves the intended page loading behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<a href="/settings">Settings</a>
```

After:
```php
<a href="/settings" wire:navigate>Settings</a>
```

#### Send provider bearer tokens in the Authorization header
- **Do:** Send OAuth bearer access tokens to provider resource/user-info endpoints through Authorization: Bearer when the provider supports that transport; avoid exposing tokens in URLs or query strings.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom provider puts reusable bearer credentials in URLs despite supported header authentication.
- **Why:** URLs are commonly retained in logs and other diagnostic records, increasing credential exposure.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Prove endpoints invoke authorization
- **Do:** Add an HTTP refusal test that proves a protected endpoint invokes its authorization boundary.
- **Flag when:** Flag when policy tests pass but no endpoint test rejects an unauthorized actor.
- **Why:** A correct policy offers no protection if the handler never calls it.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Only PostPolicy unit tests exist.
```

After:
```php
$this->actingAs($outsider)->delete("/posts/1")->assertForbidden();
```

#### Lower hashing cost in isolated tests
- **Do:** Set BCRYPT_ROUNDS=4 in the testing environment when hashing dominates tests and production configuration remains separate.
- **Flag when:** Flag when ordinary authentication tests use production bcrypt cost without needing to measure it.
- **Why:** A reduced test cost speeds the suite without weakening production hashes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<!-- phpunit.xml: production hashing cost inherited -->
```

After:
```php
<env name="BCRYPT_ROUNDS" value="4"/>
```

#### Use a secret maintenance bypass
- **Do:** Use a strong maintenance bypass secret when authorized operators need access during maintenance.
- **Flag when:** Flag when maintenance access is provided by disabling maintenance for everyone or exposing a predictable bypass.
- **Why:** A secret bypass permits controlled verification.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Reject live integration keys in nonproduction environments
- **Do:** Reject live integration keys in nonproduction environments.
- **Flag when:** Flag when local/test/staging configuration can invoke live services contrary to environment policy.
- **Why:** A preflight guard prevents real charges and production side effects.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Staging accepts any Stripe secret.
```

After:
```php
if (! app()->isProduction() && str_starts_with(config("services.stripe.secret"), "sk_live_")) throw new LogicException("Live key outside production");
```

#### Support password managers with correct autocomplete values
- **Do:** Support password managers with correct autocomplete values.
- **Flag when:** Flag when password forms disable autocomplete or fail to distinguish new and existing credentials.
- **Why:** Correct metadata enables reliable secure password manager use.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<input type="password" autocomplete="off">
```

After:
```php
<input type="password" autocomplete="new-password">
```

#### Combine burst and sustained request limits when both matter
- **Do:** Combine burst and sustained request limits when both matter.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a long-window quota permits an unacceptable immediate burst.
- **Why:** Short and long windows constrain different abuse patterns.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return Limit::perHour(1000)->by($key);
```

After:
```php
return [Limit::perMinute(30)->by("burst:".$key), Limit::perHour(1000)->by("total:".$key)];
```

#### Use direct filter/reject predicates instead of double negation
- **Do:** Use direct filter/reject predicates instead of double negation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when filter or reject callbacks negate a predicate that the complementary method expresses directly.
- **Why:** Direct predicates are easier to read.
- **Enforced by:** rector:AvoidNegatedCollectionFilterOrRejectRector

Before:
```php
$items->filter(fn ($item) => ! $item->isExpired());
```

After:
```php
$items->reject(fn ($item) => $item->isExpired());
```

#### Invalidate other-device sessions after password changes when required
- **Do:** Invalidate other-device sessions after password changes when required.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a password change leaves other sessions valid contrary to the account security policy.
- **Why:** Revocation limits continued access through stolen sessions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Change hash without invalidating other sessions.
```

After:
```php
Auth::logoutOtherDevices($currentPassword);
```

#### Drive deployment-specific framework options through configuration-backed environment values
- **Do:** Drive deployment-specific framework options through configuration-backed environment values.
- **Flag when:** Flag when deployments patch configuration source files for values already exposed through environment variables.
- **Why:** Environment values keep one code artifact usable across deployments.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"default" => "redis",
```

After:
```php
"default" => env("CACHE_STORE", "database"),
```

#### Preserve referenced public APIs through an explicit deprecation transition
- **Do:** Preserve referenced public APIs through an explicit deprecation transition.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a replaced public method is removed while supported docs/callers still depend on it.
- **Why:** A forwarding deprecated method supports an orderly upgrade.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Remove old public method immediately.
```

After:
```php
/** @deprecated Use newName(). */ public function oldName() { return $this->newName(); }
```

#### Pre-aggregate expensive analytics when raw aggregation exceeds the workload budget
- **Do:** Pre-aggregate expensive analytics when raw aggregation exceeds the workload budget.
- **Flag when:** Flag when repeated raw-data analytics scans remain too slow despite suitable indexing/query tuning.
- **Why:** Materialized aggregates trade refresh complexity for bounded read cost.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Recompute the same expensive historical totals per request.
```

After:
```php
// Read an indexed materialized view with a documented refresh schedule.
```

#### Allowlist the fields passed to credential authentication
- **Do:** Build authentication credentials from the configured login identifier and password plus any explicitly intended server-side conditions; read remember-me separately as a boolean instead of passing arbitrary request fields to the guard.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a login handler passes request()->all() to attempt/validate or hard-codes an identifier that differs from the configured authentication field.
- **Why:** Unrelated request fields can become unintended lookup conditions or break custom provider behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Auth::attempt($request->all());
```

After:
```php
Auth::attempt($request->only(Fortify::username(), 'password'), $request->boolean('remember'));
```

#### Confirm passwords without performing a new login
- **Do:** Use a credential-validation operation or Fortify's supported confirmation hook to check the current user's password; record recent confirmation only after success rather than invoking a fresh login as the check.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a password-confirmation handler authenticates another account or changes the active guard/session while merely verifying the current user's credentials.
- **Why:** Password confirmation should establish recent knowledge of the current credential without changing the authenticated identity.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Persist trusted security state without broadening public fillable fields
- **Do:** Write explicitly selected, validated internal authentication attributes through direct assignment or trusted forceFill()->save() paths; keep those privileged fields outside public mass-assignment allowlists.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a trusted security-state update is silently discarded by fillable guards or a developer exposes privileged fields to request mass assignment just to make it persist.
- **Why:** Internal state transitions must persist without turning public request input into a way to write authentication state.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Preserve active authenticator secrets on repeated enable requests
- **Do:** Make repeated enable/setup requests preserve an existing active or pending TOTP secret unless an explicitly authorized replacement is requested. After an actual disable, discard the old secret and generate a fresh one on reenrollment.
- **Flag when:** Flag when retrying the enable action silently replaces the secret already shown to a user or breaks a working authenticator.
- **Why:** Idempotent enrollment avoids accidental factor replacement while deliberate reenrollment still invalidates obsolete credentials.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Provide concise repeatable project onboarding commands
- **Do:** Document a short onboarding path and automate repeatable local setup for dependencies, missing environment files, required secrets, database initialization and asset builds. Preserve existing configuration and keys when setup is rerun.
- **Flag when:** Flag when developers must reconstruct undocumented setup steps or a setup script overwrites a populated .env or existing application key.
- **Why:** A repeatable entry point reduces environment drift and makes a fresh checkout usable without risking existing secrets or data.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Resolve dashboard user labels in one batch
- **Do:** Collect dashboard user keys, call Pulse::resolveUsers once, and reuse the loaded resolver through find($key) for each aggregate row.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Pulse card queries a user separately per row or treats resolveUsers() as returning a Collection.
- **Why:** Batch resolution avoids a dashboard N+1 pattern while retaining custom user lookup behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$rows->map(fn ($row) => User::find($row->key));
```

After:
```php
$users = Pulse::resolveUsers($rows->pluck("key"));
$display = $rows->map(fn ($row) => ["user" => $users->find($row->key), "count" => $row->count]);
```

#### Include partial buckets correctly in rolling aggregate queries
- **Do:** When custom analytics combine preaggregated buckets with raw events, query only complete in-window buckets and fill the partial boundary from raw entries using nonoverlapping timestamp bounds.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a rolling-window query omits its partial tail, counts events outside the selected window, or double-counts events shared by raw and aggregate ranges.
- **Why:** Boundary handling preserves exact rolling-window results while avoiding a full raw-event scan.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Index long telemetry keys through a consistent compact digest
- **Do:** For long observational keys that cannot be indexed economically in full, maintain a fixed-width digest column using engine-compatible generated columns or a consistent application fallback, and keep the original key available for display and collision-sensitive verification.
- **Flag when:** Flag when telemetry tables repeatedly index oversized text keys, or generated and application-filled digest encodings disagree between database drivers.
- **Why:** A compact digest supports bounded aggregate indexes without treating a noncryptographic key hash as an authorization or integrity guarantee.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Offer JSON output for inspection commands used by automation
- **Do:** Provide an explicit JSON output mode on application/package inspection commands consumed by scripts or agents, returning structured data without mixing human tables, banners or progress text into that output.
- **Flag when:** Flag when automation must scrape human-formatted diagnostic tables or a JSON mode emits additional non-JSON output on its data stream.
- **Why:** A structured output contract is more reliable for automation than parsing presentation text.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Match encrypted fixture storage to production writes
- **Do:** Populate encrypted factory attributes in the same persisted format the application uses: encrypt explicit raw encrypted fields and let encrypted casts handle their own inputs rather than encrypting twice.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a fixture writes plaintext into a field decrypted explicitly by the authentication flow, or double-encrypts a cast-managed field.
- **Why:** Incorrect fixture encoding creates misleading authentication tests and decryption failures unrelated to the behavior under test.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Lazy-load Pulse cards and cache their aggregate queries
- **Do:** Make expensive custom Pulse cards lazy and use the Pulse card query-remembering facility for aggregates reused between polls, with cache identity scoped to the relevant card and reporting period.
- **Flag when:** Flag custom Pulse cards that block the initial dashboard on expensive aggregation or repeat identical aggregate queries for every poll despite an acceptable cache interval.
- **Why:** Deferred loading and query reuse reduce dashboard latency and repeated database work.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Preserve rate-limit durations when migrating minute-based constructors
- **Do:** On Laravel 13, pass decay in seconds to Limit, GlobalLimit and ThrottlesExceptions constructors. Convert legacy minute-valued arguments explicitly, or use named unit factories such as Limit::perMinute.
- **Flag when:** Flag when upgraded limiter or exception-throttle constructor arguments retain old minute units and shorten the intended decay window.
- **Why:** A valid integer in the wrong unit silently weakens throttling by a factor of sixty.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
new ThrottlesExceptions(10, 2); // Intended two minutes from legacy code.
```

After:
```php
new ThrottlesExceptions(10, 2 * 60);
```

#### Configure SMTP TLS through the current transport protocol settings
- **Do:** Configure the actual SMTP scheme, endpoint, port and supported TLS options in the installed Laravel/Symfony mail transport. Use smtp with negotiated STARTTLS or smtps for implicit TLS as the provider specifies, rather than relying on a stale MAIL_ENCRYPTION variable.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a deployment assumes MAIL_ENCRYPTION alone controls TLS in the current transport, disables required TLS, or selects implicit TLS for an endpoint expecting SMTP plus STARTTLS.
- **Why:** A port number or an unused environment variable does not establish the transport security policy.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
MAIL_ENCRYPTION=tls # Assumed to configure an otherwise unchanged Laravel 13 transport.
```

After:
```php
MAIL_SCHEME=smtp # Provider STARTTLS endpoint; configure required-TLS policy through supported transport options.
```

#### Normalize external strings at the persistence boundary
- **Do:** Validate or normalize external strings for the database column encoding immediately before persistence, using an explicit reject-or-replace policy. Preserve the original request/header value for consumers that need its original representation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when malformed external strings crash a storage write or global middleware rewrites request headers solely to satisfy one database sink.
- **Why:** Sink-specific normalization avoids corrupting unrelated request behavior and keeps the original input available for diagnosis.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$request->headers->set('User-Agent', $sanitized); // Global mutation for one database write.
```

After:
```php
$storedAgent = mb_convert_encoding($request->userAgent(), 'UTF-8', 'UTF-8'); // Explicit replacement policy at this UTF-8 sink.
```

#### Combine related aggregate queries
- **Do:** Compute counts over the same filtered rows with one conditional aggregate query.
- **Flag when:** Flag when separate queries repeat the same filters solely to count different subsets.
- **Why:** One scan avoids redundant database work.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
User::where("active", true)->count(); User::where("active", false)->count();
```

After:
```php
User::selectRaw("count(case when active = 1 then 1 end) as active_count, count(case when active = 0 then 1 end) as inactive_count")->first();
```

#### Keep queued context out of logs
- **Do:** Use hidden context for metadata that should propagate to jobs without entering log context.
- **Flag when:** Flag when queue metadata that must not be logged is added with Context::add.
- **Why:** Hidden context propagates without appearing in ordinary log context; it still needs protection in queue storage.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Context::add("internal_ref", $ref);
```

After:
```php
Context::addHidden("internal_ref", $ref);
```

#### Centralize exception policy
- **Do:** Keep application exception reporting and rendering policy in bootstrap/app.php withExceptions callbacks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when application-wide exception policy is duplicated across controllers.
- **Why:** Central policy keeps error behavior consistent.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
try { $service->run(); } catch (DomainFailure $e) { return response("Failed", 422); }
```

After:
```php
->withExceptions(function (Exceptions $exceptions) { $exceptions->render(fn (DomainFailure $e) => response("Failed", 422)); })
```

#### Scope exception throttling keys
- **Do:** Use independent exception throttle keys for integrations, tenants or classes that need separate budgets.
- **Flag when:** Flag when unrelated failures share one limiting key and suppress each other.
- **Why:** Independent keys prevent one noisy source from hiding another.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return Limit::perMinute(10)->by("errors");
```

After:
```php
return Limit::perMinute(10)->by($e::class.":".$e->integrationId);
```

#### Retain security controls alongside throttling
- **Do:** Keep authentication, authorization and upstream traffic protection appropriate to the endpoint even when it is rate limited.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a throttle is the only control on a protected resource or an assumed substitute for upstream protection.
- **Why:** Rate limiting controls volume rather than identity or permissions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Exclude unauthorized sensitive fields from input rules
- **Do:** Keep sensitive attributes out of client validation rules unless the operation explicitly permits changing them.
- **Flag when:** Flag when is_admin or another privileged field is validated solely to facilitate mass assignment.
- **Why:** Validation can accidentally turn a protected attribute into accepted user input.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return ["name" => "string", "is_admin" => "boolean"];
```

After:
```php
return ["name" => "required|string"];
```

#### Inspect repository conventions before changing code
- **Do:** Inspect existing base classes, shared traits, tenancy scopes, names and helpers before applying a new convention.
- **Flag when:** Flag when new code bypasses a consistent existing house pattern without a reason.
- **Why:** Repository conventions often encode required behavior such as tenancy.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Let configured tools enforce mechanical rewrites
- **Do:** Use enabled Pint and Rector rules for formatting and canonical syntax rewrites.
- **Flag when:** Flag when manual convention instructions duplicate or conflict with enabled automated rules.
- **Why:** One automated source reduces inconsistent rewrites.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use a consistent authorization call style
- **Do:** Follow the established server-side authorization call convention for equivalent contexts.
- **Flag when:** Flag when equivalent protected handlers mix authorization APIs without a reason or convention.
- **Why:** Consistent calls make omitted enforcement easier to spot.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$this->authorize("update", $post);
```

After:
```php
Gate::authorize("update", $post);
```

#### Keep model guard conventions consistent
- **Do:** Follow the repository's deliberate mass-assignment strategy and use Laravel 13 Fillable or Guarded class attributes for modern model declarations; keep the selected writable-field boundary explicit.
- **Flag when:** Flag inconsistent allowlist/blocklist strategies or legacy property examples when standardizing on Laravel 13 model attributes.
- **Why:** A consistent guard strategy makes writable fields easier to audit.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
protected $guarded = ["is_admin"];
```

After:
```php
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Fillable;

#[Fillable(["name", "email"])]
class User extends \Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\User {}
```

#### Redeploy after Cloud configuration changes
- **Do:** Redeploy affected Cloud environments after changing variables, attached resources or linked secrets.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a changed Cloud setting or secret is assumed to affect a running deployment immediately.
- **Why:** The running environment needs a deployment to consume changed configuration.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use ephemeral Cloud authentication in CI
- **Do:** Supply LARAVEL_CLOUD_TOKEN in headless automation when credentials should not be persisted locally.
- **Flag when:** Flag when CI automation saves reusable Cloud tokens to the runner filesystem unnecessarily.
- **Why:** Ephemeral injection avoids persistent credential copies.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Pipe Cloud secret values through stdin
- **Do:** Pass Cloud secret plaintext on stdin instead of a command-line value argument.
- **Flag when:** Flag when secret:create uses --value with a real secret.
- **Why:** Arguments may appear in shell history and process listings.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Select the matching Cloud organization
- **Do:** Keep Cloud tokens scoped to their intended organization and configure organization_id consistently.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an explicit organization selector is paired with a token for another organization.
- **Why:** Mismatched contexts can fail operations or target unintended resources.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Clear sensitive form fields after success
- **Do:** Reset password and other sensitive Inertia form fields after successful submission.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a successful form retains secrets in client form state.
- **Why:** Clearing state reduces accidental redisplay or reuse.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
form.post("/password");
```

After:
```php
form.post("/password", {onSuccess: () => form.reset("password")});
```

#### Limit background polling
- **Do:** Enable usePoll keepAlive only when polling must continue in inactive tabs and choose autoStart deliberately.
- **Flag when:** Flag when keepAlive is enabled without a background-refresh requirement.
- **Why:** Inactive-tab throttling reduces unnecessary server work.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
usePoll(2000, {}, {keepAlive: true});
```

After:
```php
usePoll(2000);
```

#### Build custom permissions on Laravel authorization
- **Do:** Use Laravel gates and policies as the authorization boundary for custom roles and permissions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom permission logic bypasses Laravel authorization with a separate incompatible system.
- **Why:** Framework integration keeps enforcement and tests consistent.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
if ($legacyAcl->allows("edit", $post)) { /* ... */ }
```

After:
```php
Gate::authorize("update", $post);
```

#### Prefer supported framework primitives
- **Do:** Use Laravel primitives before adding abstraction packages that duplicate their capabilities.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a new repository/DTO/service layer duplicates supported behavior without an application need.
- **Why:** Avoiding unnecessary layers reduces maintenance.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return $genericRepository->getById($id);
```

After:
```php
return Post::findOrFail($id);
```

#### Keep secrets out of shared artifacts
- **Do:** Redact secrets from screenshots, CI output and copied configuration artifacts.
- **Flag when:** Flag when shared artifacts contain live credentials or tokens.
- **Why:** Secondary artifacts can leak credentials even when source control is clean.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Limit CSRF exceptions to specific externally authenticated endpoints
- **Do:** Limit CSRF exceptions to specific externally authenticated endpoints.
- **Flag when:** Flag when request-forgery exceptions cover broader paths than the intended webhooks.
- **Why:** Narrow exceptions preserve protection on browser endpoints.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$middleware->preventRequestForgery(except: ["*"]);
```

After:
```php
$middleware->preventRequestForgery(except: ["stripe/webhook"]);
```

#### Configure framework middleware through supported configuration APIs
- **Do:** Configure framework middleware through supported configuration APIs.
- **Flag when:** Flag when copied framework middleware exists only to change options exposed by static/bootstrap configuration.
- **Why:** Supported APIs avoid maintaining framework copies.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class EncryptCookies extends BaseEncryptCookies { protected $except = ["theme"]; }
```

After:
```php
$middleware->encryptCookies(except: ["theme"]);
```

#### Offer multi-factor authentication for user accounts
- **Do:** Offer multi-factor authentication for user accounts.
- **Flag when:** Flag when sensitive user accounts have no supported second-factor enrollment or challenge flow.
- **Why:** MFA reduces reliance on a single password.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Password is the only supported factor.
```

After:
```php
Features::twoFactorAuthentication(["confirm" => true, "confirmPassword" => true]),
```

#### Lock Livewire identity properties and reauthorize actions
- **Do:** Store sensitive Livewire identities as locked scalar IDs and reauthorize the resolved models in actions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a client-mutable Livewire ID selects a protected record without action authorization.
- **Why:** Locked IDs prevent tampering while policies protect current access.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public int $postId;
```

After:
```php
#[Locked] public int $postId; // Also Gate::authorize in every sensitive action.
```

#### Complete generated Form Request authorization stubs
- **Do:** Complete generated Form Request authorization stubs.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a generated authorize() still returns false unintentionally or duplicates authorization handled elsewhere.
- **Why:** The generated stub can reject every request until its access policy is set.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function authorize(): bool { return false; }
```

After:
```php
public function authorize(): bool { return $this->user()->can("create", Post::class); }
```

#### Use validation failures for invalid input and authorization failures for denied actors
- **Do:** Use validation failures for invalid input and authorization failures for denied actors.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a policy returns 403 solely because a request value is invalid.
- **Why:** Clients need the correct failure reason and status.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function authorize(): bool { return $this->input("age") >= 18; }
```

After:
```php
public function rules(): array { return ["age" => "required|integer|min:18"]; }
```

#### Enforce route permissions with can middleware when adopting route-level authorization
- **Do:** Enforce route permissions with can middleware when adopting route-level authorization.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a route-level authorization convention is bypassed by equivalent controller-only checks.
- **Why:** Route declarations make the permission boundary visible beside the endpoint.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::put("/posts/{post}", $update);
```

After:
```php
Route::put("/posts/{post}", $update)->can("update", "post");
```

#### Reserve trusted-HTML wrappers for trusted content
- **Do:** Use AsHtmlString casts and toHtmlString() only for content already safe to render unescaped.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an unsanitized user-controlled value is cast to AsHtmlString or converted with toHtmlString().
- **Why:** The cast opts the value out of ordinary escaping.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"body" => AsHtmlString::class,
```

After:
```php
"body" => "string", // Sanitize intentional HTML at its boundary.
```

#### Generate an application key for each newly created application
- **Do:** Generate an application key for each newly created application.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a new application runs with an empty APP_KEY or a copied key from another app.
- **Why:** Encryption needs a stable unique application secret.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Key two-factor challenge limits to the pending login identity
- **Do:** Key two-factor challenge limits to the pending login identity.
- **Flag when:** Flag when MFA guesses rotate IP/session details to evade the account challenge budget.
- **Why:** The pending identity ties guesses to the authentication attempt.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Limit::perMinute(5)->by($request->ip());
```

After:
```php
Limit::perMinute(5)->by($request->session()->get("login.id"));
```

#### Throttle passkey operations using the credential or session and IP
- **Do:** Throttle passkey operations using the credential or session and IP.
- **Flag when:** Flag when passkey endpoints have no stable credential/session abuse budget.
- **Why:** Identity-aware limits constrain repeated credential ceremony attempts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// No passkey limiter.
```

After:
```php
Limit::perMinute(10)->by($credentialId."|".$request->ip());
```

#### Clear temporary MFA setup state when setup closes or restarts
- **Do:** Clear temporary MFA setup state when setup closes or restarts.
- **Flag when:** Flag when abandoned setup retains sensitive QR, shared-secret or recovery-code state in the client.
- **Why:** Clearing temporary state reduces accidental exposure.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Close modal without clearing setup data.
```

After:
```php
// Clear QR code, secret and recovery code state on close/restart.
```

#### Keep authentication session cookies HttpOnly
- **Do:** Keep authentication session cookies HttpOnly.
- **Flag when:** Flag when session authentication cookies are readable by JavaScript without an explicit supported requirement.
- **Why:** HttpOnly reduces credential theft through script access.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"http_only" => false,
```

After:
```php
"http_only" => true,
```

#### Require authentication and every mandatory token ability
- **Do:** Require authentication and every mandatory token ability.
- **Flag when:** Flag when ability middleware accepts unauthenticated callers or only one of several required abilities.
- **Why:** Required capabilities must all hold for the operation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Check any one ability for an operation requiring both.
```

After:
```php
Route::middleware(["auth:sanctum", "abilities:orders:read,orders:update"])->put($path, $handler);
```

#### Grant deployment tokens only the scopes and targets they require
- **Do:** Grant deployment tokens only the scopes and targets they require.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Cloud tokens have unnecessarily broad actions/environments or assume creator-role inheritance.
- **Why:** Explicit least privilege limits infrastructure credential impact.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use ForwardsCalls for framework-style method delegation
- **Do:** Use ForwardsCalls for framework-style method delegation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when dynamic delegated calls use call_user_func and lose consistent missing-method handling.
- **Why:** The trait provides framework-compatible forwarding behavior.
- **Enforced by:** partial: rector:UseForwardsCallsTraitRector

Before:
```php
return call_user_func_array([$target, $method], $args);
```

After:
```php
return $this->forwardCallTo($target, $method, $args);
```

#### Validate recipient addresses before passing them to the mail transport
- **Do:** Validate recipient addresses before passing them to the mail transport.
- **Flag when:** Flag when user-controlled email addresses reach Mail without validated safe address syntax.
- **Why:** Malformed addresses can manipulate message headers or content on vulnerable transports.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Mail::to($request->input("email"))->send($mail);
```

After:
```php
$data = $request->validate(["email" => "required|email"]); Mail::to($data["email"])->send($mail);
```

#### Make dashboard gate signatures compatible with approved external authentication
- **Do:** Make dashboard gate signatures compatible with approved external authentication.
- **Flag when:** Flag when IP- or proxy-authenticated diagnostic access is unintentionally denied solely because a gate requires a Laravel user.
- **Why:** A nullable user can support an alternate access boundary, but must not grant unauthenticated public access.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Gate::define("viewHorizon", fn (User $user) => $networkCheck());
```

After:
```php
Gate::define("viewHorizon", fn (?User $user) => $networkCheck());
```

#### Pass trusted model identifiers to unique-rule ignore clauses
- **Do:** Pass trusted model identifiers to unique-rule ignore clauses.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Rule::unique()->ignore receives request-controlled ID or column data.
- **Why:** The uniqueness exception must target the trusted resource being updated.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Rule::unique("users")->ignore($request->id)
```

After:
```php
Rule::unique("users")->ignore($user)
```

#### Exclude passwords and secrets from flashed input
- **Do:** Exclude passwords and secrets from flashed input.
- **Flag when:** Flag when redirect withInput/flash stores sensitive submitted fields in session old input.
- **Why:** Secret values can be retained or redisplayed on later pages.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return back()->withInput();
```

After:
```php
return back()->withInput($request->except(["password", "password_confirmation", "token"]));
```

#### Keep encryption and signing on cookies trusted by the application
- **Do:** Keep encryption and signing on cookies trusted by the application.
- **Flag when:** Flag when application-trusted cookie values are accepted without encryption/signature verification.
- **Why:** Clients can read or alter plaintext cookie state.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Disable EncryptCookies for all routes.
```

After:
```php
// Retain EncryptCookies; explicitly exclude only nontrusted display preferences if needed.
```

#### Bind untrusted SQL values and allowlist dynamic SQL structure
- **Do:** Bind untrusted SQL values and allowlist dynamic SQL structure.
- **Flag when:** Flag when request data is interpolated into raw SQL or unprepared statements.
- **Why:** Bindings protect values; identifiers and raw SQL structure need explicit allowlists.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
DB::select("select * from users where email = '".$email."'");
```

After:
```php
DB::select("select * from users where email = ?", [$email]);
```

#### Isolate databases and shared resources for each parallel test process
- **Do:** Isolate databases and shared resources for each parallel test process.
- **Flag when:** Flag when parallel tests use the same mutable database/files/cache namespace.
- **Why:** Process-specific namespaces prevent races and false failures.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$path = storage_path("test-output.json");
```

After:
```php
$path = storage_path("test-output-".ParallelTesting::token().".json");
```

#### Size password columns for the selected hash algorithm
- **Do:** Size password columns for the selected hash algorithm.
- **Flag when:** Flag when password hash storage is shorter than required by bcrypt or the configured algorithm.
- **Why:** Truncated hashes can make valid credentials unusable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$table->string("password", 32);
```

After:
```php
$table->string("password", 255);
```

#### Pass the submitted plaintext password to Auth::attempt
- **Do:** Pass the submitted plaintext password to Auth::attempt.
- **Flag when:** Flag when request passwords are prehashed before Auth::attempt.
- **Why:** The provider verifies against the stored adaptive hash.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Auth::attempt(["email" => $email, "password" => Hash::make($password)]);
```

After:
```php
Auth::attempt(["email" => $email, "password" => $password]);
```

#### Use gates for nonresource abilities and policies for resource abilities
- **Do:** Use gates for nonresource abilities and policies for resource abilities.
- **Flag when:** Flag when nonresource authorization is forced into unrelated model policies or duplicated resource checks remain in closures.
- **Why:** The two supported homes serve distinct permission shapes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Dashboard access duplicated inline.
```

After:
```php
Gate::define("viewDashboard", fn (User $u) => $u->is_admin);
```

#### Schedule cleanup for expired API-token records
- **Do:** Schedule cleanup for expired API-token records.
- **Flag when:** Flag when expiring Sanctum tokens accumulate indefinitely.
- **Why:** Pruning limits stale credential metadata and storage growth.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// No expired-token cleanup schedule.
```

After:
```php
Schedule::command("sanctum:prune-expired --hours=24")->daily();
```

#### Handle expired SPA sessions by returning users to authentication
- **Do:** Handle expired SPA sessions by returning users to authentication.
- **Flag when:** Flag when 401/419 session-expiry responses leave the SPA stuck or trigger CSRF bypasses.
- **Why:** A deliberate reauthentication path restores valid session state.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Retry the same failing write indefinitely.
```

After:
```php
// On expired-session 401/419, clear local auth state and route to login.
```

#### Enable only required Fortify features
- **Do:** Enable only required Fortify features.
- **Flag when:** Flag when unused registration/recovery/passkey features expose unnecessary routes.
- **Why:** A smaller enabled feature set reduces unneeded account entry points.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"features" => [/* every feature */],
```

After:
```php
"features" => [Features::registration(), Features::resetPasswords(), Features::emailVerification()],
```

#### Preserve required authentication stages when customizing Fortify
- **Do:** Preserve required authentication stages when customizing Fortify.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom login pipeline omits throttling, canonicalization, MFA challenge or session preparation without replacement.
- **Why:** Each stage contributes to the authentication boundary.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Fortify::authenticateThrough(fn () => [AttemptToAuthenticate::class]);
```

After:
```php
// Start from the documented installed-version pipeline and retain required safeguards.
```

#### Verify OIDC nonce binding for token-based social login
- **Do:** Verify OIDC nonce binding for token-based social login.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Facebook Limited Login/OIDC authentication omits the initiating nonce during token verification.
- **Why:** Nonce validation binds the token to the initiating login attempt.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$provider->userFromToken($token);
```

After:
```php
$provider->userFromToken($token, $expectedNonce);
```

#### Use the framework password broker for reset flows
- **Do:** Use the framework password broker for reset flows.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom reset handling reimplements token generation, checking and consumption without a requirement.
- **Why:** The broker integrates expiry, hashing and one-time reset behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Custom predictable reset token table and comparison.
```

After:
```php
Password::sendResetLink(["email" => $email]);
```

#### Configure deliberate reset-token expiry and request throttling
- **Do:** Configure deliberate reset-token expiry and request throttling.
- **Flag when:** Flag when password reset broker defaults are used without matching the account security policy.
- **Why:** Expiry and throttling bound recovery credential exposure and message abuse.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"expire" => 1440, "throttle" => 0,
```

After:
```php
"expire" => 60, "throttle" => 60,
```

#### Validate reset token, identity and new password before reset execution
- **Do:** Validate reset token, identity and new password before reset execution.
- **Flag when:** Flag when reset requests skip required token/email/password validation.
- **Why:** Recovery inputs must meet the broker and password contracts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Password::reset($request->all(), $callback);
```

After:
```php
$data = $request->validate(["token" => "required", "email" => "required|email", "password" => ["required", "confirmed", Password::defaults()]]); Password::reset($data, $callback);
```

- **Do:** Dispatch PasswordReset after a successful custom reset.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom reset saves the password without emitting the framework lifecycle event.
- **Why:** Listeners and audit trails depend on the successful reset event.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php

```

After:
```php
$user->save(); event(new PasswordReset($user));
```

- **Do:** Use the verified email request contract before marking an address verified.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an email verification handler marks a user verified without validating the request identity/hash/signature.



#### Keep supported centralized hasher costs unless measured requirements justify tuning
- **Do:** Keep supported centralized hasher costs unless measured requirements justify tuning.
- **Flag when:** Flag when per-call hashing overrides create inconsistent costs without an operational need.
- **Why:** Central defaults are easier to benchmark and upgrade.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:

- **Do:** Keep hash algorithm and configuration verification enabled except during a controlled migration.
- **Flag when:** Flag when HASH_VERIFY is disabled indefinitely or client-provided precomputed hashes bypass algorithm/cost checks.

After:

- **Do:** Quote environment-file values containing spaces.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an unquoted .env value contains spaces and fails parsing.

- **Do:** Keep console commands thin and delegate application work to services.

- **Do:** Disable arbitrary cache object unserialization when unnecessary.
- **Flag when:** Flag when cache.serializable_classes permits arbitrary PHP classes without a required object-caching use case.

- **Do:** Name middleware after the condition it enforces.

#### Avoid stuffing long prefixes or keys into bcrypt password input
- **Do:** Avoid stuffing long prefixes or keys into bcrypt password input.
- **Flag when:** Flag when password preprocessing can push the meaningful password beyond bcrypt 72-byte input.

Before:


After:

- **Do:** Store keyed proofs rather than password hashes in client-visible authentication artifacts.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a cookie/token embeds a raw password hash or an unkeyed derivative.
- **Why:** A leaked password hash enables offline guessing.

Before:


#### Use strict equality or timing-safe comparison for digest strings
- **Do:** Use strict equality or timing-safe comparison for digest strings.
- **Flag when:** Flag when hash strings are compared with loose == equality.

- **Enforced by:** partial: pint:strict_comparison

Before:
```php

```

After:
```php
$digest === $expected // use hash_equals for secret authentication values
```

#### Support Escape and click-away dismissal for dismissible overlays
- **Do:** Support Escape and click-away dismissal for dismissible overlays.
- **Flag when:** Flag when reusable modals/popovers offer no expected keyboard or outside-click close behavior.
- **Why:** Predictable dismissal improves usability and accessibility.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<div x-show="open">...</div>
```

After:
```php
<div x-show="open" @keydown.escape.window="open=false" @click.outside="open=false">...</div>
```

#### Persist selected layout elements across Livewire navigation
- **Do:** When adopting Livewire navigation, wrap layout elements that should retain DOM state, such as a toast container or media player, in matching @persist blocks with stable unique names.
- **Flag when:** Flag when navigation destroys a layout element whose state must continue, or repeated persisted elements reuse an ambiguous identity.
- **Why:** Persistent DOM identity preserves intended media and notification continuity across page swaps.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Reference Laravel 13 request-forgery middleware in code and tests
- **Do:** Reference Illuminate\Foundation\Http\Middleware\PreventRequestForgery (not the deprecated VerifyCsrfToken/ValidateCsrfToken aliases) in withoutMiddleware calls, route exclusions and custom CSRF middleware; packages supporting older Laravel versions should list each version's class.
- **Flag when:** Flag when maintained code or test middleware controls target only deprecated VerifyCsrfToken/ValidateCsrfToken aliases while the active Laravel 13 stack uses PreventRequestForgery.
- **Why:** A reference to the wrong middleware class may leave a test bypass ineffective or a custom middleware integration disconnected from the active stack.
- **Enforced by:** partial: rector:RenameClassRector

After:
```php
use Illuminate\Foundation\Http\Middleware\PreventRequestForgery; $this->withoutMiddleware([PreventRequestForgery::class]); // BEFORE: $this->withoutMiddleware([VerifyCsrfToken::class]);
```

#### Select the intended database driver explicitly
- **Do:** Set DB_CONNECTION or the equivalent deployment configuration to the intended database backend rather than accidentally relying on the Laravel skeleton's SQLite default when the application expects another engine.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a MySQL/PostgreSQL deployment supplies host/database credentials but leaves the default connection on SQLite.
- **Why:** Other connection credentials do not automatically change the selected driver, leading to missing-file errors or use of the wrong database.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Space Blade echo expressions under the chosen formatting convention
- **Do:** When the project adopts spaced Blade echoes, place one space inside ordinary escaped and raw echo delimiters and enforce the convention with a Blade-aware formatter.
- **Flag when:** Flag when maintained Blade templates mix {{$value}} with {{ $value }} under the adopted spaced-echo convention; do not rewrite escaped client expressions or Blade comments as ordinary echoes.
- **Why:** One mechanical convention keeps template expressions readable and avoids recurring formatting review.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
{{$name}}
```

After:
```php
{{ $name }}
```

#### Keep cancellation and exit flows free of deliberate obstruction
- **Do:** Make subscription/payment cancellation and application exit discoverable and usable. Use proportionate confirmations for real consequences without adding unrelated steps intended to prevent users leaving.
- **Flag when:** Flag when cancellation or exit is hidden, requires unrelated work, or uses repeated misleading prompts solely to discourage completion.
- **Why:** Protecting users from mistakes does not justify preventing an intended cancellation or exit.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Hide cancellation behind unrelated retention screens with no clear exit.
```

After:
```php
Offer a clear cancel action, state its consequences and confirm the resulting cancellation state.
```

#### Mark intentionally unreported exceptions
- **Do:** Implement ShouldntReport on exceptions that application policy says must never be reported.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the same intentionally unreported exception is repeatedly filtered at reporting call sites.
- **Why:** The class exposes its reporting policy consistently.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class ExpectedFailure extends RuntimeException {}
```

After:
```php
class ExpectedFailure extends RuntimeException implements \Illuminate\Contracts\Debug\ShouldntReport {}
```

#### Authorize bound resources
- **Do:** Authorize access to a resolved model independently of scoped route binding.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a protected resource handler relies only on successful route model binding.
- **Why:** Binding constrains resolution but does not decide whether the actor may perform the action.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return $post;
```

After:
```php
Gate::authorize("view", $post); return $post;
```

#### Keep intentionally public actions public
- **Do:** Omit redundant permission checks on operations explicitly intended for everyone.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an intentionally public operation requires a permission with no access-control purpose.
- **Why:** An unnecessary check can accidentally deny intended public access.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Gate::authorize("viewPublicCatalog"); return $catalog;
```

After:
```php
return $catalog;
```

#### Test the permission matrix at the policy boundary
- **Do:** Test each relevant role, ownership state and ability directly against its policy or gate.
- **Flag when:** Flag when permission combinations are only covered indirectly or not covered.
- **Why:** Direct tests identify the permission rule that failed.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$this->actingAs($owner)->get("/posts/1")->assertOk();
```

After:
```php
$this->assertTrue($owner->can("view", $post)); $this->assertFalse($outsider->can("view", $post));
```

#### Choose first-party API authentication by requirements
- **Do:** Use Sanctum for SPA/mobile/simple token authentication and Passport when OAuth2 delegation is required.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom authentication stack duplicates supported first-party behavior without a requirement.
- **Why:** Matching the authentication scheme to the client avoids unnecessary protocol complexity.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Implement a custom bearer-token table and middleware.
```

After:
```php
Route::middleware("auth:sanctum")->get("/me", fn (Request $r) => $r->user());
```

#### Name event timestamps consistently
- **Do:** Name event timestamp columns with an action_at convention.
- **Flag when:** Flag when event timestamps use inconsistent names without a domain reason.
- **Why:** Consistent names reveal that values represent times.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$table->timestamp("verification");
```

After:
```php
$table->timestamp("verified_at")->nullable();
```

#### Encrypt queued payloads containing sensitive data
- **Do:** Encrypt queued payloads containing sensitive data.
- **Flag when:** Flag when queued jobs, listeners, notifications or mailables serialize secrets or personal data without payload encryption.
- **Why:** Queue storage otherwise exposes serialized sensitive values.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class ExportJob implements ShouldQueue {}
```

After:
```php
class ExportJob implements ShouldQueue, \Illuminate\Contracts\Queue\ShouldBeEncrypted {}
```

#### Throttle sensitive actions outside the routing layer when needed
- **Do:** Throttle sensitive actions outside the routing layer when needed.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an abusable operation can be invoked through non-HTTP paths without the intended rate limit.
- **Why:** Operation-level limits cover all callers.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$sendMessage->handle($user);
```

After:
```php
RateLimiter::attempt("send:".$user->id, 5, fn () => $sendMessage->handle($user));
```

#### Configure trusted proxies and hosts for the actual deployment
- **Do:** Configure trusted proxies and hosts for the actual deployment.
- **Flag when:** Flag when forwarded headers from untrusted callers affect client IP, scheme or generated host.
- **Why:** Correct trust boundaries prevent spoofed limit identities and poisoned signed/reset links.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$middleware->trustProxies(at: "*");
```

After:
```php
$middleware->trustProxies(at: ["10.0.0.10"]); $middleware->trustHosts(at: ["^example\.com$"]);
```

#### Separate and validate shell arguments before execution
- **Do:** Separate and validate shell arguments before execution.
- **Flag when:** Flag when user input is concatenated into a shell command or only escapeshellcmd protects the whole string.
- **Why:** Argument injection can run unintended options or commands.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Process::run("convert ".$request->input("file"));
```

After:
```php
Process::run(["convert", "--", $validatedPath]); // validate path and option semantics
```

#### Sign links whose parameters must resist tampering
- **Do:** Sign links whose parameters must resist tampering.
- **Flag when:** Flag when unsubscribe or preview links trust changeable resource identifiers without integrity protection.
- **Why:** Signatures bind the intended URL parameters.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
route("preview", ["post" => $post]);
```

After:
```php
URL::temporarySignedRoute("preview", now()->addMinutes(30), ["post" => $post]);
```

#### Return not-found denials when resource existence is private
- **Do:** Return not-found denials when resource existence is private.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an authorization denial discloses a protected resource existence contrary to the access policy.
- **Why:** A 404 response can avoid exposing record existence.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return Response::deny();
```

After:
```php
return Response::denyAsNotFound();
```

#### Restrict CORS origins to trusted clients
- **Do:** Restrict CORS origins to trusted clients.
- **Flag when:** Flag when config/cors.php allows arbitrary or untrusted origins (wildcards or broad patterns) for endpoints that use cookie/session credentials (supports_credentials true), or for private APIs whose clients are known.
- **Why:** Trusted origin lists constrain browser cross-origin access.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"allowed_origins" => ["*"],
```

After:
```php
"allowed_origins" => ["https://app.example.com"],
```

#### Use timeboxing for custom timing-sensitive credential checks
- **Do:** Use timeboxing for custom timing-sensitive credential checks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom secret checks have observable success/failure timing differences despite timing-safe comparison.
- **Why:** A minimum duration reduces useful whole-operation timing differences.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return $repository->checkToken($token);
```

After:
```php
return (new Timebox)->call(fn ($box) => $repository->checkToken($token), 200000);
```

#### Use state-changing HTTP methods for mutations
- **Do:** Use state-changing HTTP methods for mutations.
- **Flag when:** Flag when GET routes change persistent state.
- **Why:** GET requests may be prefetched and do not receive normal mutation CSRF checks.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::get("/posts/{post}/delete", $delete);
```

After:
```php
Route::delete("/posts/{post}", $delete)->middleware("auth");
```

#### Keep private files off public disks and authorize delivery
- **Do:** Keep private files off public disks and authorize delivery.
- **Flag when:** Flag when sensitive files are publicly addressable without an intended access boundary.
- **Why:** Private storage plus authorized temporary delivery limits disclosure.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Storage::disk("public")->put($path, $contents);
```

After:
```php
Storage::disk("local")->put($path, $contents); // Serve after policy authorization or a scoped expiring link.
```

#### Sanitize or isolate uploaded SVG files
- **Do:** Sanitize or isolate uploaded SVG files.
- **Flag when:** Flag when user SVGs render on the application origin without sanitization.
- **Why:** SVG can carry active content.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Storage::disk("public")->putFile("images", $request->file("svg"));
```

After:
```php
// Reject SVG, sanitize with a maintained SVG sanitizer, or serve it from an isolated origin.
```

#### Require SSH key authentication on production hosts
- **Do:** Require SSH key authentication on production hosts.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production SSH permits password authentication contrary to the access policy.
- **Why:** Keys avoid reusable password-based remote login.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use production password defaults with at least 12 characters and compromised-password checks
- **Do:** Use production password defaults with at least 12 characters and compromised-password checks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production password enrollment uses a shorter adopted minimum or omits compromised checks.
- **Why:** Longer passwords and reuse checks improve resistance to guessing.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Password::defaults(fn () => Password::min(6));
```

After:
```php
Password::defaults(fn () => Password::min(12)->uncompromised());
```

#### Test that an incorrect password blocks account deletion
- **Do:** Test that an incorrect password blocks account deletion.
- **Flag when:** Flag when account deletion tests omit a wrong-password refusal.
- **Why:** The test proves the destructive action honors its password check.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Only successful deletion is tested.
```

After:
```php
$this->actingAs($user)->delete("/user", ["password" => "wrong"])->assertSessionHasErrors("password");
```

#### Test reset links through faked reset notifications
- **Do:** Test reset links through faked reset notifications.
- **Flag when:** Flag when password reset tests bypass generated tokens or send real mail.
- **Why:** Faked notifications let tests exercise the actual token contract safely.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Hard-code a reset token.
```

After:
```php
Notification::fake(); Password::sendResetLink(["email" => $user->email]); Notification::assertSentTo($user, ResetPassword::class);
```

#### Inject services when adopting dependency injection over facades
- **Do:** Inject services when adopting dependency injection over facades.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a class uses facades despite an explicit dependency-injection convention.
- **Why:** Constructor dependencies make service requirements visible and substitutable.
- **Enforced by:** partial: rector:ArgumentFuncCallToMethodCallRector, partial: rector:StaticCallToMethodCallRector

Before:
```php
Hash::make($password);
```

After:
```php
public function __construct(private \Illuminate\Contracts\Hashing\Hasher $hasher) {}
```

#### Move shared job throttling into supported queue middleware
- **Do:** Move shared job throttling into supported queue middleware.
- **Flag when:** Flag when jobs duplicate throttling inside handle despite equivalent built-in middleware.
- **Why:** Middleware centralizes the cross-cutting limit.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function handle() { /* duplicated limiter */ }
```

After:
```php
public function middleware(): array { return [new RateLimited("provider")]; }
```

#### Reuse the route-bound model in request authorization
- **Do:** Reuse the route-bound model in request authorization.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Form Request re-queries a resource already resolved by route binding.
- **Why:** Reusing the instance avoids redundant queries and mismatched resolution.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$this->user()->can("update", Post::findOrFail($this->route("post")));
```

After:
```php
$this->user()->can("update", $this->post);
```

#### Isolate browser-test environment configuration
- **Do:** Isolate browser-test environment configuration.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Dusk uses production/dev secrets or mismatched APP_URL instead of an explicit test environment.
- **Why:** Separate browser-test configuration avoids wrong-target actions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Dusk points to the production APP_URL.
```

After:
```php
// Use .env.dusk.ci with the CI host and isolated database.
```

#### Use request-carried API credentials for nonbrowser service clients
- **Do:** Use request-carried API credentials for nonbrowser service clients.
- **Flag when:** Flag when remote service authentication unnecessarily depends on browser session cookies.
- **Why:** Explicit API credentials suit independent service requests.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Service persists browser session cookies for API access.
```

After:
```php
Authorization: Bearer <scoped-api-token>
```

#### Allow nullable policy users only for deliberately guest-accessible abilities
- **Do:** Allow nullable policy users only for deliberately guest-accessible abilities.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an intended guest ability requires a nonnullable authenticated user or nullable access is added without guest rules.
- **Why:** The method signature participates in guest authorization behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function view(User $user, Post $post): bool {}
```

After:
```php
public function view(?User $user, Post $post): bool { return $post->is_public || $user?->id === $post->user_id; }
```

#### Broadcast user-specific data only on authorized resource-scoped private channels
- **Do:** Broadcast user-specific data only on authorized resource-scoped private channels.
- **Flag when:** Flag when sensitive events use public channels or a private channel broader than the intended audience.
- **Why:** Channel scoping controls who receives the payload.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return new Channel("orders");
```

After:
```php
return new PrivateChannel("orders.".$this->order->id);
```

#### Validate storage paths before normalization and use
- **Do:** Validate storage paths before normalization and use.
- **Flag when:** Flag when untrusted paths are trusted after normalization without checking allowed roots or characters.
- **Why:** Normalization can change path meaning and does not authorize a destination.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Storage::get($request->path);
```

After:
```php
Storage::get($pathValidator->withinAllowedRoot($request->path));
```

#### Use query-only bulk mutations only when policies and model events are unnecessary
- **Do:** Use query-only bulk mutations only when policies and model events are unnecessary.
- **Flag when:** Flag when fetchSelectedRecords(false) bypasses needed per-record checks or observers.
- **Why:** A single query trades model lifecycle behavior for speed.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
DeleteBulkAction::make()->fetchSelectedRecords(false)
```

After:
```php
DeleteBulkAction::make()->authorizeIndividualRecords()
```

#### Test authorization after a Livewire model ownership or permission change
- **Do:** Test authorization after a Livewire model ownership or permission change.
- **Flag when:** Flag when tests cover only the initial mount state of a retained model.
- **Why:** Subsequent requests must respect changed tenancy and permissions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Only initial authorized mount tested.
```

After:
```php
// Mount as owner, transfer the record, then assert the next mutation is denied.
```

#### Derive Inertia asset versions from the build manifest
- **Do:** Use an Inertia asset version that changes with each client build. When relying on manifest changes, hash the production manifest explicitly or ensure the default middleware is not overridden by a stable ASSET_URL.
- **Flag when:** Flag a fixed asset version, or a stable CDN ASSET_URL whose default Inertia version stays unchanged across new client manifests.
- **Why:** Version changes synchronize frontend assets with the deployed backend.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function version(Request $request): ?string { return "1"; }
```

After:
```php
public function version(Request $request): ?string
{
    $manifest = public_path('build/manifest.json');

    return is_file($manifest) ? hash_file('xxh128', $manifest) : null;
}
```

#### Restrict dependency auto-merge automation to verified bot updates and required checks
- **Do:** Restrict dependency auto-merge automation to verified bot updates and required checks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an auto-merge workflow runs for arbitrary PR actors or bypasses required validation.
- **Why:** Actor gating limits privileged automation to its intended update source.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Enable hover prefetching only where unused requests are acceptable
- **Do:** Enable hover prefetching only where unused requests are acceptable.
- **Flag when:** Flag when wire:navigate.hover is broadly enabled without considering speculative request cost.
- **Why:** Prefetches can load pages the user never visits.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<a href="/expensive-report" wire:navigate.hover>Report</a>
```

After:
```php
<a href="/expensive-report" wire:navigate>Report</a>
```

#### Write custom policies and generated application code outside vendor
- **Do:** Write custom policies and generated application code outside vendor.
- **Flag when:** Flag when application changes or generated policies are placed in Composer-managed vendor files.
- **Why:** Composer updates overwrite those changes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
vendor/package/src/Policies/PostPolicy.php
```

After:
```php
app/Policies/Vendor/PostPolicy.php
```

#### Prevent submitted file paths from selecting unauthorized shared-storage files
- **Do:** Prevent submitted file paths from selecting unauthorized shared-storage files.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a FileUpload field can submit another user path on a shared disk.
- **Why:** A configured directory alone does not authorize existing file paths.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
FileUpload::make("attachment")->directory("uploads")
```

After:
```php
FileUpload::make("attachment")->preventFilePathTampering()
```

#### Consume the saved PKCE verifier during token exchange
- **Do:** Consume the saved PKCE verifier during token exchange.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a verifier remains available for reuse after its authorization attempt.
- **Why:** A one-time verifier belongs to one code exchange.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$verifier = session("code_verifier");
```

After:
```php
$verifier = session()->pull("code_verifier");
```

#### Send OAuth token exchange credentials in the POST body
- **Do:** Send OAuth token exchange credentials in the POST body.
- **Flag when:** Flag when authorization codes, client secrets or verifiers are placed in a token endpoint URL query.
- **Why:** URL parameters are more readily retained in logs and intermediaries.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Http::get($tokenUrl."?client_secret=".$secret);
```

After:
```php
Http::asForm()->post($tokenUrl, ["client_secret" => $secret, "code" => $code]);
```

#### Index both model type and ID on polymorphic authorization pivots
- **Do:** Index both model type and ID on polymorphic token-ownership and authorization tables.
- **Flag when:** Flag when token-owner or authorization-pivot lookups filter model type and ID without a matching composite index.
- **Why:** Polymorphic ownership queries need both discriminator and identifier.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$table->index("model_id");
```

After:
```php
$table->index(["model_id", "model_type"]);
```

#### Drop dependent authorization pivots before their referenced tables
- **Do:** Drop dependent authorization pivots before their referenced tables.
- **Flag when:** Flag when migration rollback drops a referenced role/permission table while pivots still depend on it.
- **Why:** Reverse dependency order avoids foreign-key rollback failures.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Schema::dropIfExists("roles"); Schema::dropIfExists("model_has_roles");
```

After:
```php
Schema::dropIfExists("model_has_roles"); Schema::dropIfExists("roles");
```

#### Offer TOTP or security keys rather than relying on SMS alone for high-assurance MFA
- **Do:** Offer TOTP or security keys rather than relying on SMS alone for high-assurance MFA.
- **Flag when:** Flag when high-assurance accounts have only an SMS second factor despite a requirement for stronger factors.
- **Why:** SMS is vulnerable to SIM swapping; stronger factors reduce that dependency.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Only SMS challenge enrollment is offered.
```

After:
```php
Features::twoFactorAuthentication(["confirm" => true]); // Offer TOTP/security keys plus secure recovery.
```

#### Capture release revision metadata before runtime Git metadata is removed
- **Do:** Resolve the deployed commit during build or deployment and expose it through release configuration or platform metadata. On Cloud, persist a derived release value before rebuilding configuration; on Vapor, supply the deployment commit metadata. Runtime code must not require a .git directory.
- **Flag when:** Flag when error reporting or release identification shells out to git at runtime on a platform that removes repository metadata, or records the wrong build revision.
- **Why:** Deployment-time revision metadata survives stripped artifacts and identifies the release that actually produced an error.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Throttle interval-based Pulse beat listeners explicitly
- **Do:** Throttle expensive Pulse listeners with the Throttling concern or equivalent shared interval state. Choose IsolatedBeat for collection protected by the shared pulse:check lock, or SharedBeat for per-instance collection; ensure the store supports the required locking.
- **Flag when:** Flag expensive work on every pulse:check tick, invocation-local throttle state, nonexistent Beat listeners, or confusing IsolatedBeat shared-lock isolation with SharedBeat per-instance execution.
- **Why:** Explicit intervals preserve the intended collection frequency independently of the daemon beat cadence.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Listen for Beat and assume its frequency enforces the interval.
```

After:
```php
class CustomRecorder
{
    use \Laravel\Pulse\Recorders\Concerns\Throttling;

    public function record(\Laravel\Pulse\Events\SharedBeat $event): void
    {
        $this->throttle(15, $event, function ($event) { /* collect per-instance metrics */ });
    }
}
```

#### Update every token consumer during credential rotation
- **Do:** For replacement API tokens, update and verify integrations before revoking the old token. When refreshing a Forge deploy-hook token invalidates its predecessor immediately, coordinate the refresh and promptly update every hook caller.
- **Flag when:** Flag revocation before replacement consumers work, or a refreshed deployment hook still called with its invalidated token.
- **Why:** Token invalidation is immediate, so uncoordinated rotation interrupts integrations and deployments.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use declarative tests for facts
- **Do:** Use Pest test() for declarative facts when that is the project convention.
- **Flag when:** Flag when fact-style Pest tests use inconsistent sentence forms with no behavioral action.
- **Why:** Consistent naming makes the suite easier to scan.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
it("has label", fn () => expect(Status::Paid->label())->toBe("Paid"));
```

After:
```php
test("paid status label", fn () => expect(Status::Paid->label())->toBe("Paid"));
```

#### Configure explicit OAuth callbacks
- **Do:** Configure absolute environment-specific OAuth callback URLs and register exact allowed URLs with the provider.
- **Flag when:** Flag when callback URLs are relative, guessed or mismatched with the provider allowlist.
- **Why:** Exact callbacks prevent misdirected authorization responses.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"redirect" => "/auth/callback",
```

After:
```php
"redirect" => env("GITHUB_REDIRECT_URI"), // absolute URL
```

#### Authorize sensitive field changes
- **Do:** Check field-specific permissions before allowing privileged attribute changes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when permission to edit a resource implicitly permits changing more sensitive fields.
- **Why:** Operation-level access may be broader than access to particular attributes.

```php
$user->password = Hash::make($request->password);
```

After:
```php
Gate::authorize("edit-passwords"); $user->password = Hash::make($request->password);
```

#### Validate deployment configuration
- **Do:** Check required configuration values before promoting a deployment.
- **Flag when:** Flag when missing or malformed required secrets are first detected by live requests.
- **Why:** Deployment checks catch broken integrations before serving traffic.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Protect and plan encryption key changes
- **Do:** Keep APP_KEY secret and inventory encrypted data and sessions before rotating it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when key rotation discards the only key able to decrypt persisted values or leaks APP_KEY.
- **Why:** Application encryption depends on access to the correct keys.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Fill time-series gaps in database queries
- **Do:** Join aggregates to a complete date series when SQL-side gap filling avoids application backfilling.
- **Flag when:** Flag when dashboard data requires repetitive application loops to synthesize missing dates.
- **Why:** A complete series gives consistent ordered buckets.

Before:
```php
foreach ($days as $day) { $counts[$day] ??= 0; }
```

After:
```php
// LEFT JOIN daily aggregates onto a generated date series supported by the database.
```

#### Group growing code by domain
- **Do:** Organize growing application code by business domain within framework folders.
- **Flag when:** Flag when large flat framework folders obscure domain ownership.
- **Why:** Domain grouping keeps related behavior discoverable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
app/Http/Controllers/CreateInvoiceController.php
```

After:
```php
app/Http/Controllers/Billing/CreateInvoiceController.php
```

#### Use middleware for shared HTTP concerns
- **Do:** Implement shared HTTP concerns such as locale, throttling and tenant resolution in middleware.
- **Flag when:** Flag when controllers duplicate the same request setup for these concerns.
- **Why:** Middleware provides one consistent execution boundary.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:


After:
