- **Do:** Use Carbon::setTestNow() and test time-travel helpers only in controlled test setup. Pass an explicit reference time or clock dependency when application behavior needs an alternate time.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production application code changes the global test clock to implement a business-time adjustment.
- **Why:** A process-global test clock can change unrelated operations and leak across long-lived requests or jobs.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Carbon::setTestNow($invoiceDate);
$calculator->calculate();
```

After:
```php
$calculator->calculate(asOf: $invoiceDate);
```

#### Use runtime state checks instead of test assertion APIs in production
- **Do:** Keep test assertion helpers such as Storage disk assert* calls inside tests. Use the normal runtime filesystem or service API and explicit application error handling for production decisions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when application runtime code depends on PHPUnit-backed assertion helpers to check storage or service state.
- **Why:** Testing helpers may require development-only dependencies and express test failures rather than application behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Storage::disk('private')->assertExists($path);
```

After:
```php
if (! Storage::disk('private')->exists($path)) {
    throw new MissingReport($path);
}
```

#### Set test configuration before resolving configuration-injected consumers
- **Do:** Apply configuration overrides before the first construction of controllers or services using #[Config] or equivalent construction-time configuration injection. If an instance already exists, reconstruct the relevant consumer deliberately.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a test changes config after constructing the consumer and expects its previously injected scalar value to change.
- **Why:** Construction-time injection captures the resolved value; later repository changes do not mutate existing arguments.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$service = app(PaymentService::class);
config(['payments.enabled' => false]);
```

After:
```php
config(['payments.enabled' => false]);
$service = app(PaymentService::class);
```

#### Keep exhaustive matrices at the lowest useful layer
- **Do:** Put exhaustive rule or component input matrices in focused tests and retain endpoint cases proving integration and user-visible errors.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the same full input matrix is repeated across unit and feature layers, or all endpoint wiring coverage is removed.
- **Why:** Distinct tests should catch distinct defects without duplicating expensive coverage.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Repeat 40 rule cases through both the rule and endpoint.
```

After:
```php
// 40 rule cases; one endpoint rejection and one valid request.
```

#### Make tests independent of order
- **Do:** Have each test arrange its mutable inputs and pass alone, in randomized order and in parallel.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a test reads records or values created by another test or depends on execution order.
- **Why:** Order dependence creates failures that vary with selection and scheduling.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$order = Order::findOrFail(1);
```

After:
```php
$order = Order::factory()->create();
```

#### Calculate expected results independently
- **Do:** Use literal expected results or a calculation independent of the implementation under test.
- **Flag when:** Flag when expected values are calculated by calling or duplicating the same production logic being tested.
- **Why:** A shared error in both calculations makes the test pass incorrectly.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
expect($invoice->total())->toBe($calculator->total($invoice));
```

After:
```php
expect($invoice->total())->toBe(1200);
```

#### Fail Pest browser tests on JavaScript errors
- **Do:** Assert no JavaScript errors in Pest browser tests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Pest browser test omits JavaScript-error checks.
- **Why:** Console errors can coexist with apparently correct rendering.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
visit("/checkout")->assertSee("Checkout");
```

After:
```php
visit("/checkout")->assertSee("Checkout")->assertNoJavaScriptErrors();
```

#### Separate browser tests from fast suites
- **Do:** Keep browser tests in a dedicated directory and run them separately from fast unit and feature tests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when normal fast-test runs start browsers because browser tests are mixed into the same unfilterable suite.
- **Why:** Separate selection preserves quick feedback and explicit browser coverage.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Browser case in tests/Feature/CheckoutTest.php
```

After:
```php
// Browser case in tests/Browser/CheckoutTest.php
```

#### Reset state in Pest browser tests
- **Do:** Use a supported database reset strategy such as RefreshDatabase for Pest browser tests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when real requests in Pest browser tests leave records for later cases.
- **Why:** Browser-driven writes must be isolated just like HTTP-test writes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
pest()->extend(Tests\TestCase::class)->in("Browser");
```

After:
```php
pest()->extend(Tests\TestCase::class)->use(Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\RefreshDatabase::class)->in("Browser");
```

#### Ignore generated browser screenshots
- **Do:** Ignore generated browser failure screenshots in version control while retaining intentional baseline fixtures.
- **Flag when:** Flag when transient browser screenshots are tracked alongside source.
- **Why:** Generated failure artifacts create noisy changes and may include test data.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
# .gitignore
```

After:
```php
# .gitignore
/tests/Browser/Screenshots/
```

#### Measure test effectiveness with mutation testing
- **Do:** Use mutation testing on important application logic and strengthen tests for meaningful surviving mutations.
- **Flag when:** Flag when critical code has high line coverage but tests do not fail when its decisions are mutated.
- **Why:** Mutation results reveal assertions that execute code without detecting defects.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Detect order dependence with randomized execution
- **Do:** Periodically run tests in randomized order and retain the seed for reproducing failures.
- **Flag when:** Flag when test independence is assumed without any varied-order check.
- **Why:** Random execution exposes hidden shared state.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Create fakes in the tests that need them
- **Do:** Declare per-test fakes inside each test so the affected boundary is visible.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a shared hook fakes side effects for tests that do not need that fake.
- **Why:** Broad setup can hide event-driven behavior in unrelated tests.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
beforeEach(fn () => Event::fake());
```

After:
```php
test("dispatches", function () { Event::fake([OrderPaid::class]); /* ... */ });
```

#### Create prerequisite records before broad event fakes
- **Do:** Create required factory records before broadly faking events; fake a factory event explicitly when that event is the subject.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Event::fake() prevents required model observers or identifier generation during fixture creation.
- **Why:** Factories may rely on model events to create valid records.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Event::fake(); $order = Order::factory()->create();
```

After:
```php
$order = Order::factory()->create();
Event::fake([OrderPaid::class]);
```

#### Disable external observability during tests
- **Do:** Disable request observability packages in the test environment unless they are the behavior under test.
- **Flag when:** Flag when ordinary tests boot Pulse, Telescope or external monitoring integrations unnecessarily.
- **Why:** Observability work adds runtime and may emit external test data.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<env name="TELESCOPE_ENABLED" value="true"/>
```

After:
```php
<env name="TELESCOPE_ENABLED" value="false"/>
```

#### Reuse test configuration and route caches safely
- **Do:** Use Laravel WithCachedConfig and WithCachedRoutes for compatible suites after measuring repeated bootstrap costs.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a costly suite repeatedly rebuilds unchanged configuration or route definitions without a compatibility reason.
- **Why:** Laravel 13 supports test-lifecycle caching; tests that alter boot-time configuration need special care.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class FeatureTest extends TestCase {}
```

After:
```php
class FeatureTest extends TestCase { use \Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\WithCachedConfig; use \Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\WithCachedRoutes; }
```

#### Split scenarios requiring different assertions
- **Do:** Write separate tests when cases need different setup, actions or assertions instead of branching inside a parameterized test.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a data-driven test uses if/switch to choose different behaviors or assertions.
- **Why:** Each specification should state one behavior clearly.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
if ($allowed) { $response->assertOk(); } else { $response->assertForbidden(); }
```

After:
```php
// Separate allowed-access and forbidden-access tests.
```

#### Assert escaping without brittle quote entities
- **Do:** Assert that malicious markup is inert without requiring one particular HTML quote entity in Markdown or inlined mail.
- **Flag when:** Flag when escaping tests fail solely because equivalent quote entities are normalized by renderers.
- **Why:** Equivalent safe HTML encodings can differ across the rendering pipeline.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
expect($html)->toContain("&#039;");
```

After:
```php
expect($html)->not->toContain("<script>");
```

#### Use synchronous concurrency only when sequencing is intended
- **Do:** Use the sync concurrency driver for deterministic tests or deliberately sequential execution.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production code expects parallel execution while configured to use sync.
- **Why:** The sync driver executes closures sequentially in the current process.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
CONCURRENCY_DRIVER=sync # production expecting parallel work
```

After:
```php
CONCURRENCY_DRIVER=process
```

#### Test flags across relevant scopes
- **Do:** Test feature flag definitions and enabled/disabled behavior for different users or scopes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when flagged functionality is tested only for one globally enabled state.
- **Why:** Scoped flags can leak access or select the wrong branch.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Only enabled-for-everyone case.
```

After:
```php
Feature::for($userA)->activate("checkout");
Feature::for($userB)->deactivate("checkout");
// assert both behaviors
```

#### Verify responsive and theme-dependent UI behavior
- **Do:** Check affected UI at supported breakpoints and in dark mode when used.
- **Flag when:** Flag when UI changes are verified at only one viewport or theme despite responsive/theme branches.
- **Why:** Layout and contrast failures often appear only at another viewport or theme.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Assert query budgets on critical paths
- **Do:** Add query-count expectations for critical paths vulnerable to N+1 regressions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a critical list/report path has no query budget and can scale queries per record.
- **Why:** Query counts catch hidden extra round trips despite correct response data.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Only response text is asserted.
```

After:
```php
$this->expectsDatabaseQueryCount(5);
$this->get("/orders")->assertOk();
```

#### Use reviewed snapshots for large stable outputs
- **Do:** Use snapshots for large stable outputs and review initial and updated baselines.
- **Flag when:** Flag when large output assertions are copied manually or snapshots are updated without reviewing the diff.
- **Why:** Reviewed baselines expose unexpected output changes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
expect($output)->not->toBeEmpty();
```

After:
```php
expect($output)->toMatchSnapshot(); // review baseline
```

#### Exercise middleware through real HTTP requests
- **Do:** Register a real test route with the required middleware and issue requests through the HTTP test client.
- **Flag when:** Flag when middleware tests disable the middleware or call handle() directly without checking routing integration.
- **Why:** HTTP coverage verifies registration, ordering, bindings and request behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$middleware->handle($request, fn () => response("ok"));
```

After:
```php
Route::get("/_test", fn () => "ok")->middleware(RequireAccount::class);
$this->get("/_test")->assertForbidden();
```

#### Use nonproduction integration credentials in tests
- **Do:** Use deliberate invalid credentials for faked integrations and sandbox credentials for dedicated live tests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when ordinary tests inherit usable production service credentials.
- **Why:** Invalid defaults prevent missing fakes from reaching live accounts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<env name="STRIPE_SECRET" value="sk_live_..."/>
```

After:
```php
<env name="STRIPE_SECRET" value="invalid-test-secret"/>
```

#### Follow a red-green-refactor cycle
- **Do:** When using TDD, observe a new behavior test fail before implementation, make it pass, then refactor with it passing.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a new TDD test has never been shown to fail when the behavior is absent.
- **Why:** The failing step checks that the test detects the missing behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Add test only after implementation and never verify failure.
```

After:
```php
// Run missing-route test: fails; implement route; run: passes; refactor.
```

#### Keep test namespaces in development autoloading
- **Do:** Declare Tests namespace mappings under Composer autoload-dev.
- **Flag when:** Flag when test namespaces or test support directories appear in production autoload mappings.
- **Why:** Development autoloading keeps test code out of normal production class discovery.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"autoload": {"psr-4": {"Tests\\": "tests/"}}
```

After:
```php
"autoload-dev": {"psr-4": {"Tests\\": "tests/"}}
```

#### Declare test environment configuration explicitly
- **Do:** Set test-only environment values in phpunit.xml or a dedicated .env.testing file.
- **Flag when:** Flag when tests rely on mutable developer .env values for database, queue or integration settings.
- **Why:** An explicit testing configuration makes local and CI execution reproducible.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<!-- Test environment inherits a developer database. -->
```

After:
```php
<php><env name="APP_ENV" value="testing"/><env name="QUEUE_CONNECTION" value="sync"/></php>
```

#### Exercise supported PHP versions in CI
- **Do:** Run the suite on the supported PHP version matrix, limited to versions compatible with Laravel 13.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the package or application claims multiple supported PHP versions but CI exercises only one.
- **Why:** Version-specific failures should be caught before a supported user encounters them.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Verify and close Mockery during teardown
- **Do:** Use Laravel test teardown or Mockery PHPUnit integration to verify and close mocks after each test.
- **Flag when:** Flag when standalone PHPUnit tests create Mockery doubles without Mockery integration or Mockery::close().
- **Why:** Closing Mockery verifies invocation expectations and clears global mock state.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class GatewayTest extends \PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase { /* Mockery mocks, no integration */ }
```

After:
```php
class GatewayTest extends \PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase { use \Mockery\Adapter\Phpunit\MockeryPHPUnitIntegration; }
```

#### Clear stale configuration before testing
- **Do:** Clear any previously built configuration cache before loading test environment overrides.
- **Flag when:** Flag when test setup changes environment variables while a stale non-test bootstrap/cache/config.php remains active.
- **Why:** Cached configuration can override the intended test database and service settings.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// CI restores a production config cache before tests.
```

After:
```php
// CI: php artisan config:clear, then php artisan test
```

#### Use named routes for internal navigation assertions
- **Do:** Generate internal navigation URLs and redirect expectations from route names.
- **Flag when:** Flag when internal navigation tests hard-code paths that are not intended as a public URL contract.
- **Why:** Named routes let internal paths change without duplicating URL strings across tests.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$response->assertRedirect("/dashboard");
```

After:
```php
$response->assertRedirect(route("dashboard"));
```

#### Test login outcomes and authentication state
- **Do:** Cover valid and invalid credentials, asserting redirects or API responses alongside authenticated or guest state.
- **Flag when:** Flag when login tests assert only a redirect or omit the rejected-credentials case.
- **Why:** A successful HTTP response alone does not establish that authentication state is correct.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$this->post("/login", $credentials)->assertRedirect();
```

After:
```php
$this->post("/login", $credentials)->assertRedirect(route("dashboard"));
$this->assertAuthenticated();
```

#### Advance the fake clock with simulated sleeping
- **Do:** Synchronize fake Sleep with Carbon when elapsed sleep time affects the behavior being tested.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a retry or expiry test fakes sleeping but expects now() to advance without configuring clock synchronization.
- **Why:** Elapsed-time logic must observe the same simulated duration as delay assertions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Sleep::fake(); // test also expects time to advance
```

After:
```php
Sleep::fake(syncWithCarbon: true);
```

#### Associate nonconventional factories with their model
- **Do:** Declare UseModel or the explicit model property when a factory cannot infer its model.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a nonconventionally named Factory subclass has no explicit model association.
- **Why:** Factory model inference must resolve the intended Eloquent class.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class LegacyAccountFactory extends Factory {}
```

After:
```php
#[UseModel(User::class)]
class LegacyAccountFactory extends Factory {}
```

#### Preserve parent test lifecycle hooks
- **Do:** Call parent::setUp() first and parent::tearDown() last when overriding Laravel test lifecycle methods.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Laravel test override skips the parent lifecycle or performs framework work before parent setup.
- **Why:** Laravel uses these hooks to boot and clean up application state.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
protected function setUp(): void { $this->user = User::factory()->create(); }
```

After:
```php
protected function setUp(): void { parent::setUp(); $this->user = User::factory()->create(); }
```

#### Supply request input through HTTP test helpers
- **Do:** Pass request payloads, headers and parameters through Laravel HTTP testing methods instead of mocking Request.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an HTTP behavior test mocks the Request facade to supply input.
- **Why:** Real request construction exercises input parsing and request integration.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Request::shouldReceive("input")->with("name")->andReturn("Ada");
```

After:
```php
$this->post("/profile", ["name" => "Ada"]);
```

#### Exercise Cashier application flows against Stripe test mode
- **Do:** Run dedicated Cashier integration tests against Stripe test mode instead of replacing Cashier internals with HTTP mocks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when application billing integration tests exclusively mock Stripe behavior and never exercise the real test API.
- **Why:** Stripe test-mode integration checks the application payment contract without reimplementing Cashier internals.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// All billing integration tests mock Stripe responses.
```

After:
```php
// Dedicated billing group uses Stripe test keys and asserts the application payment flow.
```

#### Share Faker generators across fixture creation
- **Do:** Use the shared fake() helper for fixtures relying on Faker uniqueness across factories and seeders.
- **Flag when:** Flag when independently constructed Faker instances each generate supposedly unique values into the same constrained dataset.
- **Why:** Faker uniqueness is tracked per generator instance.
- **Enforced by:** partial: rector:ReplaceFakerInstanceWithHelperRector

Before:
```php
$faker = Faker\Factory::create(); // separate generator in each helper
```

After:
```php
$email = fake()->unique()->safeEmail();
```

#### Expose a reachable sandbox webhook callback
- **Do:** Use a reachable development callback URL when testing provider webhooks locally.
- **Flag when:** Flag when local webhook integration uses an unreachable localhost URL at the provider.
- **Why:** The provider must reach the application to exercise real webhook handling.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep test-double behavior method-specific
- **Do:** Implement separate test-double behavior for unrelated methods rather than routing every method through one ambiguous callback.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a shared callback cannot distinguish unrelated collaborator methods and masks call-contract differences.
- **Why:** Method-specific doubles make expected interactions explicit.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Every fake method invokes the same undifferentiated callback.
```

After:
```php
$mock->shouldReceive("fetch")->andReturn($record);
$mock->shouldReceive("delete")->once()->with($record->id);
```

#### Defer request-dependent construction until request context is ready
- **Do:** Inject a factory into the controller and create request-dependent services inside the action.
- **Flag when:** Flag when controller construction instantiates services requiring middleware-populated request state before middleware runs.
- **Why:** Action-time construction sees the resolved authentication and request context.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function __construct(CurrentUserReport $report) {}
```

After:
```php
public function show(ReportFactory $factory) { return $factory->forUser(request()->user())->render(); }
```

#### Package substantial domain modules coherently
- **Do:** Organize a large modular application into Composer packages that own their domain models, routes, providers, configuration and tests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an application choosing package-based domain modules scatters each module implementation and tests across unrelated global directories.
- **Why:** Cohesive module ownership makes dependencies and test boundaries explicit.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// One domain scattered across global app folders.
```

After:
```php
// app-modules/Billing/{composer.json,src/,routes/,config/,tests/}
```

#### Track upcoming PHP compatibility without blocking stable jobs
- **Do:** Run experimental upcoming-PHP jobs as allowed failures while keeping supported PHP jobs required.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an advertised experimental PHP check blocks stable releases or upcoming compatibility is never exercised despite a stated policy.
- **Why:** An isolated experimental job provides early warning without changing the current support contract.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Simulate Octane request reset in lifecycle tests
- **Do:** Exercise simulated Octane requests through one booted worker using the Octane FakeWorker/FakeClient test harness or an equivalent worker harness. Assert that state changed in the first request is reset in the next request after the actual sandbox lifecycle runs.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an Octane reset test replaces the entire application with refreshApplication() or never processes a second request through the same worker, thereby bypassing the sandbox reset behavior.
- **Why:** Lifecycle tests must exercise the reset hook they claim to validate.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$this->refreshApplication();
// A new application cannot prove that Octane resets its existing worker correctly.
```

After:
```php
// In a harness defining createOctaneContext() as in Octane tests/TestCase.php:
[$app, $worker, $client] = $this->createOctaneContext([
    \Illuminate\Http\Request::create("/first", "GET"),
    \Illuminate\Http\Request::create("/second", "GET"),
]);
$app["config"]->set("octane.test", "original");
$app["router"]->get("/first", function (\Illuminate\Foundation\Application $app) { $app["config"]->set("octane.test", "changed"); return "ok"; });
$app["router"]->get("/second", fn (\Illuminate\Foundation\Application $app) => $app["config"]->get("octane.test"));
$worker->run();
$this->assertSame([], $client->errors);
$this->assertSame("original", $client->responses[1]->getContent());
```

#### Use a predictable package filesystem layout
- **Do:** Put package providers/source, config, migrations, factories, resources and routes in the established package skeleton locations.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a package following the standard skeleton stores equivalent artifact types in arbitrary undocumented locations.
- **Why:** A predictable layout helps tooling and maintainers locate package integration artifacts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Package artifacts scattered in unrelated directories.
```

After:
```php
// src/, config/, database/{migrations,factories}/, resources/{views,lang,dist}/, routes/
```

#### Keep Workbench fixtures development-only
- **Do:** Autoload Workbench application fixtures only through autoload-dev and exclude them from dist archives.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Workbench fixture models are production-autoloaded or shipped as package runtime code without need.
- **Why:** Development host fixtures should not become part of the package runtime surface.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"autoload": {"psr-4": {"Workbench\\App\\": "workbench/app/"}}
```

After:
```php
"autoload-dev": {"psr-4": {"Workbench\\App\\": "workbench/app/"}} // /workbench export-ignore
```

#### Use fail-fast model lookup for required resources
- **Do:** Use findOrFail() or equivalent required lookup when a missing model should return 404.
- **Flag when:** Flag when request code assumes find() cannot return null and uses an inline type assertion instead of handling absence.
- **Why:** Required lookups encode the missing-resource contract and remove invalid null assumptions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
/** @var User $user */
$user = User::find($id);
```

After:
```php
$user = User::findOrFail($id);
```

#### Test container binding types and promised lifetimes
- **Do:** Resolve public service contracts through the bootstrapped container and assert the promised implementation type and any singleton or scoped lifetime the integration guarantees.
- **Flag when:** Flag when contract mappings or lifetimes are part of a package integration contract but tests instantiate implementations directly and never exercise those bindings.
- **Why:** A correct implementation can still fail at runtime if a provider binds the wrong class or lifetime.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$client = new ApiClient();
$this->assertInstanceOf(ApiClient::class, $client);
```

After:
```php
$first = $this->app->make(ApiClientContract::class);
$this->assertInstanceOf(ApiClientContract::class, $first);
$this->assertSame($first, $this->app->make(ApiClientContract::class)); // Promised singleton.
```

#### Provide bounded execution modes for custom daemons
- **Do:** Give custom polling or ingestion commands a supported single-pass or stop-when-empty mode when tests or the scheduler need a bounded invocation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom daemon can only loop forever and tests or scheduled runs must kill the process to finish ordinary work.
- **Why:** A bounded mode makes the same command usable in controlled automation and deterministic tests.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
while (true) { $this->ingest(); Sleep::for(1)->second(); }
```

After:
```php
do { $this->ingest(); if (! $this->option('once')) { Sleep::for(1)->second(); } } while (! $this->option('once')); // Declare {--once} in the signature.
```

#### Use the model returned by creation
- **Do:** Keep and use the model returned by create()/save-oriented application operations; reload by its identity if needed instead of querying the globally latest record.
- **Flag when:** Flag when code creates a record and then uses latest()->first() or a similar unrelated ordering query to identify that newly created record.
- **Why:** Concurrent writes can make the latest row belong to another request or user.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
User::create($attributes);
$user = User::latest()->first();
Welcome::sendTo($user);
```

After:
```php
$user = User::create($attributes);
Welcome::sendTo($user);
```

#### Use focused request builders for complex validation scenarios
- **Do:** Use plain payload arrays for simple validation cases and a compatible reusable request builder when conditional fields make them repetitive. Give builders a minimal valid baseline, named scenario states and lazy related-model creation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when conditional-validation tests duplicate large payloads, eagerly create unused related records, or hide scenario differences in unrelated defaults.
- **Why:** Focused request builders expose the input variation while maintaining valid prerequisites.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Many tests copy a large request array and eagerly create relations each case may not need.
```

After:
```php
$payload = StoreMovieRequestFactory::new()->withDirector()->create();
// The project builder defines a minimal valid baseline and creates the director only when needed.
```

#### Assert job release, deletion and failure through the queue-interaction fake
- **Do:** For a job whose behavior includes releasing, deleting or failing itself, call withFakeQueueInteractions(), execute its handler and assert the intended interaction and contractual delay or exception.
- **Flag when:** Flag when job-control behavior is untested or requires a handwritten queue-job mock despite the supported interaction fake.
- **Why:** The interaction fake tests the job control decision without a live worker or fragile queue internals.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Custom mock of the queue job solely to observe release(30).
```

After:
```php
$job = (new ProcessOrder($order))->withFakeQueueInteractions();
$job->handle($service);
$job->assertReleased(delay: 30);
```

#### Put each entry of a multiline array on its own line
- **Do:** When an array spans multiple lines under the adopted coding standard, put each key/value entry on a separate line so keys and separators remain easy to inspect.
- **Flag when:** Flag when multiline factory or payload arrays pack several entries onto one line and obscure missing keys or separators.
- **Why:** One entry per line makes malformed definitions and small diffs easier to review.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$attributes = [
    'name' => $name, 'email' => $email,
];
```

After:
```php
$attributes = [
    'name' => $name,
    'email' => $email,
];
```

#### Exercise the intended route action and HTTP verb in feature tests
- **Do:** Send the HTTP method declared for the behavior under test and assert an outcome that distinguishes that action from other methods sharing its URI.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a store/update validation test sends GET to a shared resource URI and passes after reaching index/show instead.
- **Why:** A valid URI can resolve to the wrong action when the HTTP verb is wrong, producing false-positive coverage.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$this->get('/posts')->assertOk(); // Intended to test store validation.
```

After:
```php
$this->post('/posts', ['title' => ''])->assertInvalid(['title']);
```

#### Give PHPUnit an intentional reusable cache directory
- **Do:** Configure an ignored project-local PHPUnit cache directory for repeated analysis/coverage and result-cache work, retaining it between compatible runs when useful.
- **Flag when:** Flag when repeated expensive PHPUnit operations discard their reusable cache without a reason or write cache artifacts into tracked source.
- **Why:** A stable runner cache reduces repeated work while keeping generated state out of the repository.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Skip redundant tests for cosmetic edits
- **Do:** Do not require new automated tests for changes limited to copy, styling, or layout when no behavior changes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a cosmetic-only patch adds tests that merely repeat static markup or copy.
- **Why:** Such assertions add maintenance without protecting a behavioral decision.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
expect(file_get_contents($view))->toContain("New heading");
```

After:
```php
// Review the rendered heading and layout.
```

#### Use the installed testing stack
- **Do:** Use the project testing tools and introduce a dependency only when required for agreed coverage.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a test change adds a competing runner or browser dependency without a coverage need.
- **Why:** Avoiding redundant tooling reduces setup and maintenance.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Install another runner for an ordinary HTTP assertion.
```

After:
```php
$this->get("/orders")->assertOk();
```

#### Assert rejected operations have no effects
- **Do:** Assert failed operations leave records and contractual side effects unchanged.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a rejected write is tested only for its error response.
- **Why:** Failures must not partially persist data or dispatch work.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$response->assertUnprocessable();
```

After:
```php
$response->assertUnprocessable();
$this->assertDatabaseCount("orders", 0);
Queue::assertNothingPushed();
```

#### Balance and persist CI test shards
- **Do:** Use installed runner sharding, refresh runtime-based shard assignments and commit the assignment file when required by that runner.
- **Flag when:** Flag when CI shards duplicate work, use stale assignments or reference an uncommitted runtime allocation.
- **Why:** Balanced shards reduce the time spent waiting for the slowest job.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep conditional validation declarative
- **Do:** Express conditional rules with the simplest suitable conditional validation API.
- **Flag when:** Flag when conditional requirements are duplicated in controller branches or custom rules without need.
- **Why:** Declarative validation is easier to review and exercise through requests.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
if ($request->type === "company" && ! $request->tax_id) { /* custom error */ }
```

After:
```php
"tax_id" => "required_if:type,company",
```

#### Smoke-test simple GET routes with valid bindings
- **Do:** Cover simple GET routes with route-wide smoke tests, supplying bound models and authenticated users where required.
- **Flag when:** Flag when simple pages are untested or protected/bound routes are skipped rather than arranged.
- **Why:** Route-wide smoke coverage cheaply catches broken page wiring.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Skip all routes containing parameters.
```

After:
```php
// Route smoke test provides a user and bound models for protected routes.
```

#### Test job logic separately from dispatch
- **Do:** Assert dispatch with a queue fake and exercise the job business logic independently with real in-process dependencies.
- **Flag when:** Flag when queue fake assertions are the only test of job logic, or every dispatch test executes the job.
- **Why:** Dispatch wiring and job behavior are separate contracts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Queue::fake(); $service->submit(); // assumed to test handle()
```

After:
```php
// Dispatch test: Queue::assertPushed(ProcessOrder::class);
// Job test: (new ProcessOrder($order))->handle($dependency);
```

#### Prefer PHPUnit and Mockery for class-based unit suites
- **Do:** Choose PHPUnit with Mockery for new class-based unit suites when selecting that project convention.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a project choosing the PHPUnit convention introduces a competing Phpspec or Pest suite without an agreed reason.
- **Why:** A consistent class-based stack gives predictable discovery and Laravel integration. Pest is a valid alternative convention.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// A new specification suite duplicates the PHPUnit suite.
```

After:
```php
final class PriceTest extends \PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase { public function test_total(): void { $this->assertSame(10, Price::total(10)); } }
```

#### Test declared Laravel compatibility in CI
- **Do:** Test each advertised Laravel major with compatible dependency constraints, including Laravel 13 when supported.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a package advertises multiple Laravel majors but CI never installs or tests some of them.
- **Why:** A compatibility matrix verifies the contract declared in Composer constraints.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Enable class-based model factory discovery
- **Do:** Use HasFactory on models whose callers rely on Model::factory().
- **Flag when:** Flag when a model is used through Model::factory() without HasFactory or equivalent custom factory support.
- **Why:** The trait supplies the factory entry point and discovery behavior.
- **Enforced by:** rector:AddHasFactoryToModelsRector

Before:
```php
class Invoice extends Model {}
```

After:
```php
class Invoice extends Model { use HasFactory; }
```

#### Use canonical PHPUnit lifecycle signatures
- **Do:** Declare protected setUp(): void and tearDown(): void with canonical casing.
- **Flag when:** Flag when PHPUnit lifecycle overrides have incorrect casing, visibility or return types.
- **Why:** Matching the runner lifecycle contract prevents discovery and inheritance errors.
- **Enforced by:** pint:php_unit_set_up_tear_down_visibility, shift:workbench/fix-phpunit-methods

Before:
```php
public function setup() {}
```

After:
```php
protected function setUp(): void { parent::setUp(); }
```

#### Represent single selected children as one-of-many relationships
- **Do:** Use latestOfMany(), oldestOfMany() or ofMany() when a relationship selects one child from many.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a relationship loads all children just to select the latest or oldest one.
- **Why:** One-of-many relations express the selection in SQL and support eager loading.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return $this->orders->sortByDesc("id")->first();
```

After:
```php
return $this->hasOne(Order::class)->latestOfMany();
```

#### Exclude the Dusk provider from production
- **Do:** Register DuskServiceProvider only in local or testing environments when registering it manually.
- **Flag when:** Flag when DuskServiceProvider is registered unconditionally or in production.
- **Why:** Dusk authentication helpers must not be exposed in production.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$this->app->register(DuskServiceProvider::class);
```

After:
```php
if ($this->app->environment(["local", "testing"])) { $this->app->register(DuskServiceProvider::class); }
```

#### Use process-visible database resets for Dusk
- **Do:** Use DatabaseMigrations or DatabaseTruncation for Dusk tests instead of transactional RefreshDatabase.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Dusk uses RefreshDatabase transactions that the browser application connection cannot see.
- **Why:** Dusk requests run in a separate process and need committed fixtures and shared reset behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
use RefreshDatabase; // Dusk test
```

After:
```php
use DatabaseTruncation; // Dusk test
```

#### Reuse Dusk authentication helpers outside login-flow tests
- **Do:** Authenticate Dusk scenarios with loginAs() unless the login screen itself is under test.
- **Flag when:** Flag when unrelated browser tests repeat the full login interaction.
- **Why:** Direct authentication reduces repeated slow setup while login behavior stays separately covered.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$browser->visit("/login")->type("email", $user->email)->type("password", "password")->press("Login");
```

After:
```php
$browser->loginAs($user)->visit("/dashboard");
```

#### Encapsulate repeated browser page workflows
- **Do:** Put repeated page-specific action sequences in expressive Dusk Page methods.
- **Flag when:** Flag when multiple tests repeat a complicated sequence for the same page action.
- **Why:** A single page action implementation makes workflow changes easier to maintain.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Repeat visit, fill, select and submit in many tests.
```

After:
```php
$browser->on(new CheckoutPage)->completePurchase($card);
```

#### Verify Dusk page identity on navigation
- **Do:** Define page-identity assertions in a Dusk Page assert() method.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Page object is used without verifying that the browser reached the intended page.
- **Why:** Page identity assertions localize navigation failures before later interactions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function assert(Browser $browser): void {}
```

After:
```php
public function assert(Browser $browser): void { $browser->assertPathIs($this->url()); }
```

#### Centralize repeated Dusk selectors
- **Do:** Define repeated page selectors in elements() and truly shared selectors in base Page siteElements().
- **Flag when:** Flag when the same long selector is duplicated across page actions and browser tests.
- **Why:** Shared selector names reduce maintenance when markup changes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$browser->type("form.login input[name=email]", $email);
```

After:
```php
// Page elements(): ["@email" => "input[name=email]"]
$browser->type("@email", $email);
```

#### Encapsulate shared browser widgets in Dusk Components
- **Do:** Use Dusk Components for repeated interactive widgets that appear on multiple pages.
- **Flag when:** Flag when date-picker or navigation interactions are duplicated in Page classes for several URLs.
- **Why:** Components keep reusable widget logic independent of page routes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Duplicate date-picker clicks across page objects.
```

After:
```php
$browser->within(new DatePicker, fn ($picker) => $picker->selectDate($date));
```

#### Point browser tests at a reachable application server
- **Do:** Set APP_URL to the application server URL reachable by the browser process and start that server before tests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Dusk uses an unreachable host/port or begins before its configured application server is available.
- **Why:** Browser requests must reach the same application and testing environment that arranged fixtures.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Start compatible headless browser infrastructure in CI
- **Do:** Start the application server and compatible Chrome/ChromeDriver processes before Dusk in headless CI.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Dusk job starts without a compatible browser driver or app server.
- **Why:** Browser automation requires running and compatible browser infrastructure.
- **Enforced by:** partial: shift:ci-generator/dusk-job

#### Start ChromeDriver exactly once
- **Do:** Disable Dusk automatic ChromeDriver startup when CI starts ChromeDriver separately.
- **Flag when:** Flag when both DuskTestCase and CI launch ChromeDriver on the same port.
- **Why:** A single owner avoids port collisions and inconsistent browser driver processes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// CI starts ChromeDriver and DuskTestCase also calls startChromeDriver().
```

After:
```php
// Use one startup path; omit startChromeDriver() when CI owns it.
```

#### Start packages from a maintained skeleton when suitable
- **Do:** Use the maintained package skeleton when its testing, formatting and analysis conventions fit the package.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a new compatible package recreates equivalent bootstrap tooling with custom unmaintained scripts.
- **Why:** A maintained skeleton provides a consistent starting point for package checks.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// New package omits test/bootstrap and standard checks.
```

After:
```php
// Adopt compatible package-skeleton composer scripts and Testbench base case.
```

#### Keep test-only CI permissions read-only
- **Do:** Grant test-only GitHub Actions workflows read-only repository permissions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when test-only workflows receive write permissions without a step requiring them.
- **Why:** Read-only permissions limit the authority of test code and dependencies.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Bound CI test runtime
- **Do:** Set explicit timeouts on CI test jobs.
- **Flag when:** Flag when test jobs can hang until the platform maximum without an intentional timeout.
- **Why:** Timeouts contain stalled services and hung tests.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Test lowest and current supported dependencies
- **Do:** Run package tests against lowest-supported and current stable dependency sets.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a package declares broad constraints but tests only one locked dependency set.
- **Why:** Boundary dependency tests expose overly broad minimum versions and upgrade incompatibilities.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Test supported test-runner major versions
- **Do:** Run framework/tooling integration tests against each advertised PHPUnit major version.
- **Flag when:** Flag when framework testing support claims several PHPUnit majors but CI exercises only one.
- **Why:** Runner integration can break across major versions even when application behavior is unchanged.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Test supported operating-system behavior
- **Do:** Run platform-sensitive tests on Windows and Linux when both are supported.
- **Flag when:** Flag when supported filesystem, process or path behavior is validated only on one operating system.
- **Why:** Operating systems differ in paths, permissions and process handling.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Wait for integration service readiness
- **Do:** Require database-service health checks to pass before running integration tests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when CI starts database tests immediately after launching a service without a readiness check.
- **Why:** Container startup does not guarantee the database accepts connections.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Mark code references clearly in Pest descriptions
- **Do:** Put referenced symbols in backticks and include parentheses on method names in Pest descriptions when using this naming convention.
- **Flag when:** Flag when test descriptions name a method ambiguously as ordinary prose in a suite adopting code-symbol formatting.
- **Why:** Clear symbol references make test intent easier to scan.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
it("supports aspectRatio", function () { expect($image->aspectRatio())->toBe(1.0); });
```

After:
```php
it("supports `aspectRatio()`", function () { expect($image->aspectRatio())->toBe(1.0); });
```

#### Scope one-file Pest helpers locally
- **Do:** Use local closures for helpers needed by a single Pest file and namespaced support functions for genuinely shared helpers.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Pest file declares a global helper function that can collide with another test file.
- **Why:** Local scope avoids global PHP function-name collisions and hidden cross-file dependencies.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
function userData() { return ["name" => "Ada"]; }
```

After:
```php
$userData = fn () => ["name" => "Ada"];
it("stores a user", function () use ($userData) { /* ... */ });
```

#### Keep Pest behavior declarations before local fixtures
- **Do:** Place local fixture class declarations after Pest test declarations when following this file convention.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Pest test file leads with substantial fixture declarations that hide its behavior tests.
- **Why:** Tests are easier to scan when behavior precedes support implementation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class LocalGateway {}
it("charges", function () {});
```

After:
```php
it("charges", function () {});
class LocalGateway {}
```

#### Enforce foreign keys in SQLite tests
- **Do:** Enable foreign_key_constraints on SQLite test connections that are intended to enforce referential integrity.
- **Flag when:** Flag when SQLite tests disable foreign keys while production relies on foreign-key constraints.
- **Why:** Disabled constraints can let invalid fixtures and writes pass tests.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"foreign_key_constraints" => false,
```

After:
```php
"foreign_key_constraints" => true,
```

#### Verify Inertia page components exist
- **Do:** Keep inertia.testing.ensure_pages_exist enabled for component assertions, and configure inertia.pages.paths and inertia.pages.extensions to match the real Inertia 3 page resolver and Laravel 13 starter-kit page directory.
- **Flag when:** Flag disabled test page-existence checks, obsolete testing.page_paths/testing.page_extensions configuration, or page paths whose directory or case does not match the actual resolver.
- **Why:** A component name alone does not establish that the frontend page can load.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Legacy Inertia test configuration / directory
'ensure_pages_exist' => false, // testing block
// page paths still point to resources/js/Pages
```

After:
```php
// config/inertia.php (Inertia 3)
'pages' => [
    'paths' => [resource_path('js/pages')],
    'extensions' => ['js', 'jsx', 'svelte', 'ts', 'tsx', 'vue'],
],
'testing' => ['ensure_pages_exist' => true],
```

#### Schedule dependency compatibility test runs
- **Do:** Run package tests on a regular CI schedule as well as on changes to detect upstream dependency breakage.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a package with floating supported dependencies is tested only when its own code changes.
- **Why:** Upstream releases can break dependency resolution and runtime behavior without a local commit.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Test action logic and entrypoint wiring separately
- **Do:** Test an action handle() business behavior with real dependencies and verify each supported entrypoint delegates correctly.
- **Flag when:** Flag when only entrypoint dispatch is tested while action business behavior is mocked in every case.
- **Why:** Two-layer coverage protects both reusable logic and HTTP/job/listener wiring.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Mock the action in every test.
```

After:
```php
// Direct handle() behavior tests plus route/job/listener delegation tests.
```

#### Enable full PHP error reporting in CI
- **Do:** Run test jobs with error_reporting=E_ALL.
- **Flag when:** Flag when CI suppresses PHP notices or deprecations through a reduced error_reporting mask.
- **Why:** Full reporting exposes compatibility problems that suppressed diagnostics conceal.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use a reproducible Testbench workbench application
- **Do:** Define package development migrations, seeders and build steps in testbench.yaml and use Workbench for application-level checks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when package development requires a separately hand-configured Laravel install with undocumented setup.
- **Why:** A versioned workbench makes the host-app context reproducible.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Manual external Laravel checkout with untracked setup.
```

After:
```php
// Commit testbench.yaml and workbench routes/models; build with testbench workbench:build.
```

#### Keep supported package code portable across operating systems
- **Do:** Use portable path, process and permission handling for packages supporting Windows and Unix.
- **Flag when:** Flag when supported package paths or commands hard-code Unix separators, chmod assumptions or shell syntax without platform handling.
- **Why:** Portable abstractions prevent OS-specific runtime and test failures.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$path = $base . "/cache/file"; // code also depends on Unix shell semantics
```

After:
```php
$path = join(DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR, [$base, "cache", "file"]);
```

#### Test package configuration override precedence
- **Do:** Assert package defaults are merged and host application overrides take precedence.
- **Flag when:** Flag when provider tests never distinguish missing defaults from explicit host overrides.
- **Why:** Configuration merging must preserve host intent while supplying absent defaults.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Assert only that config exists.
```

After:
```php
config(["package.mode" => "custom"]);
expect(config("package.mode"))->toBe("custom"); // also assert a missing key gets its default
```

#### Install test runners as development dependencies
- **Do:** Put Pest and testing-only plugins in Composer require-dev.
- **Flag when:** Flag when test-only runner dependencies are shipped as required production dependencies.
- **Why:** Test tooling is unnecessary in runtime installs.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"require": {"pestphp/pest": "^4.0"}
```

After:
```php
"require-dev": {"pestphp/pest": "^4.0"}
```

#### Discover colocated Livewire tests explicitly
- **Do:** Include colocated Livewire *.test.php files in Pest bindings and PHPUnit test-suite discovery.
- **Flag when:** Flag when colocated tests exist but no configured test directory or suffix discovers them.
- **Why:** Undiscovered tests silently provide no regression coverage.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// phpunit.xml searches only tests/.
```

After:
```php
<testsuite name="Components"><directory suffix=".test.php">resources/views</directory></testsuite>
```

#### Declare module namespace ownership in Composer
- **Do:** Give each nwidart module explicit production PSR-4 mappings for app, factory and seeder namespaces and development mappings for tests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a module namespace depends on incidental root autoloading or ships test mappings in production autoload.
- **Why:** Explicit module maps keep discovery reliable and test classes development-only.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Module has no namespace map.
```

After:
```php
"autoload": {"psr-4": {"Modules\\Billing\\": "app/"}}, "autoload-dev": {"psr-4": {"Modules\\Billing\\Tests\\": "tests/"}}
```

#### Include enabled modules in coverage source paths
- **Do:** Refresh PHPUnit coverage source configuration when modules are added or enabled.
- **Flag when:** Flag when coverage reports exclude application directories belonging to enabled modules.
- **Why:** Omitted source makes overall coverage appear better while hiding module gaps.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<source><include><directory>app</directory></include></source>
```

After:
```php
<!-- Run module:update-phpunit-coverage; include enabled module app directories. -->
```

#### Exclude unavailable optional-integration tests per CI leg
- **Do:** Group optional-integration tests and exclude them only from matrix entries where the dependency cannot be installed.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a matrix job fails solely because an optional dependency is unavailable, or optional tests are excluded everywhere.
- **Why:** Selective exclusions retain core compatibility checks while exercising integrations in supported jobs.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use persistent cache stores for production caching
- **Do:** Use a persistent cache store for deployed behavior that relies on cross-request caching.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production caching uses the array store and silently discards cached entries between requests.
- **Why:** The array store is useful for isolation but cannot provide cross-request caching.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
CACHE_STORE=array # production
```

After:
```php
CACHE_STORE=redis
```

#### Rehearse backup restoration and decryption
- **Do:** Regularly restore and, when applicable, decrypt backup archives using the documented recovery procedure.
- **Flag when:** Flag when backup monitoring checks archive creation without any successful restore rehearsal.
- **Why:** A backup is useful only if its data and keys can be restored in practice.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Test the migration schema consumers actually install
- **Do:** Use the package published migration stub when validating installed database behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag when integration tests recreate a hand-written schema that can drift from the distributed migration.
- **Why:** Testing the installed artifact catches migration and fixture-schema divergence.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Schema::create("package_rows", fn ($t) => $t->id()); // duplicate schema
```

After:
```php
// Publish/load and run the package migration stub in the test host.
```

#### Version shared tool defaults and ignore local overrides
- **Do:** Commit .dist tool configurations and ignore machine-specific override files when using an override convention.
- **Flag when:** Flag when local phpunit.xml/phpstan.neon overrides are committed over shared .dist defaults.
- **Why:** Shared defaults remain reproducible while developers retain local configuration.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Commit each developer phpunit.xml override.
```

After:
```php
// Commit phpunit.xml.dist; .gitignore: /phpunit.xml
```

#### Autoload distributed package factories explicitly
- **Do:** Map package factory namespaces to database/factories in Composer PSR-4 autoloading.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a package ships consumer-facing factories without an autoload mapping for their namespace.
- **Why:** Consumer installs must resolve factories without the package test autoloader.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Distributed factory namespace exists only in autoload-dev.
```

After:
```php
"autoload": {"psr-4": {"Acme\\Package\\Database\\Factories\\": "database/factories/"}}
```

#### Create only required host tables in isolated package tests
- **Do:** Build minimal host-application fixture tables in Testbench when they are not the package migration being validated.
- **Flag when:** Flag when isolated package tests require unrelated application migrations merely to create a small host fixture.
- **Why:** Minimal host schemas keep tests independent of a particular application; package migration tests still use the installed schema.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Load a full unrelated application migration tree.
```

After:
```php
Schema::create("users", function (Blueprint $table) { $table->id(); $table->string("email"); });
```

#### Associate model factories explicitly for static analysis
- **Do:** Declare the concrete factory class on models when the project prefers explicit factory association for analysis.
- **Flag when:** Flag when model factory return types remain ambiguous because the factory association is only inferred by naming.
- **Why:** Explicit association improves discovery and analyzer precision.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class User extends Model { use HasFactory; }
```

After:
```php
class User extends Model { /** @use HasFactory<UserFactory> */ use HasFactory; protected static string $factory = UserFactory::class; }
```

#### Restore test-owned external state
- **Do:** Clean up files, provider resources and other test-owned external state in afterEach/teardown hooks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a test leaves external resources that affect later runs or users.
- **Why:** Database rollback does not clean non-database resources.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Test creates remote object without cleanup.
```

After:
```php
afterEach(function () { $this->sandboxClient->delete($this->createdObjectId); });
```

#### Treat assertion-free tests as risky by default
- **Do:** Keep assertion-free tests risky and declare intentional no-assertion cases explicitly.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a test performs no assertion or mock expectation and the suite suppresses risky-test reporting globally.
- **Why:** A green test should verify a contract unless lack of assertions is deliberate and documented.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function test_service(): void { $service->run(); }
```

After:
```php
public function test_service(): void { $this->assertSame("done", $service->run()); }
```

#### Provision required PHP extensions before tests
- **Do:** Install required package and integration-test PHP extensions before executing CI tests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a required test extension is absent and relevant tests fail or silently skip.
- **Why:** A complete runtime makes test execution representative of the supported environment.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use notification channels for notification-like integrations
- **Do:** Represent notification-like outgoing integrations through Laravel notification channels when shared delivery and fake support fit the behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a notification-like integration duplicates delivery orchestration and cannot use notification testing boundaries.
- **Why:** Channels reuse recipient routing and Laravel notification fakes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Controller manually posts a delivery message through an ad hoc client.
```

After:
```php
$user->notify(new BuildCompleted($build)); // custom channel performs external delivery
```

#### Define first-party PHPUnit source paths
- **Do:** Include maintained first-party directories in PHPUnit source configuration for correct issue attribution.
- **Flag when:** Flag when PHPUnit cannot distinguish application/package diagnostics from dependency diagnostics because source paths are missing or wrong.
- **Why:** Correct attribution enables useful deprecation and warning policies.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<source><include><directory>vendor</directory></include></source>
```

After:
```php
<source><include><directory>src</directory></include></source>
```

#### Enforce an adopted work-in-progress deployment guard before release changes
- **Do:** If the release policy excludes work-in-progress commits, check FORGE_DEPLOY_MESSAGE at the beginning of the Forge deployment script and exit nonzero on the configured WIP marker before changing the running release.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a deployment claiming to reject WIP commits checks its marker only after release changes, or continues after the rejection condition.
- **Why:** An early explicit deployment guard prevents a commit excluded by the release policy from reaching the live release.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Isolate the measured layer in load-test experiments
- **Do:** When attributing a capacity bottleneck, establish a controlled baseline for the layer being measured before adding other dependencies. Separate compute-only from database-backed scenarios and internal-network measurements from public end-to-end traffic.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a benchmark attributes degradation to compute without controlling database or network contributions.
- **Why:** Changing one source of cost at a time makes the cause of degraded throughput identifiable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Validate branch changes in independent full-stack previews
- **Do:** When using deployment previews, provision a branch or pull-request environment with the application, database, cache and workers needed by the changed flow, keeping its mutable resources separate from production, and use it for review before promotion.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a preview cannot exercise its required background/backend behavior or writes to production resources.
- **Why:** A complete independent preview reveals integration problems while allowing reviewers to exercise the proposed change.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Bind every framework-dependent Pest directory to the Laravel test case
- **Do:** When adding or moving a Pest test directory, include it in tests/Pest.php bindings for the application TestCase and any compatible database-reset trait needed by those tests, and ensure the runner discovers it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a newly discovered framework test executes without Laravel bootstrapping or required database isolation because its directory was omitted from Pest bindings.
- **Why:** Test discovery and Pest base-case/trait bindings are separate configuration steps.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
pest()->extend(Tests\TestCase::class)
    ->use(Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\RefreshDatabase::class)
    ->in('Feature', 'StarterKit');
```

#### Round-trip queued job payloads in serialization-sensitive tests
- **Do:** Enable serializeAndRestore() on Queue or Bus fakes in tests intended to detect job serialization problems, then assert the restored job payload and dispatch behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a serialization-sensitive regression passes only because the fake retains the original in-memory job object.
- **Why:** A fake that skips serialization can miss failures encountered by a real asynchronous queue.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
Queue::fake()->serializeAndRestore();
ProcessOrder::dispatch($order);
Queue::assertPushed(ProcessOrder::class, fn ($job) => $job->order->is($order));
```

#### Separate queued notification intent from worker execution
- **Do:** Use Notification::fake() to assert notification recipients and payloads, verify ShouldQueue when queueing is a promised class contract, and test worker middleware or delivery execution separately because the notification fake bypasses that work.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a notification fake assertion is treated as proof that queue middleware or actual delivery ran.
- **Why:** Notification delivery intent and queued execution are different contracts with different test boundaries.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
Notification::fake();
$user->notify(new OrderReady($order));
Notification::assertSentTo($user, OrderReady::class);
$this->assertInstanceOf(ShouldQueue::class, new OrderReady($order));
```

#### Submit real file fixtures as test-mode uploads
- **Do:** When an upload test needs the actual bytes or format of an existing fixture, construct UploadedFile with that fixture and test mode enabled instead of replacing it with an unrelated generated fake.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a content-sensitive upload regression uses dummy bytes that cannot exercise the reported file behavior.
- **Why:** A real fixture preserves the relevant file content while test mode permits a file that did not arrive through PHP HTTP upload handling.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
$file = new UploadedFile(base_path('tests/Fixtures/report.pdf'), 'report.pdf', test: true);
$this->post('/reports', ['file' => $file])->assertSuccessful();
```

#### Use an in-memory mail transport when real message execution is the subject
- **Do:** Use the array mail transport for tests requiring actual message construction, MessageSent events or generated message IDs. Use Mail::fake() for delivery-intent assertions and never expect that fake to execute the real transport or message-sent lifecycle.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Mail::fake() test waits for MessageSent or inspects a sent message that the fake never constructs/transmits.
- **Why:** An in-memory transport runs the mail pipeline without sending email to an external recipient.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
config(['mail.default' => 'array']);
// Resolve/send the mailable and inspect MessageSent or the array transport messages.
```

#### Inspect the live browser state at a failing test step
- **Do:** When a browser test fails and the cause is unclear, reproduce it locally in headed/debug mode and pause immediately before the failure to inspect the actual page, selectors and navigation state.
- **Flag when:** Flag when repeated speculative selector or timing changes are made without inspecting the failing browser state.
- **Why:** Observing the rendered page distinguishes missing state, wrong selectors and navigation timing from test assumptions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
visit('/checkout')->debug()->assertSee('Payment complete'); // Temporary local diagnostic.
```

#### Migrate PHPUnit XML configuration with the installed runner
- **Do:** When upgrading PHPUnit or Pest and the runner reports a deprecated XML schema, run the installed runner configuration migration, review the resulting settings and commit the updated configuration.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an upgraded runner continues to use a deprecated schema or an XML rewrite silently drops required paths and failure policies.
- **Why:** Version-compatible configuration preserves discovery and validation behavior as the runner evolves.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Explain domain-specific expectation failures
- **Do:** Give custom domain expectations a failure message that names the failed contract and useful expected/actual context rather than exposing only a generic boolean assertion failure.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a reusable domain expectation fails with only false-is-true output and no indication of the violated condition.
- **Why:** Actionable failure messages make custom assertions easier to diagnose without reading their implementation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$this->assertTrue($matchesExpectedState);
```

After:
```php
$this->assertTrue($matchesExpectedState, 'Expected order to be paid after settlement.');
```

#### Assert status and content as distinct facts
- **Do:** Assert each contract fact once and retain both response status and content checks where both matter.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a response test checks only content that could appear on an error page, or repeats identical assertions.
- **Why:** Content checks alone can pass on incorrect response statuses.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$this->get("/orders")->assertSee("Orders");
```

After:
```php
$this->get("/orders")->assertOk()->assertSee("Orders");
```

#### Test tenant isolation
- **Do:** Request another tenant, team or organization record and assert access is rejected without changing it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when tenant-scoped endpoints have no tests using a record owned by a different tenant.
- **Why:** Cross-tenant fixtures reveal missing ownership scopes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Test only the current tenant.
```

After:
```php
$this->actingAs($tenantAUser)->getJson("/orders/{$tenantBOrder->id}")->assertNotFound();
```

#### Test route and scope rejection
- **Do:** Test invalid route constraints and scoped bindings with real fixture records.
- **Flag when:** Flag when routes with constrained or nested bindings lack rejection cases.
- **Why:** Binding and scope mistakes can expose records outside the requested resource hierarchy.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Only /teams/1/orders/1 is tested.
```

After:
```php
$this->getJson("/teams/{$teamA->id}/orders/{$teamBOrder->id}")->assertNotFound();
```

#### Assert concealed cross-tenant existence
- **Do:** Return and test a 404 for cross-tenant resources when the security contract conceals their existence.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a resource-concealing tenant boundary returns or tests a revealing 403 response.
- **Why:** A consistent not-found contract avoids confirming another tenant owns the identifier.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
abort(403);
```

After:
```php
abort(404);
```

#### Assert browser and persisted state
- **Do:** Assert both visible results and saved database state for browser interactions that write data.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a browser write test only checks a toast or page text.
- **Why:** Visible success does not prove the intended record was saved.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$browser->press("Save")->assertSee("Saved");
```

After:
```php
$browser->press("Save")->assertSee("Saved");
$this->assertDatabaseHas("orders", ["reference" => "A1"]);
```

#### Disable global sleep and exception-reporting side effects
- **Do:** Configure suite-wide fake sleeping and exception reporting for suites that must never wait or send error reports externally.
- **Flag when:** Flag when ordinary tests perform real sleeps or send external exception reports.
- **Why:** A baseline fake prevents incidental latency and external reporting across the suite.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
protected function setUp(): void { parent::setUp(); }
```

After:
```php
protected function setUp(): void { parent::setUp(); Sleep::fake(syncWithCarbon: true); Exceptions::fake(); }
```

#### Protect schema-coupled queries with integration tests
- **Do:** Test complex joins and raw SQL that embed table or column names.
- **Flag when:** Flag when schema-coupled queries have no database-backed coverage.
- **Why:** Renames and engine differences can break explicit SQL despite valid PHP types.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
DB::select("select users.id from users join teams on ..."); // untested
```

After:
```php
// Integration test executes the query with related records and asserts the result.
```

#### Test interactive UI states
- **Do:** Exercise interactive component states separately from initial rendering.
- **Flag when:** Flag when UI tests cover static markup but omit opening, loading, errors or other interactive states.
- **Why:** A component can render correctly while its interactions fail.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
visit("/checkout")->assertSee("Pay");
```

After:
```php
visit("/checkout")->click("Pay")->assertSee("Confirm payment");
```

#### Protect behavior before restructuring
- **Do:** Establish tests for important workflows before reorganizing their implementation and make small verified changes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a broad refactor changes untested business flows.
- **Why:** Behavioral coverage distinguishes intended restructuring from regressions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Move checkout logic before any behavior tests.
```

After:
```php
// Add checkout feature coverage, then move logic with tests passing.
```

#### Keep a schema dump for alternate test connections
- **Do:** Generate a schema dump for the testing connection when it differs from the normal connection and schema dumps are used.
- **Flag when:** Flag when tests rebuild old migrations because only another connection has a schema dump.
- **Why:** Connection-specific dumps provide the correct fast bootstrap.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Limit private-state reflection to unavoidable integration seams
- **Do:** Use public contracts in tests and document temporary private-state access to third-party internals while seeking a supported API.
- **Flag when:** Flag when ordinary application behavior tests use reflection to invoke private methods or inspect internal state.
- **Why:** Private-state coupling makes harmless refactors break tests.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$value = invade($service)->privateValue;
```

After:
```php
expect($service->publicResult())->toBe($expected);
```

#### Keep maintained branches passing
- **Do:** Require passing suites on main and maintained long-lived branches.
- **Flag when:** Flag when maintained branches tolerate persistent test failures.
- **Why:** Broken baselines conceal new regressions and obstruct merges.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Evaluate Laravel-dependent skip conditions after boot
- **Do:** Wrap skip conditions that access config or Laravel services in a closure evaluated after application boot.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Pest skip condition calls config() while the test file is being loaded.
- **Why:** The container may not be ready during test discovery.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
test("provider", $test)->skip(! config("services.api.key"));
```

After:
```php
test("provider", $test)->skip(fn () => ! config("services.api.key"));
```

#### Use strict closures for null or typed view data
- **Do:** Use assertViewHas callbacks with strict comparisons for null or type-sensitive values.
- **Flag when:** Flag when assertViewHas(key, null) is used to require null or loose equality hides a wrong type.
- **Why:** A null expected argument checks key presence rather than requiring a null value.
- **Enforced by:** partial: pint:strict_comparison

Before:
```php
$response->assertViewHas("status", null);
```

After:
```php
$response->assertViewHas("status", fn ($value) => $value === null);
```

#### Investigate flaky timing failures
- **Do:** Find the missing synchronization or isolation condition before adding sleeps or retries to a failing test.
- **Flag when:** Flag when fixed sleeps or whole-test retries are added solely to conceal intermittent failures.
- **Why:** Delay-based patches leave the underlying race unresolved.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$browser->pause(5000); // fix intermittent failure
```

After:
```php
$browser->waitForText("Ready");
```

#### Track and complete deferred tests
- **Do:** Track intentionally deferred test cases and complete them before treating the affected behavior as covered.
- **Flag when:** Flag when todo or skipped placeholders remain while a feature is reported fully tested.
- **Why:** A placeholder does not provide regression protection.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Test cached bootstrap behavior
- **Do:** Run relevant integration tests with route/view caching and assert parity with uncached behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag when deployment uses cached routes/views that are never exercised in CI.
- **Why:** Caching can expose serialization and registration bugs absent from development.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep cohesive multi-request scenarios together
- **Do:** Use multiple requests in one test when the comparison itself is the contract, such as pagination defaults and custom page sizes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a cohesive multi-request comparison is split so the shared contract becomes obscured.
- **Why:** Some behavior is naturally expressed as a controlled comparison across requests.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Unrelated setup obscures pagination comparison.
```

After:
```php
$this->getJson("/orders")->assertJsonCount(15, "data");
$this->getJson("/orders?per_page=5")->assertJsonCount(5, "data");
```

#### Capture nonproduction mail safely
- **Do:** Route development and staging mail to an isolated mail sink or safe recipient policy.
- **Flag when:** Flag when nonproduction mail configuration can deliver to real user addresses.
- **Why:** Testing workflows should not contact actual customers.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Restrict access to nonproduction sites
- **Do:** Protect staging/testing sites and debugging tools with explicit authentication or network access controls.
- **Flag when:** Flag when QA sites or Telescope are publicly accessible without an access boundary.
- **Why:** Nonproduction environments often expose diagnostic data and test-only behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use deliberate Faker locales
- **Do:** Set Faker locale explicitly for region-sensitive fixture behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag when locale-sensitive assertions rely on the machine default Faker locale.
- **Why:** Representative regional values expose formatting assumptions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
