```php
"faker_locale" => "en_US",
```

After:
```php
"faker_locale" => env("APP_FAKER_LOCALE", "nl_NL"),
```

#### Select AI models by cost or capability when flexibility is intended
- **Do:** Use UseCheapestModel or UseSmartestModel for agents whose requirements permit provider model selection to change.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an intentionally flexible agent duplicates SDK model rankings in hard-coded names.
- **Why:** Selection attributes express cost or capability intent, but upgrades may change the chosen model.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
#[Model("hard-coded-model")]
```

After:
```php
#[UseCheapestModel]
```

#### Debounce jobs whose latest dispatch supersedes earlier work
- **Do:** Apply DebounceFor and a stable debounceId when repeated dispatches should execute only the latest job.
- **Flag when:** Flag when bursts of equivalent replaceable jobs perform every intermediate update.
- **Why:** Debouncing coalesces work while preserving the latest intended state.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class RefreshSearchIndex implements ShouldQueue { /* every dispatch executes */ }
```

After:
```php
#[DebounceFor(10)]
class RefreshSearchIndex implements ShouldQueue { public function debounceId(): string { return "index:{$this->documentId}"; } }
```

#### Anchor trusted-host patterns
- **Do:** Anchor trustHosts patterns to the complete intended hostname.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a trusted-host regex can match unintended leading or trailing hostname text.
- **Why:** Hostname entries are regular expressions and partial matches can trust attacker-controlled hosts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$middleware->trustHosts(at: ["laravel.test"]);
```

After:
```php
$middleware->trustHosts(at: ["^laravel\.test$"]);
```

#### Order by related values inside the database
- **Do:** Use a scalar subquery or equivalent SQL ordering when sorting models by related data.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a large result set is fully loaded and sorted in PHP by a related value before pagination.
- **Why:** Database ordering preserves correct pagination and avoids unnecessary hydration.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$flights = Flight::all()->sortByDesc(fn ($f) => $f->arrivals->max("arrived_at"));
```

After:
```php
$flights = Flight::orderByDesc(Arrival::select("arrived_at")->whereColumn("flight_id", "flights.id")->latest("arrived_at")->limit(1))->paginate();
```

#### Provision a coverage driver for coverage jobs
- **Do:** Install and enable Xdebug or PCOV in jobs that collect PHP code coverage.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a coverage job runs without a supported enabled coverage driver.
- **Why:** The runner cannot produce meaningful coverage without a driver.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Open the Laravel server when testing application pages
- **Do:** Visit the application server URL rather than the Vite asset server URL.
- **Flag when:** Flag when browser validation opens the Vite development server as if it served Laravel routes.
- **Why:** Vite serves frontend assets; the Laravel server handles application routing and sessions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Browser visits http://localhost:5173/dashboard.
```

After:
```php
// Browser visits the Laravel APP_URL/dashboard.
```

#### Use action spies when real behavior must execute
- **Do:** Use an action spy or allowToRun() when the test needs the actual action result plus an invocation assertion.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a strict action mock suppresses business behavior the test is supposed to exercise.
- **Why:** Spies preserve execution while recording the orchestration contract.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Action::shouldRun()->andReturn(null); // real effect is needed
```

After:
```php
Action::spy(); // or allowToRun(), then assert invocation after real execution
```

#### Co-locate feature tests when using feature modules
- **Do:** Place feature-specific unit and browser tests beside their owning package feature when following that layout.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a package using colocated feature tests stores new feature tests in unrelated distant folders.
- **Why:** Colocation keeps implementation and verification under the same feature ownership.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// src/Features/SupportUpload plus distant ungrouped test files.
```

After:
```php
// src/Features/SupportUpload/{UnitTest.php,BrowserTest.php}
```

#### Migrate Volt classes when adopting Livewire 4 built-in components
- **Do:** Replace class-based Volt usage with supported Livewire 4 component forms and remove obsolete Volt registration when migrating.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Livewire 4 migration retains unnecessary class-based Volt dependencies and provider registration.
- **Why:** Built-in component support avoids a redundant integration layer after migration.
- **Enforced by:** partial: shift:livewire-4/volt-to-sfc

Before:
```php
// Legacy class-based Volt component and VoltServiceProvider.
```

After:
```php
// Livewire\Component single-file component; route via Route::livewire().
```

#### Scope PHPUnit notices and warnings to first-party source deliberately
- **Do:** Configure first-party source paths and restrict notice/warning reporting when the project intentionally excludes vendor diagnostics.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a package intends first-party diagnostics but misattributes its source or suppresses it with an overbroad scope.
- **Why:** Correct source attribution keeps project diagnostics actionable; notice/warning restriction does not itself filter deprecations.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<source><include><directory>vendor</directory></include></source>
```

After:
```php
<source restrictNotices="true" restrictWarnings="true"><include><directory>src</directory></include></source>
```

#### Use macros for framework extension when suitable
- **Do:** Register supported framework macros in the package provider instead of replacing framework classes solely to add utility methods.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a package subclasses/rebinds a macroable framework class just to add stateless helper methods.
- **Why:** Macros extend supported surfaces without forcing consumers to adopt replacement classes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class PackageCollection extends Collection { public function custom() {} }
```

After:
```php
Collection::macro("custom", function () { /* ... */ });
```

#### Register package providers for analysis bootstrap
- **Do:** Declare required package providers in testbench.yaml so Larastan can resolve package views and services.
- **Flag when:** Flag when analysis fails to resolve vendor-namespaced views because the package provider is absent from its test application.
- **Why:** Analysis needs the same provider registrations that supply runtime package resources.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// testbench.yaml omits the package provider.
```

After:
```php
providers:
  - Acme\Package\PackageServiceProvider
```

#### Match Rector upgrade rules to installed framework versions
- **Do:** Use Composer-aware Rector configuration for Laravel and related packages.
- **Flag when:** Flag when upgrade rules target versions inconsistent with composer.json constraints.
- **Why:** Version-aware transformations avoid introducing APIs unavailable to the installed dependency set.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Manually selected Laravel upgrade set drifts from Composer.
```

After:
```php
return RectorConfig::configure()->withComposerBased(laravel: true);
```

#### Type-hint dispatched-object assertion predicates
- **Do:** Type-hint the event/job argument of dispatch assertion closures.
- **Flag when:** Flag when dispatch predicate closures use untyped payloads despite a known event or job class.
- **Why:** Typed predicates preserve static checking and make the asserted dispatch type explicit.
- **Enforced by:** partial: rector:AssertWithClassStringToTypeHintedClosureRector

Before:
```php
Event::assertDispatched(OrderCreated::class, fn ($event) => $event->orderId === $id);
```

After:
```php
Event::assertDispatched(fn (OrderCreated $event) => $event->orderId === $id);
```

#### Resolve fixture datasets after per-test setup
- **Do:** Use bound dataset closures for fixture data that needs Laravel or per-test setup.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a dataset creates database records during discovery before the application or database reset is ready.
- **Why:** Delayed dataset resolution aligns fixture creation with the active test lifecycle.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
dataset("users", [User::factory()->create()]);
```

After:
```php
dataset("users", [fn () => User::factory()->create()]);
```

#### Require passing validation before production deployment
- **Do:** Gate production deployment on passing application tests and agreed formatting checks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a production deployment proceeds after required validation failed or never ran.
- **Why:** Deployment gates prevent known regressions and invalid changes from being released.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Migrate to Pest incrementally
- **Do:** Retain working PHPUnit tests while introducing Pest incrementally.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Pest adoption rewrites or deletes functioning PHPUnit coverage without a behavior need.
- **Why:** Pest can coexist with PHPUnit, allowing migration without losing regression protection.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Remove PHPUnit suite before equivalent Pest coverage exists.
```

After:
```php
// Keep existing TestCase classes and add new Pest tests under the agreed convention.
```

#### Load-test representative traffic and runtime configurations
- **Do:** Run representative concurrent load tests before accepting capacity assumptions or runtime changes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when capacity claims rely only on functional tests or a single-request benchmark.
- **Why:** Traffic bursts can expose throughput and contention limits absent from isolated checks.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Fix new analysis errors instead of hiding them
- **Do:** Resolve new PHPStan errors rather than regenerating a baseline or adding untrue inline assertions to suppress them.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a change expands the baseline or adds a false @var/@phpstan-assert solely to hide a new error.
- **Why:** False suppressions remove static evidence without correcting the defect.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
/** @var User $user */
$user = User::find($id);
```

After:
```php
$user = User::findOrFail($id);
```

### Validation

#### Write multi-rule validation as arrays
- **Do:** Express each field ruleset as an array of individual rules, especially when adding rule objects or regex patterns.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a multi-rule field uses a pipe-delimited string, particularly a regex containing a literal pipe or a field that needs a rule object.
- **Why:** Arrays compose with objects and closures and avoid splitting regex alternation at pipe delimiters. They also make individual constraints easier to review.
- **Enforced by:** partial: rector:ValidationRuleArrayStringValueToArrayRector, partial: shift:workbench/adopt-validation-arrays

Before:
```php
'name' => 'required|string|max:255'
```

After:
```php
'name' => ['required', 'string', 'max:255']
```

#### Extract complex or reusable validation into Form Requests
- **Do:** Move substantial or reusable request rules into a Form Request and type-hint that class on the controller action.
- **Flag when:** Flag when large or repeated controller rulesets remain inline, or an extracted Form Request is constructed manually instead of being injected.
- **Why:** Form Requests run validation before the action and give substantial input logic a reusable home. Simple single-use rulesets can follow the project's inline convention.
- **Enforced by:** partial: shift:workbench/convert-controller-validation

Before:
```php
public function update(Request $request) { $data = $request->validate($largeRuleset); }
```

After:
```php
public function update(UpdateOrderRequest $request) { $order->update($request->validated()); }
```

#### Normalize accepted input before applying validation rules
- **Do:** Put intentional input normalization in prepareForValidation() or the input adapter's equivalent before validating the normalized value.
- **Flag when:** Flag when input is normalized only after format rules have rejected an accepted user representation, or controllers repeat normalization before each ruleset.
- **Why:** Preparing a canonical value gives validation and downstream code the same representation. Normalize only variants that the product intends to accept.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$data = $request->validated();
$data['slug'] = Str::slug($data['slug']);
```

After:
```php
protected function prepareForValidation(): void {
    $this->merge(['slug' => Str::slug((string) $this->input('slug'))]);
}
```

#### Use validated interactive console prompts
- **Do:** Use Laravel Prompts with clear labels, placeholders and validation for interactive command input.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an interactive command accepts arbitrary input from raw reads without field feedback or validation.
- **Why:** Validated prompts help users correct command input before side effects begin.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$name = trim(fgets(STDIN));
```

After:
```php
$name = \Laravel\Prompts\text(label: 'Project name', placeholder: 'acme', required: true, validate: ['max:80']);
```

#### Use a Form Request for each meaningful input action
- **Do:** Extract controller input validation and request authorization into an operation-specific Form Request and inject it into the action.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a controller action accepts meaningful input and defines validation inline instead of using a dedicated Form Request under this convention.
- **Why:** A Form Request gives each action a named input boundary and keeps controllers focused on orchestration. This is the stricter architectural alternative to allowing small inline rulesets.
- **Enforced by:** partial: shift:workbench/convert-controller-validation

Before:
```php
public function store(Request $request) { $data = $request->validate($rules); }
```

After:
```php
public function store(StorePostRequest $request) { Post::create($request->validated()); }
```

#### Make validation messages actionable
- **Do:** Customize validation messages to identify the correction and include valid examples or choices where useful, including MCP and upload clients.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom validation failures return generic messages such as invalid input without telling the client how to correct the field.
- **Why:** Actionable messages help users and automated clients recover without guessing the accepted input.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'format.in' => 'Invalid format.'
```

After:
```php
'format.in' => 'Choose csv or json, for example csv.'
```

#### Keep HTTP boundary classes in conventional directories
- **Do:** Keep controllers, middleware and Form Requests in their conventional app/Http subdirectories, with Form Requests in app/Http/Requests and App\Http\Requests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when HTTP classes are scattered outside their conventional app/Http directories without a deliberate project convention.
- **Why:** Conventional placement makes input boundary classes predictable for framework generators and contributors.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
namespace App;
class StorePostRequest extends FormRequest {}
```

After:
```php
namespace App\Http\Requests;
class StorePostRequest extends FormRequest {}
```

#### Run cross-field and application-state checks after base validation
- **Do:** Put checks that require completed field validation in FormRequest::after() or Validator::after(), returning callables that add field errors.
- **Flag when:** Flag when cross-field or application-state validation is embedded in controller flow or runs before base rules establish usable values.
- **Why:** The after hook keeps dependent validation with the input contract and reports failures through Laravel's normal error machinery. Guard invalid prerequisite fields before using their values.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
if (! $this->shippingAvailable()) { abort(422); }
```

After:
```php
public function after(): array {
    return [function ($validator) {
        if (! $validator->errors()->has('postcode') && ! $this->shippingAvailable()) {
            $validator->errors()->add('postcode', 'Delivery is unavailable here.');
        }
    }];
}
```

#### Choose consistent ownership for validation messages
- **Do:** Keep shared messages and attribute names in language files and request-specific ones in their request methods according to a documented convention.
- **Flag when:** Flag when equivalent custom messages or attribute names are duplicated across language files and Form Requests with conflicting text.
- **Why:** Clear ownership prevents drift and makes localization easier to maintain.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Same email label differs across multiple requests.
public function attributes(): array { return ['email' => 'Email']; }
```

After:
```php
// lang/en/validation.php
'attributes' => ['email' => 'email address'],
```

#### Group related cache entries with tags
- **Do:** Tag related cached entries and invalidate the affected tag group when the configured store supports tags.
- **Flag when:** Flag when related cache entries are individually tracked or globally flushed despite a tag-capable store and a shared invalidation boundary.
- **Why:** Tags express a group invalidation boundary without maintaining a separate list of keys.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Cache::flush();
```

After:
```php
Cache::tags(['posts'])->flush();
```

#### Isolate multiple forms with named validation error bags
- **Do:** Give forms sharing a page separate named error bags and render errors from the matching bag.
- **Flag when:** Flag when forms sharing fields such as email read the default bag and show each other’s failures.
- **Why:** Named bags preserve which form failed even when field names overlap.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
@error('email') {{ $message }} @enderror
```

After:
```php
// LoginRequest uses #[ErrorBag('login')]
@error('email', 'login') {{ $message }} @enderror
```

#### Use readable field and value labels in validation messages
- **Do:** Configure human-friendly attribute names and displayed values for raw identifiers used in validation messages.
- **Flag when:** Flag when messages expose internal field names or encoded values that users cannot interpret.
- **Why:** Readable labels explain the rejected value without requiring knowledge of implementation names.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Error refers to payment_type and cc.
```

After:
```php
// lang/en/validation.php
'attributes' => ['payment_type' => 'payment method'],
'values' => ['payment_type' => ['cc' => 'credit card']],
```

#### Keep custom rule objects in the conventional rules directory
- **Do:** Place custom ValidationRule classes in app/Rules unless the project has an explicit alternative convention.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom rule classes are scattered across unrelated directories without a documented layout.
- **Why:** A predictable location makes validation behavior discoverable and follows make:rule generation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
namespace App\Misc;
class AllowedDomain implements ValidationRule { /* ... */ }
```

After:
```php
namespace App\Rules;
class AllowedDomain implements ValidationRule { /* ... */ }
```

#### Display per-field validation errors in Blade
- **Do:** Render each field's validation error next to its input with @error and associate the message with that input.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Blade form accepts validated input but does not display the corresponding field errors near its controls.
- **Why:** Field-local feedback makes correction clear and avoids forcing users to match a generic error list to the form.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<input name="email">
```

After:
```php
<input name="email" aria-describedby="email-error">
@error('email')<p id="email-error">{{ $message }}</p>@enderror
```

#### Use fluent rule builders for complex parameterized constraints
- **Do:** Prefer supported fluent Rule builders for complex parameterized constraints; express a date after tomorrow as Rule::date()->after('tomorrow').
- **Flag when:** Flag complex parameter strings with clearer supported fluent equivalents and calls to nonexistent conveniences such as Rule::date()->afterTomorrow().
- **Why:** Named methods reduce delimiter and parameter-order errors and expose the available options in an editor.
- **Enforced by:** partial: shift:workbench/convert-validation-rules

Before:
```php
'starts_at' => ['date', 'after:tomorrow']
```

After:
```php
'starts_at' => [Rule::date()->after('tomorrow')]
```

#### Set explicit HTTP cache policy on reusable generated responses
- **Do:** Send Cache-Control with suitable browser, shared-cache and stale-while-revalidate lifetimes for frequently requested cacheable generated responses.
- **Flag when:** Flag when expensive public generated responses have no explicit cache policy despite permitting response reuse.
- **Why:** Explicit lifetimes let browsers and CDNs reuse responses within the intended freshness budget.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Migrate Form Request behavior properties to Laravel 13 attributes
- **Do:** When adopting Laravel 13 attributes, migrate redirect and error-bag values to their matching attributes and migrate stopOnFirstFailure=true to the parameterless StopOnFirstFailure marker; preserve any explicit false override needed for inheritance.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an attribute migration changes redirect/error-bag values, loses an explicit false override, or incorrectly passes a boolean to the parameterless StopOnFirstFailure attribute.
- **Why:** Attribute migrations must preserve behavior; the legacy properties remain supported. StopOnFirstFailure is a marker that enables global stopping, not a boolean-valued attribute.
- **Enforced by:** partial: rector:ErrorBagPropertyToErrorBagAttributeRector, partial: rector:StopOnFirstFailurePropertyToStopOnFirstFailureAttributeRector

Before:
```php
protected $errorBag = 'login';
protected $stopOnFirstFailure = true;
```

After:
```php
#[\Illuminate\Foundation\Http\Attributes\ErrorBag('login')]
#[\Illuminate\Foundation\Http\Attributes\StopOnFirstFailure]
class LoginRequest extends FormRequest {}
```

#### Avoid ambiguous validation syntax in input field names
- **Do:** Prefer validated field names without literal asterisks or pipe characters, especially when generating wildcard paths or cross-field rule references. Adapt external keys at an explicit boundary when they would conflict with rule syntax.
- **Flag when:** Flag literal asterisks that are unintentionally treated as wildcard patterns, or pipe-bearing field references embedded in pipe-delimited rule strings.
- **Why:** These characters participate in validation syntax and can create ambiguous paths or rule references. Simple literal-key validation can work, but does not establish that all wildcard and cross-field uses are unambiguous.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'contacts.*name' => ['required'] // intended literal key contains a wildcard
```

After:
```php
'contacts.name' => ['required'] // normalize external keys at the adapter boundary
```

#### Keep oversized-post rejection early and independent of session startup
- **Do:** Retain ValidatePostSize early in the global middleware stack. Render or recover from PostTooLargeException without assuming session middleware has run or that the discarded POST/files payload can be recovered.
- **Flag when:** Flag moving post-size validation behind session-dependent middleware, or an oversized-post error handler unconditionally accessing an unavailable request session.
- **Why:** PHP can discard oversized form/file data before Laravel handles it, and the early exception can occur before the session is attached.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Avoid validating a Form Request twice
- **Do:** Use the injected Form Request as the single source of its validation rules; consume its validated result in the controller.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a controller receiving a Form Request repeats its rules in validate() or Validator::make().
- **Why:** Laravel validates an injected Form Request before entering the action. Repeating those rules creates two versions of the same input contract.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$request->validate(['title' => ['required']]); // already in StorePostRequest
```

After:
```php
$post = Post::create($request->validated());
```

#### Follow the surrounding validation syntax
- **Do:** Use the established local rule syntax when extending an existing ruleset unless a rule object or delimiter makes a change necessary.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a new rule mixes string and array styles with adjacent equivalent fields without a technical reason.
- **Why:** Consistent local syntax reduces review noise and makes a ruleset easier to scan.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'name' => ['required', 'string'],
'email' => 'required|email'
```

After:
```php
'name' => ['required', 'string'],
'email' => ['required', 'email']
```

#### Use built-in rules before inventing custom validators
- **Do:** Use Laravel's existing rules where they express the contract and add a custom rule only for application-specific constraints.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom validation code reimplements an equivalent built-in rule without a deliberate behavioral difference.
- **Why:** Built-in rules avoid duplicated validation logic. Opinionated constraints such as forbidding HTML belong in a project-specific rule.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
new class implements ValidationRule { /* reimplements UUID validation */ }
```

After:
```php
'id' => ['required', 'uuid']
```

#### Keep one-off custom checks as closure rules
- **Do:** Use a closure with $fail for a small single-use custom check; extract it into a rule object when reused.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a trivial single-use rule is given an otherwise unused class, or the same closure logic is copied to multiple rulesets.
- **Why:** A closure keeps local checks readable while a rule object provides a stable home for repeated behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
new AllowedEmailDomainForThisOneForm
```

After:
```php
function (string $attribute, mixed $value, Closure $fail) {
    if (! str_ends_with($value, '@example.com')) { $fail('Use your company email.'); }
}
```

#### Show Inertia field errors beside their inputs
- **Do:** Render each field's server validation message beside the corresponding Inertia input using the form errors object.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an Inertia form receives errors but omits field feedback or displays errors next to unrelated inputs.
- **Why:** Nearby messages help users identify and correct the rejected field. Inertia already supplies the server-side errors.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<input v-model="form.email" />
```

After:
```php
<input v-model="form.email" />
<p v-if="form.errors.email">{{ form.errors.email }}</p>
```

#### Report business validation failures with ValidationException
- **Do:** Throw ValidationException::withMessages() for business input failures that should use Laravel's normal field-error response.
- **Flag when:** Flag when business validation failures use abort(422), ad hoc JSON or a generic exception that loses Laravel's validation error format.
- **Why:** ValidationException gives browser and JSON clients the expected field messages and response behavior. It keeps custom checks consistent with declarative rules.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
abort(422, 'Seats unavailable');
```

After:
```php
throw ValidationException::withMessages(['seats' => 'Choose fewer seats.']);
```

#### Verify email ownership separately from DNS validation
- **Do:** Require an ownership verification flow when email ownership matters, regardless of email:dns validation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an account or privileged workflow treats a passing MX lookup as proof that the user owns the mailbox.
- **Why:** A domain's mail records do not prove that a mailbox exists or that the submitting user controls it.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// email:dns passed, so mark verified.
$user->markEmailAsVerified();
```

After:
```php
// Send a verification challenge and mark verified only after it succeeds.
$user->sendEmailVerificationNotification();
```

#### Validate each wizard step before advancing
- **Do:** Validate every field in the current step, including untouched fields, and advance only after successful validation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a wizard advances on a click or successful validation of only touched fields while other visible fields are invalid.
- **Why:** Each transition preserves a valid intermediate state and prevents errors accumulating at final submission.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function next(): void { $this->nextStep(); }
```

After:
```php
public function next(): void {
    $this->validate($this->stepRules());
    $this->nextStep();
}
```

#### Extract substantial Livewire forms into form objects
- **Do:** Move crowded or reused Livewire form state and validation into a Livewire Form class.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a component mixes a substantial repeated form ruleset and field state with unrelated page behavior.
- **Why:** A form object groups the input contract and operations and can be reused across components.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class EditPost extends Component { public string $title = ''; /* many fields and rules */ }
```

After:
```php
class EditPost extends Component { public PostForm $form; }
class PostForm extends \Livewire\Form { /* fields, rules and form operations */ }
```

#### Validate two-factor codes as fixed-length strings
- **Do:** Validate a six-digit two-factor confirmation code as a six-character string so leading zeroes are preserved.
- **Flag when:** Flag when two-factor code input is cast to an integer or validated only as numeric, losing leading zeroes or accepting the wrong length.
- **Why:** One-time codes are identifiers with fixed length rather than arithmetic values.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'code' => ['required', 'integer']
```

After:
```php
'code' => ['required', 'string', 'size:6', 'regex:/\A[0-9]{6}\z/']
```

#### Merge trusted server values into validated data
- **Do:** Persist validated data plus server-derived fields (e.g. $request->safe()->merge([...])->all(), [...$request->validated(), 'user_id' => ...], or create through the owning relationship) instead of merging them into raw input and persisting the whole request.
- **Flag when:** Flag when server-derived ownership or metadata is merged into request input and the persisted payload then comes from unvalidated input ($request->all(), input(), except()) rather than validated()/safe().
- **Why:** Starting with validated input keeps arbitrary client keys outside the trusted payload.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$request->merge(['user_id' => auth()->id()]);
Post::create($request->all());
```

After:
```php
Post::create($request->safe()->merge(['user_id' => auth()->id()])->all());
```

#### Validate required acceptance explicitly
- **Do:** Use accepted or accepted_if for terms or consent fields that must represent affirmative acceptance.
- **Flag when:** Flag when required agreement fields use only required or boolean, accepting an explicitly false value.
- **Why:** Presence and boolean type do not prove the user accepted the agreement.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'terms' => ['required', 'boolean']
```

After:
```php
'terms' => ['accepted']
```

#### Reuse server rules for interactive validation through Precognition
- **Do:** On routes that serve Precognition live validation, add HandlePrecognitiveRequests and keep the rules in an injected Form Request, which is resolved before the skipped handler, so precognitive requests run the same server rules.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a route using HandlePrecognitiveRequests validates only inside the handler body (e.g. $request->validate() in the closure or controller method), so precognitive requests return 204 success without running any rules.
- **Why:** Precognition reuses the authoritative server contract, including state-dependent checks, without running the controller method.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::post('/posts', fn (Request $r) => $r->validate($rules));
```

After:
```php
Route::post('/posts', function (StorePostRequest $request) { /* persist */ })
    ->middleware(\Illuminate\Foundation\Http\Middleware\HandlePrecognitiveRequests::class);
```

#### Validate fields after meaningful input interactions
- **Do:** Update form data on change and trigger initial live validation on blur or completed change after the user has had time to enter a value.
- **Flag when:** Flag when initial field errors appear before the user can finish input or live validation uses stale state because form data was not updated first.
- **Why:** Completed-interaction validation provides timely feedback without immediately rejecting incomplete input.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<input onChange={() => form.validate('email')} />
```

After:
```php
<input onChange={e => form.setData('email', e.target.value)} onBlur={() => form.validate('email')} />
```

#### Invalidate session data when logging out
- **Do:** Invalidate the session after Auth::logout(), and use invalidate() rather than only ID regeneration when the operation must discard existing session data.
- **Flag when:** Flag when logout leaves session data intact or a full-reset operation only regenerates the session identifier.
- **Why:** Invalidation clears the old state as well as rotating the identifier.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Auth::logout();
$request->session()->regenerate();
```

After:
```php
Auth::logout();
$request->session()->invalidate();
```

#### Protect signed routes with signature middleware
- **Do:** Attach signed middleware to routes whose signed URL is an access precondition.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a signed URL points to a handler that omits signature middleware or inconsistently reimplements the check.
- **Why:** The middleware rejects invalid signatures before handler execution.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::get('/invite/{id}', $handler);
```

After:
```php
Route::get('/invite/{id}', $handler)->middleware('signed');
```

#### Fail Fortify authentication callbacks explicitly
- **Do:** Return null or false when a Fortify authenticateUsing callback rejects credentials; return a user only after successful verification.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a callback returns a user on a failed password check or a truthy non-user failure value.
- **Why:** Fortify relies on the callback result to distinguish rejected credentials from an authenticated user.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return $user; // password not checked
```

After:
```php
return $user && Hash::check($request->password, $user->password) ? $user : null;
```

#### Reconcile abandoned Fortify two-factor setup before rendering settings
- **Do:** Use Fortify's InteractsWithTwoFactorState on the authenticated, session-backed settings Form Request and call ensureStateIsValid() before reading two-factor status when the feature is enabled.
- **Flag when:** Flag two-factor settings handlers that read pending setup state without running the Fortify reconciliation flow, leaving abandoned unconfirmed setup state behind.
- **Why:** Fortify tracks setup and confirmation across requests. Its reconciliation handles abandoned setup while preserving the state needed for an active confirmation retry.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$props['twoFactorEnabled'] = $request->user()->hasEnabledTwoFactorAuthentication();
```

After:
```php
// TwoFactorAuthenticationRequest uses \Laravel\Fortify\InteractsWithTwoFactorState.
if (Features::canManageTwoFactorAuthentication()) {
    $request->ensureStateIsValid();
    $props['twoFactorEnabled'] = $request->user()->hasEnabledTwoFactorAuthentication();
}
```

#### Keep authoritative validation on the server and client feedback lightweight
- **Do:** Keep domain validation and translated failure messages authoritative on the server. Render returned field errors in Inertia or map API 422 errors to the corresponding fields; use simple matching browser constraints for immediate feedback instead of independently maintaining a second full ruleset.
- **Flag when:** Flag separately maintained full browser/mobile validation policies that drift from server rules, or a client that ignores returned field errors and forces users to infer what failed.
- **Why:** Thin client feedback helps users correct input while the server remains the reusable enforcement boundary for every client.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Independently maintain all business rules and translations in PHP and each client.
```

After:
```php
// Render errors.email from the server; use a matching required/type=email hint for immediate browser feedback.
```

#### Validate backed-enum input with its enum type
- **Do:** Use Rule::enum(YourBackedEnum::class) for primitive input represented by a PHP backed enum.
- **Flag when:** Flag when validation duplicates a backed enum's values in an in rule or accepts any string for an enum field.
- **Why:** Using the enum as the accepted value source prevents validation from drifting when cases change.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'status' => ['in:draft,published']
```

After:
```php
'status' => [Rule::enum(PostStatus::class)]
```

#### Share repeated profile validation rules
- **Do:** Extract common profile constraints into a reusable concern or rule provider and pass the authenticated user's identity when excluding the current record.
- **Flag when:** Flag when registration and profile-update rules drift, or unique profile checks ignore an ID supplied by the client.
- **Why:** Shared constraints keep the same profile contract across entry points. A trusted current-user ID prevents excluding an arbitrary record.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Rule::unique('users')->ignore($this->input('id'))
```

After:
```php
$rules = $this->profileRules($this->user()->id);
```

#### Use an explicit consistent request-access convention
- **Do:** Use the project's explicit accessor convention and validated()/safe() for validated writes, avoiding ambiguous property access.
- **Flag when:** Flag when controllers mix dynamic request properties with input() and validated() in equivalent code paths without a deliberate convention.
- **Why:** Explicit accessors make the origin and validation status of values easier to review.
- **Enforced by:** partial: shift:workbench/normalize-request-access

Before:
```php
Post::create(['title' => $request->title]);
```

After:
```php
Post::create($request->safe()->only(['title']));
```

#### Allow null explicitly on nullable typed fields
- **Do:** Combine nullable with the field's type rule when null is an accepted value.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an optional typed field rejects null values produced by empty-string normalization even though null is allowed by the contract.
- **Why:** Optional presence and null acceptance are different concerns. Nullable lets a present null bypass non-implicit type checks.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'nickname' => ['string']
```

After:
```php
'nickname' => ['nullable', 'string', 'max:80']
```

#### Validate optional update fields only when present
- **Do:** Use sometimes for fields that may be omitted but must meet constraints if supplied, adding required when empty values must fail.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a partial-update contract requires an omitted field or silently accepts empty supplied values contrary to the contract.
- **Why:** Sometimes controls whether the rules apply; required still controls whether a supplied value may be empty.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'email' => ['required', 'email'] // partial update
```

After:
```php
'email' => ['sometimes', 'required', 'email']
```

#### Keep simple Livewire rules beside their properties
- **Do:** Declare simple static rules using Validate attributes beside the form properties they constrain.
- **Flag when:** Flag when simple static rules are scattered away from their properties without a project convention or dynamic rule requirement.
- **Why:** Adjacent declarations make a field and its input contract easier to review together.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public string $title = '';
protected function rules(): array { return ['title' => 'required|min:3']; }
```

After:
```php
#[\Livewire\Attributes\Validate('required|min:3')]
public string $title = '';
```

#### Validate Livewire state again at final submission
- **Do:** Call validate() in a Livewire submitting action before persistence even when properties have Validate attributes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a save action trusts real-time property validation and persists without validating the entire submitted state.
- **Why:** Untouched properties may never have triggered real-time validation. Final validation checks the complete form.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function save(): void { Post::create(['title' => $this->title]); }
```

After:
```php
public function save(): void { Post::create($this->validate()); }
```

#### Import the Validator facade explicitly
- **Do:** Import Illuminate\Support\Facades\Validator at call sites instead of depending on the global alias.
- **Flag when:** Flag when application PHP relies on an unimported global Validator alias.
- **Why:** An explicit import makes the dependency visible to readers and static tooling.
- **Enforced by:** rector:RenameClassRector

Before:
```php
\Validator::make($data, $rules);
```

After:
```php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Validator;
Validator::make($data, $rules);
```

#### Localize validation messages including custom rules
- **Do:** Supply translated validation messages for supported locales and translate custom-rule keys through the validator-provided fail()->translate() API.
- **Flag when:** Flag when new rules have missing locale entries or custom rules embed literal messages or translate through the global translator despite a validator-specific translator.
- **Why:** Complete locale entries keep errors understandable; the validator translator preserves its configured locale and message source.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$fail(__('validation.company'));
```

After:
```php
$fail('validation.company')->translate();
// lang/en/validation.php includes the company message.
```

#### Preserve Inertia parent shared props
- **Do:** Include parent::share($request) when overriding HandleInertiaRequests::share().
- **Flag when:** Flag when the override returns only application props and drops the parent-provided validation errors prop.
- **Why:** Parent shared props carry the validation errors consumed by Inertia forms.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return ['user' => $request->user()];
```

After:
```php
return [...parent::share($request), 'user' => $request->user()];
```

#### Keep client validation semantics aligned with server rules
- **Do:** Use matching field constraints and string-length semantics in client and server validation, including multibyte input.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the same input passes one layer and fails the other because limits, requiredness or string-length measurement differ.
- **Why:** Conflicting validators create misleading feedback and unnecessary failed submissions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Server min:2; client value.length >= 2 counts UTF-16 code units.
```

After:
```php
// Server rules: 'name' => ['string', 'min:2']
const meetsMin = Array.from(value).length >= 2; // Unicode code points, matching mb_strlen
```

#### Check presence in the validated payload when branching on accepted fields
- **Do:** Use safe()->has()/missing() or an explicit key check on validated() when a branch depends on whether a field survived validation and exclusion, rather than testing the raw request.
- **Flag when:** Flag a persistence or business branch checking raw request presence even though that field may have been excluded or is outside the accepted input contract.
- **Why:** Raw presence does not prove a field is part of the validated payload; accepted-data checks keep branching aligned with the data being consumed.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
if ($request->has('discount')) { /* apply discount even if excluded */ }
```

After:
```php
if ($request->safe()->has('discount')) { $discount = $request->validated('discount'); }
```

#### Verify membership-rule comparison semantics against the input contract
- **Do:** For type-sensitive membership validation, check the actual scalar/array semantics of in, not_in, contains and doesnt_contain in the deployed Laravel version. Normalize intentionally or add an explicit typed/custom constraint when the built-in comparison does not match the contract.
- **Flag when:** Flag treating all membership validators as interchangeable strictness guarantees, particularly for numeric-looking strings or mixed-type arrays.
- **Why:** These rules use different comparison paths: scalar in uses strict string membership while contains and doesnt_contain do not share identical array comparison behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep small single-use validation inline
- **Do:** Keep a small endpoint-specific ruleset in $request->validate() when a separate class adds no reuse or clarity.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Form Request contains only a trivial single-use ruleset with no authorization or preparation and the project permits inline validation.
- **Why:** Inline validation keeps a simple input contract next to its only consumer. Extraction is useful when complexity or reuse justifies it.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function store(StoreLabelRequest $request) { Label::create($request->validated()); }
```

After:
```php
public function store(Request $request) {
    $data = $request->validate(['name' => ['required', 'string', 'max:80']]);
    Label::create($data);
}
```

#### Preserve form values after validation failure
- **Do:** Repopulate failed forms from old input and rely on Laravel's automatic input flashing, adding withInput() on custom validation redirects.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a validation redirect discards user input or form fields ignore old input on the next render.
- **Why:** Preserving entered values lets users correct only the invalid fields. The built-in validation flow already flashes old input.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<input name="title" value="">
```

After:
```php
<input name="title" value="{{ old('title', $post->title ?? '') }}">
```

#### Apply post-validation normalization in passedValidation
- **Do:** Use passedValidation() for transformations that must happen only after the original input passes validation, and pass the transformed value explicitly to its consumer.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a transformation intended to follow successful validation runs before rules or is scattered across controllers.
- **Why:** Separating pre-validation preparation from post-validation normalization preserves the intended input contract. Mutating request input does not by itself guarantee validated() returns the transformed value.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$this->merge(['name' => strtoupper($this->name)]); // before validating original text
```

After:
```php
protected function passedValidation(): void {
    $this->merge(['normalized_name' => mb_strtoupper($this->input('name'))]);
}
// Controller explicitly uses normalized_name after validation.
```

#### Name Form Requests after the operation and resource
- **Do:** Use operation-specific singular resource names such as StoreUserRequest and UpdateUserRequest.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Form Request names hide the operation or use generic names shared by unrelated input contracts.
- **Why:** A descriptive class name makes the request contract clear at the controller signature.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class UserValidation extends FormRequest {}
```

After:
```php
class UpdateUserRequest extends FormRequest {}
```

#### Give accepted fields substantive validation rules
- **Do:** Remove empty rulesets or add the actual constraints required for each field passed on as validated input.
- **Flag when:** Flag when rules contain a field mapped to an empty array or empty string and downstream code treats that value as checked.
- **Why:** Listing a field without constraints can make it look vetted without enforcing any input contract.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'amount' => []
```

After:
```php
'amount' => ['required', 'numeric', 'min:0']
```

#### Compose upload constraints with the File rule builder
- **Do:** Use Illuminate\Validation\Rules\File to compose file type, size and relevant image constraints in a readable ruleset.
- **Flag when:** Flag when complex upload constraints remain scattered across strings or handwritten checks where a File builder would express them together.
- **Why:** The builder keeps related file constraints together and makes size and image limits clear.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'report' => ['file', 'mimes:pdf', 'max:10240']
```

After:
```php
'report' => ['required', File::types(['pdf'])->max('10mb')]
```

#### Express file limits with the correct size units
- **Do:** Use kilobytes in raw file size/min/max rules or explicit unit suffixes with the File builder.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a file limit uses bytes as a raw rule number or an unlabelled value whose intended size disagrees with Laravel's kilobyte units.
- **Why:** Unit mistakes can allow files far larger than intended or reject normal uploads. Explicit builder units make limits easier to audit.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'photo' => ['file', 'max:2097152'] // intended 2 MB
```

After:
```php
'photo' => [File::image()->max('2mb')]
```

#### Keep SVG excluded from ordinary image uploads
- **Do:** Keep the default SVG exclusion in image rules unless the app has a deliberate safe handling policy for SVG content.
- **Flag when:** Flag when image:allow_svg or File::image(allowSvg: true) is enabled without corresponding SVG sanitization or safe serving controls.
- **Why:** SVG may carry active content. Laravel 13 excludes it by default because a generic image check is insufficient for safe browser rendering.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'avatar' => ['image:allow_svg']
```

After:
```php
'avatar' => [File::image()->max('2mb')]
```

#### Bind untrusted values in database and process calls
- **Do:** Validate user input and pass values through parameterized database queries and structured process arguments.
- **Flag when:** Flag when user data is interpolated into raw SQL or a command string, even if a preceding validator checks it.
- **Why:** Validation establishes acceptable values but is not an escaping mechanism. Binding keeps values separate from executable syntax.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
DB::select("select * from users where email = '{$email}'");
```

After:
```php
DB::select('select * from users where email = ?', [$email]);
```

#### Restrict URL input to supported schemes
- **Do:** Set an explicit URL scheme allowlist such as url:http,https when the application supports only those protocols.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a URL field used for HTTP links or requests uses an unrestricted url rule.
- **Why:** Syntactically valid URLs may use protocols the consuming code should not accept. Scheme constraints enforce the actual contract.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'website' => ['required', 'url']
```

After:
```php
'website' => ['required', 'url:http,https']
```

#### Require mandatory keys as well as rejecting unknown ones
- **Do:** Combine allowed-key checks with required_array_keys when specified keys must be present.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a structured array restricts permitted keys but omits required keys without a validation error.
- **Why:** Allowed-key rules and required-key rules enforce different parts of an array shape. Both are needed for a fixed required subset.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'options' => ['array:currency,locale']
```

After:
```php
'options' => ['array:currency,locale', 'required_array_keys:currency']
```

#### Choose field-level and global short-circuiting deliberately
- **Do:** Use bail to stop rules for one failing field; enable stopOnFirstFailure only when the whole validation flow should stop immediately.
- **Flag when:** Flag when global stopOnFirstFailure is used merely to avoid later rules on one field, unexpectedly suppressing errors for other fields.
- **Why:** The two controls have different scopes. Choosing the intended scope preserves useful feedback while avoiding dependent checks.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Validator::make($data, $rules)->stopOnFirstFailure()->validate(); // wanted per-field stop
```

After:
```php
Validator::make($data, ['email' => ['bail', 'required', 'email', 'unique:users']])->validate();
```

#### Choose additional email checks from actual requirements
- **Do:** Add explicit email validation styles for required DNS, strict RFC or spoofing checks instead of assuming the default email rule supplies them.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an email input requires MX existence or spoof protection but the rules use only the default email check.
- **Why:** Email syntax, DNS validity and spoof resistance are separate checks. Select only the additional guarantees the workflow needs.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'email' => ['required', 'email'] // requires MX checks
```

After:
```php
'email' => ['required', 'email:rfc,dns']
```

#### Exclude inapplicable fields from validated output
- **Do:** Use conditional exclude rules to omit fields that do not apply to the submitted mode or current actor.
- **Flag when:** Flag when inapplicable fields are validated and forwarded anyway, or consumers repeatedly remove them after validation.
- **Why:** Exclusion makes the validated result match the operation's active input shape. Use prohibition instead when supplying a value should itself be an error.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'appointment_date' => ['nullable', 'date']
```

After:
```php
'appointment_date' => ['exclude_unless:has_appointment,true', 'required', 'date']
```

#### Use valid preg_match patterns in regex rules
- **Do:** Include valid preg_match delimiters and options in regex and not_regex validation patterns.
- **Flag when:** Flag when regex or not_regex contains an undelimited or otherwise invalid PHP regex pattern.
- **Why:** Laravel passes these patterns to preg_match. Invalid patterns cause runtime failures instead of a reliable input check.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'code' => ['regex:^[A-Z]+$']
```

After:
```php
'code' => ['regex:/\A[A-Z]+\z/']
```

#### Write through the memoized store used for reads
- **Do:** Perform cache writes through the same Cache::memo() repository used for request-local reads.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a request memoizes a key and then writes only to its backing store before reading that key again.
- **Why:** The memoized repository invalidates its local value on writes; bypassing it can leave a stale value within the request.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$cache = Cache::memo();
$cache->get('count');
Cache::put('count', 2);
```

After:
```php
$cache = Cache::memo();
$cache->get('count');
$cache->put('count', 2);
```

#### Keep non-configuration PHP files outside config
- **Do:** Put validation definitions and support classes outside config/ and keep configuration files returning configuration arrays.
- **Flag when:** Flag when config/ contains support PHP files that cannot be loaded as configuration during config:cache.
- **Why:** Laravel loads configuration files while building its cache; unrelated PHP files can break that process.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// config/Rules.php
class Rules {}
```

After:
```php
// app/Validation/ConfigRules.php
namespace App\Validation;
class ConfigRules {}
```

#### Reuse shared rules across HTTP and Livewire adapters
- **Do:** Extract shared validation rules so Form Requests and Livewire components use the same policy with their own runtime context.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Livewire component copies an HTTP ruleset and fixes must be repeated in both places.
- **Why:** Sharing rules prevents drift. Preserve any dependencies, authorization and request preparation needed by each adapter.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
protected function rules(): array { return ['name' => ['required', 'max:80']]; } // copied
```

After:
```php
protected function rules(): array { return app(ProfileRules::class)->forUser(auth()->user()); }
```

#### Enable session authentication checks for other-device revocation
- **Do:** Apply auth.session middleware to the authenticated routes whose sessions must be invalidated by logoutOtherDevices().
- **Flag when:** Flag when logoutOtherDevices() is used but the affected authenticated routes omit AuthenticateSession middleware.
- **Why:** Other-device revocation depends on the middleware checking the session credential state on subsequent requests.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::middleware('auth')->group($routes);
```

After:
```php
Route::middleware(['auth', 'auth.session'])->group($routes);
```

#### Check Nginx templates before applying them
- **Do:** Validate custom Nginx template syntax before applying a template to Forge sites.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a deployment applies a custom Nginx template without a syntax validation step.
- **Why:** A syntax error can prevent reload and disrupt every affected site.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Run static analysis at a useful level before release
- **Do:** Run PHPStan or Larastan in CI before release at level 2 or higher so receiver calls and PHPDoc contracts are checked.
- **Flag when:** Flag when release workflows omit static analysis or its configured level cannot check the PHPDoc and receiver-expression errors being relied upon.
- **Why:** PHP does not enforce PHPDoc contracts at runtime; static analysis catches incompatible uses before release.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Replace deprecated Livewire Rule attributes
- **Do:** Use Livewire\Attributes\Validate in place of the legacy Rule attribute.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Livewire components import or use the deprecated Rule attribute.
- **Why:** Using the current attribute avoids reliance on the legacy name during upgrades.
- **Enforced by:** rector:RenameAttributeRector

Before:
```php
use Livewire\Attributes\Rule;
#[Rule('required')]
```

After:
```php
use Livewire\Attributes\Validate;
#[Validate('required')]
```

#### Install the Laravel 13 email validation security fix
- **Do:** Deploy laravel/framework 13.10.0 or later to include the default email rule CRLF-injection fix.
- **Flag when:** Flag when composer.lock pins a Laravel 13 framework version earlier than 13.10.0.
- **Why:** The affected email rule can allow crafted addresses to interfere with outbound email handling.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Handle JSON validation failures as field error responses
- **Do:** Handle HTTP 422 validation responses, display their errors object, and resolve nested field errors using flattened dot keys.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a JSON client treats 422 as a generic server failure or reads a nested error object instead of keys such as users.0.email.
- **Why:** Laravel returns field validation messages in the errors object, with flattened keys for nested fields.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
const message = body.errors.users[0].email;
```

After:
```php
if (response.status === 422) {
    showFieldError('users.0.email', body.errors['users.0.email']?.[0]);
}
```

#### Create a manual validator only when the flow needs custom control
- **Do:** Use Validator::make() and an explicit passes()/fails() branch when the failure flow needs control beyond normal request validation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom failure handling is forced through automatic validation redirects despite requiring another response or destination.
- **Why:** Manual branching makes a nonstandard validation response explicit.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$request->validate($rules); // automatically redirects to the wrong step
```

After:
```php
$validator = Validator::make($request->all(), $rules);
if ($validator->fails()) {
    return to_route('wizard.review')->withErrors($validator)->withInput();
}
```

#### Apply conditional constraints to the correct input scope
- **Do:** Use sometimes() for conditional additional rules, inspecting the current item for wildcard fields whose constraint depends on a sibling value.
- **Flag when:** Flag when conditional wildcard validation checks a root value instead of each item’s sibling or applies a condition globally to heterogeneous items.
- **Why:** The current item supplies the correct context for per-row conditional rules.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$validator->sometimes('channels.*.address', 'email', fn ($input) => $input->type === 'email');
```

After:
```php
$validator->sometimes('channels.*.address', 'email', fn ($input, $item) => $item->type === 'email');
```

#### Build value-dependent array rules per element
- **Do:** Use Rule::forEach() for array element rules whose constraints depend on that element’s value or path.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a value-dependent permission or existence rule is calculated once and incorrectly reused for all array elements.
- **Why:** Per-element rule construction evaluates each submitted value in its own context.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'companies.*.id' => [new AllowedCompany($firstCompanyId)]
```

After:
```php
'companies.*.id' => Rule::forEach(fn ($value, $attribute) => [new AllowedCompany($value)])
```

#### Keep unvalidated array keys excluded
- **Do:** Retain the default exclusion of unvalidated nested array keys unless an explicit compatibility contract requires the legacy behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Validator::includeUnvalidatedArrayKeys() is enabled without a documented compatibility need.
- **Why:** Including unchecked keys weakens the meaning of validated array output.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Validator::includeUnvalidatedArrayKeys();
```

After:
```php
Validator::excludeUnvalidatedArrayKeys(); // also the framework default
```

#### Return after a custom rule failure when later logic must stop
- **Do:** Return immediately after $fail() when subsequent rule logic assumes the value passed that check.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a rule calls $fail() then continues into unsafe parsing, expensive work or additional checks that should not run.
- **Why:** The failure callback records an error; it does not automatically return from the custom rule.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
if (! is_string($value)) { $fail('Must be text.'); }
parseText($value);
```

After:
```php
if (! is_string($value)) { $fail('Must be text.'); return; }
parseText($value);
```

#### Prefer rule objects or closures to new global rule registrations
- **Do:** Implement new custom validation as a reusable rule object or a local closure rather than adding global Validator::extend registrations.
- **Flag when:** Flag when new custom behavior is registered globally when an object or local closure provides the required scope.
- **Why:** Objects and closures expose dependencies and keep validation behavior local or explicitly reusable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Validator::extend('valid_code', $callback);
```

After:
```php
'code' => [new ValidCode]
```

#### Define repeated cross-layer payload shapes once
- **Do:** Use a typed Data class when the same payload shape is otherwise repeated across validation, serialization and frontend types.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the same substantial payload properties are manually repeated across requests, response serializers and TypeScript definitions.
- **Why:** A shared typed shape reduces drift between layers when those layers share a contract.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Separate request, response and TS copies of the same fields.
```

After:
```php
class ProfileData extends \Spatie\LaravelData\Data {
    public function __construct(public string $name, public string $email) {}
}
```

#### Inject request-backed Data objects at controller boundaries
- **Do:** When laravel-data is the request validation boundary, build request Data objects through a validated path: type-hint the Data class in the controller action, or call Data::from($request) / validateAndCreate(), never from() on a raw input array.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a controller manually creates an unvalidated Data object from all request input instead of using the configured request-backed validation path.
- **Why:** Request-backed injection validates and maps input before the action handles it.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function store(Request $request) { $data = SongData::from($request->all()); }
```

After:
```php
public function store(SongData $data) { /* handle validated typed input */ }
```

#### Add DTO validation constraints that PHP types cannot infer
- **Do:** Declare validation attributes for length, format and domain constraints beyond the DTO property type.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an untrusted DTO string or number relies only on inferred type rules despite a stricter documented contract.
- **Why:** A PHP type does not express constraints such as maximum length, UUID format or accepted date format.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public string $title;
```

After:
```php
#[\Spatie\LaravelData\Attributes\Validation\Max(200)]
public string $title;
```

#### Avoid repeating DTO type-inferred validation rules
- **Do:** Let the active laravel-data rule inferrers supply type, requiredness and nullability rules rather than repeating equivalent property attributes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when DTO attributes restate rules already inferred from the same PHP property type without overriding behavior.
- **Why:** Redundant declarations add maintenance noise and can drift from the type contract.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
#[Required, StringType]
public string $title;
```

After:
```php
public string $title; // required and string inferred
```

#### Declare nested DTO collection item types
- **Do:** Annotate each nested DTO array or collection with its item Data class.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a nested collection is declared only as array or Collection so laravel-data cannot infer item validation and transformation.
- **Why:** Item types give the package the nested schema needed to validate each element.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public array $songs;
```

After:
```php
/** @var array<int, SongData> */
public array $songs;
```

## Consider (3727)

### Architecture

#### Replace default Cloud npm build steps when changing package manager
- **Do:** When using Yarn, PNPM or Bun for a Laravel Cloud build, replace the default npm dependency-install and asset-build steps with the chosen manager commands.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Cloud build commands run both the default npm install/build sequence and an alternative package manager sequence for the same assets.
- **Why:** Competing installation and build steps waste work and can resolve dependencies under conflicting lockfiles.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Respect the non-root Cloud Rust build environment
- **Do:** For Rust services built on Laravel Cloud, avoid build commands requiring root package installation and select dependency features that work with the available build image, such as rustls when suitable.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Cloud Rust build depends on apt-get, sudo or unavailable system libraries without a supported provisioning path.
- **Why:** Cloud Rust build commands lack root privileges, so installing missing system packages during the build fails.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Register package development daemons with Artisan dev
- **Do:** Register a package process needed during local development with Illuminate\Foundation\DevCommands so php artisan dev includes it; guard registration when also supporting older framework versions without that facility.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a required package development daemon must be started separately despite the package supporting the Laravel dev-process registry.
- **Why:** One development entry point starts the processes needed for the integrated feature.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Users must remember a separate php artisan reverb:start terminal.
```

After:
```php
if (class_exists(DevCommands::class)) {
    DevCommands::artisan('reverb:start', 'reverb');
}
```

#### Refactor monolith boundaries before extracting services or packages
- **Do:** Before extracting a monolith subsystem into a service or package, establish its cohesive responsibility, public contract and dependency direction and refactor cross-boundary coupling while the code is still local.
- **Flag when:** Flag when extraction moves a tangled subsystem behind a deployment or package boundary while preserving circular dependencies and calls into internal classes.
- **Why:** Extraction makes existing coupling harder to change and can turn a local design problem into distributed coordination.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Move Billing to a service while it and Shipping still call each other's internal repositories.
```

After:
```php
// First define and refactor Billing/Shipping public contracts and dependency direction; then extract the cohesive boundary.
```

#### Review module dependencies with an exported graph
- **Do:** When reviewing a modular application with Deptrac, export its dependency graph alongside analysis results to inspect module coupling and forbidden dependency directions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a module-boundary review relies only on directory names and has no graph or equivalent evidence of the actual dependency directions.
- **Why:** A dependency graph makes cycles, unexpected edges and boundary violations easier to inspect.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Module review lists folders without inspecting dependency edges.
```

After:
```php
vendor/bin/deptrac analyse --formatter=graphviz-image --output=build/dependencies.png
```

#### Use a compatible browser layer for Lambda browser workloads
- **Do:** For ZIP-deployed Lambda browser workloads using a suitable maintained browser layer, attach a trusted version compatible with the runtime and architecture instead of bundling a duplicate Chrome binary and its full dependency tree.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Lambda browser function duplicates a browser runtime already supplied by its chosen compatible layer or relies on an unverified runtime/architecture match.
- **Why:** A compatible reusable layer keeps the application package focused and separates browser-runtime maintenance from application code.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Integrate completed work in small increments
- **Do:** Split feature work into reviewable increments and integrate completed, validated changes into the main branch frequently instead of keeping months of completed work on a long-lived feature branch.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a feature branch accumulates independently releasable work while integration is deferred for unrelated polishing.
- **Why:** Frequent integration exposes conflicts earlier and delivers useful changes sooner.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use a Forge wildcard domain for dynamic subdomains
- **Do:** Configure a Forge wildcard domain such as *.example.com when one site must serve dynamically created or catch-all subdomains, rather than registering each hostname individually.
- **Flag when:** Flag when deployment or tenant onboarding repeatedly adds individual Forge domains for subdomains that should share the same site and wildcard routing policy.
- **Why:** Wildcard domain routing lets new matching subdomains reach the site without a separate Forge domain-registration step.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use site-level Composer credentials for distinct Forge package access
- **Do:** In Forge, configure site-level Composer credentials when sites running under the same Ubuntu user need different authentication or licenses for the same package provider.
- **Flag when:** Flag when sites requiring different private-package identities rely on one shared server-level Composer credential, causing the wrong account or license to be used.
- **Why:** Server-level Composer credentials are shared by sites under the same Ubuntu user; site-level configuration selects the credentials intended for each site.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Centralize explicit runtime package versions in a release-maintained constant
- **Do:** When a package maintains an explicit runtime version for vendor SDK metadata or diagnostics, define one VERSION constant on its main package class, reuse it at reporting call sites, and update it with each release.
- **Flag when:** Flag when runtime package-version strings are duplicated across SDK integrations or diagnostics, or the package VERSION constant disagrees with the release being shipped.
- **Why:** One runtime version value keeps vendor telemetry and diagnostics consistent and makes release updates easy to locate.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$sdk->setAppInfo('Acme Billing', '1.2.3');
$agent = 'Acme Billing/1.2.2';
```

After:
```php
class AcmeBilling { public const VERSION = '1.2.3'; }
$sdk->setAppInfo('Acme Billing', AcmeBilling::VERSION);
$agent = 'Acme Billing/'.AcmeBilling::VERSION;
```

#### Declare class-constant visibility explicitly under the adopted style
- **Do:** When enforcing explicit member visibility, include class constants as well as properties and methods, choosing public, protected or private to match the intended API.
- **Flag when:** Flag a class constant that relies on implicit public visibility in a codebase configured to require explicit constant visibility.
- **Why:** Explicit visibility makes the intended constant API clear and lets the formatter enforce the same member policy consistently.
- **Enforced by:** partial: pint:modifier_keywords

Before:
```php
class Status { const READY = "ready"; }
```

After:
```php
class Status { public const READY = "ready"; }
```

#### Make global Composer executables available to the development shell
- **Do:** For a Valet setup installed with composer global require laravel/valet, include the actual Composer global binary directory in the development shell PATH and verify the valet executable resolves.
- **Flag when:** Flag a documented global Composer CLI setup that installs Valet but leaves its global binary directory unavailable to the shell or assumes a directory that differs from Composer configuration.
- **Why:** A globally installed package is not a usable CLI until the shell can find its executable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Complete Paddle account and domain approval before production checkout
- **Do:** Before launching a Cashier Paddle integration, obtain the production vendor account and approval for the production application domain; complete sandbox validation before switching to production credentials.
- **Flag when:** Flag a production Paddle checkout launch whose account or application-domain approval is still pending.
- **Why:** An otherwise working sandbox checkout can remain unavailable to customers until the provider approves the production domain.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Handle absent path inputs before calling application path helpers
- **Do:** When an input path may be null, decide how to handle its absence before passing it to storage_path() or another helper documented to take a string. Use an empty string only when resolving the base directory is explicitly intended.
- **Flag when:** Flag a nullable path passed to a documented string path helper with no deliberate missing-path behavior, especially before a file read, write or deletion.
- **Why:** An absent file path must not silently become an operation on the base application directory; matching the documented string contract also keeps static analysis accurate.
- **Enforced by:** partial: larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Functions\CallToFunctionParametersRule

Before:
```php
$path = storage_path($optionalRelativePath);
```

After:
```php
if ($optionalRelativePath === null) { throw new InvalidArgumentException("A relative path is required."); }
$path = storage_path($optionalRelativePath);
```

#### Assign one accountable owning team to each module
- **Do:** In a multi-team modular application, assign one accountable owning team to each module and route cross-team module changes through that team's review process; a team may own several modules.
- **Flag when:** Flag a module jointly changed by several teams with no single accountable owner or clear approval path for its shared contract.
- **Why:** A clear ownership boundary reduces conflicting changes and gives other teams a reliable contact for module behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Skip irrelevant documentation searches
- **Do:** Allow documentation searches to be skipped for copy-only edits and changes unrelated to package behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag when agent instructions mandate package documentation searches for every edit, including plain text changes.
- **Why:** Searches should resolve uncertainty about behavior rather than add work to changes that cannot affect it.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// AGENTS.md: search package docs for every text edit
```

After:
```php
// AGENTS.md: search docs when the change depends on package behavior.
```

#### Document departures from Laravel layout
- **Do:** Document a module or domain layout, its namespaces, and its ownership conventions before extending that layout.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the repository uses a custom module/domain structure without instructions describing where new code belongs.
- **Why:** An explicit layout convention lets contributors place code consistently.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Modules/Billing exists; contributor instructions only mention app/.
```

After:
```php
// AGENTS.md: Billing code lives in Modules/Billing; document its namespace and tests.
```

#### Verify documented architecture against real call sites
- **Do:** Inspect representative action invocations and database-write paths before recording their conventions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when architecture instructions assert an action entry method or idempotent-write convention that representative call sites contradict.
- **Why:** Evidence from implementation prevents inferred conventions from teaching contributors the wrong pattern.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// AGENTS.md: all actions use execute(); actual callers use handle().
```

After:
```php
// AGENTS.md: Billing actions use handle(); cite representative callers.
```

#### Scope repository rules to the actual layout
- **Do:** Match rule globs to real module/domain paths and include each path affected by a cross-domain convention.
