- **Flag when:** Flag when a typed Sweet Alert option duplicates an available enum value as a string.
- **Why:** Enums expose supported choices and prevent misspellings.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
function showToast(string $position): void {
    Alert::toast('Saved')->position($position);
}
```

After:
```php
function showToast(Position $position): void {
    Alert::toast('Saved')->position($position);
}
```

#### Use typed NativePHP platform icon values
- **Do:** Bind NativePHP iOS and Android icon attributes to their generated platform enum cases.
- **Flag when:** Flag when native icon attributes use unchecked strings despite available project icon enums.
- **Why:** Typed icons make platform-specific choices explicit and catch invalid names.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<native:icon ios="gearshape" android="settings" />
```

After:
```php
<native:icon :ios="\App\Icons\Ios::Gearshape" :android="\App\Icons\Android::Settings" />
```

#### Treat TallStackUI block identifiers as literal keys
- **Do:** Use literal array-key access for TallStackUI personalization block names containing dots.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a block such as wrapper.second is changed using nested dot-path traversal.
- **Why:** Dots are part of the block identifier; nested access changes the wrong structure.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
data_set($blocks, 'wrapper.second', $classes);
```

After:
```php
$blocks['wrapper.second'] = $classes;
```

#### Use backing storage in backed property hooks
- **Do:** In non-virtual get/set hooks, read or assign the property’s backing value as appropriate; declare intentionally computed properties as virtual.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a property intended to store state has a get hook that never reads backing storage or a set hook that never writes it.
- **Why:** Hooks that bypass intended storage can discard assignments or expose stale values.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Properties\GetNonVirtualPropertyHookReadRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Properties\SetNonVirtualPropertyHookAssignRule

Before:
```php
// PHP >=8.4
public string $name { set { trim($value); } }
```

After:
```php
// PHP >=8.4
public string $name { set { $this->name = trim($value); } }
```

#### Honor native readonly property lifecycles
- **Do:** Give native readonly properties a type, initialize them directly before reading, and avoid static declarations, non-promoted defaults, reference writes, and later reassignment except version-supported clone reinitialization.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a native readonly property violates its declaration or initialization contract, or is mutated again outside a permitted clone operation.
- **Why:** Readonly protects property identity only when writes follow the supported lifecycle.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Properties\ReadOnlyPropertyRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Properties\ReadOnlyPropertyAssignRefRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Properties\MissingReadOnlyPropertyAssignRule

Before:
```php
public function rename(string $name): void { $this->name = $name; } // name is readonly
```

After:
```php
public function __construct(public readonly string $name) {}
```

#### Respect readable and writable property directions
- **Do:** Read only properties with a readable side and write only properties with a writable side.
- **Flag when:** Flag when code reads a set-only property or writes a get-only property.
- **Why:** Directional property contracts separate supported reads from supported mutations.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Properties\ReadingWriteOnlyPropertiesRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Properties\WritingToReadOnlyPropertiesRule

Before:
```php
$value = $object->writeOnly;
```

After:
```php
$object->writeOnly = $value;
```

#### Respect reference parameter input and output contracts
- **Do:** Keep values written through by-reference parameters compatible with declared input types and any @param-out contract.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a referenced parameter is assigned a value outside its permitted output type.
- **Why:** Reference writes change the caller’s variable and must preserve its promised resulting type.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Variables\ParameterOutAssignedTypeRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Variables\ParameterOutExecutionEndTypeRule

Before:
```php
/** @param-out int $count */
function update(int &$count): void { $count = 'unknown'; }
```

After:
```php
/** @param-out int $count */
function update(int &$count): void { $count = 0; }
```

#### Break foreach reference aliases after iteration
- **Do:** Unset a by-reference foreach variable immediately after its loop, or stop reusing that variable name.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a referenced loop variable remains aliased and is later assigned or reused in another loop.
- **Why:** The variable still refers to the last element and later assignments can corrupt the source array.
- **Enforced by:** partial: larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Variables\AssignToByRefExprFromForeachRule

Before:
```php
foreach ($items as &$item) {}
$item = 'other';
```

After:
```php
foreach ($items as &$item) {}
unset($item);
$item = 'other';
```

#### Remove unused legacy application directories
- **Do:** Delete empty or unused directories left by earlier application layouts after confirming no registrations or autoload mappings depend on them; remove unused application providers from bootstrap/providers.php.
- **Flag when:** Flag unused legacy directories or registrations with no active behavior, references, or documented purpose, including stale entries in bootstrap/providers.php.
- **Why:** Removing unused structure keeps the current architecture clear.
- **Enforced by:** partial: shift:public/linter/unused-directories

Before:
```php
// bootstrap/providers.php
return [App\Providers\AppServiceProvider::class, App\Legacy\LegacyProvider::class];
```

After:
```php
// bootstrap/providers.php; remove the unused provider and directory after checking references.
return [App\Providers\AppServiceProvider::class];
```

#### Publish default translations only for customization
- **Do:** Publish Laravel’s bundled language files when overriding default language lines; avoid copying untouched defaults solely to create a lang directory.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the application maintains unchanged copies of framework language files without intended customization.
- **Why:** Default language lines already ship with the framework. Unnecessary copies create stale translation maintenance.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// lang/en/validation.php: unnecessary unchanged snapshot
return ['required' => 'The :attribute field is required.'];
```

After:
```php
// No local validation.php is needed to use the framework defaults.
$message = __('validation.required', ['attribute' => 'name']);
```

#### Use AI provider enum cases
- **Do:** Reference built-in Laravel AI providers using Laravel\Ai\Enums\Lab cases rather than repeated provider-name strings where the API supports them.
- **Flag when:** Flag when supported provider arguments or attributes use handwritten built-in provider names.
- **Why:** Provider enum cases make identifiers discoverable and prevent spelling mistakes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
#[Provider('anthropic')]
```

After:
```php
#[Provider(Lab::Anthropic)]
```

#### Restrict inspection agents to read-only filesystem tools
- **Do:** Expose FileStorage::readOnly($disk) to agents that only need to inspect files.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an inspection-only agent receives FileStorage::all() or write/delete tools without a required mutation capability.
- **Why:** Read-only tools prevent unintended writes and deletion by constraining the exposed capability.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
FileStorage::all('local')
```

After:
```php
FileStorage::readOnly('local')
```

#### Order AI skill sources by intended priority
- **Do:** List higher-priority skill sources before lower-priority fallbacks in an agent’s skills() definition.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a fallback source appears first and shadows the intended same-named project skill.
- **Why:** The first source wins for duplicate skill names, so ordering controls which instructions load.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return [$sharedSkills, $projectSkills];
```

After:
```php
return [$projectSkills, $sharedSkills];
```

#### Give delegated AI tools task-specific metadata
- **Do:** Implement CanActAsTool with a descriptive name() and description() when an AI sub-agent’s default metadata does not explain its specialization.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a specialized delegated agent exposes only a generic class-derived tool name and description that do not identify when to use it.
- **Why:** Task-specific metadata helps the calling agent choose the appropriate specialist.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class HelperAgent implements Agent {}
```

After:
```php
class RefundsAgent implements Agent, CanActAsTool {
    public function name(): string { return 'refunds_specialist'; }
    public function description(): string { return 'Assess refund eligibility.'; }
}
```

#### Name structured classification options
- **Do:** Supply Collection::decide() with a by field or callback for options that are not strings or enums.
- **Flag when:** Flag when decide() classifies object/array options without a meaningful option-name mapping.
- **Why:** Explicit names give the model an identifiable set of choices.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$departments->decide($question, $text);
```

After:
```php
$departments->decide($question, $text, by: 'name');
```

#### Explain ambiguous classification options
- **Do:** Provide describe criteria to Collection::decide() when option names alone do not distinguish the intended choices.
- **Flag when:** Flag when ambiguous named choices have no descriptions explaining their matching criteria.
- **Why:** The model needs selection criteria to distinguish options reliably.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$priorities->decide($question, $text);
```

After:
```php
$priorities->decide($question, $text, describe: fn (Priority $p) => $p->description());
```

#### Use descriptive MCP tool class names
- **Do:** Name MCP tool classes for the capability they expose, accounting for class-derived tool names and titles.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a generic MCP tool class name produces an ambiguous public tool identifier and has no meaningful override.
- **Why:** Clients use tool names to identify capabilities.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class HelperTool extends Tool {}
```

After:
```php
class CurrentWeatherTool extends Tool {}
```

#### Name concurrent task results
- **Do:** Use associative keys for Concurrency::run() closures when results represent distinct named tasks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when callers rely on numeric positions to distinguish unrelated concurrent results.
- **Why:** Names keep result access stable when tasks are reordered or added.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$results = Concurrency::run([fn () => loadUsers(), fn () => loadOrders()]);
$users = $results[0];
```

After:
```php
$results = Concurrency::run(['users' => fn () => loadUsers(), 'orders' => fn () => loadOrders()]);
$users = $results['users'];
```

#### Set subprocess working directories explicitly
- **Do:** Set Process::path() when a subprocess uses project-relative paths or depends on a particular working directory.
- **Flag when:** Flag when such a process inherits the PHP entry point’s working directory implicitly.
- **Why:** Explicit paths keep subprocess behavior consistent across HTTP, CLI, and worker entry points.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Process::run('npm run build');
```

After:
```php
Process::path(base_path())->run('npm run build');
```

#### Validate upload extensions when names must match content
- **Do:** Combine content-based mimes validation with extensions when the user-supplied extension must match the allowed formats.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an upload requires a matching filename extension but validation checks content MIME only.
- **Why:** mimes verifies content and can accept a PNG named photo.txt; a separate extension rule enforces the naming requirement.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'photo' => ['file', 'mimes:png'],
```

After:
```php
'photo' => ['file', 'mimes:png', 'extensions:png'],
```

#### Reuse enum cases in database enum definitions
- **Do:** Use the PHP enum’s cases() in $table->enum() when the database column and application enum share the same allowed values.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a migration manually duplicates the same enum cases as a string list and can drift from the application contract.
- **Why:** A shared definition avoids mismatched allowed states; released migrations must still remain reproducible.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$table->enum('difficulty', ['easy', 'hard']);
```

After:
```php
$table->enum('difficulty', Difficulty::cases());
```

#### Match Laravel contribution formatting
- **Do:** When contributing to Laravel repositories, follow their documented PSR-2-based formatting and repository-specific formatter configuration.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Laravel contribution differs from the target repository’s accepted formatting.
- **Why:** Upstream contributions should follow the host repository’s style instead of importing an application’s unrelated preset.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
function run(){return true;}
```

After:
```php
function run()
{
    return true;
}
```

#### Synchronize customer billing data with Stripe
- **Do:** Synchronize application changes to Stripe-backed customer billing details and tax IDs through the appropriate Cashier customer APIs.
- **Flag when:** Flag when billing fields or tax IDs change locally without updating Stripe before invoices or tax calculations use them.
- **Why:** Stripe Tax and invoices rely on Stripe’s customer data, which must match the current billing details.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$user->update(['name' => $name]);
```

After:
```php
$user->update(['name' => $name]);
$user->syncStripeCustomerDetails();
```

#### Keep subscription type identifiers stable
- **Do:** Use stable internal subscription type identifiers without spaces; for one subscription type use a consistent name such as default or primary and do not rename persisted types.
- **Flag when:** Flag when subscription type names contain spaces, vary across creation/lookups, or are renamed without a data migration.
- **Why:** Cashier uses the internal type to find subscriptions; unstable names break lookups.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$user->newSubscription('Premium Plan', $price);
```

After:
```php
$user->newSubscription('default', $price);
```

#### Handle checkout webhook delays
- **Do:** Show a pending state after Stripe Checkout until webhook-driven payment and subscription updates confirm activation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a checkout return immediately assumes the local subscription is active or grants service solely because the return URL was reached.
- **Why:** Checkout redirects and webhook delivery can arrive in either order.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return view('billing.success', ['active' => true]);
```

After:
```php
return view('billing.return', ['pending' => ! $user->subscribed('default')]);
```

#### Declare SFTP file and directory visibility
- **Do:** Set SFTP disk visibility and directory_visibility explicitly to the access policy required by the stored data.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an SFTP disk relies on unintended permission defaults or sensitive files/directories are configured public.
- **Why:** File and directory permissions are separate and should reflect who may read or traverse them.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'driver' => 'sftp',
```

After:
```php
'driver' => 'sftp',
'visibility' => 'private',
'directory_visibility' => 'private',
```

#### Use automatic Head metadata attribute selection
- **Do:** Let Head::meta() choose name versus property unless a particular metadata entry requires an intentional override.
- **Flag when:** Flag when redundant property flags duplicate the package’s normal selection logic.
- **Why:** Automatic selection reduces duplicated metadata classification rules.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Head::meta('description', $text, property: false);
```

After:
```php
Head::meta('description', $text);
```

#### Scope isolatable command locks to the intended work
- **Do:** Define isolatableId() from relevant arguments/options when independent command inputs should be allowed to run concurrently.
- **Flag when:** Flag when unrelated input values collide on a command-name-only lock despite requiring independent isolation.
- **Why:** The lock key should identify the protected work rather than serialize unrelated tasks.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function isolatableId(): string { return 'tenants:sync'; }
```

After:
```php
public function isolatableId(): string
{
    return 'tenant:'.$this->argument('tenant');
}
```

#### Map Homestead applications individually
- **Do:** Give each Homestead application its own shared-folder mapping instead of mounting a large parent containing many projects.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Homestead.yaml maps an entire multi-project parent directory.
- **Why:** Large mappings increase filesystem tracking and I/O overhead.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Do not mount the Homestead current directory
- **Do:** Avoid a Homestead shared-folder mapping whose host path is the current directory represented by a dot.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Homestead.yaml folders contains map: . for the current Homestead directory.
- **Why:** This can interfere with Vagrant’s /vagrant mapping and break provisioning features.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Install Windows NFS permission support for Homestead
- **Do:** When using Homestead NFS shared folders on Windows, consider vagrant-winnfsd to maintain correct user/group permissions, and verify that the selected sharing setup preserves the required permissions.
- **Flag when:** Flag Windows NFS shared folders with incorrect user/group permissions and no working permission-support configuration; do not flag plugin absence alone.
- **Why:** The plugin maintains expected user/group permissions for shared files.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Resolve every configured Homestead site hostname
- **Do:** Use per-project mDNS where suitable, or add hosts-file entries for each site when a shared Homestead VM serves multiple domains or automatic resolution is unavailable.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a configured Homestead site domain cannot resolve to the VM.
- **Why:** Web-server site mappings only work when the host resolves the corresponding domain.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Recreate the Homestead VM during upgrades
- **Do:** Follow the Homestead update workflow by backing up required VM-only data, destroying the old VM, and recreating it from the updated box and configuration.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an update procedure reuses an incompatible old VM instead of recreating it as required by the documented upgrade.
- **Why:** Recreation applies box and provisioning changes consistently.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep personal Homestead customizations local
- **Do:** Put personal VM setup in user-customizations.sh and exclude that file from version control; keep shared provisioning in the team’s shared configuration.
- **Flag when:** Flag when personal customizations are committed or mixed into shared provisioning unintentionally.
- **Why:** Local setup should not alter teammates’ environments.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Return the real authentication primary key
- **Do:** Implement getAuthIdentifierName() and getAuthIdentifier() using the model’s actual primary-key name and value.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom authenticatable code returns a login field such as email instead of the identity primary key.
- **Why:** Authentication persistence and provider lookup depend on a stable primary-key identity.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function getAuthIdentifierName() { return 'email'; }
```

After:
```php
public function getAuthIdentifierName() { return $this->getKeyName(); }
public function getAuthIdentifier() { return $this->getKey(); }
```

#### Provide international currency formatting support
- **Do:** Install ext-intl in runtimes using Cashier Paddle to format currencies for non-English locales.
- **Flag when:** Flag when locale-aware Cashier Paddle currency formatting is configured but the runtime lacks ext-intl.
- **Why:** Locale-aware currency formatting depends on the Intl extension.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Resolve past-due Paddle payment information first
- **Do:** Prompt past-due Paddle customers to update their payment details and complete that step before subscription modifications requiring current payment information.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the app modifies a past-due subscription without providing the required payment-update flow.
- **Why:** Paddle restricts subscription changes while payment issues remain unresolved.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$user->subscription('default')->swap($price);
```

After:
```php
if ($subscription->pastDue()) {
    return $subscription->redirectToUpdatePaymentMethod();
}
$subscription->swap($price);
```

#### Cancel Paddle subscriptions when removing the final price
- **Do:** Cancel a Paddle subscription instead of removing its last remaining price.
- **Flag when:** Flag when removePrice() can remove the subscription’s final item.
- **Why:** A Paddle subscription must retain a price; cancellation represents ending the subscription.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$subscription->removePrice($lastPrice);
```

After:
```php
$subscription->cancel();
```

#### Name foreign keys explicitly before table renames
- **Do:** Give foreign-key constraints stable explicit names before renaming tables, and use those names in subsequent constraint operations.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a renamed table retains convention-derived constraint names but later migrations infer names from the new table name.
- **Why:** Convention-derived names incorporate the original table and can become misleading or unresolvable after a rename.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$table->foreignId('user_id')->constrained();
// Later rename the table and infer the new constraint name.
```

After:
```php
$table->foreign('user_id', 'orders_user_fk')->references('id')->on('users');
// Preserve and use orders_user_fk across the rename.
```

#### Encode PKCE challenges using base64url
- **Do:** Compute S256 PKCE challenges from the raw SHA-256 verifier hash and encode using URL-safe Base64 with no padding or whitespace.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a PKCE challenge uses hex hashing, standard +/ Base64 characters, padding, or inserted whitespace.
- **Why:** The authorization server expects the exact PKCE base64url representation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$challenge = base64_encode(hash('sha256', $verifier));
```

After:
```php
$challenge = rtrim(strtr(base64_encode(hash('sha256', $verifier, true)), '+/', '-_'), '=');
```

#### Preserve legacy morph-pivot table names explicitly
- **Do:** When upgrading custom MorphPivot models that relied on singular inferred names, set their table property to the existing table name.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom polymorphic pivot model relies on inference but its existing schema uses the pre-Laravel-13 singular name.
- **Why:** Laravel 13 pluralizes inferred custom morph-pivot table names; explicit names preserve existing data access.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class Taggable extends MorphPivot {} // existing table: taggable
```

After:
```php
class Taggable extends MorphPivot { protected $table = 'taggable'; }
```

#### Keep stub publishing prompts focused
- **Do:** Use human-readable labels in stub-publishing prompts and offer commonly customized stubs as the primary choices.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a stub selector exposes opaque filenames or an overwhelming undifferentiated list of internal templates.
- **Why:** Focused readable choices make generator customization easier to discover.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$choices = ['model.stub' => 'model.stub', 'model.pivot.stub' => 'model.pivot.stub'];
```

After:
```php
$choices = ['model.stub' => 'Model', 'controller.stub' => 'Controller'];
```

#### Build class generators on GeneratorCommand
- **Do:** Extend Illuminate\Console\GeneratorCommand for make:* class generators and expose stable AsCommand metadata.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a class generator hand-rolls namespace/path/stub substitution already handled by GeneratorCommand, or lacks the intended lazy command metadata.
- **Why:** The base generator centralizes conventional class generation and published-stub behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class MakeData extends Command { /* manual path and namespace replacement */ }
```

After:
```php
#[AsCommand(name: 'make:data')]
class MakeData extends GeneratorCommand {
    protected function getStub() { return __DIR__.'/stubs/data.stub'; }
}
```

#### Start Spatie-style packages with a compatible skeleton
- **Do:** For new packages built on Spatie Package Tools conventions, start from the compatible Laravel package skeleton or preserve its expected resource and source layout.
- **Flag when:** Flag when PackageServiceProvider resource discovery is used but package paths differ from its configured layout.
- **Why:** A compatible skeleton aligns providers, source, and publishable resources with package-tool defaults.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$package->name('reports')->hasViews();
// Templates incorrectly stored only in templates/.
```

After:
```php
$package->name('reports')->hasViews();
// Template: resources/views/report.blade.php
<h1>{{ $title }}</h1>
```

#### Deduplicate ReplacingMergeTree reads when required
- **Do:** Use SELECT ... FINAL or an equivalent deliberate query-time deduplication strategy when a ClickHouse ReplacingMergeTree read requires current deduplicated rows.
- **Flag when:** Flag when correctness-sensitive reads assume background merges have already removed old row versions.
- **Why:** ReplacingMergeTree merges are asynchronous; query-time deduplication provides the required view at a query cost.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$sql = 'SELECT count() FROM events';
```

After:
```php
$sql = 'SELECT count() FROM events FINAL';
```

#### Organize large applications by product capability
- **Do:** For a large application adopting capability modules, group each capability’s code together and keep third-party integration adapters in a deliberate integration area.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a capability’s behavior is scattered across unrelated directories or provider-specific integration details are mixed throughout domain code.
- **Why:** Capability grouping makes feature boundaries visible and keeps external dependencies easier to replace.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
namespace App\Services; class BillingAndShippingService {}
```

After:
```php
namespace App\Billing\Actions; class IssueInvoice {}
// Provider adapter: App\Integrations\Stripe\StripeBillingGateway
```

#### Define module responsibilities before moving code
- **Do:** Document module responsibilities, public interfaces, and allowed dependencies before reorganizing application directories around modules.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a modularization change moves files without defining ownership or dependency boundaries and leaves cross-module internals coupled.
- **Why:** Directory names alone do not create independent modules.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
namespace App\Modules\Billing;
// Still imports Shipping\Internal repositories directly.
```

After:
```php
namespace App\Billing;
// Depends on a documented Shipping public contract, not its internal repositories.
```

#### Search documentation by the required capability
- **Do:** Describe the required capability in documentation searches before narrowing to a remembered function name.
- **Flag when:** Flag when repository search guidance prescribes only remembered API names and omits capability-oriented queries.
- **Why:** Capability queries can find supported features whose API names are not yet known.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Avoid redundant package names in Boost queries
- **Do:** Keep Boost search-docs queries focused on the capability rather than adding package names already supplied by the tool’s installed-package context.
- **Flag when:** Flag when repository Boost query examples repeat package names instead of stating the topic or capability.
- **Why:** The tool already knows the installed packages; focused queries reduce redundant search terms.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Relax PHPDoc certainty deliberately at defensive library boundaries
- **Do:** For library code that deliberately checks values callers may supply contrary to PHPDoc, consider treatPhpDocTypesAsCertain: false rather than deleting meaningful defensive checks solely to silence constant-condition diagnostics.
- **Flag when:** Flag defensive library guards removed only because PHPStan treats a documentation-only input promise as a runtime guarantee.
- **Why:** PHPDoc does not enforce input types at runtime; trusting it as certain can misclassify required boundary checks.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Combine equivalent consecutive isset and unset operations
- **Do:** Where the project enables the corresponding fixer rules, combine compatible isset checks joined by && and adjacent unset calls into multi-argument calls while preserving evaluation order.
- **Flag when:** Flag redundant repeated isset/unset calls that the selected formatter can combine without changing behavior.
- **Why:** A single call states the same related presence check or cleanup operation with less repetition.
- **Enforced by:** pint:combine_consecutive_issets, pint:combine_consecutive_unsets

Before:
```php
isset($a) && isset($b); unset($a); unset($b);
```

After:
```php
isset($a, $b); unset($a, $b);
```

#### Brace interpolated variables under the explicit interpolation policy
- **Do:** When explicit_string_variable is part of the selected style, wrap interpolated variables in {$variable} syntax in double-quoted strings and heredocs.
- **Flag when:** Flag unbraced interpolated variables in files governed by that explicit formatting policy.
- **Why:** Visible interpolation boundaries keep variable names distinct from surrounding text and align generated formatting.
- **Enforced by:** pint:explicit_string_variable

Before:
```php
"Hello $name"
```

After:
```php
"Hello {$name}"
```

#### Resolve only declared template names in PHPStan extensions
- **Do:** Pass getTemplateType() the declaring class and template parameter name that the referenced generic class actually defines.
- **Flag when:** Flag extension code asking for a nonexistent or mismatched template parameter and then relying on the resulting type.
- **Why:** A lookup against the wrong generic declaration loses the type information the extension intends to preserve.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Api\GetTemplateTypeRule

#### Choose numeric or moving maximum PHPStan levels deliberately
- **Do:** Use level: max when the project intends to adopt newly added levels on upgrades; choose an explicit numeric level when level increases require a separate rollout.
- **Flag when:** Flag an unexpected strictness jump caused by max in a project whose analysis policy expects a fixed numeric level.
- **Why:** A moving maximum and a pinned level have different upgrade behavior even with the same analyzer version policy.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Opt in deliberately to upcoming PHPStan checks
- **Do:** When the project wants early feedback from upcoming PHPStan behavior, include the installed bleedingEdge.neon configuration and review its new diagnostics as part of analysis upgrades.
- **Flag when:** Flag an intended early-check analysis lane whose bleeding-edge configuration is installed but not loaded, or whose new diagnostics are ignored without review.
- **Why:** An explicit opt-in lets the project discover analyzer changes before a major upgrade.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Enable strict benevolent-union checking when adopting that policy
- **Do:** Enable checkBenevolentUnionTypes when the project requires argument compatibility for every possible member of benevolent unions, then fix the newly exposed unsafe uses.
- **Flag when:** Flag an adopted strict-union analysis configuration that still accepts a benevolent union where only one member meets the called API’s parameter contract.
- **Why:** Lenient unions can otherwise conceal a value reaching an API that cannot accept it.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Do not assume repeated impure calls return the same value
- **Do:** When functions may return changing values and a project-wide conservative policy is intended, set rememberPossiblyImpureFunctionValues: false; use accurate impure annotations for isolated cases.
- **Flag when:** Flag analysis that treats repeated possibly impure calls as the same narrowed result despite an intentional conservative policy or known changing return values.
- **Why:** A value observed in one call need not describe the result of a later call.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Fix errors that prevent PHPStan from analyzing the program
- **Do:** Resolve parse errors, broken autoloading and missing parent classes before relying on PHPStan results; do not try to hide analysis-blocking errors in ignoreErrors or a baseline.
- **Flag when:** Flag analysis output with non-ignorable bootstrap, parse or inheritance blockers left unresolved while the run is treated as a completed check.
- **Why:** An analyzer cannot reliably inspect a program whose declarations it cannot load or understand.
- **Enforced by:** partial: larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Classes\ExistingClassInClassExtendsRule

#### Use long echo tags under the selected Symfony formatter policy
- **Do:** When following Symfony’s echo_tag_syntax long-format policy, write PHP template output with <?php echo rather than the short <?= tag.
- **Flag when:** Flag short echo tags in templates governed by an explicitly selected long-tag formatting policy.
- **Why:** Template output syntax should match the chosen formatter configuration.
- **Enforced by:** pint:echo_tag_syntax

Before:
```php
<?= $title ?>
```

After:
```php
<?php echo $title ?>
```

#### Use while true for intentional unbounded loops under Symfony style
- **Do:** When the Symfony empty_loop_condition policy is adopted, express deliberate unbounded loops as while (true) while preserving their existing exit and cleanup behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag for (;;) or equivalent do-while true loops in source governed by that selected style.
- **Why:** One spelling makes intentional unbounded processing recognizable without changing its termination contract.
- **Enforced by:** pint:empty_loop_condition

Before:
```php
for (;;) { processNext(); }
```

After:
```php
while (true) { processNext(); }
```

#### Combine adjacent constant string literals
- **Do:** Under the selected no_useless_concat_operator policy, replace concatenations of adjacent constant string literals with an equivalent single literal.
- **Flag when:** Flag adjacent literal concatenations that add no interpolation, conditional behavior or useful layout.
- **Why:** Removing redundant concatenation simplifies the expression while preserving the exact resulting bytes.
- **Enforced by:** pint:no_useless_concat_operator

Before:
```php
'in'.'voice'
```

After:
```php
'invoice'
```

#### Terminate PHP instructions before closing template tags
- **Do:** Under the selected semicolon_after_instruction policy, write the statement semicolon explicitly even for the final instruction before a closing PHP tag.
- **Flag when:** Flag template instructions that rely on ?> to terminate the statement under a policy requiring explicit semicolons.
- **Why:** Explicit statement termination keeps the syntax convention consistent when template boundaries move.
- **Enforced by:** pint:semicolon_after_instruction

Before:
```php
<?php echo $title ?>
```

After:
```php
<?php echo $title; ?>
```

#### Use prefix increments under the selected Symfony policy
- **Do:** When the Symfony prefix-increment policy is selected, use ++$value and --$value where replacing the postfix form preserves the expression’s behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag postfix increments in unused-result positions governed by the selected prefix policy; do not rewrite consumed postfix results as equivalent.
- **Why:** Prefix and postfix forms can differ when their values are consumed, so style normalization must preserve evaluation semantics.
- **Enforced by:** pint:increment_style

Before:
```php
$index++; // result unused
```

After:
```php
++$index; // result unused
```

#### Use ordinary comments for prose inside method bodies
- **Do:** When adopting Symfony’s structural-docblock policy, use ordinary comments for inline prose and configure preservation for any analyzer-significant inline PHPDoc before enabling phpdoc_to_comment.
- **Flag when:** Flag prose-only /** */ blocks inside executable code under the structural policy, or conversion of semantic type annotations without a preservation plan.
- **Why:** Comment syntax can distinguish structural API documentation from implementation prose while keeping meaningful type annotations available.
- **Enforced by:** pint:phpdoc_to_comment

Before:
```php
/** Choose the active connection. */
return $connection;
```

After:
```php
/* Choose the active connection. */
return $connection;
```

#### Document project verification commands for coding agents
- **Do:** Record the actual formatting-check and static-analysis entry points in the repository’s shared agent instructions, keeping them synchronized with Composer scripts.
- **Flag when:** Flag agent instructions that omit required project checks or name commands that no longer exist.
- **Why:** Explicit executable checks let agents validate changes using the same workflow as contributors.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Normalize value-object quantities to one internal unit
- **Do:** For a quantity value object, choose one internal unit and convert every unit-specific constructor or factory into that representation.
- **Flag when:** Flag a value object whose stored numeric field changes unit according to which constructor was used without carrying a reliable conversion contract.
- **Why:** One canonical unit makes arithmetic and comparison independent of how callers supplied the quantity.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Duration::minutes(2); // stores 2 in the same field that seconds() uses
```

After:
```php
Duration::minutes(2); // stores 120 seconds
```

#### Enable Xdebug debugging in the configuration actually loaded
- **Do:** For a debugging session, load an ini override setting xdebug.mode=debug from the scan directory used by the intended PHP SAPI, then restart the relevant process when required.
- **Flag when:** Flag a debugger configuration edited in a PHP ini directory the intended CLI or web process never loads, leaving step debugging disabled.
- **Why:** CLI and web runtimes may load different configuration files, so editing an unrelated ini cannot activate the intended mode.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use model-aware primary-key query helpers
- **Do:** Use Eloquent whereKey() and whereKeyNot() for primary-key inclusion and exclusion instead of hard-coding an id column in equivalent predicates.
- **Flag when:** Flag primary-key whereIn/whereNotIn predicates that hard-code id in reusable model code, especially when the model uses a custom key.
- **Why:** Model-aware predicates retain the configured key name and appropriate key handling.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Order::query()->whereIn('id', $orderIds)->get();
```

After:
```php
Order::query()->whereKey($orderIds)->get();
```

#### Adopt strict-analysis extension rules selectively
- **Do:** When introducing phpstan-strict-rules incrementally, set strictRules.allRules to false and explicitly enable the individual rules the project is ready to enforce; review extension-provided PHPStan parameter changes separately.
- **Flag when:** Flag an incremental strict-rules rollout that unintentionally enables every extension rule or assumes allRules: false disables all other configuration changes.
- **Why:** Selective adoption makes the policy reviewable without overwhelming maintained code.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Teach PHPStan about custom deprecation markers
- **Do:** If the project marks deprecated APIs with custom attributes, implement and register the corresponding PHPStan deprecation extension so deprecation rules recognize those markers; use a PHPStan version supporting the extension API.
- **Flag when:** Flag a custom deprecation marker whose API usages are silently accepted by the configured deprecation analysis.
- **Why:** Project-specific metadata should produce the same actionable upgrade feedback as standard deprecations.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Expand anonymous bodies under the framework formatting policy
- **Do:** When adopting Laravel framework braces_position settings, expand anonymous-function bodies and empty anonymous-class bodies instead of keeping their braces and body on one line; preserve arrow-function syntax where otherwise appropriate.
- **Flag when:** Flag single-line closure bodies or empty anonymous classes where the committed braces_position policy disallows them.
- **Why:** The selected formatter policy keeps anonymous bodies consistent with neighboring framework-style code.
- **Enforced by:** pint:braces_position

Before:
```php
$callback = function () { return 1; };
```

After:
```php
$callback = function () {
    return 1;
};
```

#### Prefer explicit arrays to compact under the selected policy
- **Do:** When following the explicit-array convention, replace fixed compact() variable-name lists with equivalent key/value array entries.
- **Flag when:** Flag fixed compact() calls in code that adopts CompactToVariablesRector or an equivalent explicit-data policy.
- **Why:** Explicit references expose values directly to readers and refactoring tools.
- **Enforced by:** rector:CompactToVariablesRector

Before:
```php
compact('user', 'roles')
```

After:
```php
['user' => $user, 'roles' => $roles]
```

#### Order named arguments by the declared parameter order
- **Do:** Under the selected named-argument ordering policy, list named arguments in the callee signature order when reordering preserves evaluation behavior; apply named arguments only to APIs whose parameter names are intentionally stable.
- **Flag when:** Flag out-of-signature-order named arguments where the configured ordering rule applies and their expressions can safely be reordered.
- **Why:** Consistent ordering makes call sites easier to compare with their signatures.
- **Enforced by:** partial: rector:SortCallLikeNamedArgsRector

Before:
```php
new DeliveryOptions(retries: 3, timeout: 10); // constructor: timeout, retries
```

After:
```php
new DeliveryOptions(timeout: 10, retries: 3);
```

#### Preserve raw environment-value semantics during refactoring
- **Do:** Review direct environment reads before replacing them with Env::get() or env(): Laravel normalizes special string values such as true, false, empty and null. Preserve deliberate raw-string comparisons rather than applying the rewrite blindly.
- **Flag when:** Flag an automated environment-access rewrite that changes raw-string comparisons, null handling or fallback behavior through Laravel normalization.
- **Why:** Equivalent-looking accessors can return different value types.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Blind rewrite of a deliberate raw protocol check:
Env::get('EXTERNAL_FLAG') === 'false'
```

After:
```php
// Preserve raw semantics where explicitly required:
($_ENV['EXTERNAL_FLAG'] ?? null) === 'false'
```

#### Separate PHPStan symbol discovery from source analysis
- **Do:** For declarations PHPStan must discover without analyzing their bodies, use scanDirectories/scanFiles outside analysis paths, or excludePaths.analyse for discoverable fixtures inside them; do not exclude required symbols with analyseAndScan.
- **Flag when:** Flag missing symbols caused by analyseAndScan exclusions or avoidable fixture-body diagnostics caused by treating discovery-only code as maintained analysis source.
- **Why:** Discovery and analysis have different responsibilities and need different exclusions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Enforce throwing native-function wrappers where adopted
- **Do:** In projects adopting thecodingmachine/safe, enable the compatible PHPStan Safe rule and use its throwing function variants for covered failure-returning native functions, handling the resulting exceptions deliberately.
- **Flag when:** Flag covered native calls that bypass the adopted Safe policy or a conversion that ignores the new exception behavior.
- **Why:** Throwing wrappers prevent false failure results from being mistaken for successful values.
- **Enforced by:** partial: larastan:TheCodingMachine\Safe\PHPStan\Rules\UseSafeFunctionsRule, partial: larastan:TheCodingMachine\Safe\PHPStan\Rules\UseSafeCallablesRule

#### Load Laravel integration when analyzing with Psalm
- **Do:** When Psalm is part of the project's analysis stack, use a psalm/plugin-laravel release compatible with the installed Laravel/Psalm versions. Suppress only verified framework-magic unused-code false positives, retaining useful application checks.
- **Flag when:** Flag Psalm analysis of Laravel code without its intended framework integration, incompatible plugin constraints, or broad suppression of genuine unused application code.
- **Why:** Framework-aware analysis reduces false positives while preserving useful diagnostics.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Enable nullable-value checks before raising to level eight
- **Do:** If the project wants nullable-value diagnostics while retaining a lower PHPStan rule level, enable checkNullables explicitly instead of assuming the lower level already includes those checks.
- **Flag when:** Flag lower-level analysis claimed to enforce nullable-value safety while checkNullables is disabled.
- **Why:** A useful safety check can be adopted independently of all higher-level diagnostics.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### State the expected output format in AI instructions
- **Do:** When application code consumes a model response, state the expected response format and required fields in the model instructions. Keep these instructions aligned with any structured-output schema and validate the received response rather than treating prompt wording as a guarantee.
- **Flag when:** Flag machine-consumed model prompts that leave the expected response format implicit or contradict the parser/schema contract.
- **Why:** Clear format instructions help the model produce a response consistent with its application consumer.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'Summarize this invoice.'
```

After:
```php
'Return a JSON object with summary:string and invoice_id:string; do not include Markdown fences.'
```

#### Share a named modal across separate triggers
- **Do:** When the same Flux modal must open from several locations, declare one named modal and reference it from separate matching modal triggers instead of duplicating modal markup or requiring a nested trigger.
- **Flag when:** Flag duplicated instances of the same dialog solely to provide multiple opening buttons.
- **Why:** Named triggers allow one dialog contract and stateful form to serve several entry points.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<!-- Two identical edit dialogs, each copied beside its own opening button. -->
```

After:
```php
<flux:modal.trigger name="edit-profile"><flux:button>Edit</flux:button></flux:modal.trigger>
<flux:modal name="edit-profile">...</flux:modal>
```

#### Finish identity-result pipelines with thenReturn
- **Do:** Use Pipeline::thenReturn() when the terminal step only returns the processed passable unchanged; retain then() when the terminal callback performs another transformation.
- **Flag when:** Flag a pipeline ending in an identity then() callback whose only purpose is to return the processed subject.
- **Why:** The dedicated terminal operation communicates that no final transformation is needed.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$pipeline->then(fn ($subject) => $subject);
```

After:
```php
$pipeline->thenReturn();
```

#### Serve responsive image candidates with matching sizes
- **Do:** For content images with multiple available widths, provide srcset width candidates and a sizes expression matching the rendered layout, with a suitable src fallback, rather than sending the largest asset to every viewport.
- **Flag when:** Flag a responsive content image that always downloads one oversized source despite available derivatives, or sizes that contradict the actual layout.
- **Why:** The browser can select a suitable image for viewport size and display density.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<img src="hero-1600.webp" alt="Mountain trail">
```

After:
```php
<img src="hero-800.webp" srcset="hero-400.webp 400w, hero-800.webp 800w, hero-1600.webp 1600w" sizes="(max-width: 800px) 100vw, 800px" alt="Mountain trail">
```

#### Resolve feature flags according to their access category
- **Do:** Distinguish plan/tier entitlement flags, optional per-customer flags and development-only release flags, and route each category through its intended scope and access policy.
- **Flag when:** Flag a feature resolver that treats all flags alike and thereby leaks development features or applies one customer's optional setting to another.
- **Why:** Feature categories have different audiences, lifetimes and authorization requirements.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Every flag uses a single unscoped application boolean.
```

After:
```php
// Plan features use entitlements; customer options use customer scope; development flags use explicit release/environment policy.
```

#### Keep internal-only enums pure
- **Do:** Use pure enums when consumers only compare cases and no scalar persistence or serialization contract is required.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an internal-only enum assigns unused backing values merely to have them.
- **Why:** Unneeded scalar values add a second representation that must be maintained.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
enum Direction: string { case Left = 'left'; case Right = 'right'; }
```

After:
```php
enum Direction { case Left; case Right; }
```

#### Analyse custom PHPStan extensions
- **Do:** Run static analysis over custom PHPStan rule and extension code as well as the application it checks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom PHPStan rules or extensions are excluded from all analysis paths.
- **Why:** Analysis tooling is executable code and can contain type errors that undermine its checks.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
parameters:
    paths: [app]
```

After:
```php
parameters:
    paths: [app, tools/phpstan]
```

#### Omit empty constructor parentheses under Laravel style
- **Do:** Omit empty parentheses for zero-argument class instantiations when the project follows the Laravel preset’s new-expression style.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a zero-argument new expression retains empty parentheses under an adopted no-parentheses policy.
- **Why:** One constructor expression style avoids incidental formatting differences.
- **Enforced by:** pint:new_with_parentheses

Before:
```php
$clock = new Clock();
```

After:
```php
$clock = new Clock;
```

#### Lead continuation lines with boolean operators
- **Do:** Put multiline boolean operators at the beginning of continuation lines when following the PER preset.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a multiline boolean expression places continuation operators at line ends under the PER style policy.
- **Why:** Leading operators expose the relationship between continued conditions.
- **Enforced by:** pint:operator_linebreak

Before:
```php
$ok = $a &&
    $b;
```

After:
```php
$ok = $a
    && $b;
```

#### Place null last in native union types
- **Do:** Put null last in native union types while preserving the other type order when following the PER preset.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a native union places null before another member under the PER policy.
- **Why:** A stable nullable-type convention makes unions easier to compare.
- **Enforced by:** pint:ordered_types

Before:
```php
function find(): null|User {}
```

After:
```php
function find(): User|null {}
```

#### Remove inner attribute bracket whitespace
- **Do:** Do not put whitespace immediately inside attribute brackets when following the PER preset.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an attribute contains extra space after #[ or before ] under the PER policy.
- **Why:** Compact attribute delimiters make metadata consistent.
- **Enforced by:** pint:attribute_block_no_spaces

Before:
```php
#[ Example ]
```

After:
```php
#[Example]
```

#### Place trait imports first in classes
- **Do:** Put class trait-use statements before other class elements when following the PER preset.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a trait-use declaration follows properties or methods under the trait-first policy.
- **Why:** Putting composition first makes the class’s shared behavior visible.
- **Enforced by:** pint:ordered_class_elements

Before:
```php
class Item { public string $name; use HasLabels; }
```

After:
```php
class Item { use HasLabels; public string $name; }
```

#### Align multiline doc-comment asterisks
- **Do:** Align multiline doc-comment asterisks with the opening comment delimiter under the Symfony preset.
- **Flag when:** Flag when doc-comment asterisks have inconsistent indentation under the selected policy.
- **Why:** Aligned documentation is easier to read and edit.
- **Enforced by:** pint:align_multiline_comment

Before:
```php
/**
   * Description.
 */
```

After:
```php
/**
 * Description.
 */
```

#### Replace backtick shell execution
- **Do:** Use shell_exec() instead of the backtick execution operator, particularly when targeting PHP 8.5 where backticks are deprecated.
- **Flag when:** Flag when source uses the backtick execution operator under PHP 8.5 or an adopted no-backticks style.
- **Why:** An explicit function call is recognizable and avoids PHP 8.5 deprecation warnings. This change does not make interpolated shell input safe.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Operators\BacktickRule, pint:backtick_to_shell_exec

Before:
```php
$output = `whoami`;
```

After:
```php
$output = shell_exec("whoami");
```

#### Give intentional empty loops braces
- **Do:** Write intentional empty loop bodies with braces rather than a bare semicolon under the selected style.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an intentional empty loop body is represented by a bare semicolon.
- **Why:** Braces make the empty body explicit and avoid the appearance of an accidental statement terminator.
- **Enforced by:** pint:empty_loop_body

Before:
```php
while (poll());
```

After:
```php
while (poll()) {}
```

#### Fully qualify globals under the Symfony policy
- **Do:** Fully qualify global classes, functions, and constants instead of importing them when the project adopts that Symfony preset policy.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a project that explicitly adopts fully qualified globals instead imports those global symbols.
- **Why:** A single global-name policy prevents ambiguous namespace resolution and incidental churn.
- **Enforced by:** pint:global_namespace_import

Before:
```php
use DateTimeImmutable;
$date = new DateTimeImmutable;
```

After:
```php
$date = new \DateTimeImmutable;
```

#### Remove empty ordinary comments
- **Do:** Remove ordinary comments containing no text under the selected style.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an ordinary comment block or line is empty and serves no retained tool directive.
- **Why:** Empty comments create visual noise without explaining behavior.
- **Enforced by:** partial: pint:no_empty_comment

Before:
```php
//
return $value;
```

After:
```php
return $value;
```

#### Omit redundant null defaults on untyped properties
- **Do:** Do not explicitly initialize an untyped property to null when following the selected no-null-initialization style.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an untyped property explicitly defaults to null under this policy.
- **Why:** Untyped properties already default to null, so the initializer adds no behavior.
- **Enforced by:** pint:no_null_property_initialization

Before:
```php
public $label = null;
```

After:
```php
public $label;
```

#### Remove else after a terminating branch
- **Do:** Remove unnecessary else nesting after a branch that unconditionally returns or throws when following the early-return style.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an else contains the remaining path after an unconditional terminating if branch.
- **Why:** Removing the extra block makes the remaining path easier to follow.
- **Enforced by:** pint:no_useless_else

Before:
```php
if (!$user) { return null; } else { return $user->name; }
```

After:
```php
if (!$user) { return null; }
return $user->name;
```

#### Use ordinary access on proven non-null receivers
- **Do:** Use -> rather than ?-> when the receiver is statically guaranteed to be non-null.
- **Flag when:** Flag when nullsafe access is used on a receiver whose type excludes null.
- **Why:** Redundant nullsafe access suggests a nonexistent nullable path and can hide the true contract.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Methods\NullsafeMethodCallRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Properties\NullsafePropertyFetchRule, pint:no_useless_nullsafe_operator

Before:
```php
function name(User $user): string { return $user?->name; }
```

After:
```php
function name(User $user): string { return $user->name; }
```

#### Omit terminal periods from annotation descriptions under Symfony style
- **Do:** Remove terminal full stops from PHPDoc annotation descriptions when following the Symfony preset policy.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a PHPDoc tag description ends in a full stop under the selected annotation style.
- **Why:** Consistent annotation punctuation avoids formatter churn. This policy applies to tag descriptions rather than general prose summaries.
- **Enforced by:** pint:phpdoc_annotation_without_dot

Before:
```php
/** @param string $name Display name. */
```

After:
```php
/** @param string $name Display name */
```

#### Place null last in PHPDoc unions under Symfony style
- **Do:** Put null last in PHPDoc union annotations while preserving the other members’ order under the Symfony policy.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a PHPDoc union places null before another member under this policy.
- **Why:** A stable null position makes annotations consistent and easy to scan.
- **Enforced by:** pint:phpdoc_types_order

Before:
```php
/** @return null|User */
```

After:
```php
/** @return User|null */
```

#### Use private visibility where inheritance cannot use protected
- **Do:** Reduce protected members to private when inheritance cannot require them, such as implementation-only members of a final class.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a protected member has no supported inheritance use and the adopted visibility policy prefers private.
- **Why:** Narrow visibility makes the actual extension contract explicit.
- **Enforced by:** pint:protected_to_private

Before:
```php
final class Client { protected string $token; }
```

After:
```php
final class Client { private string $token; }
```

#### Keep throw expressions together under Symfony style
- **Do:** Write a short throw expression on one line when following the Symfony preset.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a short throw expression is split across lines under the selected single-line policy.
- **Why:** Keeping the keyword and expression together makes the exit visible.
- **Enforced by:** pint:single_line_throw

Before:
```php
throw
    new RuntimeException("Failed");
```

After:
```php
throw new RuntimeException("Failed");
```

#### Use increment syntax for single-step updates under Symfony style
- **Do:** Use increment or decrement operators for equivalent standalone single-step numeric self-assignments under the selected policy.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a standalone numeric update uses an equivalent plus-or-minus-one assignment contrary to the selected style.
- **Why:** A consistent update notation avoids multiple spellings of the same simple operation.
- **Enforced by:** pint:standardize_increment

Before:
```php
$count += 1;
```

After:
```php
++$count;
```

#### Use break to exit a switch case
- **Do:** Use break rather than continue when the intended operation is only to leave the current switch.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an unqualified continue is used to exit a switch case.
- **Why:** continue in a switch behaves unexpectedly to readers and triggers warnings in supported PHP versions. Explicit loop continuation needs the appropriate nesting level.
- **Enforced by:** pint:switch_continue_to_break

Before:
```php
switch ($value) { case 1: continue; }
```

After:
```php
switch ($value) { case 1: break; }
```

#### Space native union pipes under the selected custom style
- **Do:** Put single spaces around union-type pipes when the project explicitly adopts that custom Pint policy.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a native union omits spaces around | under the project’s selected single-space policy.
- **Why:** One union spacing convention prevents repeated formatting differences.
- **Enforced by:** pint:types_spaces

Before:
```php
function find(): string|Closure|null {}
```

After:
```php
function find(): string | Closure | null {}
```

#### Keep sealed hierarchies valid
- **Do:** Apply @phpstan-sealed only to classes or interfaces, list existing object types, and restrict descendants to the declared permitted types.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a sealed declaration uses invalid targets or symbols, or an unlisted class extends or implements the sealed type.
- **Why:** Valid sealed contracts make the supported closed hierarchy analysable.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Classes\AllowedSubTypesRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\PhpDoc\SealedDefinitionTraitRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\PhpDoc\SealedDefinitionClassRule

Before:
```php
/** @phpstan-sealed MissingType */
interface Result {}
```

After:
```php
/** @phpstan-sealed Success|Failure */
interface Result {}
```

#### Implement real interfaces on enums
- **Do:** Declare only existing interfaces in an enum’s implements list.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an enum implements list includes a class, trait, or missing type.
- **Why:** Enums can satisfy interface contracts but cannot implement unrelated symbol kinds.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Classes\ExistingClassesInEnumImplementsRule

Before:
```php
enum State implements MissingInterface { case Draft; }
```

After:
```php
enum State implements Labelled { case Draft; public function label(): string { return "Draft"; } }
```

#### Keep local PHPDoc type aliases resolvable
- **Do:** Declare and import PHPDoc type aliases with unique names, valid source classes, and no circular definitions or class-name conflicts.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a local type alias is duplicated, circular, unresolved, or conflicts with a class name.
- **Why:** Resolvable aliases allow complex shared type structures without hiding invalid annotations.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Classes\LocalTypeAliasesRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Classes\LocalTypeTraitAliasesRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Classes\LocalTypeTraitUseAliasesRule

Before:
```php
/** @phpstan-type Payload Payload */
```

After:
```php
/** @phpstan-type Payload array{id: int, name: string} */
```

#### Declare and satisfy required base classes
- **Do:** Use a valid @phpstan-require-extends contract on traits or interfaces that require a particular existing base class, and satisfy it in consumers.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a base-class-dependent trait or interface has a malformed required-base declaration or is used without its required base.
- **Why:** The contract exposes otherwise implicit inheritance assumptions to analysis.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Classes\RequireExtendsRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\PhpDoc\RequireExtendsDefinitionClassRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\PhpDoc\RequireExtendsDefinitionTraitRule

Before:
```php
trait HasOwner { public function owner(): User { return $this->modelOwner(); } }
```

After:
```php
/** @phpstan-require-extends Model */
trait HasOwner { public function owner(): User { return $this->modelOwner(); } }
```

#### Use contextual magic constants in meaningful contexts
- **Do:** Use class, trait, method, and namespace magic constants only where their contextual value matches the intended identifier.
- **Flag when:** Flag when code expects a class or method identifier from a magic constant used outside that context.
- **Why:** An empty or unexpected contextual value can silently corrupt registry keys or diagnostics.
- **Enforced by:** partial: larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Constants\MagicConstantContextRule

Before:
```php
$key = __CLASS__; // global scope
```

After:
```php
$key = Report::class;
```

#### Use valid interval specifications
- **Do:** Construct DateInterval with valid supported interval specifications.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a known malformed interval string is passed to DateInterval.
- **Why:** Malformed intervals throw instead of defining the intended duration.
- **Enforced by:** partial: larastan:PHPStan\Rules\DateIntervalInstantiationRule

Before:
```php
$interval = new DateInterval("one hour");
```

After:
```php
$interval = new DateInterval("PT1H");
```

#### Keep no-throws declarations honest
- **Do:** Do not declare @throws void on a function, method, or hook that can explicitly throw.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an explicitly throwing body is annotated as throwing no exceptions.
- **Why:** Incorrect no-throws contracts cause callers and analysis to miss real failure paths.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Exceptions\ThrowsVoidFunctionWithExplicitThrowPointRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Exceptions\ThrowsVoidMethodWithExplicitThrowPointRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Exceptions\ThrowsVoidPropertyHookWithExplicitThrowPointRule

Before:
```php
/** @throws void */
function load(): void { throw new RuntimeException; }
```

After:
```php
/** @throws RuntimeException */
function load(): void { throw new RuntimeException; }
```

#### Do not return nullsafe expressions by reference
- **Do:** Return a stable variable when a function must return by reference; do not return nullsafe access by reference.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an arrow function or function returns a nullsafe expression by reference.
- **Why:** A conditional nullsafe expression does not provide a valid stable reference target.
- **Enforced by:** partial: larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Functions\ArrowFunctionReturnNullsafeByRefRule, partial: larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Functions\ReturnNullsafeByRefRule

Before:
```php
function &name(?User $user): ?string { return $user?->name; }
```

After:
```php
function name(?User $user): ?string { return $user?->name; }
```

#### Accept real-world personal names
- **Do:** Avoid mandatory first/middle/last structures and unnecessary character or length restrictions; justify constraints needed by storage or external systems.
- **Flag when:** Flag when personal-name validation requires a fixed Western structure, bans legitimate characters, or imposes an unexplained limit.
- **Why:** Names vary across cultures, scripts, and structures; arbitrary restrictions exclude valid users.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'last_name' => ['required', 'alpha', 'max:20'],
```

After:
```php
'name' => ['required', 'string'],
```

#### Use string names for dynamic class constants
- **Do:** Ensure dynamically fetched class-constant names are strings and refer to the intended existing accessible constant.
- **Flag when:** Flag when ClassName::{$name} can receive a non-string name or an unresolved constant.
- **Why:** Laravel 13’s PHP floor supports dynamic constant fetches, but invalid names still fail at runtime.
- **Enforced by:** partial: larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Constants\DynamicClassConstantFetchRule

Before:
```php
$name = 123;
$value = Status::{$name};
```

After:
```php
$name = 'ACTIVE';
$value = Status::{$name};
```

#### Respect template variance positions
- **Do:** Use covariant templates only in permitted output positions and contravariant templates only in permitted input positions; keep read/write properties invariant when necessary.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a variant template is used in a prohibited parameter, return, or mutable property position.
- **Why:** Incorrect variance allows callers to pass or receive values outside the advertised generic contract.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Generics\FunctionSignatureVarianceRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Generics\MethodSignatureVarianceRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Generics\PropertyVarianceRule

Before:
```php
/** @template-covariant T */
class Box { /** @param T $value */ public function set($value): void {} }
```

After:
```php
/** @template T */
class Box { /** @param T $value */ public function set($value): void {} }
```

#### Apply callable timing annotations to callable parameters
- **Do:** Attach @param-immediately-invoked-callable and @param-later-invoked-callable only to existing callable parameters whose execution timing matches the implementation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when invocation-timing tags reference absent/non-callable parameters or contradict callback storage or invocation.
- **Why:** Accurate timing tells analysis whether captured state can change before a callback executes.
- **Enforced by:** partial: larastan:PHPStan\Rules\PhpDoc\IncompatibleParamImmediatelyInvokedCallableRule

Before:
```php
/** @param-immediately-invoked-callable $missing */
```

After:
```php
/** @param-immediately-invoked-callable $callback */
function run(callable $callback): void { $callback(); }
```

#### Pipe values into compatible callables
- **Do:** When using PHP 8.5 pipes, send values to callable targets whose first parameter accepts the value and is not by reference.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a pipe target is non-callable, rejects the incoming type, or requires a by-reference first argument.
- **Why:** A pipe passes a value rather than a writable reference; incompatible targets fail at runtime.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Operators\PipeOperatorRule

Before:
```php
$items |> sort(...); // sort requires a reference
```

After:
```php
$items |> (fn (array $values): int => count($values));
```

#### Describe receiver state changes with valid self-out types
- **Do:** Use @phpstan-self-out only on instance methods, with a resolvable subtype of the receiver and complete generics/iterable/callable types.
- **Flag when:** Flag when self-out appears on a static method or function, widens beyond the receiver, or contains incomplete type arguments.
- **Why:** Valid self-out contracts let analysis track generic receiver changes after mutation.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\PhpDoc\IncompatibleSelfOutTypeRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Methods\MissingMethodSelfOutTypeRule

Before:
```php
/** @phpstan-self-out OtherClass */
public function add($value): void {}
```

After:
```php
/** @phpstan-self-out self<T|NewValue> */
public function add(NewValue $value): void {}
```

#### Honor PHPDoc readonly property lifecycles
- **Do:** Initialize @readonly properties through the analyzer-permitted declaring-class constructor path, avoid declaration defaults and reference writes, and do not read before initialization or assign again.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a PHPDoc-readonly property is uninitialized on use, has a declaration default, escapes by reference, or is assigned outside its permitted initialization path.
- **Why:** PHPDoc readonly has no runtime enforcement; analysis must preserve the promised lifecycle.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Properties\MissingReadOnlyByPhpDocPropertyAssignRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Properties\ReadOnlyByPhpDocPropertyRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Properties\ReadOnlyByPhpDocPropertyAssignRefRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Properties\ReadOnlyByPhpDocPropertyAssignRule

Before:
```php
/** @readonly */
public string $id = 'pending';
```

After:
```php
/** @readonly */
public string $id;
public function __construct(string $id) { $this->id = $id; }
```

#### Respect property write visibility for references
- **Do:** Acquire or pass a property by reference only from a scope allowed to write that property.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a reference can bypass private(set), protected(set), or another property write-access restriction.
- **Why:** A writable reference exposes mutation even if the current statement only appears to read.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Properties\PropertyAssignRefRule

Before:
```php
$ref =& $account->balance; // balance is private(set)
```

After:
```php
$balance = $account->balance;
```

#### Keep set-hook input types compatible
- **Do:** For PHP 8.4+ set hooks, accept a type at least as broad as the property’s write contract and use a valid single non-variadic value parameter.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a set hook narrows accepted values incompatibly or declares an invalid parameter signature.
- **Why:** The hook must accept every value promised by the property contract.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Properties\SetPropertyHookParameterRule

Before:
```php
public Animal $pet { set(Dog $value) { $this->pet = $value; } }
```

After:
```php
public Animal $pet { set(Animal $value) { $this->pet = $value; } }
```

#### Keep purity promises truthful
- **Do:** Keep callables and property hooks marked @pure or @phpstan-pure free of observable side effects and remove conflicting purity annotations.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a pure callable mutates external state, performs I/O, invokes impure operations, or also declares itself impure.
- **Why:** Analysis may treat pure operations as safe to reorder or ignore; false promises make its conclusions unsound.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Pure\PureFunctionRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Pure\PureMethodRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Pure\PurePropertyHookRule

Before:
```php
/** @pure */
function notify(): void { mail('ops@example.test', 'Alert', '...'); }
```

After:
```php
function notify(): void { mail('ops@example.test', 'Alert', '...'); }
```

#### Keep parameter output types precise
- **Do:** Remove @param-out union members the implementation never assigns, subject to inherited contract constraints.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a documented output type contains a member that no reachable write can produce.
- **Why:** Precise output contracts let callers safely use values written through references.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\TooWideTypehints\TooWideFunctionParameterOutTypeRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\TooWideTypehints\TooWideMethodParameterOutTypeRule

Before:
```php
/** @param-out int|string $count */
function countItems(&$count): void { $count = 1; }
```

After:
```php
/** @param-out int $count */
function countItems(&$count): void { $count = 1; }
```

#### Keep closed property types precise
- **Do:** Remove property union members never assigned when visibility, initialization, and extension contracts make all writes analyzable.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a closed property’s union contains unused members and no external writer can supply them.
- **Why:** Narrow property types reduce unsupported states without breaking valid external writes.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\TooWideTypehints\TooWidePropertyTypeRule

Before:
```php
private int|string $count = 0; // only integer writes
```

After:
```php
private int $count = 0;
```

#### Prefer native readonly over documentation-only promises
- **Do:** Replace PHPDoc @readonly with native readonly when the property’s initialization and mutation semantics satisfy PHP readonly requirements.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a documentation-only readonly property is eligible for native enforcement but still relies solely on analyzer conventions.
- **Why:** Native readonly enforces the promise at runtime as well as during analysis.
- **Enforced by:** shift:workbench/set-readonly-properties

Before:
```php
/** @readonly */
public string $id;
```

After:
```php
public readonly string $id;
```

#### Remove unreferenced goto labels
- **Do:** Remove labels that no goto statement can reference.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an ordinary statement label has no corresponding goto target reference.
- **Why:** Unused labels suggest obsolete control flow and distract readers.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Keywords\UnusedLabelRule

Before:
```php
finished:
return $result;
```

After:
```php
return $result;
```

#### Separate navigation group identity from HTML labels
- **Do:** Keep Filament navigationGroup values as string identifiers or UnitEnum cases and configure HTML labels through keyed navigationGroups entries.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a resource/page navigationGroup contains an Htmlable object instead of a stable identifier.
- **Why:** Stable identity lets Filament match and order groups independently of their rendered labels.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
protected static $navigationGroup = new HtmlString('<strong>Shop</strong>');
```

After:
```php
protected static string|UnitEnum|null $navigationGroup = 'Shop';
```

#### Tie SMS MFA to a verified normalized phone number
- **Do:** Store SMS MFA phone numbers consistently in E.164 format and disable their MFA enrollment when the phone number changes until the replacement is verified.
- **Flag when:** Flag when SMS MFA remains enabled after a number change or equivalent numbers are stored in inconsistent formats.
- **Why:** Changing the destination invalidates proof of possession of the old number.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$user->update(['phone' => $request->phone]);
```

After:
```php
$user->update([
    'phone' => $normalizedE164,
    'phone_verified_at' => null,
    'sms_mfa_enabled' => false,
]);
```

#### Scaffold Laravel Modules features with their generator
- **Do:** When using nwidart/laravel-modules, create modules with module:make so each follows the adopted Modules/{Name} layout.
- **Flag when:** Flag when manually created modules omit required module structure or diverge from the package’s configured generator paths.
- **Why:** The generator keeps module registration and layout consistent.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Modules/Billing/module.json missing; files are loose and unregistered
namespace Modules\Billing; class Invoice {}
```

After:
```php
// Scaffolded with module:make Billing
// Modules/Billing/module.json
{"name":"Billing","alias":"billing","providers":["Modules\\Billing\\Providers\\BillingServiceProvider"]}
```

#### Keep Spatie data objects in the configured discovery location
- **Do:** Place spatie/laravel-data classes in app/Data by default, or update generator and structure-discovery configuration together for a deliberate alternative.
- **Flag when:** Flag when DTO classes are scattered outside the configured discovery paths and can be missed by structure caching.
- **Why:** A coherent location keeps generated classes and cached discovery aligned.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
namespace App\Misc; class PostData extends Data {}
```

After:
