- **Flag when:** Flag when code loads all translated records and filters them in PHP or compares the entire JSON document to one locale string.
- **Why:** Database filtering preserves pagination and avoids loading unrelated records.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Product::all()->filter(fn ($p) => $p->getTranslation('name', $locale) === $name);
```

After:
```php
Product::whereLocale('name', $locale)->where('name->'.$validatedLocale, $name)->get(); // Allowlist locale/path segments.
```

#### Add a settings migration for every new persisted setting
- **Do:** Create a versioned settings migration that adds each new persisted setting with its intended default.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a settings class expects a new property absent from installed persisted settings.
- **Why:** A code declaration alone does not add the stored setting to existing installations.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public string $theme; // Added without a settings migration.
```

After:
```php
public function up(): void {
    $this->migrator->add('general.theme', 'system');
}
```

#### Provide class defaults when settings must work before migrations
- **Do:** Give settings properties defaults when code must construct the settings class before persisted settings migrations run.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a required pre-migration code path reads an uninitialized/missing setting property.
- **Why:** Class defaults support that bootstrapping path; they do not replace persisted setting migrations.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public string $theme; // Read during pre-migration boot.
```

After:
```php
public string $theme = 'system';
```

#### Configure STI child hydration explicitly
- **Do:** Add the STI trait, type discriminator column, and valid child mapping when parent queries must hydrate subtype models.
- **Flag when:** Flag when parent model queries return the base class despite behavior requiring mapped child instances.
- **Why:** Subtype hydration depends on a stored discriminator and configured mapping.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class Person extends Model {} // Expected to hydrate Admin subclasses.
```

After:
```php
class Person extends Model {
    use HasChildren;
    protected $childTypes = ['admin' => Admin::class];
}
// Migration: $table->string('type');
```

#### Audit console mutations when the audit contract requires them
- **Do:** Enable console auditing for commands/seeders whose data mutations must appear in the audit trail.
- **Flag when:** Flag when required audited changes made through CLI commands or seeders are omitted because console auditing is disabled.
- **Why:** Audit coverage should follow the mutation requirement rather than only the HTTP entry point.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// config/audit.php
'console' => false, // Required CLI changes are omitted.
```

After:
```php
// config/audit.php
'console' => true,
```

#### Protect tenant identity and connection attributes from mass assignment
- **Do:** Exclude tenant IDs and internal database/connection names from user-controlled mass assignment and authorize any deliberate change.
- **Flag when:** Flag when tenant update endpoints pass unfiltered request data into internal tenant identity/connection attributes.
- **Why:** Changing these attributes can redirect requests into another tenant’s database.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$tenant->update($request->all());
```

After:
```php
$tenant->update($request->validate(['display_name' => ['required', 'string', 'max:255']]));
// Keep tenant identity and tenancy_db_name outside the assignable input.
```

#### Enable runtime tenant-database ownership checks when required
- **Do:** Enable the tenancy database bootstrapper’s hardening checks when the isolation requirement demands runtime database ownership verification.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a deployment requiring runtime verification leaves database hardening disabled.
- **Why:** The check can reject connections to another tenant’s or the central database, with extra runtime cost.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
DatabaseTenancyBootstrapper::$harden = false; // Runtime ownership validation required.
```

After:
```php
DatabaseTenancyBootstrapper::$harden = true;
```

#### Restore the central connection after temporary tenant work
- **Do:** End temporary tenant contexts in a finally block or the package’s scoped helper so subsequent work returns to the central database.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a temporary tenant switch can leak its connection into later central work after success or failure.
- **Why:** Long-lived processes can otherwise execute later queries in the wrong tenant context.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
tenancy()->initialize($tenant);
$this->runTenantWork(); // Never ends context.
```

After:
```php
tenancy()->initialize($tenant);
try { $this->runTenantWork(); } finally { tenancy()->end(); }
```

#### Limit spreadsheet upserts to permitted update columns
- **Do:** For a Laravel Excel import using WithUpserts, also implement WithUpsertColumns and return only permitted update attributes from upsertColumns(). Preserve the uniqueBy() lookup contract and the backing unique index.
- **Flag when:** Flag spreadsheet upserts that can overwrite immutable columns or define upsertColumns() without implementing WithUpsertColumns.
- **Why:** A deliberate update set constrains the effect of externally supplied rows.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Spreadsheet upsert updates every imported model attribute.
```

After:
```php
use App\Models\User;
use Maatwebsite\Excel\Concerns\ToModel;
use Maatwebsite\Excel\Concerns\WithUpserts;
use Maatwebsite\Excel\Concerns\WithUpsertColumns;

class UsersImport implements ToModel, WithUpserts, WithUpsertColumns
{
    public function model(array $row): User
    {
        return new User(['email' => $row[0], 'name' => $row[1]]);
    }

    public function uniqueBy(): string
    {
        return 'email'; // Backed by a unique database index.
    }

    public function upsertColumns(): array
    {
        return ['name'];
    }
}
```

#### Allow staged parent creation for deferred related forms
- **Do:** Make the relationship key nullable when Filament creates the owner before saving and associating its BelongsTo/MorphTo related form.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the first owner insert violates a non-null relation key that Filament can populate only after creating the related form.
- **Why:** Deferred relationship saving needs a valid intermediate schema state, or a different explicitly atomic creation strategy.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$table->foreignId('profile_id')->constrained(); // Owner saved before profile form.
```

After:
```php
$table->foreignId('profile_id')->nullable()->constrained();
```

#### Map public sort names to internal columns
- **Do:** Map public API sort names to internal database columns with AllowedSort::field() and pass aliases individually to allowedSorts(), or unpack an allowlisted array.
- **Flag when:** Flag request-controlled column names without an allowlist, unmapped public aliases, or an array passed directly to the pinned variadic allowedSorts() API.
- **Why:** A sort mapping keeps the API stable while allowing schema changes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$query->orderBy($request->input('sort')); // Public name does not match DB field.
```

After:
```php
QueryBuilder::for(User::class)
    ->allowedSorts(AllowedSort::field('joined', 'created_at'))
    ->get();
```

#### Preserve accessible table headers when hiding them visually
- **Do:** Keep accessible table-repeater heading text on Repeater\TableColumn and call hiddenHeaderLabel() on that column when its heading should be visually hidden.
- **Flag when:** Flag empty/removed accessible repeater headings or hiddenHeaderLabel() incorrectly called on an input component.
- **Why:** Assistive technology still needs a header label for each data column.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Remove the column heading text entirely.
```

After:
```php
use Filament\Forms\Components\Repeater;
use Filament\Forms\Components\Repeater\TableColumn;
use Filament\Forms\Components\TextInput;

Repeater::make('people')
    ->table([TableColumn::make('Name')->hiddenHeaderLabel()])
    ->schema([TextInput::make('name')->required()]);
```

#### Use roving tabindex for tab controls
- **Do:** Give only the active tab tabindex=0, move focus with arrow keys, and set inactive tabs to tabindex=-1.
- **Flag when:** Flag when every tab in a tablist becomes a separate Tab-key stop or keyboard focus cannot move between tabs.
- **Why:** Roving tabindex supports expected keyboard navigation without excessive tab stops.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<button role="tab" tabindex="0">One</button><button role="tab" tabindex="0">Two</button>
```

After:
```php
<button role="tab" tabindex="0" aria-selected="true">One</button><button role="tab" tabindex="-1" aria-selected="false">Two</button> <!-- Arrow keys update focus/selection. -->
```

#### Design blind indexes for the data’s leakage and threat model
- **Do:** Use a vetted keyed blind-index construction, scope keys appropriately, and assess equality/frequency leakage before indexing sensitive encrypted fields.
- **Flag when:** Flag when sensitive low-entropy fields use plaintext or unkeyed hashes as search indexes without a leakage assessment.
- **Why:** Deterministic indexes reveal repeated values; weak constructions can enable guessing or known-plaintext attacks.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$model->email_index = hash('sha256', $email);
```

After:
```php
// Use a vetted keyed blind-index implementation with managed keys
// and a documented field/domain-specific leakage assessment.
```

#### Optimize and measure before distributing the database
- **Do:** Keep the database architecture simple while it meets measured needs, and optimize queries/indexes/schema before adding servers for performance.
- **Flag when:** Flag when new replicas/shards are proposed without measuring and addressing avoidable query/schema costs.
- **Why:** Distribution adds consistency and operating complexity that should solve an observed capacity problem.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Separate central and tenant database connections
- **Do:** Define distinct central/landlord and tenant connections when using database-per-tenant isolation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when tenant switching mutates the central connection or central models follow the active tenant connection accidentally.
- **Why:** Separate connection roles preserve the boundary between tenant registry data and tenant business data.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Reuse and mutate the default central connection for every tenant.
```

After:
```php
'connections' => [
    'central' => [/* central database */],
    'tenant' => [/* tenant template, no central database target */],
],
```

#### Run schema updates for every tenant database
- **Do:** Apply tenant migrations to each tenant connection and track failures/completion independently from central migrations.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a release migrates only the central database while tenant schemas remain old.
- **Why:** Separate databases each need their own versioned schema progress.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Centralize tenant resource switching and cleanup
- **Do:** Switch database, cache namespace/store, and filesystem context through a coordinated tenant-switch lifecycle with matching cleanup.
- **Flag when:** Flag when independent request code switches only some tenant resources or fails to restore them.
- **Why:** Tenant isolation must cover every stateful backing resource consistently.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
config(['database.connections.tenant.database' => $name]); // Cache/disk and restoration omitted.
```

After:
```php
// config/multitenancy.php (Spatie tenancy integration)
'switch_tenant_tasks' => [
    SwitchTenantDatabaseTask::class,
    PrefixCacheTask::class,
    SwitchTenantDiskTask::class, // Application task with matching forgetCurrent cleanup.
],
```

#### Keep the transactional database authoritative for product data
- **Do:** Treat a search engine as a derived read index for large product search and validate authoritative product state in the transactional store.
- **Flag when:** Flag when checkout/pricing/inventory correctness depends only on a potentially stale search document.
- **Why:** Search indexes may update asynchronously and should not become the source of transactional truth.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$price = $searchHit['price']; // Used directly for the order amount.
```

After:
```php
$product = Product::findOrFail($searchHit['id']);
$price = $product->price; // Revalidate authoritative state during purchase.
```

#### Move multi-step database workflows into focused orchestration
- **Do:** Extract multi-step business/database orchestration from controllers into a service/action or pipeline of focused stages, with an explicit atomic boundary.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a controller performs a long chain of validation, row mutation, inventory/payment persistence, and side effects directly.
- **Why:** A focused orchestrator makes ordering and transaction scope easier to review and reuse.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function store(Request $request) { /* many ordered persistence steps */ }
```

After:
```php
public function store(StoreOrderRequest $request, PlaceOrder $action) {
    return new OrderResource($action->handle($request->validated()));
}
```

#### Verify replacement behavior through shadow replay
- **Do:** Replay captured events into an isolated shadow legacy-compatible schema and compare resulting data before a replacement cutover.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a gradual replacement changes persistence behavior without checking equivalence against representative legacy events.
- **Why:** Shadow replay exposes behavioral/data differences without changing the authoritative system.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep legacy and replacement systems interoperable during migration
- **Do:** Maintain explicit compatible integration contracts while legacy and replacement components coexist, and remove them only after migration completion.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a partial cutover breaks workflows that still cross the old/new system boundary.
- **Why:** Gradual migration requires both systems to cooperate until the remaining paths are moved.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Retain source events needed to rebuild changed projections
- **Do:** Retain replayable source events and verify projection rebuilds before changing or retiring a projection schema.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a projection drops data that cannot be reconstructed because source events were discarded.
- **Why:** A derived schema can evolve safely only if the necessary original facts remain available.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Retune database memory settings after server resizing
- **Do:** Review cache/buffer allocations and connection capacity after changing the database server’s memory/CPU size.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a resized database retains memory settings that overcommit the new host or waste its additional capacity.
- **Why:** Database memory settings do not always automatically track the host’s resources.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Target measured request bottlenecks before enabling JIT
- **Do:** Profile requests and optimize database/network I/O when they dominate latency rather than expecting PHP JIT to accelerate them.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a JIT rollout is justified as a fix for request time spent predominantly waiting on database/network calls.
- **Why:** JIT targets CPU execution; it does not remove external I/O wait.
- **Enforced by:** manual

### Eloquent

#### Exclude generated and tooling-only directories from Vite file watching
- **Do:** Keep vendor dependencies, compiled Blade views and generated agent metadata directories such as .agents, .claude, .cursor and .junie outside Vite development watch/refresh paths when those files are not frontend source.
- **Flag when:** Flag watch/refresh patterns that include generated views or tooling metadata and trigger needless reloads, file scans or watch loops.
- **Why:** Ignoring non-source churn avoids unnecessary rebuilds and reduces development watcher overhead.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
refresh: ['**/*'],
```

After:
```php
refresh: ['app/Livewire/**', 'resources/views/**', 'routes/**'],
// Keep tooling/generated directories outside refresh paths; add server.watch.ignored as needed.
```

#### Persist percentage-rollout decisions per Pennant scope
- **Do:** For a percentage rollout that should keep each user/entity in a stable cohort, define a Pennant feature with Lottery odds and a persistent driver so the initial result is stored per scope instead of rerolling on every request.
- **Flag when:** Flag a percentage-based feature gate that calls a random generator on every check even though users must remain in a stable rollout cohort.
- **Why:** Stored scope decisions keep a user experience consistent across requests while permitting a controlled percentage rollout.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$enabled = random_int(1, 100) <= 10;
```

After:
```php
Feature::define('new-checkout', fn (User $user) => Lottery::odds(1, 10));
$enabled = Feature::for($user)->active('new-checkout');
```

#### Delete Redis ingest entries only after their bounded batch is stored
- **Do:** When draining a Redis stream into durable telemetry storage, read a bounded batch, persist it successfully, then delete only the stream IDs in that completed batch; retain unprocessed entries after a failure.
- **Flag when:** Flag custom stream ingestion that deletes/trims entries before successful storage, clears more IDs than it persisted, or reads the entire backlog without a bound.
- **Why:** A persist-before-delete boundary prevents silent data loss and bounds memory; a crash between storage and deletion may cause a replay, so the destination must handle duplicates appropriately.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$redis->del($stream); // entries have not yet been persisted
```

After:
```php
$entries = $redis->xrange($stream, "-", "+", $batchSize);
$storage->store($entries);
$redis->xdel($stream, array_keys($entries));
```

#### Preserve Socialite authorization parameters through supported customization hooks
- **Do:** In custom OAuth2 Socialite providers, build authorization URLs with buildAuthUrlFromBase() and adapt scope separators/encoding through the provider extension points. Use with() only for provider-specific optional parameters, leaving state, response_type, client_id, redirect_uri, scope and enabled PKCE parameters to Socialite.
- **Flag when:** Flag hand-built authorization URLs that omit standard state/PKCE fields or with() payloads that override Socialite-owned protocol parameters.
- **Why:** Keeping protocol fields under the provider machinery preserves configured redirects, scope encoding and authentication-attempt integrity.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return Socialite::driver('google')->with(['state' => 'constant'])->redirect();
```

After:
```php
return Socialite::driver('google')->with(['hd' => 'example.com'])->redirect();
// Custom getAuthUrl($state): return $this->buildAuthUrlFromBase($endpoint, $state);
```

#### Omit unused exception bindings from catch clauses
- **Do:** Use catch (ExceptionType) without an exception variable when the handler does not read that exception; retain a binding when it is needed for reporting, chaining or recovery.
- **Flag when:** Flag catch clauses whose exception variable is never used and whose removal preserves the handler behavior.
- **Why:** An omitted binding makes it clear that handling depends on the exception type rather than its contents.
- **Enforced by:** rector:RemoveUnusedVariableInCatchRector

Before:
```php
try { $entry = $storage->find($id); } catch (ModelNotFoundException $e) { return null; }
```

After:
```php
try { $entry = $storage->find($id); } catch (ModelNotFoundException) { return null; }
```

#### Namespace package-owned database tables to avoid host collisions
- **Do:** Choose a stable package-specific prefix or configurable table-name namespace for package-owned persistence tables so they do not collide with host application or other package tables.
- **Flag when:** Flag package migrations that create broadly named tables such as entries or monitoring in the shared application database without a deliberate collision-avoidance namespace.
- **Why:** Namespaced persistence resources let independently installed packages share a database safely.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$schema->create('entries', $defineColumns); // reusable package schema
```

After:
```php
$schema->create('example_entries', $defineColumns);
```

#### Derive a configurable dashboard SPA router base from the server path
- **Do:** When a package dashboard uses history-based client routing, derive its router base and navigation URLs from the server-configured dashboard path, normalizing empty/root paths and slashes.
- **Flag when:** Flag a dashboard SPA that hard-codes /telescope or another default base while the server route prefix can be configured, or mishandles a root-mounted dashboard.
- **Why:** A shared base-path contract keeps deep links and client navigation working when the dashboard is moved.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
const history = createWebHistory('/telescope/'); // server prefix is configurable
```

After:
```php
const base = '/' + window.Dashboard.path.replace(/^\/+|\/+$/g, '');
const history = createWebHistory(base === '/' ? '/' : base + '/');
```

#### Normalize environment-derived configuration to the consumer type
- **Do:** In configuration files, normalize environment-derived values to the scalar type the consumer expects, using valid defaults and explicit parsing/validation where a simple cast would conceal invalid input.
- **Flag when:** Flag environment-derived configuration that reaches a strictly typed consumer with an unintended scalar type or relies on misleading raw string truthiness.
- **Why:** A stable configuration value type prevents environment-dependent type errors and inconsistent boolean or numeric behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'port' => env('SERVICE_PORT', '8080'), // integer consumer
```

After:
```php
'port' => (int) env('SERVICE_PORT', 8080), // validate the supported range as needed
```

#### Declare Vue component v-model contracts with typed defineModel
- **Do:** In Vue 3.4+ components using the script-setup convention, use typed defineModel() for component two-way binding contracts, including named models, instead of manually repeating matching model props and update events.
- **Flag when:** Flag new or substantially edited model-bound Vue components that duplicate the model prop/update-event protocol despite the installed Vue version supporting defineModel.
- **Why:** The macro keeps the prop and update event synchronized while retaining the value type expected by the parent.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
const props = defineProps<{ isOpen: boolean }>();
const emit = defineEmits<{ 'update:isOpen': [boolean] }>();
```

After:
```php
const isOpen = defineModel<boolean>('isOpen', { required: true });
```

#### Separate cold wide-table attributes only for a measured read benefit
- **Do:** When measurements show that a heavily read, very wide table carries substantial rarely used data, consider moving the cold attributes into a separate related table/model and load that data only for operations that need it.
- **Flag when:** Flag a proven wide-row read or working-set bottleneck where large rarely read attributes are fetched on every hot path without considering a targeted projection or vertical partition.
- **Why:** Separating cold data can reduce common read volume and working-set size when the extra relationship and consistency cost is justified.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Every hot user read fetches a large rarely used legacy metadata payload.
```

After:
```php
// Keep hot user fields together; put proven cold metadata in a related record loaded only by its consumers.
```

#### Register the actual Cashier billable model through its supported boot hook
- **Do:** When the billable model is not App\Models\User, register it with Cashier::useCustomerModel() in a service provider boot() method before billing lookups run. Use the supported registration hook rather than assuming CASHIER_MODEL or cashier.model selects it.
- **Flag when:** Flag a non-default billable model whose Cashier registration is missing or placed only in a nonexistent environment/config option.
- **Why:** Cashier customer resolution must use the model that owns the stored Stripe customer identifiers.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'model' => env('CASHIER_MODEL', App\Models\Account::class), // Cashier does not read this option
```

After:
```php
public function boot(): void { \Laravel\Cashier\Cashier::useCustomerModel(\App\Models\Account::class); }
```

#### Keep Cashier subscription predicates and query scopes consistent
- **Do:** Use Cashier active() and active query-scope semantics for activity checks. In custom subscription models, keep both implementations consistent with the configured deactivatePastDue and deactivateIncomplete policy; both states are inactive by default. Preserve the other ended, unpaid and expired-incomplete exclusions.
- **Flag when:** Flag custom activity checks or scopes that disagree for the same subscription, ignore Cashier activity-policy flags, or treat every non-canceled subscription as active.
- **Why:** Entitlement decisions must not change depending on whether a subscription was checked in memory or selected by a database query.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$active = $subscription->stripe_status !== 'canceled';
```

After:
```php
$active = $subscription->active();
$activeSubscriptions = Subscription::query()->active()->get();
```

#### Keep synchronized local copies of vendor details needed only for display
- **Do:** For frequently rendered vendor details that are safe to cache, keep the required display fields on the local model and update them when the vendor state changes. For payment-method labels, retain only display metadata such as type and last four digits.
- **Flag when:** Flag a routine display path that retrieves unchanged payment-method metadata from the vendor on every render, or a local display snapshot with no synchronization path.
- **Why:** A local display snapshot removes unnecessary network latency and vendor availability from ordinary page rendering.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$lastFour = $user->defaultPaymentMethod()->card->last4; // vendor call during rendering
```

After:
```php
$lastFour = $user->pm_last_four; // synchronized when the default payment method changes
```

#### Honor model configuration hooks before package defaults
- **Do:** When a package exposes a model-specific configuration hook, use that hook consistently before falling back to package defaults. Use preferredCurrency() for Cashier operations that consult the billable currency, and honor an available typesenseCollectionSchema() override before the configured default schema.
- **Flag when:** Flag package or integration code that reads a global default directly despite a supported model override, or documents a model override that its consumers ignore.
- **Why:** A model override only works when every relevant consumer respects its precedence over the default configuration.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$currency = config('cashier.currency'); // ignores the supported customer override
```

After:
```php
$currency = $customer->preferredCurrency();
```

#### Fill vendor payload defaults without overwriting explicit caller values
- **Do:** When building a vendor payload from caller options and model hooks, fill a default only when the caller omitted the key. Use a presence check such as array_key_exists() when explicit null is a meaningful caller choice.
- **Flag when:** Flag defaults from model hooks that overwrite an explicitly supplied payload value, including null, because the builder uses truthiness, isset() or null coalescing as a missing-key test.
- **Why:** Caller intent must retain precedence over inferred model defaults, including deliberate clearing of optional vendor fields.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$options['name'] = $options['name'] ?? $customer->stripeName();
```

After:
```php
if (! array_key_exists('name', $options) && ($name = $customer->stripeName())) { $options['name'] = $name; }
```

#### Preserve provider cursor semantics when adapting external lists to Laravel pagination
- **Do:** When wrapping a cursor-based vendor list in a Laravel CursorPaginator, translate the cursor direction and boundary identifier into the provider next/previous parameters, preserve the expected item order, and supply enough page information to determine whether another page exists.
- **Flag when:** Flag an external cursor adapter that sends starting_after for previous-page navigation, loses provider boundaries, or builds pagination metadata from an already-truncated list without has-more information.
- **Why:** A paginator wrapper must preserve the provider traversal contract to avoid repeated, skipped or reversed pages.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$parameters['starting_after'] = $cursor->parameter('id'); // also used for previous pages
```

After:
```php
$parameters[$cursor->pointsToNextItems() ? 'starting_after' : 'ending_before'] = $cursor->parameter('id');
```

#### Announce a presence member only on their first channel connection
- **Do:** In custom presence-channel implementations, register every physical connection but emit member_added only when the user first becomes present in that application and channel. Additional tabs or devices for the same user must not create duplicate membership announcements.
- **Flag when:** Flag presence bookkeeping that emits member_added for every socket connection or skips registering a second connection because its user is already present.
- **Why:** Presence membership describes users; multiple simultaneous connections must not appear as repeated joins by the same member.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Dispatch optional driver behavior through capability contracts
- **Do:** When selecting an optional operation on a resolved driver, check its capability interface with instanceof rather than comparing configured driver names. Keep a defined unsupported-capability path.
- **Flag when:** Flag optional engine behavior selected by a hard-coded driver-name allowlist despite an available capability contract, excluding compatible custom drivers or accepting an incompatible implementation.
- **Why:** Capabilities describe what the actual implementation supports, including third-party drivers registered under new names.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
if (config('scout.driver') === 'meilisearch') { /* assume capability */ }
```

After:
```php
if ($engine instanceof \Laravel\Scout\Contracts\UpdatesIndexSettings) { /* invoke supported settings operation */ }
```

#### Limit import progress listeners to the command operation lifetime
- **Do:** For commands that temporarily subscribe to import chunk events, report completed-chunk progress from those events and release the temporary registration when the operation completes or fails. Preserve unrelated listeners already registered on a shared dispatcher.
- **Flag when:** Flag command-local progress listeners that accumulate across repeated command invocations, outlive the import, or remove unrelated shared handlers during cleanup.
- **Why:** An operation-scoped listener provides useful progress without duplicate callbacks or retained command state in a reused process.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Restore search hit order after hydrating Eloquent models
- **Do:** When an external search engine returns ranked identifiers and a second query hydrates the models, restore the engine hit order before returning the collection. Do not assume a database whereIn query preserves the identifier order.
- **Flag when:** Flag a custom Scout engine or search adapter that returns hydration-query order instead of the search engine relevance order.
- **Why:** Fetching matching rows and preserving their relevance ranking are separate operations; SQL membership filtering does not retain input order.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return $models; // order from a whereIn hydration query
```

After:
```php
$positions = array_flip($hitIds);
return $models->filter(fn ($model) => isset($positions[$model->getScoutKey()]))->sortBy(fn ($model) => $positions[$model->getScoutKey()])->values();
```

#### Restrict bulk search-index deletion to the application namespace
- **Do:** On shared search infrastructure, delete only indexes proven to belong to the intended application and environment. If ownership is expressed with scout.prefix, require a nonempty, unambiguous prefix and restrict deletion to that namespace; otherwise use an explicit owned-index list.
- **Flag when:** Flag delete-all-index operations that delete every discovered index, treat an empty prefix as isolation, or can match another application namespace.
- **Why:** Bulk index cleanup must not erase another application or environment sharing the same search service.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
foreach ($indexes as $index) { $index->delete(); }
```

After:
```php
if ($prefix === '') { throw new LogicException('An isolated index namespace is required'); }
foreach ($indexes as $index) { if (str_starts_with($index->getUid(), $prefix)) { $index->delete(); } }
```

#### Persist derived search columns without retriggering model lifecycle effects
- **Do:** When writing derived search data such as an embedding after model persistence, use a deliberately scoped base-query update if model events and updated_at changes must be bypassed. Restrict the row by its stable key and any required tenant boundary, prepare the storage value explicitly, and update the in-memory attribute if the instance is reused.
- **Flag when:** Flag a derived embedding write that recursively triggers indexing observers or changes business timestamps, or an event-free base write that omits required row scope or storage conversion.
- **Why:** Derived indexing work should not start another model lifecycle or appear as a new business edit; bypassing Eloquent also makes row scope and value encoding the caller responsibility.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$model->update(['embedding' => $vector]); // can trigger indexing observers again
```

After:
```php
$model->newQuery()->whereKey($model->getKey())->toBase()->update(['embedding' => json_encode($vector, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR)]);
$model->setAttribute('embedding', $vector);
```

#### Configure Scout embedding inputs and its AI generation dependency
- **Do:** For an installed Scout engine that supports Scout-generated embeddings, implement toSearchableEmbedding() with the intended nonempty source text or a compatible precomputed vector array. Install and configure laravel/ai whenever Scout generates document or query embeddings.
- **Flag when:** Flag Scout-generated embedding paths without the AI SDK/provider configuration, or a model embedding hook returning neither supported source text nor a usable vector array.
- **Why:** Scout needs an explicit embedding source and its generation dependency; precomputed document vectors can avoid document-generation calls but do not supply query embeddings automatically.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Read collection identifiers through Eloquent model key metadata
- **Do:** When extracting the primary keys of an Eloquent collection, use modelKeys() rather than hard-coding an id attribute.
- **Flag when:** Flag pluck('id') when the operation means model primary keys and supports configurable or nonstandard keys.
- **Why:** Model key metadata keeps identifier extraction correct when the primary key is renamed.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$ids = $models->pluck('id')->all();
```

After:
```php
$ids = $models->modelKeys();
```

#### Defer expensive conditional resource values with closures
- **Do:** Pass a closure for an expensive conditional JsonResource value so the computation runs only when the field is included.
- **Flag when:** Flag a costly method call evaluated before when() rejects the field.
- **Why:** Function arguments are evaluated eagerly unless the computation is deferred.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'report' => $this->when($includeReport, $this->buildReport()),
```

After:
```php
'report' => $this->when($includeReport, fn () => $this->buildReport()),
```

#### Bound client-requested JSON:API include depth
- **Do:** Retain a deliberate maximum relationship depth for JSON:API includes. Configure JsonApiResource::maxRelationshipDepth() when the default does not fit the endpoint, alongside explicit relationship exposure and authorization.
- **Flag when:** Flag an excessive include-depth override that permits unexpectedly deep relationship traversal.
- **Why:** Bounded include depth limits response expansion and relationship query work.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
JsonApiResource::maxRelationshipDepth(100);
```

After:
```php
JsonApiResource::maxRelationshipDepth(3); // chosen from endpoint requirements
```

#### Use Scout lifecycle synchronization for ordinarily saved searchable models
- **Do:** Use Scout Searchable on models whose search index should follow ordinary Eloquent create/update/delete operations. Configure the engine and indexing payload, and handle bulk writes that bypass events separately.
- **Flag when:** Flag duplicated manual index synchronization for normal model lifecycle writes when the application has adopted Scout for those models.
- **Why:** Scout provides a consistent synchronization boundary for ordinary persisted models.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$article->save();
$searchClient->indexArticle($article); // repeated across normal write entry points
```

After:
```php
class Article extends Model { use \Laravel\Scout\Searchable; }
```

#### Close terminal prompt streams after incremental output
- **Do:** Use the Prompts stream abstraction for incrementally arriving terminal text, and close it on completion or failure so terminal cursor state is restored.
- **Flag when:** Flag a manually appended prompt stream left open when generation exits or throws.
- **Why:** Stream cleanup restores terminal state and prevents subsequent output from rendering incorrectly.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$stream->append($chunk); // command exits without closing
```

After:
```php
try { foreach ($chunks as $chunk) { $stream->append($chunk); } } finally { $stream->close(); }
```

#### Use typed Cashier webhook events for package-aware reactions
- **Do:** For application reactions to supported Cashier Paddle webhook types, listen to the corresponding package event when it supplies the processed billable/subscription models, rather than reimplementing raw webhook parsing and model resolution.
- **Flag when:** Flag raw webhook-type branching that duplicates Cashier event dispatch and related-model resolution for an already supported event.
- **Why:** Typed events reuse the package processing boundary and model context.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
if ($payload['event_type'] === 'subscription.created') { $billable = lookupCustomer($payload); }
```

After:
```php
Register an application listener for Laravel\Paddle\Events\SubscriptionCreated.
```

#### Make Carbon 3 difference rounding and direction explicit
- **Do:** Audit diffIn* consumers for Carbon 3 floating-point and signed results. Explicitly choose absolute versus directional differences and the rounding/truncation required by an integer contract.
- **Flag when:** Flag a Carbon 2 assumption that diffInDays() always returns a nonnegative integer.
- **Why:** A changed difference type or sign can alter thresholds, billing and displayed durations.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$days = $start->diffInDays($end); // assumed unsigned int
```

After:
```php
$days = (int) $start->diffInDays($end, true); // explicit absolute, truncated whole days
```

#### Add SQL bindings while building clauses, before grammar compilation
- **Do:** In custom builder extensions, add values to the matching builder binding group when adding the clause. Keep grammar compilation free of binding mutations so later clauses cannot reorder placeholders relative to bindings.
- **Flag when:** Flag a grammar compile method that calls addBinding() or mutates the query bindings.
- **Why:** Bindings must remain in the same order as their placeholders as the query is composed.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// In Grammar::compileCustom(): $query->addBinding($value);
```

After:
```php
// When adding the where clause:
$query->addBinding($value, 'where');
// Grammar compilation only emits SQL.
```

#### Configure resource collection items as resources rather than models
- **Do:** Set ResourceCollection item metadata ($collects or #[Collects]) to a JsonResource subclass, not an Eloquent model class.
- **Flag when:** Flag a collection configured to collect User::class instead of UserResource::class.
- **Why:** The collection invokes resource transformation behavior on each item.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public $collects = User::class;
```

After:
```php
public $collects = UserResource::class;
```

#### Declare custom cast read and write generic types
- **Do:** Annotate a custom CastsAttributes implementation with its actual getter and setter types so analysis can follow the attribute conversion contract.
- **Flag when:** Flag an unparameterized custom cast interface or generic types inconsistent with get()/set() behavior.
- **Why:** Precise cast generics expose attribute type mistakes before execution.
- **Enforced by:** partial: larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Generics\ClassAncestorsRule

Before:
```php
class MoneyCast implements CastsAttributes { /* ... */ }
```

After:
```php
/** @implements CastsAttributes<Money, Money|int> */
class MoneyCast implements CastsAttributes { /* matching get/set */ }
```

#### Preserve historical creation order when backfilling time-based ULIDs
- **Do:** When an integer-to-ULID migration must retain creation-time ordering, derive each new ULID from that record original creation timestamp and preserve uniqueness and reference mappings. Do not timestamp every historical row at migration time.
- **Flag when:** Flag a historical ULID backfill using only the current time despite a required chronological key order.
- **Why:** ULID ordering follows the encoded timestamp, not the old integer key.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$newId = (string) Str::ulid(); // all historical rows get migration-time timestamps
```

After:
```php
$newId = (string) Str::ulid($record->created_at);
```

#### Run pruning-wide maintenance from pruning-run events
- **Do:** Use ModelPruningStarting/ModelPruningFinished for maintenance that belongs once around a model:prune run, instead of repeating it in per-model or per-chunk pruning callbacks.
- **Flag when:** Flag expensive post-prune maintenance executed once per chunk when it is needed only after the command finishes.
- **Why:** Run-level hooks avoid repeated maintenance and identify the completed operation boundary.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// ModelPruning per chunk: run ANALYZE TABLE repeatedly
```

After:
```php
Listen to Illuminate\Database\Events\ModelPruningFinished for required post-run maintenance.
```

#### Choose JSON casts that preserve required object versus array shape
- **Do:** If a JSON attribute must round-trip an object including {}, use an object-preserving cast or custom value type. Do not rely on array or AsArrayObject casts to preserve the empty-object distinction.
- **Flag when:** Flag an object-shaped JSON contract that becomes [] after an array-based cast and save/serialization cycle.
- **Why:** Empty JSON objects and arrays are distinct values even when PHP array conversion makes them look alike.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
protected function casts(): array { return ['settings' => 'array']; } // requires {}
```

After:
```php
protected function casts(): array { return ['settings' => 'object']; }
```

#### Keep model trait initializers independent of trait iteration order
- **Do:** Make each model trait initializer safe without assuming another trait initializer has already executed. Move cross-trait orchestration to an explicit phase that has the required state; booted callbacks are suitable only for class-level registration, not as a substitute for completed per-instance initialization.
- **Flag when:** Flag an initializeTrait method that reads another trait initialized property before it is guaranteed to exist.
- **Why:** Trait composition order is a fragile dependency for object state.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function initializeHasInvoice(): void { $this->invoice = buildFrom($this->otherTraitState); }
```

After:
```php
public function initializeHasInvoice(): void { $this->invoice = null; }
// Derive cross-trait state explicitly after construction when required.
```

#### Exclude database-generated columns from model writes and replication
- **Do:** Let the database compute generated columns. Exclude them from insert/update input, and omit their copied attributes when replicating an existing model.
- **Flag when:** Flag an explicit assignment to a database-generated column or a replicate() insert carrying its old generated value.
- **Why:** Generated columns are derived by the database and often reject ordinary explicit values.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$copy = $invoice->replicate();
$copy->save(); // copies generated total
```

After:
```php
$copy = $invoice->replicate(['total']);
$copy->save();
```

#### Provide both numeric deviation methods for numeric custom casts
- **Do:** For custom numeric casts used with Eloquent increment()/decrement(), implement both deviation methods with the correct storage-value semantics, using DeviatesCastableAttributes when declaring that capability.
- **Flag when:** Flag a custom numeric cast relied upon for atomic counter updates with only one deviation method or with values in the wrong storage units.
- **Why:** Laravel recognizes deviation support only when increment and decrement are both present.
- **Enforced by:** partial: larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Methods\MissingMethodImplementationRule

Before:
```php
class AmountCast implements CastsAttributes { /* getter/setter only, callers expect domain-aware increment */ }
```

After:
```php
class AmountCast implements CastsAttributes, DeviatesCastableAttributes { /* get, set, increment and decrement with matching units */ }
```

#### Keep broadcasts on approved infrastructure when payload residency requires it
- **Do:** When broadcast data policy prohibits sending payloads to a third-party realtime provider, use an approved self-hosted Reverb deployment or another compliant transport, with authenticated channels and protected connections.
- **Flag when:** Flag confidential realtime payloads routed to an unapproved external broadcaster despite an explicit infrastructure boundary.
- **Why:** Private-channel authorization alone does not stop the hosting provider from processing the payload.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Measure and provision private-channel authorization traffic
- **Do:** Include broadcasting/auth in monitoring and capacity planning when many private-channel subscriptions generate repeated authorization requests. Measure its request volume, latency and database cost as subscriptions reconnect or fan out.
- **Flag when:** Flag a high-channel-count realtime application whose authorization endpoint load is omitted from capacity and performance checks.
- **Why:** Subscription authorization can be one of the busiest application endpoints.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Own transferable company resources at the organization boundary
- **Do:** When infrastructure resources must survive employee changes or company/project transfers, model ownership through an organization/account rather than an individual user. Grant people membership and permissions separately.
- **Flag when:** Flag a company-owned server or credential whose lifetime and transferability are inseparable from one employee account.
- **Why:** Organization ownership supports membership changes and explicit resource transfer.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Server belongs directly and permanently to its creator User.
```

After:
```php
Server belongs to Organization; users receive authorized organization memberships.
```

#### Check named product entitlements instead of scattering plan names
- **Do:** Centralize subscription-to-capability mapping and ask whether the account is entitled to the requested feature or limit. Avoid repeating plan-name comparisons throughout application code.
- **Flag when:** Flag duplicated hard-coded plan-name checks for the same capability across controllers, views and jobs.
- **Why:** Entitlement changes should be implemented once when plans or product packaging change.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
if ($team->plan === 'pro') { exportReport(); }
```

After:
```php
if ($entitlements->allows($team, 'report-export')) { exportReport(); }
```

#### Represent variable-length related values as rows rather than numbered columns
- **Do:** Store a variable number of related items in a child or association table with deliberate ordering and keys, instead of adding item_1/item_2/item_3 columns whenever cardinality grows.
- **Flag when:** Flag numbered repeated columns whose count can grow with ordinary domain data.
- **Why:** Adding an item should add data rather than require a schema change.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
questions: answer_1_text, answer_2_text, answer_3_text
```

After:
```php
questions -> hasMany answers; answers: question_id, text, position
```

#### Bound retained container images and registry permissions
- **Do:** Configure lifecycle/retention rules for obsolete container images while retaining required release/rollback images. Grant push and pull privileges only to the deployment actors that need each operation.
- **Flag when:** Flag an actively used deployment registry with unlimited obsolete image growth or unnecessarily broad push permissions.
- **Why:** Registry retention and scoped credentials control storage growth and unauthorized image replacement.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Inspect the existing database schema before changing models or migrations
- **Do:** Inspect the existing database schema before changing models or migrations.
- **Flag when:** Flag when model or migration changes assume columns, keys or types that disagree with the deployed schema.
- **Why:** Schema inspection prevents incompatible migrations and incorrect relationship definitions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Schema::table('users', fn (Blueprint $table) => $table->string('external_id')); // existing type unchecked
```

After:
```php
$columns = Schema::getColumns('users'); // inspect types/indexes before drafting the migration
```

#### Filter package documentation searches to the relevant installed packages
- **Do:** Filter Boost documentation searches to the relevant installed packages and pass search text through the queries array.
- **Flag when:** Flag known-package documentation searches that omit the packages filter or use the unsupported singular query parameter.
- **Why:** Package filters reduce irrelevant guidance and version confusion.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
{"queries":["casts"]}
```

After:
```php
{"queries":["casts"],"packages":["laravel/framework"]}
```

#### Mirror database defaults in model attributes only when unsaved models need them, and keep both definitions synchronized
- **Do:** When a model's $attributes mirrors a column default, keep both values identical. Add the mirror only when application code must observe the default before the model is saved.
- **Flag when:** Flag a model $attributes default that differs from the migration/schema default for the same column.
- **Why:** Database defaults apply at insert time; matching model defaults make pre-persistence behavior predictable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
protected $attributes = ['active' => true]; // DB default is false
```

After:
```php
protected $attributes = ['active' => false];
```

#### Document deliberate repository choices that differ from active tooling defaults
- **Do:** Document deliberate repository choices that differ from active tooling defaults.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the project intentionally keeps legacy accessors or binding conventions but agent instructions do not record that exception.
- **Why:** Explicit exceptions prevent automated work from repeatedly undoing intentional choices.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Model convention is implicit.
```

After:
```php
// app/Models/**: retain legacy getXAttribute accessors in this codebase.
```

#### Confirm nonstandard application directories represent repeated patterns before documenting them as conventions
- **Do:** Confirm nonstandard application directories represent repeated patterns before documenting them as conventions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a convention mandates an architecture solely because an empty or generator-created directory exists.
- **Why:** Observed repeated use is better evidence than directory presence alone.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Empty app/Observers implies all events must use observers.
```

After:
```php
// Document observer ownership only after reviewing representative event handlers.
```

#### Document cross-domain conventions under each relevant path scope
- **Do:** Document cross-domain conventions under each relevant path scope.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a convention coupling model keys to migrations is discoverable from only one affected directory.
- **Why:** Both editing contexts need the same invariant to avoid incompatible changes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// UUID rule only applies to app/Models/**.
```

After:
```php
// UUID rule applies to app/Models/** and database/migrations/**.
```

#### Require an explicit authorized purpose before writing persistent data from Tinker
- **Do:** Require an explicit authorized purpose before writing persistent data from Tinker.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a debugging workflow creates or modifies live records merely to inspect behavior.
- **Why:** Read-only investigation avoids accidental persistent state changes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// tinker: User::factory()->create();
```

After:
```php
// tinker: User::query()->limit(5)->get();
```

#### Declare the Rapyd validation rules needed to preserve edited unsaved model attributes
- **Do:** In modern Livewire forms, expose explicit scalar properties or a Form object, validate that state, then fill and save an authorized model.
- **Flag when:** Flag legacy direct model-property bindings or rules relied on to hydrate an unsaved Eloquent model across modern Livewire requests.
- **Why:** Rapyd only carries allowed unsaved attributes across Livewire requests.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
<input wire:model="model.title">
```

After:
```php
public string $title = "";
public function save(): void
{
    $data = $this->validate(["title" => "required|string"]);
    $post = auth()->user()->posts()->findOrFail($this->postId);
    $this->authorize("update", $post);
    $post->update($data);
}
// <input wire:model="title">
```

#### Extract repeated domain checks into clearly named model methods
- **Do:** Extract repeated domain checks into clearly named model methods.
- **Flag when:** Flag when callers repeat the same compound model-state condition.
- **Why:** A shared predicate keeps domain decisions consistent.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
if ($user->approved_at && ! $user->suspended_at) { /* ... */ }
```

After:
```php
if ($user->isApproved()) { /* ... */ }
```

#### Migrate incompatible column types through a new column and a bounded verified backfill
- **Do:** Migrate incompatible column types through a new column and a bounded verified backfill.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a migration casts incompatible data in place without transformation or completeness checks.
- **Why:** A staged transformation preserves data and gives a validation point before replacement; use DDL transactions only where the database supports them.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Create a custom pivot model only when the pivot needs additional behavior
- **Do:** Create a custom pivot model only when the pivot needs additional behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a dedicated pivot class adds no casts, methods or lifecycle behavior.
- **Why:** Ordinary belongsToMany already handles the intermediate table.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class RoleUser extends Pivot {}
```

After:
```php
return $this->belongsToMany(Role::class);
```

#### Provide concrete application-user type information for authenticated-user values
- **Do:** Provide concrete application-user type information for authenticated-user values.
- **Flag when:** Flag when analysis sees only the authentication contract when code requires application-specific user members.
- **Why:** Accurate type information enables member checking without unchecked dynamic assumptions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$user = Auth::user(); // application fields unknown
```

After:
```php
/** @var User|null $user */
$user = Auth::user();
```

#### Load subtype-specific relationships through an STI-aware loading API
- **Do:** Load subtype-specific relationships through an STI-aware loading API.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a mixed STI collection loads a relationship absent from some concrete types.
- **Why:** Type-aware loading avoids undefined relationship errors.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$mixed->load('author');
```

After:
```php
Entry::query()->childrenWith([Post::class => ['author']])->get();
```

#### Use AsArrayObject when JSON attributes must support direct nested-offset mutation
- **Do:** Use AsArrayObject when JSON attributes must support direct nested-offset mutation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when code modifies offsets on an array-cast attribute through the model property.
- **Why:** A primitive array cast does not provide the mutable object behavior needed for indirect offset changes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$user->settings['theme'] = 'dark'; // array cast
```

After:
```php
protected function casts(): array { return ['settings' => AsArrayObject::class]; }
```

#### Disable object caching for accessors that must return a fresh value on every access
- **Do:** Disable object caching for accessors that must return a fresh value on every access.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an object accessor reuses a stale object despite a fresh-value contract.
- **Why:** Eloquent retains accessor objects by default, so fresh values need an explicit exception.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return Attribute::get(fn () => $this->freshSnapshot());
```

After:
```php
return Attribute::get(fn () => $this->freshSnapshot())->withoutObjectCaching();
```

#### Reset long-lived diagnostic aggregation state after storing a batch
- **Do:** Reset long-lived diagnostic aggregation state after storing a batch.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom Telescope watcher retains model counters across request or storage boundaries.
- **Why:** Resetting state prevents cross-request contamination and growing memory.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Static counters accumulate after store.
```

After:
```php
// Clear counters from the Telescope after-storing lifecycle callback.
```

#### Handle soft deletion and restoration explicitly in search synchronization
- **Do:** Handle soft deletion and restoration explicitly in search synchronization.
- **Flag when:** Flag when search results retain hidden records or restored records stay absent contrary to the search policy.
- **Why:** The search lifecycle must match the application visibility rules.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Index synchronization handles saved only.
```

After:
```php
// Configure Scout soft-delete behavior and test delete/restore visibility.
```

#### Validate Reverb HTTP event payloads before broadcasting them
- **Do:** Validate Reverb HTTP event payloads before broadcasting them.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an event endpoint broadcasts malformed or unchecked client fields.
- **Why:** Validation gives broadcast consumers a stable event contract.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
broadcast($request->all());
```

After:
```php
$payload = $request->validate($eventRules); // broadcast only validated fields
```

#### Scope npm credentials to the site that needs them
- **Do:** Scope npm credentials to the site that needs them.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a site-specific registry token is configured globally across unrelated sites.
- **Why:** Narrow credential scope limits unintended package-registry access.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use environment-scoped IAM roles with rotating credentials instead of static cloud keys
- **Do:** Use environment-scoped IAM roles with rotating credentials instead of static cloud keys.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Private Cloud environments rely on shared long-lived AWS access keys.
- **Why:** Scoped temporary credentials reduce cross-environment access and credential exposure.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Declare only available relationships in model eager-load defaults
- **Do:** Declare only available relationships in model eager-load defaults.
- **Flag when:** Flag when with or withCount defaults refer to undefined relations.
- **Why:** Invalid defaults make otherwise unrelated model queries fail.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:ModelRelationDefaultsRule

Before:
```php
protected $with = ['missingRelation'];
```

After:
```php
protected $with = ['team']; // team() is defined
```

#### Import Laravel classes explicitly instead of relying on global aliases
- **Do:** Import Laravel classes explicitly instead of relying on global aliases.
- **Flag when:** Flag when code relies on global Broadcast or Eloquent aliases that analysis or runtime configuration may not supply.
- **Why:** Explicit imports make dependencies unambiguous.
- **Enforced by:** rector:RenameClassRector

Before:
```php
class User extends Eloquent {}
```

After:
```php
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
class User extends Model {}
```

#### Use collection all() when nested model objects must remain objects
- **Do:** Use collection all() when nested model objects must remain objects.
- **Flag when:** Flag when toArray recursively converts models despite the caller needing raw collection elements.
- **Why:** all preserves element instances while toArray intentionally serializes nested Arrayable values.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$models = $users->toArray(); // caller expects User objects
```

After:
```php
$models = $users->all();
```

#### Memoize a lazy sequence only when repeated enumeration is required and retained memory is acceptable
- **Do:** Memoize a lazy sequence only when repeated enumeration is required and retained memory is acceptable.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a one-shot lazy database sequence is enumerated repeatedly and repeats database work.
- **Why:** remember reuses enumerated values but retains them, so it changes the memory tradeoff.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$users = User::cursor(); $users->each($a); $users->each($b);
```

After:
```php
$users = User::cursor()->remember(); $users->each($a); $users->each($b);
```

#### Exclude oversized tool events from broadcasts and retrieve their full data from stored messages
- **Do:** Exclude oversized tool events from broadcasts and retrieve their full data from stored messages.
- **Flag when:** Flag when AI stream tool events exceed transport payload limits.
- **Why:** Small broadcast events keep the stream reliable while persisted messages retain full results.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Broadcast full multi-megabyte tool results.
```

After:
```php
#[WithoutBroadcasting(ToolCall::class, ToolResult::class)]
class ResearchAgent implements Agent { /* fetch full stored messages after completion */ }
```

#### Provide a web-search tool when agents must answer time-sensitive questions
- **Do:** Provide a web-search tool when agents must answer time-sensitive questions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an agent promises current information with no retrieval source.
- **Why:** Retrieval supplies evidence beyond model training data.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Current-events agent has no retrieval tool.
```

After:
```php
// Register the provider WebSearch tool and require source-grounded answers.
```

#### Verify provider and model capabilities before relying on tools or multimodal input restrictions
- **Do:** Verify provider and model capabilities before relying on tools or multimodal input restrictions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when code assumes a provider honors unsupported web filters, code execution or embedding modalities.
- **Why:** Provider capabilities differ and may change, so unsupported assumptions break behavior or policy.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Assume every provider enforces WebSearch allow domains.
```

After:
```php
// Check current provider docs and enforce required restrictions in application code where necessary.
```

#### Cast database vector attributes with AsVector when application code needs numeric vectors
- **Do:** Cast database vector attributes with AsVector when application code needs numeric vectors.
- **Flag when:** Flag when vector columns are consumed as driver-specific raw values rather than the expected float arrays.
- **Why:** A vector cast normalizes database/application representation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// embedding is an unparsed database vector string.
```

After:
```php
protected function casts(): array { return ['embedding' => AsVector::class]; }
```

#### Give MCP prompts and resources meaningful descriptions
- **Do:** Give MCP prompts and resources meaningful descriptions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a prompt or resource lacks a useful description of its purpose.
- **Why:** Descriptions make available context and prompt capabilities discoverable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class InvoiceGuide extends Resource {}
```

After:
```php
#[Description('Invoice field definitions for interpreting billing records.')] class InvoiceGuide extends Resource {}
```

#### Enforce MCP access policy in application authorization rather than unsupported custom OAuth scopes
- **Do:** Enforce MCP access policy in application authorization rather than unsupported custom OAuth scopes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when MCP access control assumes arbitrary Passport scopes are enforced by the MCP integration.
- **Why:** The integration scope does not replace per-user or per-tool authorization.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Assume a custom token scope alone protects a tool.
```

After:
```php
// Enforce the authenticated user policy in tool/server authorization.
```

#### Use a model-aware exists rule when validation must follow model table and connection configuration
- **Do:** Use a model-aware exists rule when validation must follow model table and connection configuration.
- **Flag when:** Flag when validation hard-codes a table that differs from the intended model configuration.
- **Why:** Model-aware validation avoids table/connection drift.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'user_id' => 'exists:users,id'
```

After:
```php
'user_id' => [Rule::exists(User::class, 'id')]
```

#### Store model default attributes in raw database format
- **Do:** Store model default attributes in raw database format.
- **Flag when:** Flag when model defaults contain PHP objects or arrays that require casts before storage.
- **Why:** Eloquent initializes raw attributes, so defaults must match their stored representation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
protected $attributes = ['options' => []];
```

After:
```php
protected $attributes = ['options' => '[]'];
```

#### Refresh database-generated attributes after writes when callers need their current values
- **Do:** Refresh database-generated attributes after writes when callers need their current values.
- **Flag when:** Flag when application code reads a stale generated attribute immediately after saving.
- **Why:** Database-calculated values are not necessarily reflected in an existing model instance.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Save then read a stale computed total.
```

After:
```php
#[Refreshes(['total'])] class Order extends Model {}
```

#### Review pruning predicates as permanent-deletion policy, including soft-deleted models
- **Do:** Review pruning predicates as permanent-deletion policy, including soft-deleted models.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a broad prunable query permanently deletes recoverable records before their retention deadline.
- **Why:** Pruning force-deletes matching soft-deletable models, so the cutoff must be deliberate.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return static::query();
```

After:
```php
return static::onlyTrashed()->where('deleted_at', '<=', now()->subDays(30));
```

#### Use addSelect() when a global scope augments selected columns
- **Do:** Use addSelect() when a global scope augments selected columns.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a global scope calls select and overwrites caller projections.
- **Why:** Augmenting the selection preserves the query caller contract.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$builder->select('computed');
```

After:
```php
$builder->addSelect('computed');
```

#### Guard saved/saving side effects when they should run only for actual attribute changes
- **Do:** Guard saved/saving side effects when they should run only for actual attribute changes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a saving/saved handler repeats side effects on unchanged saves.
- **Why:** These lifecycle events can fire even without dirty attributes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
static::saved(fn ($model) => sendChangedNotification($model));
```

After:
```php
static::saved(function ($model) { if ($model->wasChanged('status')) { sendChangedNotification($model); } });
```

#### Avoid one-of-many aggregates over PostgreSQL UUID columns unless the database supports the required aggregate
- **Do:** Avoid one-of-many aggregates over PostgreSQL UUID columns unless the database supports the required aggregate.
- **Flag when:** Flag when ofMany/latestOfMany generates MAX over a UUID column on a PostgreSQL installation without that aggregate.
- **Why:** Unsupported UUID aggregation fails at query time; choose an aggregatable selection column or supported design.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return $this->orders()->one()->latestOfMany(); // PostgreSQL UUID key
```

After:
```php
// Select by an aggregatable sequence/tie-breaker supported by the database.
```

#### Use withPivotValue() when a pivot constraint must also apply to new attachments
- **Do:** Use withPivotValue() when a pivot constraint must also apply to new attachments.
- **Flag when:** Flag when wherePivot filters an association but new records omit the required pivot state.
- **Why:** A filter alone does not supply inserted pivot values.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return $this->belongsToMany(Role::class)->wherePivot('approved', 1);
```

After:
```php
return $this->belongsToMany(Role::class)->withPivotValue('approved', 1);
```

#### Use a regular model when an association record needs soft deletion
- **Do:** Use a regular model when an association record needs soft deletion.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Pivot or MorphPivot class uses SoftDeletes.
- **Why:** Pivot models do not support the normal soft-deletion model lifecycle.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class Membership extends Pivot { use SoftDeletes; }
```

After:
```php
class Membership extends Model { use SoftDeletes; } // model the association explicitly
```

#### Reserve dynamic relationships for extension boundaries and register them during provider boot
- **Do:** Reserve dynamic relationships for extension boundaries and register them during provider boot.
- **Flag when:** Flag when ordinary application relationships are hidden in runtime registration or dynamic relations are registered before boot.
- **Why:** Explicit model methods are easier to discover; package extensions sometimes need runtime registration.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Basic app relations scattered through resolveRelationUsing callbacks.
```

After:
```php
// Define ordinary relations on models; register necessary package extensions in boot().
```

#### List required morph types explicitly when a wildcard discovery query is unnecessary
- **Do:** List required morph types explicitly when a wildcard discovery query is unnecessary.
- **Flag when:** Flag when whereHasMorph uses * despite a known fixed set of relevant types.
- **Why:** Explicit types avoid the extra discovery query and clarify permitted target models.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Comment::whereHasMorph('commentable', '*', $filter)->get();
```

After:
```php
Comment::whereHasMorph('commentable', [Post::class, Video::class], $filter)->get();
```

#### Handle nullable attributes explicitly rather than expecting their casts to convert null
- **Do:** Handle nullable attributes explicitly rather than expecting their casts to convert null.
- **Flag when:** Flag when code invokes methods on a nullable cast result without a null policy.
- **Why:** Eloquent generally leaves null attributes uncast.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$user->verified_at->format('Y-m-d');
```

After:
```php
$user->verified_at?->format('Y-m-d');
```

#### Reject invalid value-object types in custom cast setters
- **Do:** Reject invalid value-object types in custom cast setters.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom cast assumes an object type and silently stores malformed input.
- **Why:** An explicit guard fails near the invalid assignment.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function set($m, $k, $v, $a) { return $v->toArray(); }
```

After:
```php
public function set($model, $key, $value, $attributes) { if (! $value instanceof Address) { throw new InvalidArgumentException('Address required'); } return ['street' => $value->street]; }
```

#### Define custom cast comparison when domain equality differs from object or raw-value equality
- **Do:** Define custom cast comparison when domain equality differs from object or raw-value equality.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom value cast produces false dirty changes or suppresses meaningful updates.
- **Why:** A comparison contract aligns dirty tracking with value semantics.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Equal value objects are always considered changed.
```

After:
```php
class MoneyCast implements CastsAttributes, ComparesCastableAttributes { /* compare normalized value and currency */ }
```

#### Account for collection operations that return a base collection
- **Do:** Account for collection operations that return a base collection.
- **Flag when:** Flag when code calls model-only collection methods after transforming elements into scalars or using base-returning operations.
- **Why:** A collection without models no longer supports Eloquent-specific operations.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$users->pluck('email')->load('roles');
```

After:
```php
$users->load('roles'); $emails = $users->pluck('email');
```

#### Preserve enabled relationship autoloading in custom newCollection() overrides
- **Do:** Preserve enabled relationship autoloading in custom newCollection() overrides.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom collection factory drops the globally enabled autoloading behavior.
- **Why:** Custom construction must preserve the selected model loading policy.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return new UserCollection($models);
```

After:
```php
$collection = new UserCollection($models); return Model::isAutomaticallyEagerLoadingRelationships() ? $collection->withRelationshipAutoloading() : $collection;
```

#### Monitor production request/query performance with an APM
- **Do:** Monitor production request/query performance with an APM.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production has no way to detect slow requests or N+1 query growth.
- **Why:** Runtime monitoring catches workload-specific problems that development fixtures may miss.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use supported deterministic ordering for cursor pagination
- **Do:** Use supported deterministic ordering for cursor pagination.
- **Flag when:** Flag when cursor pagination lacks a unique stable order, orders by unsupported columns or uses parameterized order expressions.
- **Why:** Cursor tokens need reproducible ordered values; selected expression aliases and supported columns are required.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Post::cursorPaginate(50);
```

After:
```php
Post::orderByDesc('created_at')->orderByDesc('id')->cursorPaginate(50);
```

#### Index the ordering columns used by high-volume cursor pagination
- **Do:** Index the ordering columns used by high-volume cursor pagination.
- **Flag when:** Flag when cursor-page queries sort or scan large unindexed data sets.
- **Why:** A matching index lets the database seek from the cursor efficiently.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$table->timestamp('published_at');
```

After:
```php
$table->timestamp('published_at'); $table->index(['published_at', 'id']);
```

#### Make asynchronously populated Scout embedding columns nullable
- **Do:** Make asynchronously populated Scout embedding columns nullable.
- **Flag when:** Flag when model inserts require a vector before Scout writes the embedding after persistence.
- **Why:** Nullable storage supports the indexing lifecycle.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$table->vector('embedding', 1536);
```

After:
```php
$table->vector('embedding', 1536)->nullable();
```

#### Declare soft-delete metadata in the selected external search engine schema
- **Do:** Declare soft-delete metadata in the selected external search engine schema.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a soft-deletable searchable model lacks the engine facet/filter field needed for its deletion policy.
- **Why:** External engines need explicit schema/filter support for soft-delete visibility.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Typesense schema lacks __soft_deleted.
```

After:
```php
// Typesense fields include {name: __soft_deleted, type: int32, optional: true}.
```

#### Eager-load relations used to build bulk search payloads
- **Do:** Eager-load relations used to build bulk search payloads.
- **Flag when:** Flag when bulk indexing lazy-loads the same relation for each model.
- **Why:** Batch relation loading avoids import-time N+1 queries; use the hook supported by the chosen sync/queued import mode.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public function toSearchableArray(): array { return ['author' => $this->author->name]; }
```

After:
```php
protected function makeAllSearchableUsing(Builder $query): Builder { return $query->with('author'); }
```
