- **Flag when:** Flag when DNS is changed before required network/firewall connectivity is restored, or the original droplet is destroyed before successful cutover verification.
- **Why:** Migration changes the server address and resets network membership; staged cutover verification preserves service connectivity and a recovery path.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Check the supported source OS before a Laravel VPS migration
- **Do:** Verify that a DigitalOcean source server runs an Ubuntu release eligible for the Laravel VPS migration workflow before attempting that migration; use a supported replacement/migration plan for an ineligible host.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the Laravel VPS migration workflow is attempted from a source Ubuntu version outside its documented eligibility requirements.
- **Why:** A supported new-server OS does not imply that the snapshot-based migration workflow accepts every older source image.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Change Forge-managed PHP and firewall inventory through Forge
- **Do:** Use Forge management operations for installing/removing PHP versions and creating/removing UFW firewall rules on a Forge-managed host so the control plane retains an accurate resource inventory.
- **Flag when:** Flag when routine out-of-band PHP installations/removals or UFW changes create resources that Forge cannot see or manage.
- **Why:** A successful shell change can leave Forge's inventory inconsistent with the server and make later management incomplete or misleading.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Migrate every Forge PHP consumer before retiring a version
- **Do:** Change existing sites' PHP versions explicitly during a runtime rollout, update CLI and new-site defaults, and move every remaining consumer off an old version before uninstalling it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a server-default change is assumed to update existing sites, or a PHP version is removed while a site or CLI/new-site default still uses it.
- **Why:** Forge tracks existing sites and server defaults separately; changing one does not complete the runtime migration for the others.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep prerelease PHP runtimes off production sites
- **Do:** Use Forge PHP beta and release-candidate builds only on nonproduction sites until a stable compatible runtime and required extensions are available.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a production Forge site selects a prerelease PHP runtime for ordinary production traffic.
- **Why:** Prerelease builds may have incomplete Forge integration or unsupported PHP extensions and are intended for compatibility experiments.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Weight load-balancer backends by their intended capacity
- **Do:** When application servers behind a Forge load balancer have unequal intended traffic capacity, set backend weights to reflect that capacity instead of assuming equal shares.
- **Flag when:** Flag when unequal-capacity backends are overloaded by an unreviewed equal-weight configuration.
- **Why:** Weighted distribution can assign a larger traffic share to a server sized to handle it.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Mark failover-only load-balancer backends as backups
- **Do:** Configure a backend intended solely for failover as a Forge load-balancer backup so it is not included in ordinary traffic distribution.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an intended standby backend is configured as an ordinary active upstream and therefore receives normal traffic.
- **Why:** Backup status encodes active/standby behavior rather than merely reducing an active server's traffic weight.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Choose a repository-backed Forge site at creation when Git deployment is needed
- **Do:** Attach the intended Git repository when creating a Forge site that must support repository deployments; do not create a repository-free site expecting to add its first repository later.
- **Flag when:** Flag when provisioning a repository-free Forge site for an application whose deployment plan requires later attaching a Git repository without recreating the site.
- **Why:** The repository-free creation path cannot acquire a first repository later, so the wrong initial choice forces site recreation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep Forge deployment work inside its execution deadline
- **Do:** Keep Forge-managed deployment scripts within the documented ten-minute limit; move substantial nonessential work to an appropriate separate workflow.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Forge deployment intentionally runs work exceeding its execution deadline or repeats timeout failures without reducing release work.
- **Why:** Forge fails a deployment that exceeds its platform deadline, even when the script would eventually finish.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Retain enough complete release directories for rollback
- **Do:** Set Forge zero-downtime release retention to keep enough previous complete deployments for the application's rollback requirements, within the host's available disk budget.
- **Flag when:** Flag when release cleanup removes every usable rollback target or retention is not aligned with the required rollback window.
- **Why:** Atomic activation does not preserve a rollback path if the required previous release directory has already been deleted.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use the project package manager and locked frontend install for releases
- **Do:** Configure Forge to use the package manager selected by the project and install frontend dependencies from its committed lockfile; for npm releases, use npm ci.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Forge uses a different package manager from the project or an npm deploy resolves dependencies with npm install instead of consuming the committed lockfile.
- **Why:** Matching the project tool and consuming its lockfile keeps deployment dependencies consistent with the reviewed dependency graph.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Do not treat Forge deployment metadata as revision selection
- **Do:** Choose the deployed revision through the site's actual branch and checkout logic; treat forge_deploy_commit and FORGE_DEPLOY_COMMIT as deployment-history metadata rather than proof of which revision was checked out.
- **Flag when:** Flag when deployment automation sends a commit label and assumes that this alone pins the code Forge deploys.
- **Why:** The hook commit field labels deployment history without selecting the deployed commit, so a release can report a revision different from its checkout.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Treat the Forge administrator as inside the isolated-site trust boundary
- **Do:** Use Forge site user isolation to separate hosted applications, but grant access to the privileged forge user only to administrators trusted to read every isolated site's files.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a security design assumes isolated-site files are confidential from an operator who can access the privileged forge user.
- **Why:** Isolated Unix users reduce cross-application access but do not prevent the Forge administrative user from reading their directories.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Check recovery retention before deleting an individual Forge backup
- **Do:** Treat deleting an individual Forge backup as destructive archive deletion and confirm it is allowed by the recovery/retention policy before removing it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an operator deletes an individual backup assuming it only removes a Forge list entry or leaves the provider archive intact.
- **Why:** Individual backup deletion removes the archive at the storage provider and can eliminate a needed recovery point.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Place private Forge server-network peers in a compatible provider topology
- **Do:** For Forge server networks that support private-IP connectivity, place the peers under compatible provider credentials/account, region and VPC/network, and verify that the platform can link them privately.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a private Forge server-network plan assumes automatic private-IP connectivity between peers in incompatible provider accounts, regions or VPCs.
- **Why:** Forge private server networks depend on provider topology; sharing the same application does not make arbitrary private addresses mutually routable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Verify effective IPv6 firewall rule ordering
- **Do:** When adding an IPv6 deny rule through Forge, inspect the effective UFW ordering and test the blocked traffic instead of assuming the deny was inserted ahead of existing allow rules.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an IPv6 block relies solely on the first-priority insertion behavior documented for IPv4 deny rules.
- **Why:** UFW does not apply Forge's first-priority positioning to IPv6 rules in the same way, so an earlier matching allow can defeat the intended block.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Preserve required server changes before resetting Git state
- **Do:** Before using Forge Reset Git State, inspect tracked-file differences and preserve any changes that must survive; proceed only when discarding the remaining tracked changes is intended.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Git state is reset as routine troubleshooting without checking for tracked server-side changes that would be lost.
- **Why:** The reset discards local modifications to tracked repository files rather than merely clearing a dashboard status.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Validate Envoyer-to-Forge migration eligibility before switching deployment ownership
- **Do:** Before migrating an Envoyer project to Forge zero-downtime deployment management, verify the workflow's supported server count, repository provider and deployment duration.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an Envoyer-to-Forge migration plan assumes multi-server or self-hosted-GitLab eligibility, or carries a deployment exceeding the target deadline.
- **Why:** The migration workflow supports a narrower topology and shorter execution limit than an arbitrary Envoyer project.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Remove stored deployment CLI credentials from retired workstations
- **Do:** Log out of the Forge CLI on a machine that no longer needs Forge access so its stored CLI authentication credentials are removed.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a retired or reassigned workstation retains a usable Forge CLI credential after its deployment-management role ends.
- **Why:** Unused credentials on a former administration machine unnecessarily extend access to deployment infrastructure.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Preflight custom Forge server reachability and host prerequisites
- **Do:** Before provisioning a custom Forge VPS, verify its minimum CPU/RAM/disk capacity, curl availability and external SSH reachability; when NAT remaps the public SSH port, configure the NAT port mapping in Forge.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom-server provisioning starts on an undersized host, without curl, or with an unconfigured NAT/public SSH mapping that prevents correct management access.
- **Why:** A clean supported OS still needs adequate resources, bootstrap tools and a reachable management endpoint for provisioning to succeed.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Test every advertised vendor SDK major in integration CI
- **Do:** For a package claiming support for multiple vendor SDK majors, add an integration-test lane for each supported major and constrain Composer so that lane actually installs the intended SDK version.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the package advertises several vendor SDK majors but CI exercises only the latest one, or all nominal SDK lanes resolve the same version.
- **Why:** A broad Composer constraint is a compatibility promise that a single SDK version cannot verify.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Subscribe to browser state with React external-store snapshots
- **Do:** For React hooks that subscribe to mutable browser state such as media queries, use useSyncExternalStore with subscription cleanup, a stable snapshot and a matching getServerSnapshot when server rendering is supported.
- **Flag when:** Flag when browser-state subscriptions can produce inconsistent concurrent snapshots or SSR hydration differences because they lack the external-store snapshot contract.
- **Why:** React coordinates external-store reads across renders, and the server snapshot gives server rendering and initial hydration the same value.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Apply the configured sampling decision inside custom Pulse recorders
- **Do:** When implementing a sampleable custom Pulse recorder, use the supported Sampling concern and return before recording when shouldSample() is false.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom recorder exposes or relies on a sample_rate but records every event without consulting the sampling decision.
- **Why:** Selecting a sample rate does not reduce ingestion if the custom recorder ignores it.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Pin analyzer versions when diagnostic changes require deliberate review
- **Do:** When a project requires a fixed PHPStan diagnostic baseline across fresh dependency resolutions, declare a reviewed exact analyzer version in require-dev and update it through deliberate compatibility review.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a project promises stable analyzer behavior but an unconstrained compatible-range resolution can silently change the analysis tool version.
- **Why:** An analyzer update can introduce new diagnostics independently of the application code being reviewed.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Lock file log writes when concurrent writers need serialization
- **Do:** When concurrent PHP processes writing one file channel risk interleaved records, enable locking on the applicable single, daily or monthly Laravel channel and verify the filesystem supports the required lock behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag a shared file log with observed or expected interleaved writes whose channel has locking disabled and no equivalent serialization.
- **Why:** File-write locking keeps concurrently emitted records intact for investigation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Age retired servers out of the Pulse server dashboard
- **Do:** For replaceable server fleets, set the Pulse servers card ignore-after interval so inactive retired servers leave the display after the intended diagnostic window.
- **Flag when:** Flag a Pulse server dashboard that indefinitely displays replaced hosts without a deliberate inactivity window.
- **Why:** Removing stale server entries keeps the dashboard representative of the active fleet.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Make Pulse capture failures observable outside Pulse
- **Do:** When Pulse data collection is operationally important, register Pulse::handleExceptionsUsing to send capture failures to a safe independent logger or monitor while preserving Pulse failure isolation.
- **Flag when:** Flag critical Pulse monitoring that can silently stop capturing data without any external diagnostic signal, or failure handling that recursively depends on the failed Pulse capture path.
- **Why:** Pulse suppresses its capture errors to protect application work, so collection failures otherwise remain invisible.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Parameterize reusable Envoy deployment inputs
- **Do:** For an Envoy deployment used across branches or targets, pass changing deployment inputs through explicit CLI options and validate required values rather than editing hard-coded task commands for each run.
- **Flag when:** Flag a reusable Envoy deployment that requires source edits to select its branch or target, or silently proceeds with a missing required input.
- **Why:** Explicit inputs keep the deployment procedure reusable and make the selected release parameters visible at invocation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep remote shell work in Envoy tasks
- **Do:** Put remote shell operations in Envoy tasks targeting the intended servers. Write before, after, error, success and finished hooks as local PHP, accounting for their local execution context.
- **Flag when:** Flag a hook containing remote shell commands or relying on a remote working directory or filesystem being local to the Envoy runner.
- **Why:** Envoy hooks execute PHP on the runner, so treating them as remote shell task bodies executes in the wrong language or location.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Normalize accepted subprocess results for scheduler success hooks
- **Do:** If an external scheduled process treats selected nonzero exit codes as success, run it in Schedule::call and return an explicit boolean derived from the accepted exit-code set. Preserve failure for every other code and exception.
- **Flag when:** Flag a scheduled external command whose documented successful nonzero outcomes trigger false failure alerts, or whose wrapper masks unexpected failures as success.
- **Why:** Laravel scheduled commands normally treat nonzero exits as failure, while a scheduled callback returning false explicitly reports failure.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Inspect schedule timing without executing scheduled work
- **Do:** Use php artisan schedule:list to inspect registered tasks and next-run timing; do not run schedule:run merely to preview what would execute.
- **Flag when:** Flag a diagnostic or deployment check that invokes schedule:run as if it were a dry run and can therefore perform real task side effects.
- **Why:** A schedule listing provides timing information without starting due production work.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Run scheduler commands under the application service account
- **Do:** Configure the cron or equivalent schedule:run trigger to use the intended application account, normally the same account that runs the web application, with compatible writable-directory ownership.
- **Flag when:** Flag scheduler cron running as root or an unrelated account when its generated files are later used by the web application and ownership can break access.
- **Why:** A consistent service account prevents scheduler-created logs, caches and files from becoming unwritable to application workers.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Centralize shared exception-reporting context
- **Do:** Register shared safe exception-reporting fields with the context callback inside withExceptions in bootstrap/app.php.
- **Flag when:** Flag repeated shared exception context at individual report calls instead of one bootstrap/app.php context callback.
- **Why:** A reporting-boundary callback adds common diagnostic context consistently while leaving exception-specific context with its owning exception.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use local signed file serving for development private-download flows
- **Do:** When development only needs private files and expiring download URLs, use a private local disk with serve enabled and Storage::temporaryUrl rather than requiring a remote production-style bucket for that flow. Keep remote-adapter integration checks where those semantics matter.
- **Flag when:** Flag a local private-download workflow that requires external bucket access solely to create expiring links, or publishes private files just to avoid that dependency.
- **Why:** Local signed file serving provides the download and expiry behavior without making ordinary development depend on a remote storage account.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Let ClickHouse perform routine background merges
- **Do:** For ordinary MergeTree maintenance, rely on ClickHouse background merging instead of habitually scheduling OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL. Reserve forced full merges for a justified bounded maintenance operation.
- **Flag when:** Flag recurring OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL used as routine housekeeping without measured need or an accepted resource budget.
- **Why:** Forced full merges can consume substantial compute and I/O and bypass the normal background merge sizing safeguards.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Ground agent debugging in application and browser diagnostics
- **Do:** For authorized agent-assisted development debugging, expose relevant application logs, the latest exception and browser console diagnostics through development tools such as Boost, with access limited to the diagnostic data needed for the task.
- **Flag when:** Flag an agent debugging workflow that repeatedly guesses about failures while available application or browser diagnostics are never supplied or inspected.
- **Why:** Direct diagnostic evidence gives the agent the actual failure context and reduces transcription errors from repeated manual copying.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Configure edge enforcement for trusted origin rate-limit signals
- **Do:** When application-aware limits must also protect origin capacity, emit the intended origin response signal and configure a supported CDN/WAF rate-limiting rule to count that signal and enforce subsequent requests using the intended client identity and duration. Keep Laravel enforcement active.
- **Flag when:** Flag a design that expects an arbitrary Laravel response header alone to enable edge limiting, or an edge rule whose counting expression does not match the origin signal and request scope.
- **Why:** Edge enforcement can shed repeated abusive traffic before PHP, but requires an explicit supported rule and correct counting configuration.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Separate Pulse dashboard serving when its load needs isolation
- **Do:** When Pulse dashboard queries would compete materially with application traffic, serve the dashboard from a separate instance configured to read the same intended Pulse storage while keeping application collection configured.
- **Flag when:** Flag measured dashboard load affecting application serving capacity with no separate dashboard instance or equivalent isolation.
- **Why:** Dashboard isolation prevents operational investigation from consuming the same web-serving capacity under pressure.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep production changes in the version-controlled deployment flow
- **Do:** Deploy reviewed repository revisions or artifacts built from them through the release tooling instead of ad hoc FTP uploads or direct server patches. For per-change deployments, record a bad-code reversal as a version-controlled revert and deliver it through the same workflow.
- **Flag when:** Flag application code changed only on the production filesystem, or a production reversal that leaves the repository describing different code from the deployed system.
- **Why:** A repository-backed release history makes production changes reviewable, repeatable and recoverable without hidden server drift.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Resolve inactive monitoring issues by a deliberate quiet period
- **Do:** When using automatic issue resolution to keep a monitoring inbox current, choose a period with no recurrence before resolution and preserve history and renewed visibility if the issue returns.
- **Flag when:** Flag automatic resolution based only on issue creation age while errors are still recurring, or recurring issues that stay silently resolved.
- **Why:** A quiet-period policy reduces stale inbox noise without treating an actively recurring failure as fixed.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Type-check frontend code in CI
- **Do:** Run the frontend type checker in CI and fail the job on type errors.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a typed frontend has no CI type-check step or the step ignores failures.
- **Why:** Asset bundlers may transpile TypeScript without checking types. A separate check catches invalid frontend contracts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Suppress only confirmed analyzer false positives
- **Do:** Use narrow documented suppressions for verified static-analysis false positives instead of changing correct application behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag when correct code is distorted to satisfy a false diagnostic or a broad suppression hides unrelated errors.
- **Why:** A targeted suppression preserves intended behavior and keeps valid diagnostics actionable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Work around an incorrect analyzer inference by changing runtime behavior.
return null;
```

After:
```php
// Adapter returns the documented type; upstream stub is incorrect.
/** @phpstan-ignore return.type */
return $adapter->value();
```

#### Make scheduled work safe to retry
- **Do:** Make scheduled tasks idempotent or record durable progress so retries and partial execution do not duplicate side effects.
- **Flag when:** Flag when rerunning a scheduled task repeats externally visible actions or partial failures cannot resume safely.
- **Why:** Schedulers and hosts can retry or terminate work. Durable progress and idempotency make recovery predictable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$gateway->charge($invoice->amount);
```

After:
```php
$gateway->charge($invoice->amount, idempotencyKey: 'invoice-'.$invoice->id);
```

#### Group schedules with shared constraints
- **Do:** Use schedule groups when multiple tasks intentionally share the same frequency or execution constraints.
- **Flag when:** Flag when several related schedule definitions duplicate the same frequency and singleton constraints and can drift independently.
- **Why:** Grouping shared constraints makes the intended scheduling policy explicit.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Schedule::command('reports:a')->daily()->onOneServer();
Schedule::command('reports:b')->daily()->onOneServer();
```

After:
```php
Schedule::daily()->onOneServer()->group(function () {
    Schedule::command('reports:a');
    Schedule::command('reports:b');
});
```

#### Enforce scheduled process deadlines with supported controls
- **Do:** Use a process manager or operating-system timeout when scheduled work requires hard termination; do not call a nonexistent scheduler takeUntilTimeout() API.
- **Flag when:** Flag when schedule definitions call takeUntilTimeout() or claim a hard deadline without an actual process termination mechanism.
- **Why:** An unsupported method cannot limit a task. Lock expiry also does not terminate the underlying process.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Exclude inappropriate activity attributes
- **Do:** Use logExcept() to exclude sensitive or irrelevant attributes when the activity policy otherwise logs a broad attribute set.
- **Flag when:** Flag when broad activity logging includes known secret or operational-only fields.
- **Why:** Exclusions prevent an audit stream from retaining data outside its intended scope.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return LogOptions::defaults()->logAll();
```

After:
```php
return LogOptions::defaults()->logAll()->logExcept(['secret_token']);
```

#### Reserve Spin MCP wait helper for MCP startup
- **Do:** Use spin-mcp-wait.sh only as part of MCP server startup, not as a general shell wrapper.
- **Flag when:** Flag when regular Spin commands are routed through the MCP startup wait helper.
- **Why:** The startup helper has a specialized lifecycle and can delay or interfere with ordinary commands.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Authorize Rapyd navigation and server actions consistently
- **Do:** Apply the same permission policy to Rapyd sidebar entries and the server actions they expose.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a hidden sidebar item points to a server action with no equivalent authorization check.
- **Why:** Hiding navigation does not prevent direct requests to the action.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
if ($user->can('export')) { showExportLink(); }
// Export action has no authorization.
```

After:
```php
$this->authorize('export', Report::class);
return $exporter->run();
```

#### Supervise the Pulse server collector
- **Do:** Run pulse:check under a process monitor configured to restart it after exit.
- **Flag when:** Flag when pulse:check is started manually or lacks an automatic restart policy.
- **Why:** A stopped collector silently removes server telemetry.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Remove the obsolete root server router
- **Do:** Remove the legacy root server.php once the application uses the framework-provided artisan serve router and has no custom dependency on it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a modern Laravel application retains an unused legacy server.php copied from an older skeleton.
- **Why:** The framework provides the development router, so an obsolete duplicate can drift or mislead maintainers.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// server.php: legacy development router copied from the old skeleton.
```

After:
```php
// Remove unused server.php; run php artisan serve.
```

#### Choose serverless hosting for an autoscaling requirement
- **Do:** Consider Lambda through Vapor when automatic scaling is required and the available deployment regions satisfy the application residency constraints.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a workload with an explicit autoscaling requirement selects fixed-capacity hosting without a scaling plan, or its serverless region violates recorded residency constraints.
- **Why:** Serverless hosting can absorb variable demand when its platform limits and regional availability fit the application.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use configured Compose service names
- **Do:** Read the project Compose configuration and target its actual service names in Spin commands.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Spin scripts refer to hardcoded service names absent from the project Compose services.
- **Why:** Repositories can rename services, so guessed names can run against the wrong container or fail.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Disable pseudo-terminals in automated container commands
- **Do:** Pass -T to Spin commands executed from CI, agents, or subprocesses without a terminal.
- **Flag when:** Flag when noninteractive automation invokes a TTY-allocating Spin command without disabling its pseudo-terminal.
- **Why:** TTY allocation can fail or hang when there is no interactive terminal.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Make automated Cloud commands noninteractive
- **Do:** Pass -n to Cloud CLI commands run by automation and supply required values explicitly.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Cloud CLI command in a noninteractive script can wait for a prompt.
- **Why:** Explicit noninteractive execution makes automated deployments deterministic.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep Cloud deployment diagnostics visible
- **Do:** Keep Cloud command output available to deployment logs instead of using -q or --silent.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Cloud automation suppresses diagnostic output with -q or --silent.
- **Why:** Visible output is needed to diagnose failed infrastructure and deployment operations.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Avoid storage:link in Cloud deploy commands
- **Do:** Use persistent object storage for Cloud file delivery and remove storage:link from Cloud deploy commands.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Cloud deploy commands rely on storage:link to expose files from the ephemeral deployment filesystem.
- **Why:** The deploy command does not create persistent shared uploads for later replicas.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Let Cloud reload services automatically
- **Do:** Rely on Cloud service lifecycle management instead of adding php artisan reload to Cloud deployments.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Cloud deploy scripts invoke artisan reload to restart platform-managed services.
- **Why:** Cloud already reloads services gracefully as part of release activation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Let Cloud build after CI triggers a deploy
- **Do:** Use CI to validate and trigger the Cloud deployment, and let the configured Cloud build stage install runtime dependencies and build the application.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Cloud deployment workflow depends on local CI build outputs that Cloud does not receive or repeats the full platform build solely to trigger deployment.
- **Why:** Cloud builds the selected source revision with the environment configuration. Keeping the actual release build there avoids mismatched artifacts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Redeploy Cloud schedule changes
- **Do:** Redeploy the Cloud environment after changing Laravel schedule definitions so the platform refreshes its schedule inventory.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a schedule definition changes without a deployment and the platform continues using the previous inventory.
- **Why:** Cloud derives scheduling information from the deployed application.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Separate public and private Cloud buckets
- **Do:** Attach separate private-default and public Cloud buckets when both visibility modes are needed, and route public writes through the public disk.
- **Flag when:** Flag when one Cloud bucket is expected to contain mixed public/private objects, or private files are routed into the public disk.
- **Why:** Cloud bucket visibility applies to every object. Separate disks make the access boundary explicit.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Storage::put('private/document.pdf', $privateContents);
Storage::put('public/avatar.jpg', $avatar);
```

After:
```php
Storage::put('documents/report.pdf', $privateContents);
Storage::disk('public')->put('avatars/user.jpg', $avatar);
```

#### Respect Cloud HTML object restrictions
- **Do:** Use another storage destination for HTML/HTM files unless Cloud support has approved an object-storage exception.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the application uploads .html or .htm objects to Cloud buckets without the required exception.
- **Why:** Cloud automatically removes those file types, so a successful write is not durable storage.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Configure the public Cloud bucket base URL explicitly
- **Do:** Set AWS_URL to the public Cloud bucket base URL when application URL generation depends on that variable.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a public disk uses env(AWS_URL) but the deployment does not supply the bucket public URL.
- **Why:** Cloud shows the public URL in bucket settings but does not automatically inject AWS_URL.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep independently changing business behavior separate
- **Do:** Keep similar code paths separate when they represent different business rules expected to change independently.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an abstraction forces unrelated business workflows through shared conditionals solely because the current code looks similar.
- **Why:** Textual duplication does not imply a shared domain responsibility.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
function calculateTotal($items, bool $isPayroll) { /* unrelated policy branches */ }
```

After:
```php
function calculateOrderTotal($items) { /* order policy */ }
function calculatePayrollTotal($items) { /* payroll policy */ }
```

#### Defer expensive custom Pulse processing
- **Do:** Use Pulse lazy callbacks for custom telemetry processing that can run after the immediate event path.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom Pulse recorders perform expensive aggregation or serialization synchronously inside hot event callbacks.
- **Why:** Deferring telemetry processing reduces overhead on application work.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$pulse->record('custom', expensiveTelemetryKey())->count();
```

After:
```php
$pulse->lazy(fn () => $pulse->record('custom', expensiveTelemetryKey())->count());
```

#### Isolate custom telemetry failures
- **Do:** Wrap custom Pulse instrumentation in the Pulse rescue boundary so telemetry errors do not fail the business operation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom telemetry exception propagates into the request, command, or job being observed.
- **Why:** Observability should not introduce a new availability dependency for business execution.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$pulse->record('custom', $key)->count();
```

After:
```php
$pulse->rescue(fn () => $pulse->record('custom', $key)->count());
```

#### Avoid accidental mutation with Collection forget
- **Do:** Copy a collection before forget() when the original keyed collection must remain unchanged.
- **Flag when:** Flag when forget() is treated as returning a separate collection and later code expects the original key to remain.
- **Why:** Collection::forget mutates the collection instance in place.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$filtered = $items->forget('internal');
// $items also lost the key.
```

After:
```php
$filtered = collect($items->all())->forget('internal');
```

#### Import the Laravel defer helper explicitly
- **Do:** Import Illuminate\Support\defer before calling defer() where Swoole’s global function may be installed.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a namespaced application file uses unqualified defer() without the Laravel function import in a Swoole runtime.
- **Why:** A global Swoole defer function can resolve instead of the Laravel helper and change lifecycle behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
defer(fn () => recordMetrics());
```

After:
```php
use function Illuminate\Support\defer;
defer(fn () => recordMetrics());
```

#### Use one AI conversation-history mechanism
- **Do:** Let Conversational agents load their own history and omit withMessages() for those agents.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an agent implementing Conversational is invoked with withMessages().
- **Why:** The AI SDK rejects the conflicting history mechanisms with a LogicException.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
(new ConversationalCoach())->withMessages($messages)->prompt($input);
```

After:
```php
(new ConversationalCoach())->prompt($input);
```

#### Exempt essential schedules from scheduler pauses deliberately
- **Do:** Mark a task evenWhenPaused() only when it is explicitly required to continue during a scheduler pause.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an essential operational task is unintentionally stopped by schedule:pause or ordinary tasks are broadly exempted.
- **Why:** A deliberate exemption keeps critical work available while retaining the purpose of a scheduler pause.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Schedule::command('health:heartbeat')->everyMinute();
```

After:
```php
Schedule::command('health:heartbeat')->everyMinute()->evenWhenPaused();
```

#### Do not assume SQL Server whereLike case sensitivity
- **Do:** Use a tested SQL Server collation or supported predicate when a query requires case-sensitive matching instead of relying on whereLike(caseSensitive: true).
- **Flag when:** Flag when SQL Server queries depend on the unsupported whereLike caseSensitive option.
- **Why:** The option is not supported by the SQL Server grammar, so the intended comparison is not portable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
DB::connection('sqlsrv')->table('users')->whereLike('name', $pattern, caseSensitive: true);
```

After:
```php
DB::connection('sqlsrv')->table('users')->whereRaw('name COLLATE Latin1_General_100_CS_AS LIKE ?', [$pattern]);
```

#### Avoid OAuth implicit grants
- **Do:** Use an appropriate current OAuth grant, such as authorization code with PKCE for public clients, instead of Passport’s implicit grant.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Passport enables or clients request the implicit grant.
- **Why:** Implicit access tokens are exposed through browser authorization responses and are no longer recommended.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Passport::enableImplicitGrant();
```

After:
```php
// Use an authorization-code client with PKCE; do not enable the implicit grant.
```

#### Report non-throwing filesystem write failures
- **Do:** Set report: true on a disk when failed writes should be reported while preserving the non-throwing return-value contract.
- **Flag when:** Flag when disk writes must remain non-throwing but failures have no reporting path.
- **Why:** Reporting preserves diagnostics without changing the caller contract.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'throw' => false,
'report' => false,
```

After:
```php
'throw' => false,
'report' => true,
```

#### Set public object visibility only on ACL-capable storage
- **Do:** For disks that support object ACLs, set public visibility when the delivery policy requires a publicly accessible object, and confirm the bucket policy permits it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a publicly delivered upload on an ACL-capable private-by-default disk lacks the intended access setting.
- **Why:** URL generation alone does not grant public access. R2 and other bucket-policy-only providers need a different visibility strategy.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Storage::disk('s3-acl')->putFile('avatars', $file);
```

After:
```php
Storage::disk('s3-acl')->putFile('avatars', $file, 'public');
```

#### Set meaningful exception log levels
- **Do:** Configure exception-type log levels when severity determines alert routing or channel selection.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an operationally critical exception is logged below the threshold of its required alerting channel.
- **Why:** Severity affects which channels receive an exception and how operators prioritize it.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// PDOException uses the default level despite a critical-only alert channel.
```

After:
```php
$exceptions->level(PDOException::class, LogLevel::CRITICAL);
```

#### Register query-duration monitors per connection
- **Do:** Register cumulative query-duration handlers on every database connection that needs monitoring.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a named connection is expected to be monitored but only the default connection has whenQueryingForLongerThan configured.
- **Why:** Cumulative query-duration tracking is connection-specific.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
DB::whenQueryingForLongerThan(500, $handler);
```

After:
```php
DB::connection('mysql')->whenQueryingForLongerThan(500, $handler);
DB::connection('reporting')->whenQueryingForLongerThan(500, $handler);
```

#### Keep durable state outside Swoole tables
- **Do:** Persist durable application data in a database or durable store instead of relying only on Swoole tables.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Swoole tables contain the only copy of business data expected to survive server restart.
- **Why:** Swoole table contents disappear when the server restarts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Octane::table('orders')->set($id, ['status' => 'paid']);
```

After:
```php
$order->update(['status' => 'paid']);
Octane::table('orders')->set($id, ['status' => 'paid']);
```

#### Use shared log context for message-level fields
- **Do:** Use Log::shareContext() for fields intended to be shared as message-level log context while preserving Laravel Context metadata placement.
- **Flag when:** Flag when code rewrites Context metadata placement merely to add shared log fields.
- **Why:** Shared log context and execution metadata serve different serialization contracts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Custom formatter copies all execution metadata into every message context.
```

After:
```php
Log::shareContext(['request_id' => $requestId]);
```

#### Avoid unnecessary action abstractions
- **Do:** Keep one-off single-entrypoint logic in a plain service or local implementation until reuse or domain boundaries justify a dedicated action.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an action wrapper adds indirection but has no reuse, orchestration boundary, or domain responsibility.
- **Why:** Abstractions should clarify a real boundary rather than add files around trivial forwarding.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
final class GetLabelAction { public function __invoke($value) { return strtoupper($value); } }
```

After:
```php
$label = strtoupper($value);
```

#### Upgrade before runtime security support ends
- **Do:** Schedule PHP and Laravel upgrades before their running versions lose security support.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the runtime inventory includes an unsupported PHP or Laravel version without a planned upgrade before end of support.
- **Why:** Security maintenance depends on running supported versions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Disable unused Xdebug in Homestead
- **Do:** Disable Xdebug and restart PHP-FPM when it is not needed in a Homestead runtime where PHP performance matters.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Homestead keeps Xdebug enabled for normal work without an active debugging need.
- **Why:** Xdebug can add substantial runtime overhead.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Publish exact mail authentication DNS records
- **Do:** Create sending-domain DNS records exactly as supplied by the mail provider and verify them before using the domain.
- **Flag when:** Flag when mail DNS record names or values differ from the provider requirements or the domain remains unverified.
- **Why:** Incorrect records prevent verification and can damage mail authentication or delivery.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Create verification records at the authoritative DNS provider
- **Do:** Add domain verification records to the active authoritative DNS zone.
- **Flag when:** Flag when verification records are added to a non-authoritative provider and never appear in authoritative answers.
- **Why:** Only the delegated DNS zone determines what verifiers can resolve.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep ACME challenge CNAMEs DNS-only
- **Do:** Disable Cloudflare proxying on ACME challenge CNAME records.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an _acme-challenge CNAME is marked proxied.
- **Why:** Certificate validation requires the original challenge record to resolve correctly.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Lower DNS TTL before a hosting cutover
- **Do:** Lower relevant DNS TTLs at least 24 hours before a planned Vapor-to-Cloud cutover.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a cutover plan changes hosting records without allowing the prior DNS TTL to expire after lowering it.
- **Why:** Reducing TTL in advance limits how long clients retain the old target.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Preserve Forge management SSH access
- **Do:** Allow Forge’s published management IPs through SSH firewall rules and preserve that access while the server is managed by Forge.
- **Flag when:** Flag when SSH allowlists block Forge or a rule change removes the management path.
- **Why:** Forge needs SSH access to provision and manage its servers.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Permit required Forge HTTP connectivity
- **Do:** Allow the required incoming and outgoing forge.laravel.com traffic when restricting server HTTP connectivity.
- **Flag when:** Flag when HTTP filtering blocks the documented Forge control-plane connectivity.
- **Why:** A restrictive network policy must retain the management service paths it depends on.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Allow Forge deployment health probes
- **Do:** Allow Forge’s published deployment health-check sources to reach the required HTTP and HTTPS endpoints.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a firewall blocks the health probes used to validate a release.
- **Why:** A healthy release can be rejected if management health checks cannot reach it.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Verify Forge command target context
- **Do:** Check the active Forge organization and server before running management commands against them.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a management script depends on mutable implicit CLI context without asserting its intended organization and server.
- **Why:** Explicit target checks reduce operations against the wrong environment.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Revoke organization SSH keys on the actual servers
- **Do:** Remove a revoked or deleted organization SSH key from every affected server authorized_keys file.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a deleted Forge organization key remains authorized on managed servers.
- **Why:** Deleting the organization record alone does not guarantee removal of existing server access.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Authorize generated site deploy keys explicitly
- **Do:** Add a generated site public deploy key to the source repository and verify clone access before deployment.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a generated deployment site has a key that the repository has never authorized.
- **Why:** Key generation does not itself grant repository access.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Choose the matching Forge server role
- **Do:** Use an App server for a conventional single-server Laravel deployment unless a different role is required.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a single-server application is provisioned with a role that omits its required web/application services.
- **Why:** The server role determines which services Forge configures.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Connect to Meilisearch over private networking
- **Do:** Use Meilisearch’s private IP for application-server connections when both servers share a private network.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an internal application connects to Meilisearch through a public address despite available private connectivity.
- **Why:** Private connectivity reduces public exposure of the search service.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Provision custom Forge servers from a fresh supported OS
- **Do:** Use a fresh supported Ubuntu installation when onboarding a custom server to Forge.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Forge provisioning is attempted on an unsupported or previously customized server image.
- **Why:** Provisioning expects a known clean baseline and can conflict with pre-existing system configuration.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Allow root SSH only as required for Forge provisioning
- **Do:** Provide the root SSH access required to provision a custom Forge server and apply the intended post-provisioning access policy afterward.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom Forge provisioning cannot connect with its required privileges or temporary provisioning access remains unnecessarily broad.
- **Why:** Provisioning needs system-level configuration authority; that access should follow an explicit lifecycle.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Enable the IP assignment required by Forge VPC provisioning
- **Do:** Enable public-IP auto-assignment on existing AWS VPC subnets when using the Forge provisioning flow that requires it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the selected subnet does not assign the address needed for Forge to reach newly provisioned servers.
- **Why:** Without the expected management address the provisioning connection cannot be established.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Update Forge after a server IP change
- **Do:** Update the server address in Forge whenever its public IP changes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the provider reports a new server IP but Forge still targets the old address.
- **Why:** Management and deployment commands depend on the registered server address.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Transfer provider ownership separately from Forge ownership
- **Do:** Coordinate the underlying cloud-provider server transfer when moving a server between Forge organizations.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a migration plan assumes moving the Forge record also moves provider ownership and billing.
- **Why:** Forge organization ownership and provider account ownership are separate boundaries.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Terminate HTTPS on the Forge load balancer
- **Do:** Install the serving HTTPS certificate on the Forge load balancer when it terminates client TLS.
- **Flag when:** Flag when clients reach an HTTPS load balancer that lacks the site certificate while the certificate exists only on backend servers.
- **Why:** The client-facing TLS endpoint must present a valid certificate.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Align PHP and proxy execution deadlines
- **Do:** Set execution-time limits through Forge’s supported configuration so PHP and the web proxy use compatible deadlines.
- **Flag when:** Flag when PHP and proxy timeouts conflict and requests are cut off earlier than the intended application deadline.
- **Why:** A longer PHP limit does not help if the proxy closes the request first.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Preserve Forge template placeholders
- **Do:** Retain the documented placeholder syntax when customizing Forge Nginx templates.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom Nginx template removes or alters placeholders Forge must replace.
- **Why:** Invalid placeholders can generate incorrect server paths or configuration.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Preserve zero-downtime release macros
- **Do:** Retain CREATE_RELEASE and ACTIVATE_RELEASE in customized Forge zero-downtime deployment scripts.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a customized zero-downtime script omits release creation or activation.
- **Why:** The macros establish and activate the new release directory safely.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Restart managed daemons after release activation
- **Do:** Restart affected Forge background processes by their daemon identifiers after activating the new release.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a deploy restarts daemons before release activation or leaves them running old code after activation.
- **Why:** A daemon started too early can retain the old working directory and code.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Reserve the FORGE_ variable namespace
- **Do:** Use project-specific names for custom deployment variables instead of the reserved FORGE_ prefix.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom variable shadows or occupies the Forge-managed variable namespace.
- **Why:** Reserved-name collisions can change deployment behavior unexpectedly.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use Forge deployment path variables
- **Do:** Use the documented Forge path variables instead of hardcoding domain-based deployment paths.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a deploy script contains a fixed site path that becomes wrong after a domain or directory change.
- **Why:** Platform path variables follow the configured site and release directories.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use the isolated user key for SFTP
- **Do:** Authorize the SSH key on the site’s isolated system user before connecting over SFTP.
- **Flag when:** Flag when SFTP setup assumes the shared forge user key grants access to an isolated site user.
- **Why:** SSH authorization is per system account, so isolation changes the required key target.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Protect private web paths
- **Do:** Apply server access rules and per-path credentials to private operational site paths when server-level protection is required.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a designated private path is publicly accessible without its required credentials or access policy.
- **Why:** Server-level path protection can guard operational resources before application handling.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Bound noninteractive Forge site commands
- **Do:** Keep Forge site commands noninteractive and within the documented five-minute execution limit.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Forge site command waits for prompts or intentionally exceeds its execution deadline.
- **Why:** Bounded command execution avoids hung remote operations and platform timeouts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Back up before expanding the OS filesystem
- **Do:** Take a restorable snapshot or backup before changing the operating-system filesystem layout or expanding it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a filesystem expansion runbook has no pre-change recovery checkpoint.
- **Why:** Filesystem operations can fail in ways that require restoring the host.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Raise process and system file limits together
- **Do:** Adjust user/process limits as well as system-wide limits when increasing open-file capacity.
- **Flag when:** Flag when only fs.file-max changes while application processes retain a lower LimitNOFILE or ulimit.
- **Why:** The smallest applicable limit still bounds each process.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Coordinate multi-server releases
- **Do:** Use Envoyer or an equivalent coordinated deployment mechanism when a release must activate consistently across multiple servers.
- **Flag when:** Flag when independent per-server deployment scripts can leave a multi-server release partially activated without coordination or rollback.
- **Why:** Coordinated releases reduce mixed-version windows and support consistent recovery.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep Vapor core in production dependencies
- **Do:** Declare laravel/vapor-core under production require in every Vapor application.
- **Flag when:** Flag when vapor.yml is present but vapor-core is absent from production dependencies.
- **Why:** Vapor core supplies the runtime integration needed by the deployed application.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Limit root-domain assets served by Vapor compute
- **Do:** List only assets that must be served from the application root in Vapor serve_assets and leave other assets on the asset CDN.
- **Flag when:** Flag when serve_assets routes broad asset directories or ordinary bundles through application compute unnecessarily.
- **Why:** Serving ordinary assets through compute adds avoidable requests and cost.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Avoid stacking an incompatible proxy before the Vapor firewall
- **Do:** Do not enable Vapor’s managed firewall behind an existing reverse proxy without a supported compatible architecture.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Vapor managed firewall is enabled while traffic first passes through another unsupported reverse proxy.
- **Why:** The managed firewall relies on its documented edge traffic path.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Avoid background scheduler processes on Vapor
- **Do:** Dispatch queued work instead of using runInBackground() in schedules deployed to Vapor.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Vapor application schedules commands with runInBackground().
- **Why:** Lambda may stop the container before background commands complete, and Vapor does not support this scheduling option.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use a custom Vapor runtime for extra extensions
- **Do:** Use a Docker runtime when a Vapor application requires PHP extensions unavailable in its standard runtime.
- **Flag when:** Flag when application-required extensions are absent from the selected standard Vapor runtime.
- **Why:** A custom image can supply native dependencies the managed runtime does not include.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use end-to-end TLS with Cloudflare and Vapor
- **Do:** Set Cloudflare SSL/TLS to Full or a supported stricter validated mode for Vapor, keeping origin traffic encrypted.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Cloudflare uses Flexible or another unencrypted-origin mode for a Vapor production domain.
- **Why:** Origin HTTPS avoids redirect conflicts and preserves encryption beyond the edge.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use a controlled production domain on Vapor
- **Do:** Use an organization-controlled custom domain for production Vapor applications.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production relies only on a Vapor vanity domain for its public identity.
- **Why:** A custom domain gives the organization a stable endpoint it can retain across hosting changes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Provide persistent shared filesystems explicitly on Vapor
- **Do:** Mount EFS when a Vapor workload truly requires a persistent shared filesystem path instead of object storage.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Vapor application depends on local files surviving invocations without a persistent mount.
- **Why:** Lambda-local storage is not a durable shared filesystem.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Create load-balancer certificates in the deployment region
- **Do:** Provision the TLS certificate used by a Vapor application load balancer in the project deployment region.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an ALB listener references a certificate from a different AWS region.
- **Why:** ALB certificate binding requires a region-compatible certificate.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Install the application Sentry SDK after linking Vapor
- **Do:** Install and configure the Sentry Laravel SDK in the application when relying on Vapor’s linked Sentry integration.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the project links Sentry in Vapor but has no runtime SDK to report application exceptions.
- **Why:** Linking accounts does not install application instrumentation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Align Cloud and source-control access boundaries
- **Do:** Align Cloud organization boundaries with the source-control organizations that own the applications.
- **Flag when:** Flag when unrelated source-control organizations are placed in one Cloud organization despite needing separate access boundaries.
- **Why:** Aligned boundaries simplify repository access and organizational ownership.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Refresh Cloud network allowlists from published addresses
- **Do:** Build Cloud firewall allowlists from the current published IP endpoint and refresh them as addresses change.
- **Flag when:** Flag when firewall rules depend on a stale hardcoded Cloud IP list.
- **Why:** Cloud egress and service addresses can change over time.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Avoid double-prefixing Redis keys during migration
- **Do:** Clear copy-connection key prefixes when copying keys returned by SCAN that already contain their prefixes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a migration applies a client prefix again to SCAN-returned source keys.
- **Why:** Double-prefixed keys become invisible to the application under their expected names.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use a dedicated IAM role per log drain
- **Do:** Give each Cloud log drain its own scoped IAM role.
- **Flag when:** Flag when multiple drains share a broad IAM role or a drain uses unrelated application credentials.
- **Why:** A dedicated role limits permissions and permits independent revocation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Bind log-drain trust to the Cloud external ID
- **Do:** Require the Cloud organization external ID in the log-drain IAM role trust policy.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the log-drain role trusts a provider principal without the required external-ID condition.
- **Why:** An external-ID condition prevents unintended cross-customer role assumption.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Separate Nightwatch agents by application
- **Do:** Run a separate Nightwatch agent process and unique listening port for each monitored application sharing an agent host.
- **Flag when:** Flag when different applications share one token-bound agent process or collide on its listening port.
- **Why:** Each agent instance belongs to its application credentials and ingestion stream.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Point remote Nightwatch ingestion at the agent service
- **Do:** Set NIGHTWATCH_INGEST_URI to the reachable agent host or service address and port when the agent runs separately.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the application uses a loopback ingestion URI while its agent is in another container or host.
- **Why:** Separate services need an explicit reachable network address.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep a full-retention log sink alongside sampled telemetry
- **Do:** Use an independent unsampled log channel when Nightwatch sampling is enabled and complete log retention is required.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Nightwatch is the only log channel even though sampling can omit logs required by the retention policy.
- **Why:** Sampled telemetry does not provide a complete log archive.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Register Nightwatch failure handling early
- **Do:** Register unrecoverable Nightwatch exception handling in AppServiceProvider::register().
- **Flag when:** Flag when unrecoverable exception handling is registered only after the instrumentation initialization it must protect.
- **Why:** Early registration permits capturing failures during application bootstrapping.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Report Nightwatch failures outside Nightwatch
- **Do:** Send unrecoverable Nightwatch errors to a logging channel that does not use Nightwatch.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Nightwatch’s unrecoverable failure callback logs back through the same failing Nightwatch channel.
- **Why:** An independent channel avoids recursive failure and preserves diagnostics during telemetry outages.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Minimize Nightwatch user metadata
- **Do:** Return only necessary approved user fields from the Nightwatch user resolver.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the resolver serializes the entire user model or exposes sensitive attributes.
- **Why:** Telemetry identity does not require retaining every account field.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep Nightwatch agent ports private
- **Do:** Bind and firewall the Nightwatch ingestion port for trusted application networks only, including the Vapor network when applicable.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the Nightwatch agent is reachable from the public Internet or accepts traffic from unrelated networks.
- **Why:** The ingestion agent is an internal service and should not become a public entry point.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Remove duplicate agents before enabling managed Cloud Nightwatch
- **Do:** Remove custom Nightwatch agents from every Cloud cluster before enabling the built-in Cloud integration.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom agent processes remain active alongside Cloud’s built-in Nightwatch agent.
- **Why:** Duplicate agents can conflict with the managed integration and its lifecycle.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Host the Vapor Nightwatch agent on long-lived compute
- **Do:** Run the Nightwatch agent on a long-lived instance in the same network as the Vapor application.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the Vapor application attempts to keep its ingestion agent running inside short-lived Lambda invocations.
- **Why:** The agent needs a continuous process lifetime that Lambda does not provide.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Synchronize remote Nightwatch agent versions
- **Do:** Deploy matching Nightwatch package and agent versions to the Vapor application and its remote agent host.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the application and remote agent resolve different Nightwatch package versions.
- **Why:** Version mismatches can prevent telemetry ingestion.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep the Vapor agent helper application unmonitored
- **Do:** Do not enable the separate Forge Nightwatch integration on the helper application used only to host a Vapor agent.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the helper site enables its own Forge integration and interferes with its manually configured Vapor-agent process.
- **Why:** The helper site installs the agent runtime; it is not another monitored application in this setup.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep private npm credentials out of the repository
- **Do:** Remove committed npm registry tokens and supply them through Forge-managed credentials or an equivalent secret store.
- **Flag when:** Flag when tracked .npmrc or build scripts contain a real registry credential.
- **Why:** Source history is not an appropriate credential store.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use non-overlapping network ranges for peering
- **Do:** Assign non-overlapping VPC CIDRs before peering application networks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the networks to be peered contain overlapping address ranges.
- **Why:** Peering cannot route overlapping private addresses unambiguously.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use Private Cloud internal service networking
- **Do:** Enable internal networking for service calls between applications in the same Private Cloud.
- **Flag when:** Flag when same-Private-Cloud services call one another through public endpoints without a requirement.
- **Why:** Internal service routing keeps private communication within the intended network path.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Prefer same-region VPC peering for local service traffic
- **Do:** Place peered services in the same region where latency, residency, and availability requirements permit.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a peer connection incurs cross-region transfer charges despite no requirement for regional separation.
- **Why:** Same-region peering avoids unnecessary transfer costs and distance.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Enable RDS backup retention before read replicas
- **Do:** Set at least one day of RDS backup/PITR retention before creating read replicas that require it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when read replica provisioning targets a source RDS instance with backup retention disabled.
- **Why:** The source must satisfy the replication prerequisites before the replica can be created.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use read-only database users for reporting
- **Do:** Give reporting and manual inspection clients read-only RDS credentials.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a reporting process or inspection tool uses application write credentials without needing write operations.
- **Why:** Read-only access limits accidental data changes and credential authority.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Allow the dedicated tracing egress addresses
- **Do:** Allowlist Private Cloud’s dedicated egress IPs when sending Datadog traces to a restricted external agent.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the Datadog receiver blocks the actual Private Cloud egress sources.
- **Why:** Tracing requires the receiver firewall to permit the source addresses used by the application.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Preserve account access before disabling SSO
- **Do:** Verify organization members have a working alternate sign-in method before disabling Cloud SSO.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an SSO removal plan leaves members with no alternate authentication path.
- **Why:** Disabling the only sign-in route can lock the team out of its infrastructure.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use constant-time Nightwatch signature verification
- **Do:** Compute the documented Nightwatch webhook signature and compare it with Nightwatch-Signature using hash_equals().
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Nightwatch receiver compares signatures with == or ===, or processes the event before comparison.
- **Why:** A constant-time comparison avoids timing leakage during shared-secret signature verification.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$valid = $computed === $request->header('Nightwatch-Signature');
```

After:
```php
$valid = hash_equals($computed, (string) $request->header('Nightwatch-Signature'));
```

#### Expose Nightwatch webhooks as HTTPS POST endpoints
- **Do:** Accept Nightwatch webhooks only through HTTPS POST endpoints.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Nightwatch webhook is received over plain HTTP or a state-changing GET endpoint.
- **Why:** TLS protects webhook transport and POST matches the event-delivery contract.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Record relevant feature states in execution context
- **Do:** Add the feature-flag states needed to explain an execution path to Laravel Context.
- **Flag when:** Flag when telemetry from an experiment-dependent path omits the feature state that selected it.
- **Why:** Feature context helps distinguish release or experiment behavior from unrelated failures.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Feature changes the code path but is not recorded.
```

After:
```php
Context::add('feature_flags', ['new_checkout' => Feature::active('new_checkout')]);
```

#### Bound Nightwatch execution context size
- **Do:** Keep execution context within Nightwatch’s 65 KB limit by recording compact identifiers and selected metadata.
- **Flag when:** Flag when context stores large payloads or models that exceed the per-execution limit.
- **Why:** Oversized context is truncated and may lose the information needed for diagnosis.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Grant read-only telemetry access to viewers
- **Do:** Assign read-only Nightwatch access to collaborators who only inspect telemetry.
- **Flag when:** Flag when telemetry viewers receive administrative or configuration privileges without needing them.
- **Why:** Viewer roles reduce unnecessary authority over monitoring configuration and access.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Redact sensitive command arguments from Nightwatch
- **Do:** Configure Nightwatch redactCommands to remove secrets and sensitive arguments before command telemetry is transmitted.
- **Flag when:** Flag when captured Artisan command arguments include credentials or sensitive values without redaction.
- **Why:** Command-line arguments are part of telemetry and can expose secrets even when application logs are clean.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Set command telemetry sampling deliberately
- **Do:** Set NIGHTWATCH_COMMAND_SAMPLE_RATE according to the required command visibility and telemetry budget.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a high-volume command workload uses an unreviewed sampling default and exceeds its telemetry budget or loses required visibility.
- **Why:** Command sampling controls monitoring volume independently of application work.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Set the Nightwatch log threshold independently
- **Do:** Set NIGHTWATCH_LOG_LEVEL when Nightwatch should receive a different severity range from the application’s retained log channels.
- **Flag when:** Flag when operators change the global LOG_LEVEL solely to reduce Nightwatch traffic and unintentionally discard required local logs.
- **Why:** A destination-specific threshold controls telemetry without changing other retention needs.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Retain old storage access until migration completes
- **Do:** Keep old-provider credentials available until all required fallback objects have migrated.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the old storage credentials are revoked while the application still performs fallback reads.
- **Why:** Premature revocation makes unmigrated objects unavailable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Approve required PNPM build scripts explicitly
- **Do:** Use PNPM’s explicit dependency build-script approval settings for required trusted packages.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a build relies on hoisted node-linker or auto-install-peers to enable dependency scripts that PNPM has blocked.
- **Why:** Module linking and peer installation do not authorize build-script execution.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Interrupt old sub-minute scheduler runs after deployment
- **Do:** Run schedule:interrupt after activating a new release when sub-minute tasks are defined and the host does not already provide that lifecycle behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a sub-minute scheduler continues running the previous release after deployment.
- **Why:** A schedule:run process can remain alive for the minute and keep executing old code.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use schedule:work for local scheduling
- **Do:** Run schedule:work during local development rather than installing project cron entries on the developer machine.
- **Flag when:** Flag when local setup requires persistent host cron entries solely to exercise the Laravel schedule.
- **Why:** A foreground local runner is easy to start, observe, and stop with the project.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use managed scheduling when cron operations are unsupported
- **Do:** Choose a managed scheduler such as Cloud when the team cannot operate the required production cron or scheduler service.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production relies on an unmanaged schedule runner with no owner capable of configuring or monitoring it.
- **Why:** A recurring-task service needs an operational owner just like the web application.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Apply file-based maintenance mode to every server
- **Do:** Run artisan down on every serving node when using file-based maintenance mode, or deliberately switch to a shared maintenance driver.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a multi-server app uses the file driver but places only one node into maintenance mode.
- **Why:** The maintenance file is local to each server, so other nodes remain available unless handled separately.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Confirm sensitive Envoy tasks explicitly
- **Do:** Mark interactive Envoy tasks with confirm when their remote effects require operator confirmation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an operator-run Envoy task performs an explicitly approval-required remote operation without a confirmation gate.
- **Why:** A task-level confirmation makes the intended execution boundary visible before remote changes occur.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Pool backend HTTP connections when TLS setup dominates
- **Do:** Use a supported connection-pooling proxy when measured PHP-FPM backend traffic repeatedly pays costly TLS setup.
- **Flag when:** Flag when profiling shows backend TLS handshakes dominate request latency and no connection reuse strategy is configured.
- **Why:** A long-lived proxy can reuse connections beyond an individual PHP-FPM request lifecycle.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Buffer telemetry through a local agent
- **Do:** Use a local telemetry agent to buffer and batch monitoring data when synchronous remote ingestion would add material application overhead.
- **Flag when:** Flag when instrumentation sends per-event synchronous remote requests on hot application paths despite an available batching agent.
- **Why:** A local buffering boundary reduces network work on the request path.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Reuse connections in repeated provisioning operations
- **Do:** Reuse a server connection within a provisioning workflow that performs multiple operations against the same host.
- **Flag when:** Flag when each adjacent remote operation creates a new connection despite a reusable authenticated session.
- **Why:** Connection reuse reduces repeated network and authentication overhead.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Start production Kubernetes deployments with redundant replicas
- **Do:** Run at least two production application replicas when the service requires availability through an individual pod failure.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a production Kubernetes Deployment has one replica despite requiring continuity through pod restart or failure.
- **Why:** Multiple ready replicas allow service to continue while one pod is unavailable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Version Jigsaw production deployment settings
- **Do:** For a Jigsaw site deployed to Netlify, commit netlify.toml with the project's production build command and build_production publish directory.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Jigsaw deployment depends on untracked dashboard-only build settings or publishes the wrong generated directory.
- **Why:** Versioned build and publish settings let the repository reproduce its intended static-site deployment.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Keep server repository deploy keys read-only
- **Do:** Grant production server deploy keys read-only repository access when deployments only need to fetch source; do not enable repository writes for those keys.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a fetch-only deployment server holds a repository deploy key with write permission.
- **Why:** A compromised application host should not be able to push malicious source changes back to the repository.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Assign an onboarding mentor to each new developer
- **Do:** Assign each new developer a named onboarding mentor to help them learn the company, its technologies and the projects they will work on.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the developer onboarding plan has no designated person responsible for helping the new hire navigate the codebase and team practices.
- **Why:** An explicit mentor gives the new developer a reliable path for project context and setup questions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Make Valet external entrypoint files available to PhpStorm
- **Do:** When debugging Valet requests in PhpStorm, add the installed global Composer Valet directory to PHP include paths so the IDE can locate Valet's server.php entrypoint outside the application.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a Valet debugging session stops at an unresolved external server.php because the IDE knows only the project files.
- **Why:** Valet routes requests through its own entrypoint, whose source location is separate from the application repository.
- **Enforced by:** manual
