```php
// Register the intended policy explicitly for the supported panel context.
```

#### Validate custom super-admin creation input and keep credentials out of code
- **Do:** Validate custom super-admin creation input and keep credentials out of code.
- **Flag when:** Flag when createSuperAdminUsing bypasses Shield validation or hard-codes live credentials.
- **Why:** Replacing the built-in flow also replaces its validation boundary.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
FilamentShield::createSuperAdminUsing(fn () => User::create(["password" => "secret"]));
```

After:
```php
// Validate email/password and hash the supplied password inside the custom callback.
```

#### Authorize role management through a registered RolePolicy
- **Do:** Authorize role management through a registered RolePolicy.
- **Flag when:** Flag when administrators can edit roles without a role-management permission boundary.
- **Why:** Role changes can grant broader application access.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"register_role_policy" => false,
```

After:
```php
"register_role_policy" => true, // provide an appropriate RolePolicy
```

#### Treat generated seeders containing real password hashes as secrets
- **Do:** Treat generated seeders containing real password hashes as secrets.
- **Flag when:** Flag when exported user hashes are published or committed without protection.
- **Why:** Password hashes remain crackable credential material.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Public seeder generated with --include-passwords.
```

After:
```php
// Exclude password hashes from exported seeders, or protect the artifact as a secret.
```

#### Require explicit authorization on Log Viewer pages and API endpoints
- **Do:** Require explicit authorization on Log Viewer pages and API endpoints.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production Log Viewer allows access without a defined gate/callback or omits AuthorizeLogViewer middleware.
- **Why:** Logs expose sensitive operational data through both HTML and API routes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"require_auth_in_production" => false,
```

After:
```php
"require_auth_in_production" => true, // keep middleware and define viewLogViewer
```

#### Authorize Log Viewer deletion and downloads separately when needed
- **Do:** Authorize Log Viewer deletion and downloads separately when needed.
- **Flag when:** Flag when every log viewer can delete/download logs despite a narrower operation policy.
- **Why:** Viewing logs does not necessarily grant destructive or export permissions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Rely on viewer access for every operation.
```

After:
```php
Gate::define("deleteLogFile", fn (User $u) => $u->can("manageLogs"));
```

#### Register package gate defaults only when the application has not defined them
- **Do:** Register package gate defaults only when the application has not defined them.
- **Flag when:** Flag when package boot overwrites an application authorization definition.
- **Why:** Applications must retain control of their permission policy.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Gate::define("downloadLogFile", $default);
```

After:
```php
if (! Gate::has("downloadLogFile")) Gate::define("downloadLogFile", $default);
```

#### Gate privileged data properties with non-bypassable conditions
- **Do:** Gate privileged data properties with non-bypassable conditions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a client include() can force a sensitive lazy property despite lacking permission.
- **Why:** Optional inclusion is separate from authorization.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Lazy::create(fn () => $secret)
```

After:
```php
Lazy::when(fn () => auth()->user()->can("viewSecret", $record), fn () => $secret)
```

#### Type conditionally excluded data properties as Optional
- **Do:** Type conditionally excluded data properties as Optional.
- **Flag when:** Flag when excluded validated keys are required by a Data constructor/property type.
- **Why:** Excluded input is absent rather than an ordinary value.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public string $internal;
```

After:
```php
public string|Optional $internal;
```

#### Do not assume magic Data factories run the normal transformation pipeline
- **Do:** Do not assume magic Data factories run the normal transformation pipeline.
- **Flag when:** Flag when custom from* factories depend on implicit name mapping, casts or defaults that are skipped.
- **Why:** Magic creation bypasses parts of the ordinary data pipeline.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
public static function fromLegacy($input): self { /* assumes automatic mapping */ }
```

After:
```php
public static function fromLegacy($input): self { return new self(name: $input["legacy_name"]); }
```

#### Use Gate-based permission APIs when access depends on Gate hooks
- **Do:** Use Gate-based permission APIs when access depends on Gate hooks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when hasPermissionTo-style calls bypass a required Gate::before super-admin rule.
- **Why:** Direct package lookups do not run the full Gate pipeline.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$user->hasPermissionTo("edit posts")
```

After:
```php
$user->can("edit posts")
```

#### Use an after-hook bypass only where explicit denials must retain priority
- **Do:** Use an after-hook bypass only where explicit denials must retain priority.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a super-admin before hook overrides business-rule denials that must apply to everyone.
- **Why:** Gate::after can fill a null result but cannot override an explicit false; policy methods must return null where bypass is intended.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Gate::before(fn ($u) => $u->isSuperAdmin() ? true : null);
```

After:
```php
Gate::after(fn ($u) => $u->isSuperAdmin() ? true : null); // only null decisions may be granted
```

#### Choose permission middleware priority deliberately relative to model binding
- **Do:** Choose permission middleware priority deliberately relative to model binding.
- **Flag when:** Flag when binding runs first and returns 404 where the application requires an actor-level 403 before resource lookup.
- **Why:** Middleware order changes denial semantics and information exposure.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Binding precedes the required global permission check.
```

After:
```php
// Configure permission middleware before SubstituteBindings for actor-only checks.
```

#### Resolve and persist team context before authorization-dependent binding
- **Do:** Resolve and persist team context before authorization-dependent binding.
- **Flag when:** Flag when team-dependent policy checks run before team resolution or later Livewire requests lose the resolver.
- **Why:** The active team must be correct at every permission boundary.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Team resolver runs after binding and is absent on Livewire updates.
```

After:
```php
// Prioritize team middleware and register it with Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware.
```

#### Separate own-resource and all-resource permissions and check ownership
- **Do:** Separate own-resource and all-resource permissions and check ownership.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an edit-own permission grants access to resources the actor does not own.
- **Why:** The permission name alone does not establish ownership.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return $user->can("edit own posts");
```

After:
```php
return $user->can("edit all posts") || ($user->can("edit own posts") && $post->user_id === $user->id);
```

#### Retain package permission integration with Gate unless explicitly replaced
- **Do:** Retain package permission integration with Gate unless explicitly replaced.
- **Flag when:** Flag when register_permission_check_method is disabled without equivalent Gate logic.
- **Why:** Native can/authorize calls need the package permission boundary.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
"register_permission_check_method" => false,
```

After:
```php
"register_permission_check_method" => true,
```

#### Translate user-facing exception messages
- **Do:** Translate user-facing exception messages.
- **Flag when:** Flag when displayed package exception messages are fixed untranslatable strings.
- **Why:** Applications need consistent localized errors.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
throw new RuntimeException("Access denied");
```

After:
```php
throw new RuntimeException(__("Access denied"));
```

#### Remove deprecated post-build backup encryption listeners
- **Do:** Remove deprecated post-build backup encryption listeners.
- **Flag when:** Flag when EncryptBackupArchive is still manually registered when the installed package encrypts during archive construction.
- **Why:** Double processing wastes work and can corrupt the intended workflow.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
EncryptBackupArchive::class // manually registered listener
```

After:
```php
// Use the package archive-build encryption configuration.
```

#### Represent finite behavior-bearing configuration choices with backed enums
- **Do:** Represent finite behavior-bearing configuration choices with backed enums.
- **Flag when:** Flag when free-form config strings are repeatedly interpreted with divergent branches.
- **Why:** A validated enum centralizes allowed values and behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
if ($config === "aes256") { /* repeated mapping */ }
```

After:
```php
$mode = EncryptionMode::from($config); $algorithm = $mode->algorithm();
```

#### Normalize absent optional secret values before enabling security features
- **Do:** Normalize absent optional secret values before enabling security features.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an empty-string secret is treated as a configured encryption credential.
- **Why:** Absent credentials must not silently enable an unusable security mode.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
if ($password !== null) enableEncryption($password);
```

After:
```php
$password = filled($password) ? $password : null; if ($password !== null) enableEncryption($password);
```

#### Use a protected cache bypass for profiling instead of globally disabling caching
- **Do:** Use a protected cache bypass for profiling instead of globally disabling caching.
- **Flag when:** Flag when profiling disables production caching for all clients or exposes an unauthenticated bypass.
- **Why:** A scoped bypass preserves normal traffic behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Replace request-specific tokens and values in cached HTML
- **Do:** Replace request-specific tokens and values in cached HTML.
- **Flag when:** Flag when cached responses replay stale CSRF tokens or another user/request value.
- **Why:** Dynamic placeholders preserve correct per-request state.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Cache rendered HTML including a session CSRF token.
```

After:
```php
// Keep CsrfTokenReplacer and add replacers for other request-specific fields.
```

#### Include host, URI, method and authorization context in response-cache keys
- **Do:** Include host, URI, method and authorization context in response-cache keys.
- **Flag when:** Flag when different users/hosts/methods share a cache entry containing distinct data.
- **Why:** Cache identities must preserve response isolation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$key = $request->path();
```

After:
```php
$key = hash("xxh128", $host."|".$method."|".$uri."|".$userSuffix);
```

#### Use deliberate readable JSON flags for database-only JSON encoding
- **Do:** Use deliberate readable JSON flags for database-only JSON encoding.
- **Flag when:** Flag when database JSON serialization escapes Unicode/slashes unnecessarily under an adopted readable-storage policy.
- **Why:** Encoding choices should match storage rather than HTML contexts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
json_encode($data);
```

After:
```php
json_encode($data, JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
```

#### Declare only additional STI child fillable fields when the package merges parent fields
- **Do:** For Parental child models whose getFillable() merges parent fields, declare only child-specific fields with the Laravel 13 Fillable attribute and retain the inherited mass-assignment boundary.
- **Flag when:** Flag duplicated inherited fields in a Parental child allowlist or replacing package inheritance behavior merely to modernize declaration syntax.
- **Why:** The HasParent merge supplies shared fields.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
protected $fillable = ["shared_name", "child_field"];
```

After:
```php
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Fillable;

#[Fillable(["child_field"])]
class ChildRecord extends ParentRecord
{
    use \Parental\HasParent;
}
```

#### Use supported relationship paths for aggregate methods
- **Do:** Use supported relationship paths for aggregate methods.
- **Flag when:** Flag when withCount/withSum/$withCount uses an unsupported dotted nested relation.
- **Why:** Aggregate APIs do not resolve all eager-loading path forms.
- **Enforced by:** partial: larastan:RelationExistenceRule

Before:
```php
Post::withCount("comments.author")->get();
```

After:
```php
// Define a supported direct/through relationship or explicit aggregate subquery.
```

#### Expose only declared count/existence aggregates for client-selectable includes
- **Do:** Expose only declared count/existence aggregates for client-selectable includes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when clients can request arbitrary relationship/column aggregates or full records when only a count is required.
- **Why:** A narrow declared include contract limits data and query work.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
AllowedInclude::relationship("permissions")
```

After:
```php
AllowedInclude::count("permissionsCount")
```

#### Verify rich-editor rendering after tightening sanitizer attributes
- **Do:** Verify rich-editor rendering after tightening sanitizer attributes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a sanitizer change removes attributes needed for legitimate editor output without checking rendered content.
- **Why:** Security restrictions must be tested against supported formatting.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Drop every attribute without testing rich-content display.
```

After:
```php
// Render representative editor content under the restricted allowlist.
```

#### Declare and migrate sensitive settings as encrypted values
- **Do:** Declare and migrate sensitive settings as encrypted values.
- **Flag when:** Flag when secret settings are persisted plaintext or an encryption declaration leaves old plaintext rows unmigrated.
- **Why:** Encryption must cover existing data as well as future writes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Settings::add("api.token", $token);
```

After:
```php
// Declare the setting encrypted and migrate existing values with the settings migrator.
```

#### Serialize queued model references using the framework model serialization traits
- **Do:** Serialize queued model references using the framework model serialization traits.
- **Flag when:** Flag when queued jobs with public Eloquent models serialize full object graphs without SerializesModels/Queueable.
- **Why:** Framework serialization stores model identifiers and restores models deliberately.
- **Enforced by:** partial: larastan:JobWithModelPropertyDeclaresSerializesModelsRule

Before:
```php
class Job implements ShouldQueue { public User $user; }
```

After:
```php
class Job implements ShouldQueue { use \Illuminate\Foundation\Queue\Queueable; public User $user; }
```

#### Consume OAuth state once during callback handling
- **Do:** Consume OAuth state once during callback handling.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the saved authorization state remains reusable after a callback.
- **Why:** One-time state consumption prevents replay of a prior browser authorization attempt.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$state = session("state");
```

After:
```php
$state = session()->pull("state");
```

#### Authorize action access before validation and business processing where the action contract requires it
- **Do:** Authorize action access before validation and business processing where the action contract requires it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an unauthorized actor can trigger validation-sensitive work before the action access check.
- **Why:** Early admission checks avoid information disclosure and wasted work; resource-dependent checks still need resolved context.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$data = $this->validate($rules); Gate::authorize("create", Record::class);
```

After:
```php
Gate::authorize("create", Record::class); $data = $this->validate($rules);
```

#### Normalize nondeterministic response values before snapshot comparison
- **Do:** Normalize nondeterministic response values before snapshot comparison.
- **Flag when:** Flag when snapshot tests compare per-request CSRF tokens or similar random values literally.
- **Why:** Stable normalization avoids unrelated failures while keeping structural assertions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
expect($html)->toMatchSnapshot();
```

After:
```php
expect($normalizer->replaceCsrfTokens($html))->toMatchSnapshot();
```

#### Return no label for unauthorized or invalid selectable options
- **Do:** Return no label for unauthorized or invalid selectable options.
- **Flag when:** Flag when getOptionLabelUsing resolves a client-submitted option outside the allowed dataset.
- **Why:** Option resolution must retain the same visibility boundary as the list.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return User::find($value)?->name;
```

After:
```php
return User::visibleTo(auth()->user())->find($value)?->name;
```

#### Test import authorization again at submission after access changes
- **Do:** Test import authorization again at submission after access changes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when import tests authorize only the initial mounted form.
- **Why:** Permission can be revoked before the import is submitted.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Only initial import form visibility is tested.
```

After:
```php
// Mount valid import, revoke permission, submit and assert denial.
```

#### Cascade authorization pivot deletion where parent removal should remove grants
- **Do:** Cascade authorization pivot deletion where parent removal should remove grants.
- **Flag when:** Flag when orphaned role/permission pivot rows remain after deleting their parent.
- **Why:** Database constraints preserve grant relationship integrity.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$table->foreignId("role_id")->constrained();
```

After:
```php
$table->foreignId("role_id")->constrained()->cascadeOnDelete();
```

#### Retain executable-extension rejection in custom upload filename sanitizers
- **Do:** Retain executable-extension rejection in custom upload filename sanitizers.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom Media Library sanitizer replaces built-in executable-extension protection without an equivalent check.
- **Why:** Sanitization must not permit executable files on a web-served disk.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Custom sanitizer only removes spaces.
```

After:
```php
// Preserve the package executable-extension denylist and safe storage policy.
```

#### Review every administrative route for its required middleware and policy
- **Do:** Review every administrative route for its required middleware and policy.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an administrative endpoint has no explicit authenticated/authorized admission path.
- **Why:** Administrative route coverage needs to include forgotten custom actions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Route::get("/admin/reports", $handler);
```

After:
```php
Route::get("/admin/reports", $handler)->middleware(["auth", "can:viewReports"]);
```

#### Use application access controls or field encryption for live-database disclosure risks
- **Do:** Use application access controls or field encryption for live-database disclosure risks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when disk encryption is treated as protecting data from a caller with a live database connection.
- **Why:** Transparent storage encryption does not restrict authorized database reads.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Rely only on encrypted database disks for API-token confidentiality.
```

After:
```php
protected function casts(): array { return ["api_token" => "encrypted"]; }
```

#### Control encryption-key access independently from encrypted-record access
- **Do:** Control encryption-key access independently from encrypted-record access.
- **Flag when:** Flag when database-only readers can also fetch the decryption keys by default.
- **Why:** Independent access limits the effect of a storage-only compromise.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use a vetted hybrid encryption design for large recipient-specific encrypted payloads
- **Do:** Use a vetted hybrid encryption design for large recipient-specific encrypted payloads.
- **Flag when:** Flag when bulk payloads are encrypted directly with asymmetric primitives or a shared key defeats recipient isolation.
- **Why:** Envelope encryption combines scalable symmetric data encryption with recipient-specific key protection.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Apply raw public-key encryption to arbitrary large data.
```

After:
```php
// Use a vetted envelope-encryption library: random data key plus recipient-wrapped data key.
```

#### Use a production-grade key provider for recipient-specific encryption
- **Do:** Bind the recipient-encryption key-provider contract to a production implementation through a service provider, keeping shared testing providers confined to tests.
- **Flag when:** Flag a shared testing key provider in production recipient isolation or an unsupported global bind() call.
- **Why:** A shared testing key cannot enforce real recipient separation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
bind(KeyProvider::class, SharedTestingKeyProvider::class);
```

After:
```php
// In AppServiceProvider::register(); these are application-specific types.
$this->app->bind(KeyProvider::class, ProductionKmsKeyProvider::class);
```

#### Delegate state-dependent behavior to the current state implementation
- **Do:** Delegate state-dependent behavior to the current state implementation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a state-pattern domain repeats large state switches in every action.
- **Why:** State objects centralize allowed behavior for each state.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
switch ($order->status) { /* repeated transition behavior */ }
```

After:
```php
$order->state->ship();
```

#### Propagate the active tenant to queued work and restore it safely
- **Do:** Propagate the active tenant to queued work and restore it safely.
- **Flag when:** Flag when tenant-specific jobs execute without their originating tenant context or leak prior worker tenant state.
- **Why:** Workers must resolve data under the intended tenant.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
TenantJob::dispatch($recordId);
```

After:
```php
TenantJob::dispatch($tenantId, $recordId); // establish and clear tenant context in execution
```

#### Wait for moderation completion before downstream video processing
- **Do:** Wait for moderation completion before downstream video processing.
- **Flag when:** Flag when video processing starts before the required moderation result is accepted.
- **Why:** The workflow must enforce its content approval dependency.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
ProcessVideo::dispatch($video);
```

After:
```php
// Dispatch ProcessVideo from the successful moderation-completion event.
```

#### Use output-only resource objects for data that never accepts requests
- **Do:** Use output-only resource objects for data that never accepts requests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an output-only spatie/laravel-data object carries unnecessary input validation/authorization behavior.
- **Why:** A Resource expresses the output contract and avoids input-pipeline work.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
class ArtistOutput extends Data {}
```

After:
```php
class ArtistOutput extends \Spatie\LaravelData\Resource {}
```

#### Make child props reactive only when parent updates must propagate
- **Do:** Make child props reactive only when parent updates must propagate.
- **Flag when:** Flag when #[Reactive] tracks a child prop that does not need parent-change synchronization.
- **Why:** Unneeded reactivity adds state synchronization work.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
#[Reactive] public array $staticOptions;
```

After:
```php
public array $staticOptions;
```

### Testing

#### Exercise two-factor enrollment and recovery flows
- **Do:** Test the application two-factor setup flow, including QR provisioning and recovery-code use or management, alongside ordinary authentication tests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when two-factor authentication is enabled but tests cover only password login and omit QR setup and recovery-code flows.
- **Why:** Enrollment and recovery are separate security-sensitive paths that ordinary login coverage does not exercise.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Authentication coverage exercises only password login.
```

After:
```php
// Exercise QR provisioning, confirm enrollment, and authenticate with an issued recovery code; verify the documented recovery-code lifecycle.
```

#### Record outbound HTTP outcomes without changing promise behavior
- **Do:** When adding outgoing-request telemetry through Guzzle middleware, record both fulfilled and rejected requests, then return the original response or propagate the original rejection.
- **Flag when:** Flag when telemetry records only successful requests, swallows rejections, or changes a successful response while observing it.
- **Why:** Missing failure observations bias latency data, and instrumentation must preserve client behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return $handler($request, $options)->then(fn ($response) => $record($request));
```

After:
```php
return $handler($request, $options)->then(
    function ($response) use ($record) { $record(); return $response; },
    function ($error) use ($record) { $record(); return new \GuzzleHttp\Promise\RejectedPromise($error); },
);
```

#### Test every advertised Redis client integration
- **Do:** Run Redis-dependent package behavior against each supported client, such as PhpRedis, Predis or Relay. Declare missing-extension skips locally and ensure CI actually exercises each advertised client.
- **Flag when:** Flag when client-specific Redis commands or response handling support multiple clients but tests run against only one.
- **Why:** Redis clients differ in method signatures and returned values even when they contact the same server.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Raw Redis integration is tested only through PhpRedis.
```

After:
```php
// Dataset: phpredis, predis, relay; configure the client before resolving Redis.
// Assert the same observable operation contract for every supported client in CI.
```

#### Exercise each supported database engine in package CI
- **Do:** For packages promising multiple database engines, run database integration tests against every advertised engine and relevant supported version using independently configured CI jobs or matrix entries.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a multi-engine package is tested only on SQLite or one database family despite driver-specific migrations or queries.
- **Why:** Real-engine compatibility tests detect SQL, schema and type-conversion differences that an in-memory substitute cannot prove.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Assert Inertia page identity and contractual props
- **Do:** Use assertInertia() to verify the intended page component and the presence, value or absence of props that belong to the response contract.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an Inertia endpoint test checks only HTTP success and ignores the page or props its consumer requires.
- **Why:** A successful response can render the wrong page or expose the wrong data.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$this->get(route('profile.edit'))->assertOk();
```

After:
```php
$this->get(route('profile.edit'))->assertInertia(fn (\Inertia\Testing\AssertableInertia $page) => $page->component('settings/profile')->where('user.id', $user->id)->missing('user.password'));
```

#### Run protocol conformance checks for protocol server changes
- **Do:** Run the relevant protocol conformance or fuzzing suite in CI alongside unit tests for a maintained protocol server, such as Autobahn for a WebSocket implementation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when protocol handling changes are checked only through hand-picked unit cases despite a maintained conformance suite.
- **Why:** Conformance suites exercise framing, malformed messages and edge cases beyond typical application examples.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Reproduce Laravel warning failures in relevant standalone tests
- **Do:** When a standalone PHPUnit regression depends on Laravel converting a PHP warning to an exception, install an equivalent scoped error handler for that scenario and restore the previous handler in finally.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an isolated regression test passes after emitting the warning that would fail the same operation inside Laravel.
- **Why:** Matching the relevant error boundary prevents a plain PHPUnit test from missing an application failure.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$provider->user(); // Undefined-array-key warning is not exercised as an application exception.
```

After:
```php
set_error_handler(static function ($severity, $message, $file, $line) { throw new \ErrorException($message, 0, $severity, $file, $line); });
try { $provider->user(); } finally { restore_error_handler(); }
```

#### Test rejection of invalid OAuth and OIDC flow bindings
- **Do:** Add negative tests for the OAuth/OIDC checks the integration implements, including missing or mismatched state and nonce and invalid issuer or audience; assert the specific rejection and absence of authentication.
- **Flag when:** Flag when social login tests cover only a successful callback and omit the security checks applicable to that flow.
- **Why:** A working happy path does not prove that an attacker cannot substitute a callback or identity token.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Only a successful social-login callback is tested.
```

After:
```php
// Separate cases arrange missing/wrong state, missing/wrong nonce and invalid issuer/audience where applicable; assert the documented exception or rejection and no authenticated user.
```

#### Test dashboard access defaults outside the local environment
- **Do:** Exercise a clean diagnostic-dashboard installation under a non-local test environment, asserting that guests and ordinary authenticated users receive the documented denial until explicitly authorized.
- **Flag when:** Flag when dashboard authorization tests run only as local or always install permissive host authorization before testing access.
- **Why:** Local access shortcuts can conceal missing production authorization defaults.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// APP_ENV=local; every dashboard request is allowed before the policy is exercised.
```

After:
```php
// Dedicated non-local test environment; no permissive host provider.
$this->get('/telescope')->assertForbidden();
$this->actingAs(User::factory()->create())->get('/telescope')->assertForbidden();
```

#### Create per-instance mutable Vue prop defaults
- **Do:** When using Vue withDefaults(), provide factory functions for array and object defaults so component instances receive separate mutable values.
- **Flag when:** Flag when withDefaults() supplies a shared array or object as a mutable prop default.
- **Why:** Shared mutable defaults let one component instance affect another.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
const props = withDefaults(defineProps<Props>(), { breadcrumbs: [] });
```

After:
```php
const props = withDefaults(defineProps<Props>(), { breadcrumbs: () => [] });
```

#### Exclude external code and intentionally invalid fixtures by path
- **Do:** Use explicit static-analysis path exclusions for vendor code and deliberately invalid diagnostic fixtures, while continuing to analyze maintained first-party code.
- **Flag when:** Flag when unrelated external code or intentionally broken fixtures are included and their diagnostics are hidden with broad error ignores instead of selecting the intended analysis scope.
- **Why:** Path-based scope expresses ownership without suppressing matching errors in valid application code.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
parameters:
    ignoreErrors:
        - '#Call to an undefined method#' # Intended only for deliberately broken fixtures.
```

After:
```php
parameters:
    excludePaths:
        analyse:
            - tests/Fixtures/Invalid/*
```

#### Keep classmap class identities unambiguous
- **Do:** Give Composer classmap-loaded classes unique fully qualified names; namespace fixtures or use descriptive suffixes such as Factory and Seeder for legacy global classes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when two files in Composer classmap paths declare the same fully qualified class name.
- **Why:** Ambiguous class resolution can load the wrong class and makes optimized autoloading unreliable.
- **Enforced by:** partial: larastan:PHPStan\Rules\Classes\DuplicateClassDeclarationRule

Before:
```php
// Two different classmap files both declare global class User {}.
```

After:
```php
// Use distinct names such as UserFactory and UserSeeder, or distinct namespaces.
```

#### Replace other module contracts in isolated module tests
- **Do:** In tests intended to isolate one module, replace collaborators from other modules through their public contracts, and retain separate integration tests for cross-module behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag when isolated module tests bootstrap unrelated module internals to exercise the subject, or reach into private collaborators instead of using the declared boundary.
- **Why:** Contract-level doubles keep module tests focused while integration coverage verifies real collaboration.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Inventory module unit test boots full Payment and Shipping implementations.
```

After:
```php
$this->mock(PaymentGateway::class)->shouldReceive('charge')->once()->andReturn($receipt);
// Exercise inventory behavior; test real module collaboration separately.
```

#### Run project checks through the intended container environment
- **Do:** For projects using a containerized development runtime, provide tooling commands that run tests, coverage and static analysis inside that runtime.
- **Flag when:** Flag when documented project checks silently use host PHP or extensions that differ from the development container.
- **Why:** A shared runtime prevents dependency, extension and configuration differences from changing check results.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
vendor/bin/phpunit # Uses whatever PHP is installed on the host.
```

After:
```php
./vendor/bin/sail test
./vendor/bin/sail php vendor/bin/phpstan analyse
```

#### Pilot new capabilities with explicitly selected cohorts
- **Do:** Use feature flags to expose a new capability to selected customers for beta feedback before a general rollout.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a planned customer beta requires enabling unfinished behavior for every user or maintaining a separate code fork.
- **Why:** A selected cohort provides feedback while keeping wider release deliberate.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// New API behavior is enabled globally to let a few customers try it.
```

After:
```php
// Resolve a beta flag per selected customer and keep the established behavior for other customers until rollout.
```

#### Preserve provider identifier formats in synthetic fixtures
- **Do:** When factories synthesize external-provider identifiers, use the identifier prefix and shape expected for that resource type without making a real provider call.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a synthetic external identifier has the wrong resource prefix or violates the identifier shape consumed by application validation or parsing.
- **Why:** Format-compatible fake identifiers exercise realistic local behavior without creating remote provider resources.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
'stripe_price' => 'subscription-item-1',
```

After:
```php
'stripe_price' => 'price_'.Str::random(40),
```

#### Reuse expensive external catalog fixtures only while they remain independent
- **Do:** Create expensive external integration fixtures that tests only read or reference once per test class in setUpBeforeClass(), and retain their provider IDs for reuse. Keep per-test mutable customer or transaction state separate.
- **Flag when:** Flag when unchanged provider catalog fixtures are recreated for every case despite substantial setup cost, or class-shared fixtures are mutated so later tests depend on earlier ones.
- **Why:** Reusing stable provider fixtures reduces API traffic and test runtime while keeping mutable scenarios independent.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
protected function setUp(): void { parent::setUp(); /* Recreate the same remote product and price for every case. */ }
```

After:
```php
protected static string $priceId;

public static function setUpBeforeClass(): void
{
    parent::setUpBeforeClass();
    static::$priceId = static::createSandboxCatalogPrice();
}
// Each case creates its own customer and references this unchanged price.
```

#### Own real server lifetimes in end-to-end process tests
- **Do:** For integration tests that exercise a real long-running server, start the test-owned server in setup, wait for readiness, and stop it in teardown even when the test fails.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a server integration test relies on an undocumented pre-existing process, runs before the server is ready, or leaves its listener or child process running after completion.
- **Why:** An explicit server lifetime makes end-to-end checks reproducible and prevents leaked processes or occupied ports from affecting later tests.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Requires a manually started daemon and never stops it.
```

After:
```php
protected function setUp(): void
{
    parent::setUp();
    $this->startTestServer();
    $this->waitForTestServer();
}

protected function tearDown(): void
{
    try {
        $this->stopTestServer();
    } finally {
        parent::tearDown();
    }
}
// Helpers must also clean up a partial startup failure.
```

#### Honor model timestamp metadata in generic ordering adapters
- **Do:** When a reusable model-aware builder or adapter supplies the default column for latest()/oldest(), derive it from the model's getCreatedAtColumn() and preserve the documented fallback and any explicit caller-supplied column.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a generic model-aware ordering implementation hard-codes created_at and therefore ignores a model's customized creation timestamp column.
- **Why:** Using model metadata keeps reusable ordering behavior compatible with models that rename their creation timestamp.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$column ??= 'created_at';
return $this->orderBy($column, 'desc');
```

After:
```php
$column ??= $this->model->getCreatedAtColumn() ?? 'created_at';
return $this->orderBy($column, 'desc');
```

#### Retain the Scout identity key in restricted search projections
- **Do:** When a custom search-engine adapter narrows retrieved attributes before hydrating Scout models, ensure the result projection still includes the model's getScoutKeyName() field.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a custom search projection can omit the Scout identity field that result-to-model mapping requires.
- **Why:** A search hit cannot be mapped back to its model when its matching identifier was removed from the returned fields.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$params['attributesToRetrieve'] = ['title']; // Adapter later needs the missing Scout key.
```

After:
```php
$key = $builder->model->getScoutKeyName();
$params['attributesToRetrieve'] = array_values(array_unique([$key, ...$params['attributesToRetrieve']]));
```

#### Keep ordinary Scout tests independent of remote indexes
- **Do:** In tests that do not exercise remote indexing, select Scout's null driver for no-op indexing or collection driver for local search, or scope model changes with withoutSyncingToSearch(). Restore syncing if it is disabled explicitly. Reserve real engine checks for dedicated integration tests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when ordinary model tests unexpectedly contact a remote search index, call a nonexistent Scout::fake(), or leave model search syncing disabled for later tests.
- **Why:** An explicit local or no-op Scout boundary prevents unrelated tests from depending on remote search services and indexing side effects.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Scout::fake(); // This API is not provided.
```

After:
```php
config(['scout.driver' => 'null']);
// Or use 'collection' when the test needs local search results.
// Product::withoutSyncingToSearch(fn () => Product::factory()->create());
```

#### Reuse backend contract scenarios across supported search engines
- **Do:** For interchangeable search engines, share the engine-independent setup and scenarios through a focused test trait or equivalent contract suite, with each engine test class selecting its driver. Keep engine-specific behavior and expected ordering explicit.
- **Flag when:** Flag when equivalent supported engines duplicate large common scenario bodies that drift, or a shared contract test assumes semantics that differ between the engines.
- **Why:** Shared scenarios keep the common search contract consistent while separate engine assertions retain meaningful backend differences.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Every engine class maintains its own copied search setup and query scenarios.
```

After:
```php
trait SearchContractScenarios
{
    abstract protected static function scoutDriver(): string;
    // Shared supported scenarios; backend-specific expectations stay in each class.
}
```

#### Repeat changed tests to expose intermittent failures
- **Do:** Use repeated local execution of new, changed or suspect timing-sensitive tests to expose intermittent failures before integration, preserving failures for diagnosis instead of retrying until a run passes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a known intermittent test is accepted after one lucky passing run or repetition hides the original failure.
- **Why:** Repeated independent runs reveal timing and random-state defects that a single run can miss.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
// In a targeted Pest test declaration:
it('preserves the concurrent update', function () { /* assertions */ })->repeat(20);
```

#### Use PHPUnit stubs when no interaction expectation is required
- **Do:** Use createStub() for PHPUnit doubles used only to supply dependency return values or exceptions; use createMock() when the test verifies an interaction contract.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a PHPUnit mock has no interaction expectations and serves only as a return-value stub.
- **Why:** The chosen double expresses whether the test controls an input or verifies a collaborator interaction.
- **Enforced by:** partial: rector:ExpressionCreateMockToCreateStubRector, partial: rector:PropertyCreateMockToCreateStubRector, partial: rector:CreateStubOverCreateMockArgRector

Before:
```php
$client = $this->createMock(Client::class);
$client->method('fetch')->willReturn($payload);
```

After:
```php
$client = $this->createStub(Client::class);
$client->method('fetch')->willReturn($payload);
```

#### Assert promised event-listener registration explicitly
- **Do:** When listener registration is an application or package integration contract, assert the event/listener pair with Event::assertListening(), separately from focused listener behavior tests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a required listener can be undiscovered or unregistered while its direct handler tests still pass.
- **Why:** A handler can work correctly yet never execute if the event dispatcher is not wired to it.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
Event::assertListening(OrderPaid::class, SendReceipt::class);
```

#### Proxy local service domains without competing for the same listener
- **Do:** When Valet must coexist with a local Docker or other HTTP service, keep that service on its own port and route the desired .test hostname through a Valet proxy instead of starting two port-80 listeners.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a local multi-service setup assigns port 80 to both Valet and the proxied application.
- **Why:** A single front listener preserves convenient local domains without port-binding collisions.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Derive selected-child relations from the existing has-many definition
- **Do:** When selecting one child from an existing has-many association, derive it with one()->latestOfMany()/ofMany() when suitable, so foreign keys and shared relationship constraints remain defined in one place.
- **Flag when:** Flag when paired has-many and selected-child relations repeat keys or shared constraints that can drift independently.
- **Why:** Deriving the relation preserves the established association while adding only its selection rule.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
public function latestLogin(): HasOne
{
    return $this->logins()->one()->latestOfMany();
}
```

#### Execute deferred callbacks deliberately when asserting their effects
- **Do:** In a focused test that needs a defer() callback effect before a lifecycle boundary would run it, call withoutDefer() before the action so callbacks execute immediately. Keep separate lifecycle tests when deferral timing is the contract.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a test reads deferred results before callbacks run or disables deferral while claiming to verify its timing.
- **Why:** Explicit callback execution prevents missing effects without confusing synchronous test behavior with production deferral.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
$this->withoutDefer();
$service->perform();
// Assert the callback-owned effect.
```

#### Verify public type annotations in the tools consumers use
- **Do:** For shared package type metadata, verify intended inference in the supported IDEs and analyzers, using portable native/PHPDoc contracts where possible rather than improving one tool by breaking another.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a public annotation change is accepted solely on one analyzer result despite breaking promised PhpStorm or VS Code inference.
- **Why:** Public type metadata serves multiple consumers and needs compatibility checks like other public interfaces.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Account for parent creation when making factory models
- **Do:** For tests intended to avoid database writes, inspect nested factories used as foreign-key defaults before choosing make(); override the relevant relationship/key with a suitable in-memory value or explicit fixture instead of assuming make() prevents all related persistence.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a supposedly database-free test calls factory make() but its foreign-key factory creates a parent row.
- **Why:** An unsaved child can still need a persisted parent ID when resolving factory relationship attributes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// user_id => User::factory() in OrderFactory
$order = Order::factory()->make(); // May create the parent user.
```

After:
```php
$order = Order::factory()->make(['user_id' => null]); // Only when a nullable unsaved parent is valid for this test.
```

#### Use an independent Faker generator for independent uniqueness state
- **Do:** When a fixture generator requires an independent unique() pool, construct a separate Faker generator rather than using the shared fake() singleton, and bound that generator to the relevant scenario.
- **Flag when:** Flag when unrelated fixture generation exhausts or alters a unique() pool that was assumed to be independent.
- **Why:** Shared Faker generators share uniqueness history, even when obtained from different callers.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
$scenarioFaker = Faker\Factory::create();
$code = $scenarioFaker->unique()->numerify('###');
```

#### Reset the resolved HTTP factory deliberately when a test needs a fresh one
- **Do:** Respect the Laravel HTTP Factory singleton during ordinary tests. If a scenario deliberately needs a fresh factory, forget the resolved container instance and clear an already resolved Http facade root before resolving it again, rather than changing its binding lifetime.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a test expects a new HTTP factory on every resolution or retains an old facade root after forgetting only the container instance.
- **Why:** The HTTP fake, recording and global configuration features depend on shared factory identity.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
$this->app->forgetInstance(Illuminate\Http\Client\Factory::class);
Http::clearResolvedInstance(Illuminate\Http\Client\Factory::class);
$factory = app(Illuminate\Http\Client\Factory::class);
```

#### Compare retained-memory measurements after garbage collection
- **Do:** When investigating retained PHP memory, collect eligible cycles before comparable memory_get_usage() snapshots, repeat the same workload, and temporarily disable optional cache events when isolating their contribution.
- **Flag when:** Flag when memory-leak conclusions compare inconsistent garbage-collection states or attribute event instrumentation overhead to the cache itself.
- **Why:** Uncollected cycles and optional instrumentation can distort the retained-memory baseline.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
gc_collect_cycles();
$before = memory_get_usage();
$runWorkload();
gc_collect_cycles();
$retainedBytes = memory_get_usage() - $before;
```

#### Verify after-commit event intent at application transaction boundaries
- **Do:** For application events implementing ShouldDispatchAfterCommit, use Event::fake() with a real application transaction and assert the event is absent before commit, recorded after commit and absent on rollback when those boundaries are the contract.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a transaction-sensitive event test checks only that an event is eventually recorded and cannot detect premature dispatch or rollback leakage.
- **Why:** Laravel event fakes preserve after-commit scheduling, so tests can verify transactional dispatch without executing listeners.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use an independent review pass for substantial AI-generated diffs
- **Do:** For substantial AI-assisted changes, give an independent reviewer model the requirements and concrete diff, request specific bugs, missing tests and convention violations, and feed confirmed findings back into a revision before human acceptance and validation.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a chosen writer/reviewer workflow lets the same generation self-approve without examining the diff against requirements.
- **Why:** A separate critique can expose assumptions and omissions the original generation repeated.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Exercise complex ingestion pipelines with realistic simulated input streams
- **Do:** For complex data pipelines, supplement focused tests with a repeatable simulator that feeds realistic ordered inputs through the full pipeline and verifies meaningful final outputs and failure cases.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a pipeline is tested only with isolated ideal samples that cannot expose realistic sequences, gaps or transitions.
- **Why:** Realistic streams reveal interactions and edge cases that unit-sized inputs can miss.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Load chat history in the direction that preserves chronological display
- **Do:** For chat/log interfaces that start at the newest entries, query the newest page first and use reverse infinite scrolling to load older pages upward while presenting entries in chronological order and preserving the reader position.
- **Flag when:** Flag when fetching older history reverses displayed chronology, appends it below newer messages or jumps the reader away from the current entry.
- **Why:** Fetch order, display order and loading direction must agree for a usable newest-first history view.
- **Enforced by:** manual

After:
```php
// Server: Message::query()->latest()->orderByDesc('id')->paginate()
// Client: <InfiniteScroll data="messages" reverse> with chronological display of messages.data.
```

#### Exercise extracted operations through existing UI entrypoints before cutover
- **Do:** When replacing a legacy UI and extracting shared application actions, route the existing UI through those tested operations before switching to the replacement UI, preserving the old response contract during the transition.
- **Flag when:** Flag when replacement actions are exercised only by the unreleased UI while the production legacy UI keeps a separate implementation that can drift.
- **Why:** Using one operation from the established flow validates the extraction independently of the new presentation layer.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Merge aggregate values atomically during conflict updates
- **Do:** When a conflict update must accumulate or retain an extremum rather than replace a stored value, express that merge atomically in the database conflict-update clause, using engine-compatible SQL and bound input values.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an aggregate upsert overwrites retained values or uses a race-prone read/modify/write sequence for an operation that must be atomic.
- **Why:** An atomic increment or maximum/minimum merge preserves concurrent contributions and the intended aggregate semantics.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use format expectations for supported formats
- **Do:** Use installed Pest format expectations rather than handwritten regular expressions for standard formats.
- **Flag when:** Flag when tests hand-write regexes for a format already supported by the installed Pest version.
- **Why:** Standard expectations avoid incomplete patterns and provide clearer diagnostics.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
expect($email)->toMatch("/.+@.+/");
```

After:
```php
expect($email)->toBeEmail();
```

#### Provision browser dependencies in CI
- **Do:** Install the browser engine and matching dependencies required by the project browser-test plugin locally and in CI.
- **Flag when:** Flag when browser jobs rely on a developer machine browser or omit required runtime dependencies.
- **Why:** Explicit provisioning makes browser tests reproducible.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use supported impact analysis for focused runs
- **Do:** Use test impact analysis for development feedback when the installed runner supports it, alongside full-suite integration checks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a costly local workflow always runs all tests despite supported impact selection, or impact-only runs replace all integration checks.
- **Why:** Impact selection reduces feedback time but still needs a complete integration gate.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Use consistent Pest declarations
- **Do:** Follow nearby Pest it()/test() conventions and use one style consistently within a file.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a test file mixes declaration styles without a semantic convention.
- **Why:** A stable declaration style makes specifications easier to scan.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
it("saves", $a); test("loads", $b);
```

After:
```php
it("saves", $a); it("loads", $b);
```

#### Test escaping for rendered untrusted text
- **Do:** Exercise HTML and mail rendering with malicious text in each user-controlled field.
- **Flag when:** Flag when rendered free-text fields lack escaping tests or are tested only with harmless values.
- **Why:** Injection regressions depend on context and individual rendering paths.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$user = User::factory()->create(["name" => "Alice"]);
```

After:
```php
$user = User::factory()->create(["name" => "<script>alert(1)</script>"]);
$this->get("/users/{$user->id}")->assertDontSee("<script>alert(1)</script>", false);
```

#### Test dynamic query input injection
- **Do:** Send injection payloads in dynamic sort columns, filter fields and directions and assert rejection or allowlisted handling.
- **Flag when:** Flag when dynamic SQL identifiers accept untested request values.
- **Why:** Bound values do not protect dynamic SQL identifiers and keywords.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Only sort=name is tested.
```

After:
```php
$this->getJson("/users?sort=name%3Bdrop%20table%20users")->assertUnprocessable();
```

#### Test protected attributes against unexpected input
- **Do:** Test that unexpected payload or configuration keys cannot modify protected attributes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when write tests omit attempts to set privileged or immutable attributes.
- **Why:** A valid payload test does not reveal overbroad mass assignment.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$this->postJson("/users", $valid)->assertCreated();
```

After:
```php
$this->postJson("/users", $valid + ["is_admin" => true]);
$this->assertDatabaseHas("users", ["email" => $valid["email"], "is_admin" => false]);
```

#### Construct MCP responses with supported factories
- **Do:** Return MCP content through Response factory methods rather than constructing Response directly.
- **Flag when:** Flag when MCP primitives instantiate new Response despite the package factory contract.
- **Why:** Factories construct the supported content and error shapes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return new Response("hello");
```

After:
```php
return Response::text("hello");
```

#### Fake spreadsheet delivery intent
- **Do:** Use Excel::fake() for spreadsheet import, export, storage or download intent assertions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when intent tests generate actual spreadsheets unnecessarily or contact storage.
- **Why:** Faking intent isolates the application dispatch contract.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$this->get("/export"); // generate full workbook
```

After:
```php
Excel::fake();
$this->get("/export");
Excel::assertDownloaded("orders.xlsx");
```

#### Inspect real spreadsheets for content tests
- **Do:** Generate and inspect a real spreadsheet when testing cells, formatting, sheets or writer behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag when spreadsheet content is considered tested solely through Excel::fake assertions.
- **Why:** An intent fake does not execute workbook generation.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Excel::fake(); Excel::assertDownloaded("orders.xlsx");
```

After:
```php
// Generate workbook in temporary storage; load it and assert cell values and sheet names.
```

#### Isolate PowerGrid test components
- **Do:** Build minimal local PowerGrid test components and keep behavior tests independent of themes and global fixtures.
- **Flag when:** Flag when PowerGrid behavior tests depend on unrelated global components or theme markup.
- **Why:** Local minimal fixtures make failures attributable to grid behavior.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Livewire::test(GlobalDemoTable::class);
```

After:
```php
Livewire::test(MinimalOrdersTable::class);
```

#### Cover PowerGrid data operations
- **Do:** Test PowerGrid search, filtering, sorting and pagination with records that distinguish their results.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a grid is tested only for initial rendering.
- **Why:** Data operations can display incorrect records even when the grid mounts successfully.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Livewire::test(OrdersTable::class)->assertOk();
```

After:
```php
// Change search/filter/sort/page and assert the resulting records and order.
```

#### Review image baselines and compare with tolerance
- **Do:** Use reviewed image snapshots with an intentional pixel-difference threshold.
- **Flag when:** Flag when image tests use unreviewed first-run baselines or require byte-identical renderer output despite harmless variation.
- **Why:** Visual output can vary slightly across renderers while remaining equivalent.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
expect($actualBytes)->toBe($expectedBytes);
```

After:
```php
// Compare against a reviewed baseline using an explicit pixel-difference tolerance.
```

#### Combine automated tests with human review
- **Do:** Use manual QA for usability and human judgment alongside automated regression tests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when release validation relies exclusively on automation for visual usability or exclusively on manual checks for regressions.
- **Why:** The two forms of checking detect different classes of defects.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Automate relevant local checks
- **Do:** Run relevant formatting and test checks from shared hooks/scripts and include JavaScript tests for staged JavaScript behavior changes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when the local workflow relies entirely on remembering checks despite shared hooks being the chosen project convention.
- **Why:** Automated selection gives fast repeatable feedback before CI.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Exercise interfaces with assistive technology
- **Do:** Test important UI flows with keyboard navigation, screen readers and relevant assistive-technology users.
- **Flag when:** Flag when accessibility verification consists only of a static automated scanner.
- **Why:** Real interactions reveal navigation and announcement failures static checks miss.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Test enlarged text and high-contrast display
- **Do:** Verify layouts and custom controls with browser zoom, larger user fonts and high-contrast settings.
- **Flag when:** Flag when UI testing uses only default scale and color settings.
- **Why:** Overflow, hidden controls and lost affordances can appear under accessibility display settings.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Run frontend behavior tests in CI
- **Do:** Run the frontend test suite in CI when the application contains tested JavaScript behavior.
- **Flag when:** Flag when frontend tests exist but CI runs only PHP checks.
- **Why:** Backend tests cannot detect regressions in browser-side JavaScript logic.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Test email-verification state after profile updates
- **Do:** Test that changing an email clears verification and leaving it unchanged preserves verification.
- **Flag when:** Flag when email-update coverage never checks email_verified_at for changed and unchanged addresses.
- **Why:** Verification of one address must not authorize a replacement address.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Assert only the new email value.
```

After:
```php
$this->actingAs($user)->patch("/profile", ["email" => "new@example.test"]);
expect($user->fresh()->email_verified_at)->toBeNull();
```

#### Rehearse database version upgrades
- **Do:** Test the target database version and application compatibility before attaching production workloads.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a production database major-version upgrade lacks a rehearsed application and migration test.
- **Why:** Database version changes can affect query behavior and compatibility.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Surface telemetry failures during tests
- **Do:** Configure telemetry integration tests to rethrow instrumentation exceptions.
- **Flag when:** Flag when telemetry failures are swallowed in tests intended to verify instrumentation.
- **Why:** Silent instrumentation failures leave observability tests falsely green.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Instrumentation test suppresses recorder exceptions.
```

After:
```php
// Test telemetry configuration: rethrow recorder exceptions.
```

#### Assert telemetry ingestion completes
- **Do:** Fail telemetry integration tests when expected entries remain un-ingested.
- **Flag when:** Flag when telemetry integration tests finish without checking recorder buffers or ingestion results.
- **Why:** Leftover entries can reveal broken flushing or delivery.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// End test with buffered telemetry.
```

After:
```php
expect($recorder->pendingEntries())->toBeEmpty(); // project recorder API
```

#### Keep PHPStan assertion contracts truthful
- **Do:** Write resolvable, type-compatible @phpstan-assert annotations against actual parameters or members.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an assertion annotation names a nonexistent parameter/member or narrows to an impossible or unverified type.
- **Why:** False assertion contracts make subsequent static analysis unsound.
- **Enforced by:** larastan:PHPStan\Rules\PhpDoc\FunctionAssertRule, larastan:PHPStan\Rules\PhpDoc\MethodAssertRule

Before:
```php
/** @phpstan-assert User $missing */
```

After:
```php
/** @phpstan-assert User $value */
function assertUser(mixed $value): void { if (! $value instanceof User) { throw new InvalidArgumentException(); } }
```

#### Handle absent AI raw responses
- **Do:** Null-check AI response raw metadata before accessing it.
- **Flag when:** Flag when agent response code dereferences raw unconditionally even though streaming, provider or fake responses may omit it.
- **Why:** Raw HTTP metadata is not present for every response mode.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$id = $step->raw->header("request-id");
```

After:
```php
$id = $step->raw?->header("request-id");
```

#### Pin AI model identity when behavior must stay stable
- **Do:** Specify Model explicitly when predictable model identity and behavior are required.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an agent requiring stable behavior uses a changing cheapest/smartest selection policy.
- **Why:** Pinning identity avoids automatic model changes on SDK upgrades; provider pricing still needs monitoring.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
#[UseSmartestModel]
```

After:
```php
#[Model("approved-model-id")]
```

#### Use typed AI classification for bounded decisions
- **Do:** Use typed classification questions for boolean, choice and score decisions instead of parsing unconstrained prose.
- **Flag when:** Flag when routing or moderation branches parse free-form AI text for an otherwise bounded decision.
- **Why:** Typed answers make downstream decision handling explicit and testable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
if (str_contains($reply, "yes")) { /* route */ }
```

After:
```php
// Ask a Boolean classification question and branch on its typed answer.
```

#### Exercise queued AI completion callbacks
- **Do:** Fake AI generation and assert then-callback effects when the callback is the behavior under test.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a queued AI callback contains business logic with no test that executes it.
- **Why:** Generation fakes can run completion callbacks with controlled responses.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Assert only that generation was queued.
```

After:
```php
// Fake generator, queue generation with then(...), assert callback persistence.
```

#### Suppress AI callbacks in dispatch-only tests
- **Do:** Fake the queue as well as AI generation when a test must verify dispatch without executing completion callbacks.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a dispatch-only AI test unintentionally executes its then callback through the generation fake.
- **Why:** Queue isolation prevents unrelated callback side effects from changing the dispatch test.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Image::fake(); // then callback still runs
```

After:
```php
Image::fake();
Queue::fake();
```

#### Test AI tool approval and continuation contracts
- **Do:** Test pending approvals and verify that approval decisions reach the resumed agent prompt.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an approval-gated tool flow lacks tests for pending approvals, accepted/rejected decisions or continuation propagation.
- **Why:** Approval tests protect the boundary between user decisions and tool execution.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Test only a prompt without pending approvals.
```

After:
```php
// Fake pending approvals; resume with decisions; assert hasApprovalDecisions() and decision values.
```

#### Assert queued AI invocation intent separately
- **Do:** Use queued assertions for queued agent and media-generation dispatches.
- **Flag when:** Flag when queued AI work is checked only with synchronous prompt/generated assertions.
- **Why:** Queued intent and completed generation are distinct contracts.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
SalesCoach::assertPrompted(); // queued-only path
```

After:
```php
SalesCoach::assertQueued();
```

#### Reject undefined AI fake invocations
- **Do:** Enable the matching preventStray API on AI fakes when every invocation must have an explicit response.
- **Flag when:** Flag when AI tests silently accept invocations for which no intended fake response was defined.
- **Why:** Strict fake coverage exposes unexpected prompts and generation paths.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
SalesCoach::fake(["Approved"]);
```

After:
```php
SalesCoach::fake(["Approved"])->preventStrayPrompts();
```

#### Reserve synchronous queues for deliberately synchronous environments
- **Do:** Use an asynchronous queue connection for production work that is intended to run in the background.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production background jobs use the sync connection and execute inside the request.
- **Why:** The sync driver provides deterministic local execution but does not offload request work.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync # production background processing
```

After:
```php
QUEUE_CONNECTION=redis
```

#### Model process failure results in tests
- **Do:** Supply realistic process output, stderr and exit codes for tested success and failure branches.
- **Flag when:** Flag when process-error handling is tested only with the default successful Process fake.
- **Why:** A default empty success cannot exercise failure parsing or exit-code handling.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Process::fake(); // failure test
```

After:
```php
Process::fake(["convert *" => Process::result(errorOutput: "invalid image", exitCode: 1)]);
```

#### Prevent stray external processes in tests
- **Do:** Enable Process::preventStrayProcesses() and define every intended command fake.
- **Flag when:** Flag when unmatched commands can execute real binaries in tests using command-pattern fakes.
- **Why:** Pattern omissions should fail immediately instead of launching uncontrolled subprocesses.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Process::fake(["git *" => "ok"]);
```

After:
```php
Process::fake(["git *" => "ok"]);
Process::preventStrayProcesses();
```

#### Choose sortable columns for one-of-many relations
- **Do:** Use an orderable aggregate column for one-of-many selection and account for database type limitations.
- **Flag when:** Flag when latestOfMany or oldestOfMany relies on an unsupported primary-key aggregate or uses the wrong ordering meaning.
- **Why:** The default ordering assumes a sortable key; chronological selection may require an explicit timestamp.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return $this->hasOne(Order::class)->latestOfMany(); // key unsuitable
```

After:
```php
return $this->hasOne(Order::class)->ofMany("placed_at", "max");
```

#### Exercise upload validation limits with deliberate file properties
- **Do:** Set fake upload dimensions and sizes to exercise accepted and rejected validation boundaries.
- **Flag when:** Flag when file-validation tests use only default fake images and never exercise configured size or dimension limits.
- **Why:** Deliberate file properties make validation boundary regressions observable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$file = UploadedFile::fake()->image("avatar.jpg");
```

After:
```php
$file = UploadedFile::fake()->image("avatar.jpg", 4000, 4000)->size(5000);
```

#### Return conventional command exit statuses
- **Do:** Return zero from successful commands and nonzero from failed commands.
- **Flag when:** Flag when an Artisan command reports success after failure or returns a failure status on success.
- **Why:** Shell scripts and CI rely on exit status to detect failure.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return 0; // required operation failed
```

After:
```php
return self::FAILURE; // required operation failed
```

#### Enable console events only for tests that need them
- **Do:** Apply WithConsoleEvents to the specific tests verifying console lifecycle events.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a test depends on suppressed CommandStarting/CommandFinished events without enabling them, or enables console events globally without need.
- **Why:** Selective enabling exercises event behavior while avoiding unnecessary listeners and memory use.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Base Tests\TestCase enables console events for every test.
```

After:
```php
class ConsoleEventsTest extends TestCase { use WithConsoleEvents; }
```

#### Prefer truncation for efficient Dusk database resets
- **Do:** Use DatabaseTruncation when full schema recreation is unnecessary in Dusk tests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a large Dusk suite reruns all migrations for every test without requiring fresh schema definitions.
- **Why:** Truncation keeps the migrated schema and removes test data between cases.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
use DatabaseMigrations;
```

After:
```php
use DatabaseTruncation;
```

#### Use a shared database for Dusk
- **Do:** Point Dusk and the served application at the same process-accessible database rather than SQLite :memory:.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Dusk fixtures are created in an in-memory database invisible to the browser server process.
- **Why:** In-memory SQLite connections cannot share state across the two processes.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
DB_DATABASE=:memory:
```

After:
```php
DB_DATABASE=/absolute/path/to/dusk.sqlite
```

#### Provision Zip for Dusk file attachment tests
- **Do:** Install and enable the Zip PHP extension wherever Dusk attach() tests run.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Dusk file-attachment tests run with ext-zip missing.
- **Why:** Dusk attachment support requires Zip in the test runtime.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Build frontend assets before browser tests
- **Do:** Install frontend dependencies reproducibly and build the assets consumed by browser tests.
- **Flag when:** Flag when CI opens application pages before required frontend assets have been built or served.
- **Why:** Browser tests need functional JavaScript and CSS to exercise the application.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Provision billing sandbox fixtures deliberately
- **Do:** Create the subscriptions, prices and other provider-side records needed by billing integration tests in the test account.
- **Flag when:** Flag when billing tests rely on undocumented manually existing live/test account records.
- **Why:** Provider fixtures make live sandbox integration tests reproducible.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Disable real broadcasting in ordinary tests
- **Do:** Use the null broadcaster or a suitable fake for tests that do not exercise broadcast delivery.
- **Flag when:** Flag when ordinary tests publish real broadcasts to external services.
- **Why:** Disabling unrelated transport prevents network side effects and cross-test interference.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
BROADCAST_CONNECTION=pusher
```

After:
```php
BROADCAST_CONNECTION=null
```

#### Provision GD for generated test images
- **Do:** Install and enable GD in test runtimes creating images with UploadedFile::fake()->image().
- **Flag when:** Flag when fake-image tests run without the GD extension.
- **Why:** Laravel image fixture generation requires GD support.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Isolate local S3-compatible storage
- **Do:** Use a dedicated local S3-compatible service or isolated test account for development storage.
- **Flag when:** Flag when local development writes to production S3 buckets.
- **Why:** An isolated endpoint exercises S3 semantics without risking production objects.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
AWS_BUCKET=production-files # local environment
```

After:
```php
AWS_ENDPOINT=http://rustfs:9000
AWS_BUCKET=local-files
```

#### Read testable application time through Laravel
- **Do:** Use now() or the Date facade instead of time() for timestamps that tests must control.
- **Flag when:** Flag when application timestamps bypass Laravel frozen time through native time().
- **Why:** Laravel clock helpers let tests exercise time-dependent behavior deterministically.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
$timestamp = time();
```

After:
```php
$timestamp = now()->unix();
```

#### Allow only deliberate live HTTP test destinations
- **Do:** Keep stray HTTP protection enabled and scope per-test allowStrayRequests exceptions to required destinations.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a live integration test removes the suite HTTP guard or allows unrestricted destinations.
- **Why:** Narrow exceptions preserve unexpected-network-call detection for the rest of the suite.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
Http::allowStrayRequests();
```

After:
```php
Http::allowStrayRequests(["https://sandbox.example.test/*"]);
```

#### Keep Faker out of production request paths
- **Do:** Use Faker only in tests, fixtures, seeders or deliberate prototypes unless it is a declared production dependency.
- **Flag when:** Flag when production request code invokes fake() while Faker is installed only through require-dev.
- **Why:** Production installs commonly omit development dependencies.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
return fake()->uuid(); // production endpoint
```

After:
```php
return (string) Str::uuid();
```

#### Use Paddle sandbox accounts outside production
- **Do:** Use a Paddle Sandbox account for local and staging payment development.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a nonproduction Paddle integration uses production account credentials or endpoints.
- **Why:** Sandbox separation prevents development payment flows from affecting real billing.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Manually verify Paddle billing integration
- **Do:** Exercise the complete Paddle billing flow manually in sandbox before releasing billing changes.
- **Flag when:** Flag when Paddle billing changes have no end-to-end sandbox verification evidence.
- **Why:** Provider-hosted checkout behavior can exceed what application tests simulate.
- **Enforced by:** manual

#### Make one-of-many selections deterministic
- **Do:** Use the built-in primary-key tie breaker for ordinary ofMany() selections. Specify an ordered aggregate map when the domain needs a different tie-breaking policy, and use columns supported by the database.
- **Flag when:** Flag when a one-of-many relationship resolves ties contrary to the required domain policy or aggregates an unsupported key type; do not flag omission of an explicit primary-key entry by itself.
- **Why:** Stable ordering makes the selected related record predictable.
- **Enforced by:** manual

Before:
```php
// Tied publication times must choose the smallest ID; the implicit tie breaker chooses the largest.
return $this->hasOne(Price::class)->ofMany("published_at", "max");
```

After:
```php
return $this->hasOne(Price::class)->ofMany(["published_at" => "max", "id" => "min"]); // Explicit domain tie-breaking policy.
```

#### Retain failed application test logs
- **Do:** Upload relevant application logs as artifacts when CI tests fail.
- **Flag when:** Flag when CI discards application logs needed to diagnose a failed integration test.
